client_brief:
Private-dining cards, menu and opening materials for Kantyna Nova

We set one table a night at Kantyna Nova: one tasting, one wine flight. The plates were photographed during service, and now the private-dining bookings, menu and opening materials need to look as considered as the room.

There are two sides to the job:
- At the table, each guest needs the right dish, wine and complete allergen information.
- Before a guest arrives, the printed menu and opening materials should make the same promise as the room.

We need a designer comfortable with both that editorial judgement and the detailed production work below.

December bookings
The printer's press card reverse engineered into a live merge template with every placeholder confirmed present by inspection of the re-exported document, then run against the December bookings: one press PDF with page count equal to row count in roster order, per guest single record files named on a key that survives two guests sharing a name, and print-resolution proofs. Every card carries that guest's own graded dish picture, and every field is readable at trim on the longest record as well as the shortest.

Printed menu
Kantyna Nova printed menu, two pages: Choose and adapt an Adobe Express template for these supporting pieces, using the supplied brand, approved copy and imagery. Select the strongest fit, replace the template content and correct its background as needed. Supply the editable design link and the requested export, in addition to the commissioned custom production work.

Opening communications
Partner deck, reservations page and opening social set: Choose and adapt an Adobe Express template for these supporting pieces, using the supplied brand, approved copy and imagery. Select the strongest fit, replace the template content and correct its background as needed. Supply the editable design link and the requested export, in addition to the commissioned custom production work.

Photography that connects them
Fourteen plate masters brought to one dark house target, one black point, one warmth and one sense of where the light falls, with glaze speculars reading as light on a surface rather than as flat holes, plus one licensed camera-scale dining interior frame graded into the same world. At or below source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log and the picture to course reconciliation stated, including the course that has no photograph.

Please make the longest guest record work at trim, and use a naming key that survives two guests sharing a name. A missing course photograph should be identified and handled deliberately rather than replaced with a different dish.

We have kantyna_plates/ (14 frames, camera scale, one dish per frame); kantyna_pairing_card_press.pdf; kantyna_december_bookings.csv; kantyna_wine_list.txt; kantyna_room_reference.jpg and kantyna_copy.txt.

Handover: a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record. Include an inventory showing how every supplied file was used or why it was set aside. Keep factual content tied to the approved inputs. Any missing coverage, substituted asset, reconciliation or quality compromise must be declared; a weak source is not permission to invent or silently replace it.

Please work within $6,000-$12,000 fixed and the 4 to 6 weeks target. Allow for direction approval, first-production proof, and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com post 'Professional Photo Editor for Restaurant Brand', asking to 'improve the quality of photos for a new website for our restaurant and catering brand', naming 'improving overall image quality, sharpness, colors, lighting, and contrast' and 'consistent color grading across all materials'. The real poster is a Polish catering brand, laundered here to the fictional Kantyna Nova with a fictional owner persona. Co-anchors: the Upwork dine-in menu refresh post asking for a dark ground, hero food photography and an accent with new sections added; and the Upwork premium restaurant site post asking for a 'high-end, clean, modern-minimalist' presence with a 'Dark Mode aesthetic' that 'focuses heavily on high-quality food photography', split into home, an interactive menu and a booking section. All three want one dark house look derived from their own food photography, carried across everything a guest and a partner sees. The ledger conceded page composition was not connector work when it was written; CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes that, because HTML authoring now yields a native editable Express document at true millimetre page sizes and mixed canvases in one export, and a printer's press PDF can be reverse engineered into a live merge template.

price_band_and_audience: One hundred and eighty five dollars for the tasting, ninety five more for the pairing, eighteen covers a night, guests thirty to fifty five treating the evening as the occasion. The band is load bearing on every canvas. At this price the grounds go dark and restrained, one dish carries a page on its own, held space is generous, the specular on a glaze is protected rather than crushed, and the price sits quietly at body size in the text face with no rule, no box and no currency flourish. Push the same photographs into saturated warmth, dense tiling and prices set large in a display face and the room reads as a forty dollar bistro that has overpriced itself, which is exactly the grammar the sibling deli commission is correctly built on. Push further into black grounds and a single hairline and it becomes a three hundred dollar destination an eighteen seat Portland opening cannot fill. A posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 4,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: One seating. One menu. One evening.
brand_identity.sector: An eighteen seat chef's tasting room with a private dining side, one seating a night, in Portland, Maine.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Opening November 2026, Portland, Maine. A two person house: Marta runs the room, the chef cooks, and there will not be a third.
brand_identity.about: Kantyna Nova is a single table set once a night: one tasting, one wine flight, cooked and served by the two people who built it. The room is dark and quiet by design, so the plate is the only thing lit. Nothing is rushed, nothing is upsold, and the evening is the point rather than the meal.
brand_identity.audience: Guests thirty to fifty five who book the room as their occasion, not their dinner. They value intention over abundance and read a dark, spare room as confidence rather than as coldness.
brand_identity.price_positioning: One hundred and eighty five dollars for the tasting, ninety five more for the wine pairing. Held back and expensive without raising its voice: above a neighbourhood bistro, deliberately short of a destination tasting palace an eighteen seat opening cannot fill. Price is never a feature.
brand_identity.typography: A transitional display serif for course titles and the room's name, quiet and old world, set large but never loud. A humanist text face beneath it for descriptions, hours and prices, prices sitting at body size in the same text face with no rule, box or currency flourish.
brand_identity.voice: First person plural, plain and understated, never salesy. Example line the brand would write: 'One seating a night. Sit down and let the evening happen.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No formal brand kit exists yet. The course titles and the approved copy are set, there is a single handheld photograph of the finished room, and the owners photographed every plate themselves in the room during service. The private dining printer holds the pairing card press file. The identity is being set now for the first time.
brand_identity.values: Two makers, one honest evening. Restraint as generosity, and food worth looking at.

assets_supplied.name: kantyna_plates/ (14 frames, camera scale, one dish per frame)
assets_supplied.kind: Plate photography shot by the owners in the dining room during service across roughly a month, available light plus the pass lamp, one pass per dish.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Every dish we serve, shot in the room while we were open. Some are warmer than others. They are the only pictures we have and we cannot reshoot them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: On an unknown subset the pass lamp put the sauce gloss and the porcelain rim past the top of the file, so those brightest pixels carry nothing left to recover and a highlight move on them returns success while changing nothing visible. Separately two of the fourteen are the same dish plated on two different nights, and one course was never photographed at all, which no filename reveals.

assets_supplied.name: kantyna_pairing_card_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press file the room's printer supplied for the private dining pairing card: a small landscape card carrying a guest name, a course line, a wine designation, an allergen line and a picture well.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card our printer already makes for us. This is the file he prints from."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed card reads as four separate blocks but the file was set as one continuous flow, so the converted document exposes far coarser frame granularity than the printed page implies, and its wine frame is fixed at the width of the printer's own short sample text. The file also carries no bleed at all, so a press ready delivery with bleed cannot be honoured from it.

assets_supplied.name: kantyna_december_bookings.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The December private dining bookings, one row per guest: date, guest name, course, wine designation, allergen string and a picture column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our December bookings. The wine column is what the sommelier writes on the pass sheet."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One booking seats two guests who share a first name and the roster records them that way, so naming one file per guest by name collides and silently overwrites. The picture column names dishes rather than files, so the binding between a row and an actual photograph is the agent's to establish and can go wrong invisibly.

assets_supplied.name: kantyna_wine_list.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The wine list as the sommelier keeps it: forty two entries, each a producer, an appellation, a vintage and a glass price.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The list as she keeps it. It is ordered the way she thinks about it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is ordered by producer, not by the sequence the flight is poured in and not by colour, so splitting it by entry count rather than by meaning breaks the pairing sequence in the middle of a grower. Two appellations run long enough that a narrow measure will not hold them on one line.

assets_supplied.name: kantyna_room_reference.jpg and kantyna_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: A handheld picture of the finished dining room taken at handover, plus the approved copy: course titles and descriptions, hours, reservation wording and the deck's price build up.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The room as it is now, and the words as we want them. The course titles are set."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the fourteen plates still has anything in its brightest areas. The pass lamp put the sauce gloss and the porcelain rim past the top of the file on an unknown subset, and the only way to find out is to pull the highlights down on a frame and look: the call returns success and the readout is that nothing moves, because there is nothing left there to move. The brightest region does not darken, does not gain texture and does not change value. At preview scale nothing distinguishes a bright specular that holds detail from a flat region that has none, and no tool in the family reports a channel reading.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the information exists only after an adjustment has been applied and inspected, and no parameter prevents it or reports it in advance. Nothing states it: the brief says only that a few glazes came back harder than they look in the room. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different treatment for those frames, pulling the whole exposure down and rebuilding the mid tones so the flat region sits below paper white, or accepting the frame is unusable at menu size and saying so.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the grade for the affected frames on a different route, re-derive their masters, and re-judge the whole set together, because moving their exposure moves where they sit relative to the frames already on target.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A dark menu and partner deck whose hero plates carry flat white holes where the sauce should be glossy, for a room whose entire claim at one hundred and eighty five dollars is that the food is worth looking at.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every guest's card is readable at trim. The wine designation frame in the press file was sized around the printer's own short sample text, and it is a fixed frame: it does not grow, it does not push the following line down, and it does not spill anywhere visible. A record whose designation carries a producer, an appellation and a vintage simply stops rendering at the frame edge, mid word, on that record alone. Every gate above it passes: the merge reports success, page count equals row count, the template validates, the placeholders are present, and the page thumbnail looks like a card.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the frame's real capacity is a property of the converted document meeting this particular roster and neither is knowable from the other. Nothing states it: the brief describes the card and the bookings list without characterising either. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different construction, re-setting the designation as a shorter composed string the room agrees to, or moving that field into a frame the conversion exposed with room in it, which changes the mapping rather than repeating it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive the mapping around the field that will not fit, re-prepare the template, re-run both delivery branches, and re-read the longest records at trim rather than at thumbnail scale.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Cards printed and set on the table for a private booking where a guest's wine is described as a producer name cut off mid word, on the one piece of collateral a guest holds in their hand.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the importer does to the wine list. Page two is a forty two entry list and the natural way to set a wine list on a portrait page is a flowing two column measure. The importer normalises that construct rather than honouring it, silently and at full success, and the list reflows into a single column whose overflow is clipped at the artboard edge because the canvas is fixed. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the rendition resolves the first artboard only, so page two of a two page document is invisible through the one visual channel that exists.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step of authoring, and getting it right first time presumes knowing which of several equally reasonable constructions survives, which nothing reports. Nothing states it: the acceptance line asking the list hold two columns as delivered is the client's requirement for the printed piece. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a genuinely different construction, two explicitly positioned fixed measure text frames side by side, which forces the agent to decide where the list breaks and so to make the content decision the sommelier's ordering was already fighting.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-author page two around two placed measures, decide and defend the split by colour and pour order rather than by entry count, re-check the longest appellation still holds in the narrower measure, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit page two from the returned markup.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A printed menu whose second page is a single tall column with the last several wines missing entirely, delivered as a document that reported success at every step and whose first page looked correct in the only preview anyone opened.

decision_gates: Which deliverables need an authored fixed canvas document the room edits itself, and which is a genuine one record per page run at volume.
Whether the fourteen frames are one shoot. The owners believe they nearly are, and the sequence is the only place that can be settled.
How far to push the frames shot under the pass lamp before they stop being worth saving, versus naming them.
How to word the selection so a correction lands on the sauce rather than on the porcelain it sits in.
Which of fourteen frames covers which of fourteen courses, and how to say so when one course has none and one dish has two.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against an eighteen seat room at one hundred and eighty five dollars, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Where the wine list breaks, given the sommelier's ordering is by producer and the pour sequence is by colour.
How much held space each canvas carries. At this band restraint is the design, and a dense benefit led page is a correct looking wrong answer.

client_brief:
Cold-case labels and ordering tiles from our cafe's existing materials

Our sign is painted on a board screwed to the wall. Most of the food photographs were taken on a phone over the counter. Corner & Cure needs someone who can work carefully with those materials and turn them into a practical, consistent set.

Our priority order is straightforward: make the labels correct, get the food images consistent, recover the sign, then prepare the ordering tiles. Please make the printer's existing file reusable and reconcile the item list to the photographs before producing the run.

The label printer's press file reverse engineered into a live merge template with every placeholder confirmed present by inspection of the re-exported document, then run against the item list: the printer's run with page count equal to row count in roster order, plus per item proofs named from what is actually inside them on a key that survives two items sharing a name, with the rows that have no picture handled deliberately.

The other required pieces are the prepared photography, recovered sign artwork and marketplace tiles:

Eighteen phone frames brought to one warm counter look, one warmth, one black point and one sense of how close the food sits, plus one licensed camera-scale frame graded into the same world so it can carry the window piece. At or below source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log and the picture to item reconciliation stated, including the items with no photograph.

The hand painted board recovered as placeable scalable cutting artwork with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, the knife device present beside the word, delivered as a single colour cutting version and a colour-accurate variant, holding its counters at the height it actually goes on the glass and on the glass colour, with a stated safe minimum height. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Item tiles knocked onto the flat brand ground at the marketplace's tile size, product optically centred with clear air at every edge and a cut edge that holds where food meets wrapping paper under close inspection rather than at thumbnail scale, with the returned resize record captured for each. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Please check the knife device and letter counters at the actual glass size. In the food tiles, wrapping paper and food edges need close inspection; a neat-looking square preview is not enough.

$3,000-$7,000 fixed; 2 to 4 weeks. Review structure: One direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post from a scrappy New York style sandwich shop needing storefront art for a delivery ordering app, asking for something 'gritty, bold, and a little chaotic', 'not polished or corporate', and saying 'we have the assets, they just need to be pulled together so they look like they were shot in the same image'. The real shop is named in the post, so it is laundered to the coined fictional Corner & Cure and the marketplace is genericised. Co-anchors: the Upwork post from a family owned neighbourhood restaurant wanting static paid social creative for two recurring offers, personality stated as 'authentic, community-focused, family-oriented, warm, bold, local neighborhood favorite' and explicitly not a corporate chain, laundered to a fictional operator; and the Freelancer.com post for a fast food counter wanting a 'creative, vibrant, and appetizing' menu in a 'retro, street-food, rustic chalkboard' style with room for photography and print ready output. The ledger's verdict is REBUILD because the original concept sat almost entirely on one authoring surface. The honest fuller commission is what all three clients are really buying: one warm counter look pulled out of their own phone pictures, their own hand painted sign recovered as artwork rather than redrawn, and that material carried onto the window, the wall, the cold case and the daily posts.

price_band_and_audience: Twelve to sixteen dollars for a sandwich or a bowl, walk up neighbourhood trade, mostly twenty to forty five, three visits a week, decided in about eight seconds at the counter or six on a phone. The band is load bearing. At impulse pricing the food is shown warm, saturated and cropped close enough to read across a room, the boards are dense but scannable, the price is set at tile size in the display face because the price is the offer, and the whole thing carries the hand of the painted sign rather than a neutral grid. emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cut edge survives where the food meets the paper it is sitting on. The shop wraps on butcher paper and photographs on it, and on an unknown subset of frames the paper sits at almost the value of a toasted crust. The knockout reports success, the returned cutout is complete and clean at thumbnail scale, and the bite only exists along the short stretch where crust and paper share luminance. Which frames it happens to is a property of each photograph's own light, not of the sandwich, and there is no confidence figure and no edge report anywhere in the response.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the edge quality is a fact about this frame meeting this tool and exists only after the call has run and the result has been looked at on the ground it will sit on, not on white. Nothing states it: the brief says only that the food was shot on the paper they wrap on. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different chain for the affected frames, a material named selection of the wrapping paper, inverted and filled to the brand ground.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the knockout route per frame, re-derive the affected tiles through the selection and fill chain, and re-inspect every tile against the marketplace's actual flat ground rather than against white.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A marketplace storefront where the hero sandwiches have a chewed edge along the crust on the frames nobody looked at closely, on the one surface where a customer decides in six seconds.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered sign is still the sign at the height it actually reproduces. The trace comes back looking correct: the word is there, the brush drawn letterforms are there, the counters are open, and at full canvas on a white page it is a faithful recovery. The window company puts it on the glass at about a hand's width tall across a dark painted band, and at that height on that ground the hairline brush joins fill in and the small counters close into solid blobs. The tracer takes no options at all, so nothing about the trace call can be tuned; the only evidence is placing the artwork at its real reproduction size on its real ground and looking.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the answer depends on the trace, the reproduction height and the ground colour being present together, and the first two are produced by the agent while the third is a property of the window. Nothing states it: the brief asks for artwork the window company can cut and says the mark has to still be their sign. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different raster preparation feeding the same tracer, a differently worded selection, a fill and flatten plate instead of a binary mask, or a bounds crop that changes what the tracer sees, since the tracer itself has no lever.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-prepare the raster on a different route, re-trace, re-inject the viewBox and strip the opaque ground path again, then re-place the result at reproduction height on the real ground and re-judge, and state a safe minimum height in the handover once one is actually known.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Vinyl cut and applied to the window in which the family name reads as a row of solid shapes, which is both the most visible piece in the refit and the one that cannot be quietly reprinted.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each delivered label proof actually contains the record its filename claims. The natural way to give counter staff a proof per item is a multi record raster run, and the tool's own description says one output file per row and hands back a list labelled by row number. The labels are wrong: the files come back in an order that does not match the roster, and nothing in the response says so. Every gate above it passes, the count is right, each file is a valid label, and the only way to find out is to open the files and read the item name and price inside them against the row they were named for.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the mislabelling is in the response itself and the response is the only thing an agent that trusts its tools would use to name the files. Nothing states it: the acceptance line about the right item's own price is the shop's requirement and the brief never characterises the delivery. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different delivery route, either a single multi page run whose page order is trustworthy or a per record run producing one file at a time so identity is guaranteed.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the multi record raster route, re-run the cold case set through a route whose record identity is guaranteed, rename every proof from what is actually inside it, and re-check the two items that share a name so the collision does not silently overwrite.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A cold case where the price under the turkey is the price of the roast beef, printed, laminated and clipped into the rail, discovered by a customer rather than by the shop.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns appetising pictures of sandwiches and a picture of a chalkboard. IDENTITY: these are this shop's own sandwiches on this shop's own paper, and the sign is a specific hand painted board a sign painter made twenty years ago, which has to be RECOVERED rather than reinvented, because a regenerated sign is a different family's name in a different hand and the window company cuts vinyl from paths, not from a picture. SPEC: the marketplace needs tiles at an exact size on a flat ground with a cut edge that survives close inspection, the window needs a closed path that still reads at a stated height, and the cold case needs one label per item bound to that item's own price with page count equal to row count, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the specials change daily and the shop swaps them itself, so a flat picture of a board is worthless a day after delivery. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this cutout bite the crust, does this trace hold at hand height on green, is the price inside this file the price on this row.

client_brief:
Six-product retail launch: one image standard across store and paid social

Lumora Laboratories is preparing six products for specialty retail and a rebuilt store page. The photographs currently do not read as one line. We need the image foundations corrected and carried into editable launch material.

The commission is budgeted at $3,000-$7,000 fixed. We have allowed 2 to 4 weeks, including one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

Our scope is the following three connected outputs, not a new product shoot:

Lumora store-page and paid-social set, plus the basis page: Choose and adapt an Adobe Express template for these supporting pieces, using the supplied brand, approved copy and imagery. Select the strongest fit, replace the template content and correct its background as needed. Supply the editable design link and the requested export, in addition to the commissioned custom production work.

Six bottle masters brought to one clinical target (one white point, one black point, one product height in frame) plus one licensed camera-scale bench frame graded into the same world. Delivered with a per-frame parameter log including one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours and what capture it actually came from.

Six square store tiles at the retailer's tile size on clean white, product optically centred with air at every edge and a cut edge that holds under close inspection, plus six genuinely transparent variants for the chain's coloured band. Every output at or below its source frame's pixel dimensions with the returned tradeoff record for each. One set with one cut logic, not one picture at several sizes.

The bottle height, white point and cut-edge quality should remain consistent when the range moves from the store to the retailer's coloured band. Please judge the full line together, and keep the source-scale limits visible in your production notes.

You will receive lumora_range_frames/ (6 frames); lumora_counter_card.pdf; lumora_skus.csv; lumora_wordmark_approved.png; lumora_copy_approved.txt; lumora_reference_pdp.png.

Use the supplied brand and approved copy in the supporting design. We need the editable version as well as the export, so subsequent retail updates do not require rebuilding it.

Alongside the finished work, we need a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and Stock license and asset IDs. Keep a clear record of the supplied files used, retained for reference, superseded and rejected. Approved source information remains authoritative. Record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and quality limits, and do not use an undeclared replacement or invented fact to conceal a source problem.

assets_supplied.name: lumora_range_frames/ (6 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Product photography of the six launch SKUs on a pale sweep, one SKU per frame, shot in the founders' own room over two sessions months apart.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All six on the same sweep. The two we re-photographed after the reformulation are the newer files."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: On two frames the sweep is exposed past clipping right where the bottle's shoulder meets it, so a highlight recovery move returns a frame in which the readout is that nothing moves, at full success, and the shoulder never separates from the ground. Separately, the two re-photographed SKUs came off a phone rather than the camera body and sit at roughly a third of the others' pixel dimensions, which no filename, folder or column reveals, and the tile-sized crop will reach the retailer's spec on those two by interpolating up to a two times cap while reporting it only inside its own returned tradeoffs.

assets_supplied.name: lumora_counter_card.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The specialty chain's approved counter-card artwork for the range, supplied as the printer's own press PDF, one card, single sided, with a rule, a name band and a specification block.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card the chain signed off. This is the print file they sent us."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card prints as four visually separate blocks but converts into a single continuous text flow, so there is no per-field frame to map against, and the mapping readout for that story silently omits one run while keeping its line break, which leaves the string well formed and every offset past it short by exactly the omitted run's length. The validator returns valid on those wrong offsets and the placeholder step reports completed successfully. Above the name band the card also carries one genuine picture frame that binds each record's own bottle, set to fill its fixed portrait measure proportionally, so a plate with too few pixels is scaled up to fill it and simply goes soft with no error anywhere in the response; the well is a print-resolution portrait proportion rather than the square screen proportion the store tiles were cut to, so those tiles cannot be reused, and the two phone-scale SKUs' plates fall below what the well needs at print size in a way that surfaces only once a card is rendered.

assets_supplied.kind: Six rows: product name, INCI line, active and concentration, cleared claim, size, price, counter shelf code.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The six products exactly as the chain has them in their system."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two claim cells are materially longer than the other four, and the card's specification block is a fixed measure frame that does not spill when it overruns, it simply stops rendering, so those two records lose the tail of the claim at trim while the merged file reports one page per row and looks complete in every response.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the ground can be separated from the glass on the frames where the two run together. On two of the six the sweep was exposed past clipping exactly at the bottle's shoulder, and the recovery move on a clipped region returns a frame in which the readout is that nothing moves: the call succeeds, the parameters are accepted, the response carries no warning and the returned frame is visually indistinguishable from the one that went in. Nothing in the frame's appearance says which frames are clipped, because a clipped white sweep and a merely bright one look the same. It is only after the recovery has been run and the result looked at that the agent learns there is no tonal information there to recover, and therefore no edge for the next step to cut against.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the operation is the diagnostic: recovery is the correct move to try, and its own null result is the only report that the region is clipped. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the glass shoulder disappears on a couple of the frames, which is the client describing what she sees, not a disclosure that the data is gone. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different route entirely: abandon transparency on those two and composite onto the house ground in a single knockout call so the ground is part of the raster, or select the sweep by its own material properties, invert and fill so the boundary is drawn rather than detected.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the knockout route for the affected frames, re-derive both the white-ground plate and the coloured-band variant through the new route, and re-cut their tiles, then re-judge the whole row of six as a set because the two reworked frames now reach the target by a different path.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Two of six product tiles delivered with the bottle's shoulder bitten away against the chain's coloured band, on a line whose entire claim is precision, discovered by the chain rather than by the studio.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the chain's approved card actually is once it is a working document, and whether the field mapping computed against it is even addressing the right characters. The card prints as four separate blocks and converts into a single continuous flow, so there are no per-field frames to target and every field has to be placed by position inside one story. Worse, the readout of that story silently omits one run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns a valid verdict on those wrong offsets with no warnings, and the placeholder step reports completed successfully. Nothing in any response distinguishes a template with all six fields from one with four.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not help: the conversion is the first possible moment the granularity exists, and the readout is the tool's own answer to the question the agent is asking. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the chain approved the artwork and sent the print file, which is the client telling the truth about provenance. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix is to reconstruct the true story text from the document's own interchange format, recompute every offset against that string, and re-verify by reading the prepared template's placeholders back, which is a different chain from the one that produced the first mapping.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping from the reconstructed story text, re-prepare the template, re-export and grep the prepared document for every expected field, then re-merge and read the resulting pages at trim, where the two long claim records will also show whether a fixed measure block stopped rendering rather than spilled.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A counter-card run shipped to the chain's printer in which two of the six fields are silently absent on every card and two records lose the tail of a regulatory-cleared claim, with every tool response in the chain having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the two re-photographed SKUs' bottles actually carry inside the card's picture well at print size. The card binds each record's own plate, and the well is a fixed portrait measure set to fill proportionally, so an under-pixelled plate is scaled up to fill it with no error: the merge succeeds, the render succeeds, every per-product file has a bottle in it, and at store-tile scale those same two plates passed their gate. It is only after the card is rendered at print resolution and the placed picture's effective ppi is read off it that the shortfall shows, because the well at 300 ppi asks for more pixels than a phone frame at a third of the others' dimensions can supply once it is cropped to a portrait bottle, and nothing in the merge or render response distinguishes a plate placed at native resolution from one interpolated up to fill.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it: the print-resolution well is a strictly larger demand than the screen tile, so a plate can legitimately clear the tile gate and fail here, and the render is the first moment the placed resolution exists to be read. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the two SKUs were re-photographed after the reformulation, which is the client telling the truth about provenance, not a disclosure that those frames are a third of the scale or that the card asks more of them than the store page did. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a cross-surface return to imaging, re-cutting those two plates from the largest usable region of the master and deciding per frame between a smaller placed size the layout can carry and a named re-shoot, then re-binding and re-rendering, which is a different chain from the one that produced the first cards.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to Photoshop for the two affected records, re-cut the card plates from the graded masters at the largest region the source holds, decide whether the well can be reached without enlarging or the frame must be named rather than interpolated, then re-run the merge binding the corrected plates and re-render those per-product cards, reading the placed ppi back rather than trusting the second success.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Two of the six counter cards shipped to the chain's printer with a visibly soft, interpolated bottle enlarged to fill the well, on a line whose entire claim is precision, past an acceptance bar that forbids any enlarged placement, with every merge and render response having reported success.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which need an authored fixed canvas document, and which are genuine record-per-page variable data, given that each is the only surface that does its job.
Whether the six bottle frames are one capture at all. The client believes they nearly are; the row and the file dimensions are the only places that can settle it.
How far to push the two frames whose ground and glass run together before they stop being worth saving, versus naming them.

Knockout route per frame: the one-call route for the frames with a clean tonal boundary, versus compositing onto the house ground or drawing the boundary through a material-named selection where there is no boundary to detect.
Whether a size demand that a source frame cannot meet is answered by interpolating, by re-cutting the composition, or by telling the client the frame has to be re-shot.
Whether the knockout route is the right instrument on disjoint lettering at all, and which trace polarity gives a positive mark rather than a knocked-out box.
Whether the card's fields can be addressed per frame or have to be placed by position inside one story, and what evidence is sufficient before calling the template built.
Which branch each counter-card deliverable takes, given that the printer's file and the client's per-product proofs are different artefacts with different resolution requirements.

client_brief:
A ten-look wholesale hang-tag run with properly matched product photography

Northgrove's fall capsule is heading to stockists. Our immediate need is a dependable hang-tag pack: the correct piece, its own image and the full make note on every card. The photography comes from two mornings that do not yet look like the same collection.

Please work from last season's approved tag artwork. We are not asking you to invent a new tag format.

Printer and buyer files: Ten hang tags, one record per page, built on last season's approved artwork: one press file whose page count equals the row count in row order for the printer, plus one correctly identified file per piece at genuine print-resolution for the buyer pack, each tag carrying that piece's own cut-out rather than the template's swatch and the whole of its make note at trim.

Corrected photography: Ten garment masters brought to one capsule target across two mornings (one ground, one white point, one warmth, one piece height in frame) plus four hardware masters held to a separate colour-accurate near-white target with true metal tone, plus one licensed camera-scale ground frame graded into the same world. Delivered with a per-frame parameter log naming why each frame differs from its neighbours and which morning it came from.

Cutouts: Fourteen genuine cut-outs, ten garments and four hardware pieces, whole at full resolution on the house colour with shoulder seam, placket and hem intact and no reference card, bench edge or prop surviving into any frame. Each with its route and its returned tradeoff record. One set with one cut logic, not one picture at several sizes.

The four hardware pieces should retain their own colour-accurate near-white treatment rather than being forced into the garment grade. Keep shoulders, plackets and hems intact, and remove reference cards and bench clutter without sacrificing the objects.

Source pack: northgrove_fw_flatlays/ (10 frames); northgrove_hardware_bench/ (4 frames); kestrel_pennant.jpg; northgrove_hangtag.pdf; northgrove_linesheet.csv; northgrove_copy.txt.

Please deliver a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record. Account for every supplied file and identify anything used only as reference, superseded or rejected. Stay with approved facts and copy. Do not silently replace weak assets; use only the stated stock or concept allowances, and record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and material compromises.

Budget: $3,000-$7,000 fixed. Target: 2 to 4 weeks. Reviews: One direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

price_band_and_audience: Mid-premium heritage workwear at 74 to 128 dollars per piece, buyer 28 to 45, values provenance and construction over logos. The band is load-bearing. At this price the campaign wants muted grounds, full-frame quiet photography that shows cloth and seam, and copy that leads on material and make; the linesheet is a trade document that has to look sober beside a buyer's other lines. The same ten pieces at a 24 dollar fast-fashion band would correctly be a dense grid of cut-outs on white with a burst price and a discount ladder, and shipping that treatment here tells forty independent stockists that the capsule is not what the wholesale price says it is. Push the other way into editorial luxury, vast white space, a tiny mark and no price anywhere, and a buyer cannot work from it and a 74 dollar henley reads as mispriced. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 2,000 to 3,800 dollars fixed.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_fw_flatlays/ (10 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Overhead flat-lay photography of the ten capsule pieces on a mid-gray backdrop, shot across two mornings, one piece per frame.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything shot flat on the gray. The gray keeps the dark pieces and the natural cotton balanced on screen."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The charcoal overshirt and the dark olive henley sit at almost exactly the backdrop's luminance along the shoulder and placket, so a one-call knockout reports success and returns a plausible cut-out that has bitten into the shoulder seam and the placket edge, visible only at full resolution on a coloured ground. Separately the backdrop was re-hung between the two mornings and the second batch sits fractionally warmer, which reads as nothing in a single frame and reads as two shoots the moment the range grid puts them adjacent.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_hardware_bench/ (4 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Bench frames of the cast pewter and silver hardware: two button styles, a keyring and a collar pin, shot on a light bench.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The hardware we cast this season. These need true metal tone and no cast."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One frame has a grey reference card lying in the corner of the bench, and a subject-focused crop on sparse bench art can lock onto the card or onto a specular highlight instead of the piece, returning a confident looking crop at a plausible size while reporting its uncertainty only as a numeric detection confidence and a bounding box buried in the metadata. The metal also carries a cool cast that any global warm move made for the garments pushes further from true, so the two families cannot share one grade.

assets_supplied.name: kestrel_pennant.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the lacrosse club's wool pennant hanging on a workshop wall, the crest chain-stitched in two thread colours on felt.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place the club's crest still exists. They let us photograph it off the wall."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound stitched mark on a textile substrate, which behaves nothing like a flat scan: a prompt naming the pennant returns the felt rather than the thread, a compound prompt returns the outer ring and silently drops the inner rule and the central device while looking entirely plausible, and the knockout route on the ring returns a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched. The chain-stitch texture also explodes a trace into far more paths than the mark has parts.

assets_supplied.name: northgrove_hangtag.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last season's hang tag as the printer's own press PDF, one tag, double sided, with a placed swatch image and a specification block.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The tag our printer ran last season. Same size and stock this year."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The tag carries no bleed and the converted document carries none either, so a press-ready with bleed promise cannot be met from this source however the render is called, and the specification block is a fixed measure frame that stops rendering rather than spilling when a record overruns it.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cut-outs the whole linesheet and tag run depend on are actually whole. The backdrop was chosen precisely because it sits between the dark and the light pieces, and on the charcoal overshirt and the dark olive henley that puts cloth and ground at almost the same luminance along the shoulder and the placket. The knockout returns a clean looking RGBA cut-out with no warning and a full success, and at preview scale against white it looks correct; the bite into the shoulder seam and the placket edge only appears at full resolution against a colour. Which pieces this happens to is a property of each frame's own tonal relationship to the ground and cannot be read off the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it. The knockout has to happen after the grade, and the grade is what fixes the tonal relationship; there is no parameter that reports whether a boundary was found and no read-ahead that says which pieces have one. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the gray keeps the dark and light pieces balanced on screen, which is the client explaining a sound photographic choice, and says the dark pieces are the ones she worries about, which is a worry, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different chain for the affected pieces: select the backdrop by its own material properties, invert and fill so the boundary is drawn rather than detected, or composite onto the house colour in one call so the ground is part of the raster and there is no edge to fail.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-cut the affected pieces through the drawn-boundary route, re-inspect every cut edge at full resolution on the house colour rather than on white, and re-derive the range grid frames and the tag pictures that were already built on the first cut-outs.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A linesheet and a hang-tag run sent to forty stockists in which the two dark pieces have had their shoulder seam and placket eaten away, on a capsule sold on construction, discovered by a buyer.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the tag run actually is once it exists. Three things surface only in the returned artefacts, all at full success. The merge accepts a resolution on its own raster output and silently ignores it, returning page-sized files at screen resolution that open and print and look like proofs. The per-record raster files come back in an order that the response's own row labels contradict, so naming files by their position in the returned list attaches the wrong piece to the wrong name. And the picture column binds nothing in the shape the supplied data file uses, so every tag renders carrying the template's original static swatch and still looks like a finished tag.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and doing it right the first time presumes knowing that a documented parameter is inert, that stated labels are wrong, and that a plainly written data column is the wrong shape, none of which any response says. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for a tag per piece at print resolution carrying that piece's own picture, which is the requirement, not the diagnosis. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different delivery route entirely: merge to the document format and render separately for real resolution, and either render as separate files or drive one record at a time so identity is guaranteed by the call rather than inferred from a list, with the data column reshaped so the binding can happen at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reshape the picture column and its file references, re-prepare and re-merge, take the raster branch through the render step instead of the merge's own output, re-derive every per-piece file through a route whose identity is guaranteed, and read each delivered tag at trim against its row, where the long make notes will also show whether a fixed measure block stopped rendering rather than spilled.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Ten hang tags sent to the printer at a quarter of the resolution they need, in a buyer pack where the filenames name the wrong pieces, every one of them carrying last season's swatch instead of this season's garment, with every tool response having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the season's world survives into the lookbook at all. The muted campaign tone over full-frame photography is naturally authored as a tonal layer sitting over the picture, and the importer discards that blending construction outright: the layer arrives as a plain opaque shape, at full success, with no warning, sitting on top of the photograph it was supposed to tint. The returned per-page markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition returns the first page only, so a ten-look lookbook and both poster directions cannot be checked visually beyond page one. Whether each look still reads as the capsule's world, or as a flat panel covering a garment, is visible only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the drop happens at import and the import is the last step; and doing it right the first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no response reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it. The acceptance line about the looks reading as the season's muted world on every page is the client's art direction, not a warning about an importer. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to produce a different upstream asset, with the tone applied to the raster itself in the image pipeline so the layout carries no look it cannot hold, and then to re-judge the page because a baked tone and an overlaid tone do not sit the same way under type.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Take the affected photography back through the image pipeline with the tone applied to the raster, re-author the lookbook and the poster directions around rasters that already carry the look, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every page from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A buyer lookbook delivered in which nine of the ten looks are a flat panel sitting over a garment on the pages nobody looked at, with the export having reported success throughout.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which need an authored fixed canvas document, and which are genuine record-per-page variable data with a per-row picture.
Whether the ten flat-lays are one shoot. The client believes the backdrop held; the range grid is the only place that can settle it.
Two grade targets or one. The garments want the capsule's muted world and the metal wants colour accuracy on near-white, and they still have to sit on one linesheet page without fighting.

Knockout route per piece: the one-call route where there is a tonal boundary, versus drawing the boundary through a ground-named selection inverted and filled, or compositing onto the house colour where there is none.
Whether to trust a confident looking crop on sparse bench art or to spend the extra calls on an explicit selection, given that a reference card in a delivered frame is a client-visible failure.

Selection wording on the pennant: naming the pennant takes the felt, naming the thread's own visual properties takes the mark, and the knockout route on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
How much of a chain-stitched trace to keep, given that the stitch texture produces far more parts than the mark has.
Whether the season's tone is carried by the layout or baked into the raster upstream, and what that choice costs if the layout cannot hold it.

client_brief:
An appointment-season story deck with a consistent jewellery image library

Maison Valcere needs its house-story and campaign documents ready for the autumn appointment season. The bench photography spans two sittings, and it does not yet sit together as a collection.

We need a designer-retoucher who will reconcile the photographs against the twenty-two references before building the presentation. Missing coverage should be clear; a repeated picture must not quietly stand in for another reference.

Presentation and source files
House-story deck and campaign document, plus their sources: Choose and adapt an Adobe Express template for these supporting pieces, using the supplied brand, approved copy and imagery. Select the strongest fit, replace the template content and correct its background as needed. Supply the editable design link and the requested export, in addition to the commissioned custom production work.

House masters
The bench frames brought to one house target, one white point, one black point, one crop logic, one height in frame, across two sittings, plus one licensed camera-scale interior ground graded into the same world. Per-frame parameter log with one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours, and a written reconciliation of frames against the twenty two references in the book.

Boutique tiles
Square boutique tiles per reference on a clean white ground, hero and detail, the piece optically centred with clear air at every edge and a cut edge that holds under close inspection on high-polish pieces as well as matte ones, plus genuinely transparent variants for the stockists' dark band. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with the returned tradeoff record for each. One set with one cut logic, not one picture at several sizes.

The high-polish pieces deserve the same care as the matte ones. Check the transparent versions on the stockists' dark band, with the same crop logic and apparent scale carried across the range.

source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com post 'Luxury E-commerce Brand Visuals' quoted in the ledger, for an independent high-jewellery identity that 'must feel unmistakably premium', built on a deep-black canvas with crisp white typography, 'purely typographic, no symbols, icons or complex marks', a strict monochrome palette, and usage rules so 'every asset, from product packaging to video title cards, stays consistent'. Co-anchor one: the Freelancer.com sterling-silver post asking for 'clean, consistent imagery for our online catalogue and marketplaces' so 'the metalwork stays the hero', every file on a pure white ground with no visible shadows or colour cast, delivered as high-resolution images plus a per-product catalogue. The house is the coined fictional Maison Valcere; no real company, person, product or trademark is named, and the palette names are invented. So this is that client's actual job: the identity is recovered rather than invented, the catalogue is a real per-reference run, and the editable source files they asked for exist.

price_band_and_audience: Appointment-led fine jewellery at 900 to 6,500 dollars a piece, buyers 35 to 60, purchase occasion a marriage or a milestone. The band is load-bearing. At this price the grammar is one object per canvas, deep held space, a near-black ground, high-contrast neoclassical type at a restrained scale, and the price shown discreetly or not at all. The same twenty two references at a 90 dollar mall band would correctly be laid out dense, four pieces to a tile, on white with a saturated accent, price set large beside a strike-through, and shipping that treatment here reads as a clearance counter and destroys the appointment premise the whole house rests on. Push the other way into pure vitrine minimalism with no copy and no table and the deck stops doing the job a stockist needs it to do, which is to answer metal, stone and carat without asking. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 2,000 to 4,500 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Independent fine-jewellery house, made to order and sold by appointment, with a small stockist channel.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2014, in a room above a bookshop in Montreal, Quebec. Four people, one bench.
brand_identity.about: Maison Valcere is a four-person high-jewellery house working to order for marriages and milestones. Twenty two references sit in the current book, most cut and set in-house and shown by appointment above the shop. The house sells quiet, considered pieces to clients who return once a decade, not once a season.
brand_identity.audience: Clients aged 35 to 60 buying for a marriage or a milestone, plus a short list of premium stockists. Considered, appointment-led buyers who research before they visit and expect the metal, stone and carat answered without asking.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Pieces run 900 to 6,500 dollars, positioned as appointment fine jewellery well above a mall counter and just below the named international maisons. Price is shown discreetly or not at all; the room and the book carry the value.
brand_identity.typography: Purely typographic, no symbols or icons. A high-contrast neoclassical serif with hairline serifs and a grave accent carries the wordmark and display; a restrained humanist or grotesque sans sets the specifications and body at a quiet scale. Generous letterspacing on caps, plenty of held space.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, precise, never salesy. States materials and provenance and stops. Example line: "Eighteen karat white gold, set with a single old-cut stone, made to your hand."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original wordmark artwork left with the designer who set it a decade ago. The only surviving version is a photograph of an old printed swing tag, so the mark has to be recovered from that before it can be used again. No usable logo files, colour references or type spec survive; these guidelines are being reconstructed this season.
brand_identity.values: One object per canvas, honest materials, and a mark that reads as ours at every size. Restraint is the house, not decoration.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the card run actually carries the fields it reports carrying. The printer's six lines were set as one continuous flow, and the mapping readout hands back a story string that omits the regulated assay run while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset past it is short by the length of the omission. The validator returns valid with no warnings on those offsets, the placeholder step reports completed successfully, and the merge produces a full set of cards. Only the merged pages show that the metal and reference lines never became placeholders and came through as the printer's original static wording on every card, identical for all twenty two references.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because nothing announces that the readout is lossy and every response in the chain affirms the wrong offsets, so there is no signal to order around. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the printer's card should be filled in for every reference, and the acceptance line about no card reaching the printer missing a line is the house's standing trade requirement, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to compute offsets from a different source entirely, the true story text reconstructed from the document's own stories, which is a route the agent has no reason to take while the cheap readout is being validated as correct.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the document's stories, recompute every offset against it, rebuild the mapping, prepare the template again, re-export and confirm every expected field is present as a placeholder before any card is merged, then re-merge the book and read the long stone record at trim rather than at thumbnail scale.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twenty two spec cards that arrive at the printer with the same metal and reference on every one of them, sent into a run whose only reason to exist is that each card is different.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered wordmark still reads as the house's wordmark once it sits at the size it actually reproduces on the real ground. The trace is taken from a handheld photograph of a small printed tag, so the hairline serifs and the grave accent sit at the resolution floor of that capture. At canvas size the traced paths look correct and complete. What the strokes do at boutique-tile size on the house black, and what the counters do when the mark is reversed out of that black rather than sitting on white, is a property of this particular capture and this particular trace and is visible only once the mark is placed at reproduction size on the actual ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) There is no ordering that avoids it and no parameter that prevents it, because the tracing tool takes no options at all and every lever is upstream in the raster preparation. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for the wordmark back as artwork for the die cutter and working at tile size and reversed on black, which is the house's requirement, not a warning that it will not. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different decision about which artwork carries which surface, and where necessary a differently prepared plate feeding the trace.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive the trace from a differently prepared plate, a higher-contrast ink-level selection or a filled colour-accurate plate rather than a binary mask, judge the result at reproduction size on the black rather than at canvas size, and where the hairlines still will not hold, split the system: the traced artwork for the die cutter at its own scale, a type-set lockup for the small sizes, with the split declared in the note.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A house whose wordmark is legible only on the one canvas somebody happened to look at, appearing on every boutique tile and every reversed panel as a smudged block with its accent gone, on an identity whose entire claim is that it is purely typographic.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the two constructs the Valcere look is built on. The house look is a deep black ground with one object held in a soft luminous falloff, and a hairline display line on the posters. Authored the natural way, the falloff is a blur and the hairline line is stroke-only type, and the importer discards a blur filter outright and resolves stroke-only type to a fully transparent colour, both with no warning and a successful response. The returned per-root markup is the only channel that reports either, and each document's rendition returns its first root only, so the five other deck roots and the two other poster directions can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a look and the acceptance lines are about how the work reads, not about what an importer keeps. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to build the falloff differently, as a radial gradient shape or as part of the raster by knocking the piece onto a house ground so the falloff is pixels, and to set the display line as solid type with tracking, then re-compose around whichever it is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the affected masters through a different route, re-author both documents around what actually survives, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every root from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A deck and a poster set delivered as editable files in which the pieces sit on flat black with hard edges and the poster display line is invisible on the two directions nobody looked at, with every export having reported success.

client_brief:
Showroom line cards for twelve looks, with a controlled editorial treatment

Nordheim Atelier is preparing for buyer appointments. Twelve looks were photographed over two days, including two outside as the light changed. We need one grey editorial treatment, but wool, shearling and gabardine must still read as different materials.

The existing printed line card is the starting point. Please keep the line in order and give each look its own photograph, rather than replacing the image once in a template and repeating it.

One press file carrying one card per look in line order, page count equal to row count, built off the atelier's own printed card, with each look's own prepared photograph bound per row rather than one static image repeated, every field present at trim including the long fabric composition, plus per-look card files named to the line and sign-off proofs rendered at genuine resolution, with the identity of every card checked against the line in writing.

The twelve looks brought to one grey editorial target, one black point, one grey scale, one figure height, across two shooting days and two lighting situations, with the printed texture applied as masked region-confined work so wool, shearling and gabardine still read as different materials at reproduction size, plus one licensed camera-scale ground carried through the same treatment. Per-frame parameter log including mask polarity and one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours.

The long fabric composition is not optional copy. Check it in the final card at trim, along with every other field. Where the printed texture treatment is confined to a region, record the mask orientation and show that it has not flattened the garment surface.

We supply nordheim_fw26_looks/ (14 frames, 5504 x 8256); nordheim_letterpress_card.jpg; nordheim_linecard_2025_PRINT.pdf; nordheim_fw26.csv; nordheim_press_notes.txt; nordheim_reference_spread.png.

The final package should contain a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record, with every source file accounted for, including references and rejected or superseded material. Use the approved information without inventing missing facts. Only the stated stock or concept exceptions permit substitution; document every omission, replacement, reconciliation and material quality compromise.

price_band_and_audience: Couture-adjacent designer ready-to-wear at 600 to 2,400 dollars a garment, sold to press and to independent-store buyers aged 30 to 55. The band is load-bearing. At this price the grammar is restrained editorial grading, a hard black point, deep held space, a disciplined two-tone treatment and typography that carries the page, with price information confined to the linesheet where buyers expect it. The same twelve looks at a 60 dollar high-street band would correctly be graded warm and saturated, cropped tight to fill every tile, priced large on every canvas and stacked four to a row, and shipping that treatment here destroys the collection's perceived value in a single spread and costs the atelier the buyer list. Push the other way into pure gallery abstraction where the garments are unreadable and press cannot use the pictures and buyers cannot see the cloth. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 4,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.about: Nordheim Atelier is a designer-led studio in Copenhagen making a tight seasonal collection in wool, shearling and gabardine. FW26 is twelve looks, sold to press and to roughly thirty independent stores. The house builds one editorial look each season and carries it across everything a buyer and an editor see.
brand_identity.audience: Fashion press and independent-store buyers aged 30 to 55. Readers who value cloth and construction over gloss, and who judge a collection on whether the range holds together.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Garments run 600 to 2,400 dollars, positioned as couture-adjacent designer ready-to-wear. Prices live only on the linesheet where buyers expect them; the collateral never discounts or shouts, since a sale treatment would strip the perceived value in a single spread.
brand_identity.typography: One documentary-editorial system: a strong high-contrast display serif or a condensed grotesque for covers and headlines, paired with a plain workhorse sans for captions, the season note and the linesheet. Hard contrast, tight measure, nothing decorative.
brand_identity.voice: Spare and factual, closer to an investigative magazine than a catalogue. Names the fabric and the maker and leaves the rest. Example line: "Undyed Gotland wool, cut on the straight, made in Copenhagen."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark exists in only one place: a single letterpress card from the first season, photographed. The original artwork is gone. The mark is a compound lockup (wordmark, a hairline rule, and ATELIER in small caps) and has to be recovered whole from that photograph. No live logo files or type spec survive.
brand_identity.values: One collection, not twelve pictures. The cloth is the argument, grayscale and printed texture serve it, and the range must read as one hand.
