emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the two exterior frames can be brought to the collection's grey scale at all. They were shot against a white sky at the end of the day, and the highlights are already at the ceiling, so a highlight correction accepts its parameters, reports success and returns a frame in which nothing has moved. There is no error, no warning and no readout that says the data was not there to move, and the returned frame looks entirely plausible on its own because it looks exactly like the frame that went in. The mismatch only exists relative to the other ten looks, so it becomes visible when the twelve are laid out as a range and not before.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the correction is applied before anyone can know whether it took, and the tool reports success either way. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the light was lost and two looks were taken outside, which describes a shooting circumstance, not a clipped file, and the acceptance line about the twelve reading as one collection is the atelier's standing requirement. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different decision about the whole set: move the collection's target to a scale those two frames can actually reach, treat them as a declared separate register, or name them as looks that cannot be brought in.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-decide the collection target against what the exterior frames can actually reach, re-grade the ten studio looks toward that revised target rather than the original one, re-assemble the range grid, and where the two still will not join, say so in writing and propose which look carries the cover instead.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A lookbook whose range grid has two blown pages sitting in the middle of it, going to press and to a buyer list on a collection whose whole argument is restraint and control.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each showroom card actually carries the look it names. When the merge is taken as per-record raster files, the outputs come back in an order the response labels contradict, so the file labelled as the first record is not the first record, while every response reports success and every card looks correct on its own because each is a well-formed card. Nothing in the tool responses exposes it, the labels are confidently wrong, and the CSV's own image column follows the shoot's numbering rather than the look numbering on part of the line, so a wrong pairing looks exactly as plausible as a right one. It surfaces only by reading each rendered card against the line, look number, garment and price together.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, and doing it right first time is actively steered against: the client asked for one card per look as separate files, and the route whose own description promises one output file per row is the raster route, which is the one whose order lies. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a card per look with that look's photograph on it, and the acceptance line about a card bound to the wrong look failing is the atelier's requirement, not a warning about output ordering. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different delivery route entirely, with identity guaranteed by construction rather than inferred from a returned list.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the per-record raster route, re-deliver through a route whose order is guaranteed, reconcile the image column against the look numbers before re-binding, re-merge, and re-read every card against the line rather than against the response, then re-render the proofs.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twelve showroom cards handed to buyers with the wrong garment, the wrong fabric and the wrong wholesale price on them, on the single document the season's orders are written from.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the two constructs the editorial look is built on. The essay pages are set to a magazine measure, and the two-tone panels that carry the campaign directions are built as an overlay reading through the photograph beneath. Authored the natural way, the measure is a multi-column text flow and the overlay is a blend mode, and the importer drops the column structure so the text reflows as one column running past the page edge, and drops the blend so the panel renders as a plain opaque shape covering the photograph entirely. Both return success with no warning of any kind, the returned per-root markup is the only channel that reports either, and each document's rendition returns its first root only, so the essay pages and the second poster direction can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for essay pages and a poster pair, and the acceptance lines are about how the pages read. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to build both differently, the measure as positioned text frames of a chosen width and the two-tone as an upstream raster treatment produced in the image pipeline, then to re-compose the pages around what actually survives.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-author the essay pages as explicitly measured text frames, produce the two-tone treatment in the imaging pipeline so it is part of the pixels rather than a page effect, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every root from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A lookbook whose essay pages run off the trim edge and a poster direction that is a flat block of colour where the photograph should be, both delivered as editable files with every export reporting success and nobody having looked past page one.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which are a genuine record-per-page run, and which need an authored fixed-canvas document, given that only one surface composes free-form layout and only one does volume personalisation.
What the collection's grey target actually is, decided against what every frame can reach rather than against the strongest frame alone.
How far to carry the two exterior frames before they stop being worth carrying, versus declaring them a separate register or naming them.
Knockout route per look: the one-call route for the dark garments versus a material-named ground selection inverted and filled for the undyed wool whose shoulder shares luminance with the seamless.
Mask polarity and texture radius: what carries the dot and what stays clean, judged at the size the piece actually reproduces rather than at preview scale.
Selection wording on the letterpress card: naming the substrate takes the card, naming the whole lockup silently returns part of it, and background removal is the wrong instrument on lettering.
What the converted line card actually exposes as mappable structure, and what a mapping can honestly promise once that is known.
How look identity is guaranteed across the card run when the image column follows one numbering and the line follows another, and which delivery route makes that guarantee by construction.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of fashion. IDENTITY: these are this atelier's twelve actual FW26 garments in their actual fabrics, photographed on the actual fit, and the wordmark must be RECOVERED off a letterpress card rather than reinvented, because a regenerated garment is not the garment a buyer will receive and a regenerated wordmark is a different label. SPEC: the showroom needs one card per look off the atelier's own printed artwork with that look's own photograph, that look's own fabric wording and that look's own wholesale and retail prices, in line order, and a generated image cannot satisfy or be checked against any of that. EDITABILITY: the lookbook, linesheet, posters and social are defined by being editable, because the line moves during the selling season and a small atelier cannot re-commission. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this highlight correction move anything, is this card actually the look it names, did the essay measure survive the import.

client_brief:
Listing photography and six agent cards for 14 Marlowe Crescent

Harbor Crest Realty needs the house to look consistent across the listing and the open-house cards. The shooter has returned the rooms as captured; wall colour and window handling now vary from room to room.

We also need to stop reordering the card one agent at a time. Please recover the printer's working structure from the supplied artwork and produce the six-agent run.

Card production
Six cards, one agent per page, in roster order, at the card's true trim, built from the printer's own artwork rather than a redrawn approximation: each carrying that agent's own photograph bound per record, the licence line reproduced exactly as supplied, and every expected field confirmed present by inspecting the template's story rather than by a success message. Delivered as one press document plus per record proofs at real print-resolution.

Property photography
The full room by room set brought to one house target: one white point, one black point, one neutral for the walls, verticals straight, rooms at a comparable size in frame, with the windows carrying the garden wherever the file allows it. One licensed camera-scale context frame graded into the same world. Delivered with a per-frame parameter log, the room reconciliation against the facts sheet, and a named list of any frame that could not be brought to the set.

The licence line must remain exactly as supplied, and each agent needs their own portrait. For the rooms, recover the garden through the windows only where the file supports it. A frame that cannot join the set should be named rather than disguised.

Attachments: marlowe_captures/ (18 frames, 6000 x 4000); harbor_crest_open_house_card.pdf; agent_headshots/ (6 portraits, 3600 x 4800); agent_roster.csv; marlowe_facts.txt; harbor_crest_basis.png.

Please work within $1,400-$3,800 fixed and the 7 to 15 business days target. Allow for one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

Alongside the finished work, we need a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note, Stock license and asset IDs and the normalised data and field-mapping record. Keep a clear record of the supplied files used, retained for reference, superseded and rejected. Approved source information remains authoritative. Record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and quality limits, and do not use an undeclared replacement or invented fact to conceal a source problem.

source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork 'Open House Finance Flyer' package post quoted in the ledger, which asks for an editable print and digital flyer set, sophisticated and approachable rather than luxury, with easily editable property photos, purchase price, payment scenarios and contact information. All identifying detail is laundered to fiction: the lender in the real post becomes a brokerage, the market becomes the invented Calderon County with the invented town of Rosewood, and the listing becomes the fictional 14 Marlowe Crescent. Co-anchor: the Upwork high volume real estate photo editing open call, whose named edit list is window pulls, colour correction, vertical alignment, lawn enhancement and general cleanup, whose deliverable is stated as portal ready images with consistent style across each property, and whose stated volume is twenty to forty photos per listing at a twenty four to forty eight hour turnaround. That post named no client, so the brokerage is laundered to the fictional Harbor Crest Realty. Third anchor: the Freelancer.com 'Vibrant Social and Web Graphics' post asking for matching website graphics, hero images, section headers and call to action spots plus banner ads, everything feeling part of one cohesive family while being perfectly sized for its destination, with a mini style reference for colours and typography so future assets stay consistent. Those three posts are the same commission split across three postings: one listing's photography, one listing's collateral, and the reusable basis. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes the fuller version honest, because HTML authoring now produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes and a bare press PDF can be reverse engineered into a live merge template.

price_band_and_audience: A 625,000 dollar suburban family home at a 2.5 percent listing side, buyers 30 to 45 making a first move up, agents 35 to 55. The band is load bearing. At this price the grammar is warm and legible: a readable feature table, honest daylight, real room sizes in frame, type that a phone renders cleanly, and an agent's face on the card because the relationship is the product. Push it toward prestige restraint, near black grounds, sparse type and a rates figure hidden in a discreet line and the same house reads as under sold and the buyer assumes something is wrong with it. Push the other way into starburst callouts, three accent colours and every fact shouted and it reads as a distress sale. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even with every technical gate green. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed, often with a per listing repeat rate attached.

brand_identity.sector: Residential real estate brokerage listing family homes across a suburban county.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2011, in Rosewood, Calderon County. A nine-agent brokerage listing around forty homes a season.
brand_identity.about: Harbor Crest Realty is a nine-person residential brokerage in Rosewood, listing suburban family homes for owners and guiding first move-up buyers through them. The firm runs a steady volume of listings a year and wants one repeatable kit that makes every listing look like it came from the same firm.
brand_identity.audience: Move-up buyers aged 30 to 45 making their first step up from a starter home, scrolling listings on a phone. Also the sellers who list with the firm and the six agents who work open houses.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Homes centre on the mid-market, with 14 Marlowe Crescent at 625,000 dollars and a 2.5 percent listing side. Positioned as sophisticated but approachable, not luxury and not discount: warm, legible, honest, with real facts and real room sizes shown plainly.
brand_identity.typography: One warm, legible system that renders cleanly on a phone and on an office printer: a friendly geometric or humanist sans for headings and figures, paired with a readable text face for the facts table and body. Comfortable sizes, clear hierarchy, nothing prestige-cold or shouty.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, welcoming, benefit-led without hype. Speaks like a neighbour who knows the street. Example line: "Four bedrooms, a garden that backs onto the ravine, and an open house this Sunday."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The firm is not rebranding. A current sign and business card are already in the field and are supplied as the basis, so the new kit must match what is out there rather than replace it. The open house card artwork is held by the printer as a press PDF; there is no central brand file beyond the sign and card reference.
brand_identity.values: Consistency across every listing, honesty in the photography, and collateral the brokerage can rebuild itself for the next home. The agent relationship is the product.

assets_supplied.name: marlowe_captures/ (18 frames, 6000 x 4000)
assets_supplied.kind: Room by room listing capture of the whole house plus front and rear exteriors, one pass, handheld on a tripod at chest height, delivered straight off the card with no processing.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything as captured. Some rooms read yellow, one bedroom is cool, and the outside was shot later than the inside."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: On five interior frames the room was exposed for the room, so every window is clipped flat to paper white with nothing behind it, and a highlight move on those frames returns success while the readout is that nothing at all changes. Separately two frames are the same living room from one tripod position a minute apart, and the study named in the facts sheet has no capture at all, which no filename or count reveals.

assets_supplied.kind: The brokerage's existing open house card exactly as its printer holds it: a real press PDF, one card per page, agent photograph at the top, then name, licence line, direct number and the office address set as printed type.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our printer's file. We just want the six agents dropped into it."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the window frames still have anything behind the glass. The client's whole case for the house is the garden through the windows, and on some of these interiors the room was exposed for the room, so the window is clipped flat with no data under it. A highlight recovery pass on those frames returns success and the readout is that nothing moves at all: the result comes back, it is a valid image, and it is indistinguishable from the input. Which frames those are is a property of how each room was metered and is not visible by looking at the thumbnail, because a merely bright window and a dead one look identical until something is asked of them.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the information does not exist in the file and no response says so. Nothing states it either: the brief asks that the windows show the garden, which is the client's goal, not a disclosure that five specific frames cannot deliver it. And the response is not a re run of the same chain, it is a different route decided per frame, either recomposing the crop so the dead window falls outside it, or selecting the window region by its own visual properties and treating it as a deliberate flat panel, or dropping the frame and re choosing which rooms carry the gallery at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re decide which rooms carry the one pager gallery and which carries the flyer hero, re cut those crops from different masters, and re balance the corrected set so the substituted rooms still agree with their neighbours, then record in the note which windows could not be brought back.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A listing page whose hero and gallery are built on windows that are blank white rectangles, on a house whose entire selling point is the view through them, delivered with every tool call reporting success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card actually is once it is a document rather than a printed page. Its frame granularity is not under anyone's control and does not follow the visual blocks, and worse, the readout of the resulting story omits one printed run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly the length of the run that vanished. The validator returns VALID on those wrong offsets with no warnings, and the placeholder step then reports completed successfully. Nothing in any response distinguishes a mapping that landed from one that silently dropped half its fields.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not help, because the omission is a property of this document and is only discoverable by comparing the readout against the story text reconstructed from the round tripped IDML, which nothing instructs and no response hints at. Nothing states it: the brief says only that the printer holds the artwork and the agents need dropping in. And it is not a propagation re run, because the fix is to recompute every offset from a different source of truth and re prepare the template, then prove the placeholders by inspection rather than by response text.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Recompute all offsets from the reconstructed story, rebuild the mapping, re prepare the template, round trip the IDML again to confirm each placeholder is present, and only then re merge and re render the six cards.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Six cards that print cleanly with the licence line or the direct number simply absent, ordered in quantity by a brokerage that read a success message and a VALID verdict as proof.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the knockout holds on the specific portraits shot against the office wall. On the agents wearing pale grey against that mottled grey ground, subject and ground sit within a hair of each other in value along the shoulder line, so the tool returns a clean, complete, entirely plausible cutout that has quietly bitten into the shoulder where the two meet. It looks correct at preview scale and it is only wrong at the size the card prints the photograph. Which portraits do this is a property of each individual frame's own contrast, not of the shoot.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is no ordering that avoids it, no parameter that controls it, and no response field that reports it, and doing it right first time would mean routing all six through the slower material selection chain on the assumption that some will fail, which is a guess rather than a decision. Nothing states it: the client says only that the portraits were taken at different times. And the fix is a different chain for the affected portraits, selecting the wall by its own material properties, inverting, and filling to the card ground, not the same chain again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re route the affected portraits through a material selection, re derive those agent plates, re bind them into the merge, and re render and re inspect those cards at card scale rather than at preview scale.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Open house cards handed out at the door on which two agents have a slice taken out of a shoulder, on the one piece of collateral whose entire job is to make the agent look like a professional.

client_brief:
Twelve seasonal villa cards and a coherent three-property image set

Looking at our Verranza photographs together, you could believe they describe three different holidays. Two trips, two photographers and a batch already edited elsewhere have left the collection inconsistent.

Please bring the usable files to a credible shared treatment. The pre-finished batch may need taking back, not pushing further. The season cards then need the correct villa, rate, stay rule and complete seasonal note.

Twelve cards, one villa and season per page, at the card's true trim, built from the printer's own artwork rather than a redrawn approximation: each carrying its own villa's finished photograph bound per record, its own rate, its own minimum stay written one consistent way, and its season note legible in full rather than stopped at a frame edge. Delivered as one press document plus per record proofs at real print-resolution, with every field confirmed present by reading the rendered pages at trim.

The full three villa set brought to one collection target: one white point, one black point, one treatment of stone and shadow, one relationship between interior and exterior brightness, with water that could exist at that hour and no fake high dynamic range look anywhere. The pre finished batch walked back rather than pushed further. Delivered with a per-frame parameter log, the duplicate and shortfall reconciliation, and a named list of any frame that could not be brought to the collection, plus any licensed frame graded into the same world or explicitly excluded.

We care about the relationship between interiors, exterior brightness, stone and water. Please do not make the water a colour it could not have been at that hour, or force an HDR look onto the rooms.

The final proofs should let us check every field at the card's actual trim. Include the duplicate and shortfall reconciliation so we understand what the photographic collection really covers.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Anchor: the Upwork real estate finishing brief quoted in the ledger, posted by a boutique vacation rental manager asking for a consistent premium visual identity across the whole portfolio with a natural, realistic look, and carrying an explicit do not want list: no fake high dynamic range, no over saturation, no unrealistically blue pools. That post named no company, place or vendor, so the collection is laundered to the fictional Verranza Coastal Retreats on the fictional cove of Anse Verranza on the southern French coast, with the invented villas Solane, Cascina and Aubine. This is a REBUILD rather than a strengthen. The killed original ran three independent short imaging passes and finished there, which is a finishing job rather than a commission and sat on one surface. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller version is, because the finishing pass is only the front half of what this client actually needs: HTML authoring now produces a native editable multi root document at mixed canvas sizes, so the presentation and the booking pages are real deliverables, and a bare press PDF from their printer can be reverse engineered into a live merge template, so the twelve in villa season cards become a genuine record per page run whose photographs are the very frames the finishing pass produced. That dependency, a badly finished frame being invisible until it lands in the card at the card's crop, is what turns three separate passes into one engagement. The same capabilities change the imaging half too: the collection's only graphic mark, a hand inked cove motif that survives as a scan and as an etch on one villa's door glass, can be recovered as real vector rather than redrawn, and the contractual welcome provision the client leaves in every house can be isolated onto the collection's own ground, so the raster surface is a full imaging engagement rather than a grade and crop pass.

price_band_and_audience: Villas at 1,800 to 4,200 dollars a night, guests 40 to 65 booking whole property stays for a milestone, comparing the collection against hotels rather than against other rentals. The band is load bearing. At this price the grammar is generous negative space, full bleed architecture allowed to be quiet, rates carried in a discreet table rather than announced, and photography that is believable before it is impressive, because the guest who pays 4,200 a night has been to the actual house and will recognise a lie in the water. Push it down into a bargain rental grid of eight thumbnails, a price badge and a book now block and the collection reads as an aggregator listing and the rate stops being defensible. Push it further up into pure sparseness with the rates hidden entirely and a travel agency cannot sell from it. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even with every technical gate green. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 4,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.typography: One quiet prestige system: an elegant high-contrast serif for display and villa names, set with air, paired with a clean humanist sans for amenity tables, the rate ladder and body. Restraint over flourish, so it reads considered without tipping into fashion-house coldness a family will not book from.
brand_identity.voice: Calm, warm, understated. Describes what the house actually is at that hour, never oversells. Example line: "Warm stone, a long terrace, and the pool in real afternoon light."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The collection has a printed in-villa season card whose artwork is held by its printer as a press PDF, and a written owner note recording what the previous editor got wrong. There is no lost wordmark here; the constraint is photographic consistency across three villas shot on two trips by two people, with the second batch already worked on by an editor no longer used. The collection's one graphic mark is a small hand inked cove motif an artist drew for the founders, which survives only as a flatbed scan of the original inking and as the mark etched on Maison Aubine's door glass; it has never been redrawn or digitised, and the foil printer and the glass etcher need it as vector artwork. The contractual welcome provision left in every house exists only as a short still life set the manager shot on a villa's limestone counter.
brand_identity.values: Believable before impressive. One collection, not three holidays. Natural light, real shadow, honest water, and no fake high dynamic range or dyed pools.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cut edge survives where a pale object meets the warm stone it is sitting on. The welcome things are shot on a villa's limestone, and on some frames the rose, the clear glass shoulder or the pale crust sit at almost the value of the stone. The knockout reports success, the returned cutout is complete and clean at thumbnail scale, and the bite only exists along the short stretch where the pale object and the stone share luminance. Which frames it happens to is a property of each frame's own light and the object's own colour, not of the object, and there is no confidence figure and no edge report anywhere in the response.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the edge quality is a fact about this frame meeting this tool and exists only after the call has run and the result is looked at on the ground it will sit on, the Linen brand ground, not on white. Nothing states it: the brief says only that the welcome things were shot on the kitchen stone. And it is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different chain for the affected frames, a material named selection of the limestone, inverted and filled to the brand ground.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re plan the knockout route per frame, re derive the affected cutouts through the selection and fill chain, and re inspect every cutout against the Linen brand ground rather than against white.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A what is included panel and a season social set in which the welcome objects have a chewed edge along the glass or the crust on the frames nobody looked at closely, on a collection whose whole pitch is that nothing is a little bit wrong.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered cove mark is still the mark at the height it actually reproduces. The trace comes back looking correct: the headland and the cove and the roofline are there, the counters are open, and at full scan scale on a white page it is a faithful recovery. The foil printer stamps it across the corner of the card at roughly a thumbnail, and the glass etcher puts it on Maison Aubine's door at hand small, and at those heights the hairline tapers fill in and the cove mouth and the window openings close into solid blobs. The tracer takes no options at all, so nothing about the trace call can be tuned; the only evidence is placing the artwork at its real reproduction size on its real ground and looking.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the answer depends on the trace, the reproduction height and the ground colour being present together, and the first two are produced by the agent while the third is a property of the card stock and the glass. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a proper file the vendors can use and says the mark has to still look drawn by hand. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different raster preparation feeding the same tracer, a differently worded ink level selection, a fill and flatten plate instead of a binary mask, or a bounds crop that changes what the tracer sees, since the tracer itself has no lever.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re prepare the raster on a different route, re trace, re inject the viewBox and strip the opaque ground path again, then re place the result at reproduction height on the card stock and on the glass colour and re judge, and state a safe minimum height in the handover once one is actually known.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The founders' mark foil stamped on the card and etched on the door glass as a row of solid blobs, on the one mark the collection has and on pieces a guest paying 4,200 a night holds and walks through.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the licensed frame belongs to this collection. The search returns only a small CDN thumbnail, so the frame's true white balance, its own baked contrast, how its horizon sits and how its water reads all exist only after the licence is taken and the full resolution file is pulled down. Even then the question is not whether the frame is good, it is whether it sits with these three specific villas at their finished target, which cannot be answered until the two are finally adjacent on the opening root. Every step up to that point returns success: the search succeeded, the licence succeeded, the download succeeded, and the thumbnail looked right.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not avoid it, because the only order that would is licensing several candidates and comparing them at full resolution, which spends licences on a guess. Nothing states it: the brief never mentions a bought frame at all, it simply asks for a collection presentation, and the do not want list is the client's art direction rather than a warning about stock. And the response is not a re run, it is a decision between grading the licensed frame to the collection target, taking a second licence on a different candidate, and restructuring the opening root around a villa frame instead, each of which changes what the presentation opens on and therefore what the social end card carries.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re grade or re license, and if neither brings the frame inside the collection, re plan the opening root and the social end card around villa photography and re cut those crops.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A presentation whose first screen is visibly a bought photograph next to three carefully finished houses, shown to a travel agency by a collection whose whole pitch is consistency.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of a beautiful villa. IDENTITY: these are three specific houses that guests will physically arrive at, and a regenerated pool, terrace or view is a misrepresentation the manager can be held to, which is precisely why the do not want list exists and why they have lost bookings before. SPEC: twelve cards at the printer's trim, one villa and season per page, each field present in full, plus crops at fixed destinations with nothing enlarged, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: rates change twice a year and the client explicitly cannot re commission, so a flat render is worth nothing to them. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: is this water believable, does this bought frame belong here, does this note fit the frame, did the type survive the import on the roots nobody can preview, did this cutout bite the pale glass against the stone, does this trace still read as the founders' mark at foil stamp height. And the cove mark is a specific hand inked drawing that has to be RECOVERED rather than reinvented, because a regenerated mark is a different drawing in a different hand that the foil printer and the glass etcher cannot cut from a picture, while the welcome objects are the villa's own things isolated onto the collection's own ground, not stock still lifes.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork collateral post quoted verbatim in the ledger's grounding_note, which specifies "DELIVERABLE 2 - One-Page Service Overview: single/double-sided 8.5\"x11\" sell sheet" carrying a "header with branding and compelling title", a "company advantage" section, "core-services bullets" and "a prominent CTA", laid out on "clean grids", with the whole set required to "feel clean, modern, trustworthy and polished, referencing the website's palette/typography". The original poster was a legal and MVA case management firm; it is laundered here to the coined, IP clean B2B SaaS company Nimbadesk (nimbus plus desk), which names no real help desk product. Co-anchor: the Upwork post from a founder whose logo was "created on AI" and who needed it turned into a "vector file so it can be used in multiple platforms" and kept "high-quality across different formats", laundered from that brief's startup to the same fictional company. emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives at the size it actually reproduces at, on the ground it actually sits on. The trace is made from a gradient raster, so it comes back as dozens of near identical fills rather than a flat mark, and at canvas size it looks correct and complete. Placed at footer size on the sheet's house ground and exported, the fine glyph counters close up and the gradient bands into visible steps. Nothing in any tool response reports this: the trace has no options, no quality readout and no size advice, and the export reports success throughout. The only way to know is to look at the mark at its real reproduction size on the real ground after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because reproduction size only exists once the mark is placed and the placement only exists after the export, and the tracing tool exposes no parameter that would let an agent get it right in advance. Nothing in the brief states it, since the client says only that the picture is the only version that exists. The response is a different raster route rather than a re run: flatten the badge to a single value plate and trace that, or split the glyph from its container and rebuild the lockup, which is a different chain of calls with a different output.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the imaging surface, prepare a flat plate instead of the gradient, retrace, redo the viewBox and ground path hygiene, produce a small size variant with opened counters and a reverse variant, then re author and re export every piece that carries the mark.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A company whose only surviving mark is shipped as a muddy blot in every footer and on fourteen badges, on collateral whose whole argument is that this is software you would put your name on.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the construction that makes the recommended tier read as recommended. Authored the natural way, the middle tier card is lifted off the table with a layered shadow and a soft translucent panel behind it. The importer truncates a layered shadow to its first layer and drops the translucent treatment entirely, keeping only the flat fill underneath, and reports success with no warning. The tier table sits on deck root five, and the document's rendition returns the first artboard only, so the returned per root markup is the sole channel in which the loss is visible at all.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The drop happens at import, which is the last step, so no ordering precedes it, and getting it right first time would require knowing which of several equally reasonable constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. Nothing in the brief or the deliverable list states it, since the client asks only for a table people can read. The response is a different construction, carrying emphasis in structure, weight, rule and scale rather than in depth effects, which changes the design rather than repeating it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re cast the emphasis into constructions the importer preserves, re author the table and the tier cards, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every root from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A pitch deck in which the tier the company most wants sold sits visually level with the other two, delivered as an editable document that reported success at every step, in front of an investor audience and a buyer who compares rows.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the badge PDF actually becomes once converted. The printed badge shows a square photo well above three tidy type lines. The converted document does not have to match that: the picture frame's true bounds can be portrait and inset, and the three lines can sit in one continuous story rather than three mappable frames, in which case fields must be placed by position inside a single story instead of by frame. On top of that, the readout of that story can omit a run while keeping its line break, so every offset past the omission is short, and the mapping still reports as valid and the template preparation still reports success.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Frame granularity is a property of the conversion, not a choice, and nothing about the printed page predicts it, so no ordering and no care can establish it without converting and inspecting. The brief states only that the printer wants one page per person. The response is not a re run: it is a different mapping strategy computed against the true story text and a re cut of all fourteen photo plates to the frame that actually exists, which is upstream imaging work rather than a repeated merge.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping from the true story text, re prepare and re verify the placeholders, return to the imaging surface to re cut every badge plate to the real frame ratio so faces still sit the same way, then re merge and re render.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen badges going to a printer with two fields blank or shifted and every face cropped differently by a frame nobody looked at, discovered at a conference booth where nothing can be reprinted.

Alderwood Scholars Fund needs one coordinated banner run for its five centres. The office must be able to trust each centre's name, address, hours and coordinator, not proofread five designs assembled independently from memory.

Our photographs were taken throughout the year by volunteers and borrowed cameras. Please bring them together without making the sourced frame for the thinly covered centre look like a different campaign.

Five banners, one page per centre, produced as a genuine record per page run from the printer's own artwork at the dimensions the printer supplied, each carrying that centre's own name, address, hours and coordinator with nothing truncated at trim and its own prepared photograph bound through the image column, at true press resolution, with a printer note stating exactly what the converted artwork does and does not carry.

A year of volunteer and borrowed camera photography from five centres brought to one house look: one white point, one black point, one warmth, one crop logic, with the sourced frame for the thin centre graded into the same world rather than sitting above it. Delivered with a per-frame parameter log, the centre reconciliation, and every reported resize.

Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

The crest comes from an enamel-sign photograph. Preserve the lamp and inner rule, and test the mark both at road-viewing banner scale and at a small report footer. Any unresolved fabrication geometry should be clearly marked for supplier review.

Both are laundered here to the coined, secular, IP clean Alderwood Scholars Fund in Providence, Rhode Island, and the regional festival season is replaced by the Western year end giving season, since every branch locality in the source is a generic address string rather than a real institution. Co-anchors: the Upwork twentieth anniversary commemorative poster brief, which asked for landmarks and community traditions woven into one cohesive composition in a "festival posters, folk-art illustration, screenprint aesthetics" register (the real client is a named Louisiana school, fully laundered), and the marketplace production brief asking for an approved mark turned into production ready files for a scholarship funding drop. The ledger's verdict is STRENGTHEN, and the concept survives whole. It is repositioned only where the connector demands it: from scratch folk illustration and regional script typesetting are not connector work, so the poster directions are built from a recovered crest, graded photography and authored vector rather than illustrated, and the per branch run becomes a genuine record per page merge off the printer's own artwork, which CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) verifies end to end.
price_band_and_audience: An average gift of 45 dollars alongside major asks of 5,000 to 50,000, from donors aged 45 to 70 who are mission motivated and who inspect the overhead ratio before the narrative. The band is load-bearing. Trust at this level is bought with restrained grounds, honest photography, evidence led charts and a spend table that reconciles in public, and every visible dollar of production has to look like it came out of an in house afternoon rather than an agency retainer. Push into glossy fundraising grammar, heavy gradients, urgency banners, countdown devices, stock smiles and a saturated hero, and this specific donor reads wasted overhead and gives less, which is the one failure mode that costs the client real money. Push the other way into austere charity minimalism, grey text on grey, no faces, no numbers, and a fifty thousand dollar ask has nothing to stand on. The twentieth year also has to feel like a milestone without becoming a celebration of the organisation rather than the students. A real posted commission of this shape runs 1,500 to 3,500 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: An education charity running five after school learning centres and a small scholarship fund across greater Providence.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2006, greater Providence, Rhode Island, four staff, a volunteer board and five centres.
brand_identity.about: Alderwood Scholars Fund runs five after school learning centres and a scholarship fund for students across greater Providence. This winter marks our twentieth year. The year end appeal carries roughly half our giving, and it works because donors trust that the money reaches the students rather than the overhead. We show our numbers plainly, name where every dollar went, and let the work speak.
brand_identity.audience: Mission motivated donors aged forty five to seventy who give because they believe in the work. Several read the overhead ratio before the narrative and reward organisations that look like they spend on students, not on production.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Average gift 45 dollars, major asks 5,000 to 50,000. Community scale and grassroots: careful and credible rather than glossy, every visible dollar of production reading as an in house afternoon rather than an agency retainer.
brand_identity.typography: A humanist serif for headlines and the twentieth year milestone, with a plain humanist sans for body, captions and tables. Numbers set in a clear tabular figure so charts and the spend breakdown read honestly. The feel is settled and civic, not corporate.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, specific, quietly proud. It credits students and staff, states periods on every figure, and never begs. Example line the brand would write: "Last year, ninety students finished the programme. Here is where your gift went, line by line."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The crest was drawn by a trustee in 2006 and the artwork files are long gone. The only surviving version is the enamel crest on the front wall of the Eastgate centre, which we have as a single handheld photograph. There is no vector, no guideline sheet and no recorded palette or type.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the licensed frame can actually live beside this photography. Everything visible while choosing is a small catalogue thumbnail, and the frame's true colour, contrast, grain and depth of field only exist after the full resolution download. Laid beside volunteer phone frames that have been pulled to one modest house target, a professionally lit frame can sit at a different level of finish entirely and read as bought, which is the precise thing this donor punishes. Whether the two can be brought to a common target, and what that target then costs the rest of the set, is only visible with the frames adjacent at full resolution.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering changes when this fires, not whether: even licensing first still requires downloading and placing the frame beside a graded set to know. Nothing states it, because the brief says only that one centre has nothing usable and asks for something honest that fits. The response is not a re run either, since the usual resolution is to move the house target itself, which re grades the whole selection, or to license a different frame chosen on different grounds.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re judge the house target with both families adjacent, re grade the volunteer set toward the new target, or abandon the licensed frame and license a different one on the light it carries rather than the subject it shows, then re cut every banner and report frame already cropped from the old grade.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An impact report and a banner run in which one centre is represented by an obviously purchased photograph sitting a level of polish above the real work, in front of donors who read production spend as overhead.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's banner artwork actually becomes once converted. The printed banner shows a centre name, a street line, an hours line and a coordinator line as four separate lines, but the conversion does not have to expose four mappable frames: a continuous block can arrive as one story, in which case fields must be placed by position inside that story rather than by frame. Worse, the readout of that story can omit an entire run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length, and the mapping still reports as valid and the template preparation still reports success.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Frame granularity is a property of the conversion rather than a choice, and nothing about the printed sheet predicts it, so no ordering and no care establishes it without converting and inspecting. Nothing in the brief states it, since the client says only that the printer wants the same file back with each centre's details. The resolution is a different mapping computed against the true story text recovered from the round tripped document, not a repeat of the same call.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild every offset from the true story text, re prepare the template, re verify that each placeholder is genuinely present rather than trusting the success message, and only then merge, since a template short two fields merges five silently incomplete banners.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Five large format banners going to the printer with the hours line or the coordinator line missing or displaced on every one of them, paid for at large format prices and hung outside five centres for the whole appeal.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the honour roll. Three hundred and forty names set the obvious way, as a multi column flow so they fit the page, come back as a single reflowed column: the multi column construction is discarded outright, the text runs down past the bottom of the fixed canvas, and the response reports success with no warning of any kind. The roll sits on the later pages of the report, and the document's rendition returns the first page only, so the returned per page markup is the sole channel in which any of this is visible, including whether the names that ran off the canvas are merely below the fold or genuinely absent.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The normalisation happens at import, which is the last step, so no ordering precedes it, and getting it right first time would mean knowing which of several reasonable ways to set a long list survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. Nothing in the brief states it, since the client says only that the roll is long and cannot lose a name. The response is a different construction, explicit sibling columns rather than a flowed one, plus a re judged page break, which changes the document rather than repeating it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the roll as explicit side by side columns with the break decided by hand, re balance the pages after it, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every page from the returned markup rather than from the first page.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An annual report delivered to a board with an unknown number of donors' names silently off the canvas, on the one page of the document those donors will look for themselves in first.

Twenty two laminates built off last year's printed artwork: one press file the printer can run with one person per page and page count equal to roster count, plus twenty two separate single passes named to the roster, plus proofs at true print-resolution sized to the pass trim. Every field carries that person's own value, nothing is inherited from last year's text, no record truncates at trim, and the role colour coding is one reconciled scheme.

Festival photographs
The fourteen archive frames brought to one festival target, one white point, one black point, one crop logic, with a per-frame parameter log and a line on why any frame differs from its neighbours, plus one licensed camera-scale field frame graded into the same world. Frames that cannot be brought to the set are named. The reconciliation of frames against approved billing is delivered with the set, including which billed act the archive does not cover.

Please reconcile the role colours into one scheme and check every pass at its actual trim. The archive photographs also need comparing with the approved billing: a folder of fourteen frames does not necessarily mean fourteen different billed acts are covered.

The supplied materials are lanternwood_pass_2026.pdf; lanternwood_roster_2027.csv; lanternwood_banner_mainstage.jpg; lanternwood_stage_frames/ (14 frames, camera scale); lanternwood_lineup_2027.txt; lanternwood_site_plan_pencil.png.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork event credential post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, an events team wanting personalised backstage and performer passes produced from a lineup list against a designer built page layout template, delivered both as one file the printer can run and as separate passes to send out. Co anchor: the second Upwork post in the ledger, whose literal ask was to BUILD a page layout plugin that automatically reduces font sizes when a record is too long for its frame, because merged text runs overset and get clipped on export. That second post is a software commission and is out of scope for any design connector, but the PAIN it names is real, it is the single most common failure of a variable data print run, and this engagement makes the agent meet it by hand rather than automate it away. Both real posts name a client nowhere, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional festival Lanternwood Folk Fest; every performer, crew member, stage and sponsor name is invented and no real festival, venue, act or trademark appears in any task facing field. The ledger's repositioning note killed the original because it merged into a convert_pdf_to_indd output and relied on a per row data merge image field that cannot exist in a converted PDF. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is: the convert, prepare, merge chain IS verified to bind fields end to end off a bare press PDF, provided the mapping offsets are computed from the true interchange story rather than from the tool's own readout, while the per row image field genuinely does not exist unless the source PDF carried a real placed image. So the corrected commission keeps the client's actual pass run and makes both of those realities load bearing, and it adds the rest of the kit that client obviously needed at the same on sale date.

price_band_and_audience: Mid tier independent festival. Weekend general admission a hundred and forty five dollars, VIP three hundred and twenty, roughly four thousand weekend tickets, audience eighteen to forty, discovery led and scene literate rather than corporate. The band is load bearing in both directions. Push sparse and luxurious, with acres of white, a hairline serif and one small photograph, and it reads as a three hundred and twenty dollar tasting event rather than a farm field weekend, which suppresses general admission conversion where nearly all the revenue sits. Push the other way into a dense bargain flyer, with every act at the same size, a starburst price and clip art, and the VIP tier stops being credible and the discovery stages read as filler. The correct register is energetic and coherent: bold type at a real hierarchy, atmospheric photography carrying the field and the night, a lineup that plainly distinguishes headline from discovery, and colour coding a gate steward reads at two metres in daylight. A posted commission of this shape and scope runs 1,800 to 3,500 dollars fixed.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What last year's pass actually becomes once it is a working document, and whether a mapping the tools blessed actually landed. The printed page shows five clearly separated blocks; the converted document can expose them as a single continuous text flow with no addressable per field frames, and the photo box that reads as a picture frame on paper can convert as drawn artwork with no graphic frame at all, which removes the per performer headshot binding the roster's filename column was written for. On top of that, the readout used to compute the mapping can silently omit a low contrast run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run. The validator answers VALID with no warnings and the prepare step answers completed successfully, and only a placeholder inventory taken back out of the document reveals that some fields never landed.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it because the granularity of a converted PDF is a property of the source artwork and is not exposed until the conversion has been run and the document read back. Nothing in the brief, the file listing or the printed page states any of it: the client believes the pass is five fields and a photo box, which is what it looks like. The response is not a re run of the same chain, it is a different mapping strategy entirely, offsets computed inside one story against a reconstructed text, plus a decision about what to do with a headshot that now has nowhere to go.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping from a reconstructed story text rather than the readout, re prepare the template, re verify the placeholder inventory field by field, and re plan the headshot: either carry it as part of the delivered artwork by another route or tell the client plainly that this year's pass cannot carry a photo from this source.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A twenty two page run that assembles cleanly and prints with several fields blank or still carrying last year's artwork text, discovered by a gate steward on the first morning of a festival that has already been laminated.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every record survives the frame it landed in. The pass measure is fixed, and a string longer than the measure does not overset visibly and does not raise a warning: it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, so the record looks complete, the run reports success and the page count still equals the row count. Which of the twenty two this happens to is a function of each act's own billing string against the inherited frame width, and no column, no count and no response says which.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is no ordering that avoids it and no parameter that prevents it, because the frame width is inherited from artwork the client supplied rather than chosen. Nothing states it either: the brief says the roster is final and lists what each pass must carry, and the acceptance line about nothing truncating is the printer's standing requirement, not a disclosure that a particular act is too long. And the response is not a re merge of the same thing, it is a craft decision per affected record about measure, about how the act line is set, or about what abbreviates without misbilling an act.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every page of the proof at trim rather than the run summary, identify the records that stop short, change the way the act and stage strings are set for the whole run so one rule covers all twenty two, then re merge, re render and re read.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Laminates printed and heat sealed with an act billed as half its own name and a performer cleared for stages the pass does not show, on the one artefact that cannot be corrected after it is made.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark still holds where it is smallest. The trace off the painted banner comes back clean, complete and convincing at canvas size, and it sits well at poster scale. At the size it actually reproduces in the announcement set corner lockup and in the site plan legend, over the dark ground both of those sit on, the lantern's window panes and the counters inside the type ring can close and fill in, and the hand painted rule can thicken into the ring. Nothing reports it, because the trace succeeded, the vector is valid and the placement is correct.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the reproduction size and the ground only exist once the canvases are composed, and no measurement is available anywhere in the connector to predict it. Nothing states it: the brief asks for the mark back as artwork for the posters, the announcement set and the programme, and never asks how small it can go. The response is not a re export, it is a different raster preparation upstream, a selection weighted to the paint body rather than to its edges, or a plate filled and traced at a different polarity, producing a second mark drawn for small use.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Prepare and trace a small use variant of the mark from the banner by a different route, judge it at true reproduction size on the actual dark ground rather than on canvas, re place it in the announcement set and the legend, re export, and record the two variants and their intended sizes in the basis page and the note.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An announcement set going out on the on sale morning to four thousand ticket buyers with the festival's mark reduced to a dark blob in the corner, and a programme legend where the lantern has no windows.

client_brief:
After Dark: a coherent poster and social campaign from six different nights

Umbra Loft's autumn programme needs to feel like a series, even though our six usable archive photographs were shot under six different lighting rigs. We want a strong two-colour and grain treatment that actually lives in the images, not a collection of unrelated pictures behind matching text.

The commissioned campaign pieces are:

Umbra after dark gig poster run, three A2 directions: Choose and adapt an Adobe Express template for these supporting pieces, using the supplied brand, approved copy and imagery. Select the strongest fit, replace the template content and correct its background as needed. Supply the editable design link and the requested export, in addition to the commissioned custom production work.

Promoter pitch deck and per release social set: Choose and adapt an Adobe Express template for these supporting pieces, using the supplied brand, approved copy and imagery. Select the strongest fit, replace the template content and correct its background as needed. Supply the editable design link and the requested export, in addition to the commissioned custom production work.

The image work underneath them is:

Six archive nights brought to one series target and carrying the two colour treatment and grain register in the raster itself, plus one licensed camera-scale frame brought under the same treatment for the night the archive does not cover. Per frame parameter log, a line on why each night differs from its neighbours, and an explicit statement of what was done with the frames whose bright regions could not be recovered.

Please be honest about bright areas that cannot be recovered. A licensed frame may cover the declared archive gap, but it needs the same treatment and must not be passed off as documentary coverage of a different night.

Pack contents: umbra_archive_nights/ (6 frames, camera scale); umbra_wordmarks/ (3 photographs); umbra_seasoncard_autumn.pdf; umbra_nights_autumn.csv; umbra_billing_autumn.txt; umbra_room_specs.txt.

Please deliver a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note. Account for every supplied file and identify anything used only as reference, superseded or rejected. Stay with approved facts and copy. Do not silently replace weak assets; use only the stated stock or concept allowances, and record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and material compromises.

Fee range: $3,000-$7,000 fixed
Delivery target: 2 to 4 weeks

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor, quoted verbatim in the ledger's grounding_note from the Freelancer.com "Modern Album Logo & Cover Design" post: the client is "getting ready to release a new project and need a striking album cover that also doubles as a recognisable logo for all my promo materials", wants "a clean modern aesthetic, nothing vintage or overly ornate, powered by bright, bold colours that jump off the screen and still look sharp in print", and explicitly asks for "a logo or word-mark element extracted from the main design so I can use it on merch and posters", with deliverables "supplied in layered PSD/AI, plus ready-to-post PNG and JPEG versions" and "scalable vector" artwork. Co anchor: the Freelancer.com open call from a dark aesthetic creative studio offering premium poster, banner and social creatives and cinematic, colour graded photo editing. That second posting names no client and attaches no images, so the brand is laundered to the coined fictional basement venue Umbra Loft, and the vague ask is fixed into a runnable job. Every act, person and street in this task is invented and no real venue, label, musician or trademark appears in any task facing field. The verdict is STRENGTHEN, so the concept and the collateral set stand and the depth is raised: the extracted wordmark ask from the first anchor becomes a genuine recovery off photographed merchandise rather than an extraction from artwork the agent drew itself, the cinematic grading ask from the second anchor becomes a real cross night consistency problem across six differently lit archive frames, and the series acquires the printed half a venue actually needs, because CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) confirms a record per page run can be built off the press PDF the venue's printer already returned.

price_band_and_audience: Independent basement room. Tickets eighteen to thirty two dollars, capacity two hundred and fifty, audience twenty one to thirty five, scene literate and discovery driven, reached almost entirely on a phone late at night. The band is load bearing in both directions. Push polished and corporate, with a clean grid, a safe grotesque and evenly lit photography, and the series reads as sponsored programming rather than as a basement, which is precisely the failure the client names outright. Push the other way into cheap gig flyer chaos, with clip art textures and unreadable type over a black rectangle, and a thirty two dollar headline ticket stops being defensible and promoters stop returning calls. The correct register is dark, high contrast and deliberately made: two colours doing the work, grain that reads as film rather than as noise, raw display type at a real hierarchy, and photography that plainly comes from this room on these nights. A posted commission of this shape and scope runs 1,500 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: An independent two hundred and fifty capacity basement live music room programming a nine night autumn jazz and after dark series.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2021, a basement room under a former textile mill in Providence, Rhode Island, a small independent team.
brand_identity.about: Umbra Loft is a two hundred and fifty capacity basement room under an old mill in Providence, programming jazz and after dark nights for a crowd that finds us through friends and phones at eleven at night. This autumn we are running nine nights as one series rather than nine separate shows. It has to look like one thing, and it has to look like the room it actually is: dark, close and made by hand.
brand_identity.audience: A scene literate, discovery driven crowd aged twenty one to thirty five, reached almost entirely on a phone late at night, who read polish as inauthentic and reward work that plainly comes from the room.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Tickets 18 to 32 dollars, capacity 250. Independent basement scale: deliberately made and high contrast, credible at a headline ticket without ever reading as corporate or sponsored programming.
brand_identity.typography: A raw, weighty display face for act names and dates, set large and blunt, paired with a plain condensed grotesque for billing, door times and the room data tables. Two colours do the work over a deep ground, with grain that reads as film. The feel is gig poster made deliberately, not clip art chaos.
brand_identity.voice: Terse, atmospheric, unvarnished. It names the act, the night and the door and gets out of the way. Example line the brand would write: "Doors 8. Downstairs. Two sets, one room, cash on the night."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: We build the look from our own archive, six photographs shot on six nights under six touring rigs, no two matching. Three headline acts sent their wordmarks only as photographs of tour shirts and a tote, which their managers say is all that survives. There is no defined palette, type or treatment yet, and last season's printed card exists only as the press PDF our printer returned.
brand_identity.values: Everything comes from this room, on these nights, and it should never look like a bank's jazz sponsorship.

assets_supplied.name: umbra_archive_nights/ (6 frames, camera scale)
assets_supplied.kind: Six performance photographs from six different nights in the room, each shot under the touring act's own lighting rig: one tungsten wash, one hard follow spot, two heavy magenta, one near darkness, one lit mostly by the bar.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Six nights, six rigs, one room. Our whole archive. We would rather use these than buy pictures."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: On two of the six the follow spot has driven the performer's face and shirt fully into the top of the channel, so a highlight recovery move returns success while nothing in the frame changes at all, which reads as a correctly conservative result rather than as a dead end. A third frame is convincingly sharp at thumbnail scale but the trumpet bell and the player's right hand are smeared, which only becomes visible at poster scale.

assets_supplied.name: umbra_wordmarks/ (3 photographs)
assets_supplied.kind: Three headline acts' wordmarks, sent by their managers as photographs of tour shirts and a tote lying on a table, described by each manager as the only artwork they still have.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All three sent us a picture of a shirt. They swear it is all they have."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: These are disjoint lettering photographed on cloth, so a one call knockout returns a clean looking transparent file holding only two or three letters of the wordmark while reporting complete success, and on the knitted shirt the letters are worked into the weave so a selection pitched at the ink returns the weave with it. One of the three files carries a different act's mark than its filename says, which only surfaces when the marks are read against the billing.

assets_supplied.name: umbra_seasoncard_autumn.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last season's A5 season card, the press PDF the printer returned, one night per card, with a date block, a billing block, a door and price line and a placed image panel.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last season's card as the printer sent it back. Same shape, new nights. They have asked about bleed."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card carries no bleed at all and none can be introduced downstream: the bleed switch is accepted without complaint and the export reports success while the trim and bleed boxes remain identical, so a press ready with bleed claim would be false. Its typography is inherited from the converted artwork and cannot be replaced with the series typeface on this surface, so the printed half will speak in a different type voice than the posters unless that is designed around and disclosed.

assets_supplied.name: umbra_nights_autumn.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Nine rows: date, headline act, support, door time, set time, ticket price, stage note, and a column of image filenames for the card's picture panel.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The nine nights as confirmed with the acts. Prices are final."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the nine rows are the same act's two night residency billed identically, so a straight row per card run ships two cards a reader cannot tell apart and a record shop stack that looks like a misprint. One row's door time carries a stray character that renders literally rather than being interpreted.

assets_supplied.name: umbra_billing_autumn.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Approved billing and copy: how each act must be credited, the support acts, the ticket tiers, the accessibility line and the room's licence line that must appear on printed matter.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Billing as agreed with the acts. The licence line is required on anything printed."

assets_supplied.name: umbra_room_specs.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The room as promoters ask about it: capacity, stage dimensions, load in, backline, PA, curfew, split terms and last season's average draw.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What every promoter asks before they will talk to us."
