price_band_and_audience: Boutique institutional advisory billing 350 to 600 dollars an hour, buyers are endowment trustees, foundation investment committees and families with 20 million dollars and up. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the portraiture is understated and uniform, the ground is a plain neutral, the crop is identical on all eight, skin is left alone, and the page is sober with wide margins and a credentials table a trustee can read. Pushed up into luxury editorial (dramatic side light, near-black grounds, heavy vignettes, one hero partner larger than the rest) it reads as a personal brand rather than a fiduciary, and a committee reads that as risk. Pushed down into startup about-us (bright saturated grounds, playful crops, mismatched candid frames, oversized first names) it reads as a firm that does not custody other people's money. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every merge field binds. A real posting of this shape runs 1,600 to 3,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Boutique institutional wealth advisory serving endowments, foundations and around forty families.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2009, Boston, Massachusetts, eight advisers on one floor on Federal Street.
brand_identity.about: Northwind Advisory Partners advises endowments, foundations and around forty families on the long term stewardship of institutional and family capital. We are eight people on one floor, and most mandates we win begin with a trustee reading our team page and deciding whether we look like a firm they can place a hundred million dollars with. The brand exists to signal exactly that: a fiduciary, uniform, unshowy, credentialled, judged by a committee rather than an audience.
brand_identity.audience: Endowment trustees, foundation investment committees and families with twenty million dollars and up. Readers aged 45 to 75, most of them reading printed pages and reviewing a credentials table before a mandate is placed.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Billed 350 to 600 dollars an hour. Boutique institutional tier: understated and fiduciary, deliberately not luxury editorial personal branding and not startup about us.
brand_identity.typography: One classical system: a restrained transitional serif for the firm name, headings and the credentials table, paired with a quiet sans for labels and contact lines. Wide margins, generous leading, a text size a trustee reads without effort. No display face, no oversized first names.
brand_identity.voice: Measured, plain, institutional. Speaks of stewardship and process, never of performance promises. Example line the firm would write: We advise a small number of institutions and families on capital they intend to hold for generations. No superlatives, no exclamation points.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The firm mark is a compass rose and wordmark. Two versions survive and neither is a working file: a flat raster export pulled off the old website, and a photograph of the letterpressed card the mark was originally cut for. The mark has to be recovered as placeable artwork with its counters intact before the rebuilt pages can carry it. A third rendering survives on a foil-blocked presentation folder that carries the compass rose alone at large scale, and the only standalone emblem the old web developer ever produced is a fuzzy favicon that blurs at any size, so the mark cannot ship as one lockup: it has to be rebuilt as a working family across formats, from letterhead down to the browser icon, with its counters holding at every reproduction size. Regulated credential designations must be reproduced exactly as the practice system holds them.
brand_identity.values: Fiduciary stewardship above all, and a uniform, sober face that reads as one firm rather than eight individuals.

assets_supplied.kind: Corporate portraits of the eight advisers made across three mornings: two sittings against the grey conference room backdrop, one sitting by the north windows, one frame sent in remotely by a partner's assistant.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Three mornings, one office, and they do not look like one firm. Two on the grey, one lot by the windows, and Hartmann's came in from his assistant."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two sitters wear mid grey suiting and one of those has silver hair, sitting within a hair of the backdrop's own value, so a knockout onto a house ground succeeds cleanly on six and quietly eats shoulder edge and hairline on those two. Separately the remotely supplied frame arrives at 1400 px because it was cropped inside an email client, which is under the card's print need, and the frame shot by the windows carries two illuminants inside one exposure.

assets_supplied.name: adviser_card_2024_press.pdf and adviser_card_2025_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The retired printer's two flat press files for the 85 x 55 mm adviser introduction card, fonts embedded, produced from real page layouts. Both print identically: name, credentials line, practice line, direct dial, email and a portrait.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Both of these are the card. She reissued it in 2025 and I could never see what changed. Keep the card, just rerun it for the eight of us."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The two files are not the same document underneath. One was built with the portrait placed as a linked graphic, so it converts into separated text frames plus a real graphic frame with an integer item id that a per adviser photograph can bind to. The other was flattened before it went to press, so it converts into a single continuous text story with no graphic frame at all and cannot carry a per record portrait by any route. Nothing on the printed card, in the file names or in the page geometry says which is which.

assets_supplied.name: roster_export.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the practice management system, one row per adviser, with columns for legal name, preferred name, title, credential designations, practice sectors, direct dial, email and a portrait filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Straight out of the system. The credentials on the card have to be exactly right, they are regulated."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The export carries nine rows for eight advisers because an associate who left in January is still flagged active, and two rows carry the legal name where the card has always run the preferred name. The credential designations are punctuated three different ways across the rows, and the portrait column is a plain header holding bare filenames that neither match the delivered frames nor satisfy the merge's own image column contract.

assets_supplied.name: northwind_mark/ (mark artwork, 2 files)
assets_supplied.kind: The firm's compass rose and wordmark: one flat 2400 px PNG export, and one photograph of the letterpressed card the mark was originally cut for, lying on a desk.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our mark. The flat one came off the old site. The other is the card the mark was first made for, which we like better."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The two files need opposite instruments: the flat export traces directly, while the photographed card returns the paper rather than the ink unless the selection names the mark's own colour and drawn character rather than the object it sits on, and the compass rose's enclosed counters cannot be punched by a background removal at all.

assets_supplied.name: northwind_folder_foil.jpg (foil-blocked presentation folder, compass rose alone)
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the firm's foil-blocked presentation folder cover, carrying the compass-rose emblem on its own at large scale with no wordmark: the only high-fidelity rendering of the emblem by itself, and the source the small formats need.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The folder we hand things across the table in. That is the compass on its own, big and clean. The little website icon our last person made is useless, it is a blur at any size."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The emblem is brass foil, not flat ink: bright metallic hits ride the raised edges and fall to dark bronze in the recessed shanks, so a selection by the object grabs only the brightest foil and drops the shanks, a raw trace shatters the emblem into a dozen banded sub-paths, and the deboss shadow around it makes a background removal grab the cover rather than the mark. The emblem recovers only if the selection names the compass rose's own drawn character and its foil gradient is flattened to the single Compass Brass ink before tracing, and its centre ring and point gaps cannot be punched. The old developer's favicon is a decoy: tracing or enlarging it produces mush.

assets_supplied.name: credentials_and_sectors.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The office manager's list of the firm's six sectors and, per adviser, the designations held and the year admitted.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What goes in the table on the capabilities page."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the house ground actually holds on all eight. The knockout onto one neutral ground reports success on every frame and each portrait looks entirely normal on its own, but on the two sitters whose suiting and hair sit within a hair of the backdrop's own value the cut bites into shoulder edge and takes a soft chew out of the hairline. Where an edge separates and where it dissolves is a property of this sitter against this backdrop under this morning's light, and no readout in the family reports edge quality. It also does not declare itself one portrait at a time: the bitten shoulder reads as an unusual jacket until the eight are laid in the grid the team page actually runs them in, where two silhouettes are visibly not the same kind of object as the other six.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it and competence cannot either, because the client's requirement is one plain ground across eight sitters and the only way to learn how each sitter's edge behaves against it is to cut it and look at the set. Nothing states it: the brief asks for the same plain ground and never mentions edges, value separation or masks, and the acceptance line about holding at the edge is the client's own standard rather than a disclosure. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a per sitter change of instrument, and for one sitter possibly abandoning the knockout entirely and correcting their original ground toward the house neutral instead.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Lay all eight in the grid and judge them as a grid. For each sitter whose edge failed, switch instrument: select the sitter by their own visual character rather than by the object, invert, and fill the surround to the house neutral so the edge comes from a selection rather than from subject detection, or leave that sitter on their original ground and bring that ground to the house neutral tonally. Then re-cut the common crop on whatever changed and re-judge the grid.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A team page in which two of eight partners have a chewed shoulder line and a halo where their hair meets the ground, on the page an investment committee reads before deciding whether to place a mandate, at the exact tier where uniformity is the entire signal.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the mark family survives at the sizes it is actually used. The vectorise reports success and every variant looks correct at lockup scale, but derived down the compass rose stops being a compass rose: at favicon scale and at the printed card-corner size the hairline strokes between the eight points fuse into a star-shaped blob and the open centre ring fills solid, and in the reversed navy-ground colourway the counters that read as paper showing through invert into navy plugs so the ring and the point gaps disappear. If the foil emblem was traced without first flattening its metallic gradient it also shatters into a dozen banded sub-paths that render as visible steps at size. None of this shows at the scale the mark is recovered at; it exists only once each derived format is rendered at its own true reproduction size.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the emblem is legible at whatever scale it is drawn and only reproduction at the target format sizes exposes the counter collapse. Nothing states it: the brief asks for the mark on the pages and the printed card and never mentions favicons, avatars, counters or a minimum size, and the acceptance line about the mark holding at its reproduction size is the client's own standard. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a per-size art-direction decision, and for the smallest formats possibly a separate simplified emblem with heavier strokes and an enlarged centre ring rather than the same vector scaled down.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Render the favicon-scale raster and the card-corner mark at their true target pixel sizes and the reversed colourway on the navy ground, and judge legibility there. Where the points fuse or the ring closes, redraw the emblem for that size with heavier counters, or supply a size-specific simplified emblem for the small formats and keep the full-detail vector for large use. If the foil emblem banded, re-trace it after flattening the metallic gradient to the single brass ink. Then re-derive the kit and re-judge each format at size.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A new website whose browser favicon and whose networked announcement avatar show a navy blob instead of a compass rose, and printed introduction cards whose corner mark is a filled dot, so the firm's mark is illegible at exactly the small sizes it appears on most.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the two press files is a card and which is a picture of one. They print identically and neither the geometry, the file names nor the client's memory distinguishes them. Converted, one exposes separated text frames plus a real graphic frame with an integer item id, so a per adviser portrait can bind; the other collapses into a single continuous text story with no graphic frame at all, so it can carry copy by offset arithmetic but cannot carry a per record photograph by any route. Frame granularity from a press file is a property of how a now retired printer built the document, is under nobody's control, has no read ahead parameter, and is invisible until the interchange file is exported and read.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it: whichever file is converted first, the structure it yields is only knowable after conversion, and picking the 2025 file because it is newer is a coin toss rather than a method. Nothing states it, because the brief says both files are the card and asks for the card to be kept. It is not a propagation re-run, because what changes is which document the entire print spine is built on and therefore which mapping strategy applies, per frame replacement against separated frames versus ordered offset arithmetic inside one continuous story.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Convert and export the interchange file from both, inventory the frames in each, and build the whole card run on the one that exposes a bindable graphic frame. If the portrait bearing file is also the one whose copy sits in a single story, drive the copy fields by offset arithmetic computed from the reconstructed story text with same frame rows ordered so their positions hold against the original, and re-verify by searching the prepared template for every placeholder. If neither file can carry a portrait, say so to the client rather than shipping eight identical cards with one static face.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A run of eight introduction cards built on the flattened file, every name and credential correct, and the same partner's portrait printed on all eight of them, handed across the table after first meetings with eight different institutions.

why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these files into a frontier image model and it returns eight convincing corporate portraits. IDENTITY: these are Northwind's actual eight advisers, and a regenerated face is a different person on a page whose entire purpose is that an institutional buyer can identify who will manage the mandate. A firm cannot ship invented partners. SPEC: the client needs one printed introduction card per current adviser at 85 x 55 mm carrying regulated credential designations reproduced exactly, bound per record to that adviser's own portrait, plus separately named single card files that each contain the adviser their filename claims, plus proofs at true print resolution. EDITABILITY: the pages are defined by being editable, because credentials and sectors change and the office will not pay for a redo each time a designation is added. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did this placeholder actually get created, is this the adviser the card claims, does this edge hold, does this licensed room belong beside these eight. MARK SYSTEM: the firm's own compass-rose mark must be recovered as a working vector family and derived to the exact formats the rebuild carries it in, its counters holding from letterhead down to a 32 px favicon; a model that redraws a plausible compass rose invents a mark the firm does not use and cannot reproduce crisply at those sizes.

client_brief:
Memorial print and a memory book for Walter Fernwood's family

My father, Walter Fernwood, died in March. We are preparing the service and would like the printed pieces to sit alongside those from my mother's service in 2019. We have the old press files, a eulogy and a shoebox of scans spanning many years.

Please help us make something coherent without making the photographs look newly invented. Damage can be handled through scale, crop and placement; we do not want missing history painted back in.

For the service
One A6 keepsake card per household attending, in list order, each binding the name and the sister's relationship line in full at trim plus that family branch's plate, accompanied by the A4 framed memorial page rendered as a single record at true print-resolution with the plate placed so the subject is whole. Produced by reverse engineering the funeral home's two 2019 press files into live merge templates so the new pieces sit with the mother's on the shelf, with the templates and a written record of what each press file turned out to be as part of the handover.

For keeping and sharing
Memory book and keepsake share card as one editable document plus its source: Choose and adapt an Adobe Express template for these supporting pieces, using the supplied brand, approved copy and imagery. Select the strongest fit, replace the template content and correct its background as needed. Supply the editable design link and the requested export, in addition to the commissioned custom production work.

For the photographs themselves
Every usable scan brought to one printable house look (one black point, one sense of warmth, one weight of print) with a deliberate era level decision recorded where a run could not be brought to the set, plus the postcard reverses raised to legibility while still reading as cream card and paired to their fronts, plus one licensed camera-scale cover frame graded into the same world. Damage handled by crop, plate scale and placement rather than invented away, every output at or below its source dimensions, with a per era treatment log and one line on why each era differs. One set with one look, not one scan at several sizes.

The household names and relationship lines should be complete, and the correct family-branch picture needs to appear on each card. Please keep postcard fronts and backs paired.

Our materials: shoebox_scans/ (26 files, mixed 1200 to 4800 px); keepsake_card_2019_press.pdf; framed_page_2019_press.pdf; guest_list.xlsx export; eulogy.txt and transcriptions.txt.

$6,000-$12,000 fixed; 4 to 6 weeks. Review structure: Direction approval, first-production proof, and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork family history restoration brief in which a private individual digitising roughly twenty four antique 1910 postcard photographs of a touring stage magician company asks for the photographic FRONT and the handwritten BACK of each, delivered legible for a printed memorial book and for sharing with family. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com posting from an individual with 'several old photo scans' to restore 'for A4 printing to mount on my wall', naming 'color fading', 'scratches or tears' and 'blurriness'. That second conceit is deliberately not taken at face value, because the three damages it names are precisely what this connector cannot do: there is no heal, clone or inpaint to rebuild a torn corner or a scratch crossing photographic texture, and no sharpen for blurriness. The honest fuller commission the same client actually needs is the one built here: the scans brought to one printable house look by tonal and colour means, damage handled by crop, plate scale and placement rather than faked, and the result carried into a keepsake the family can print and keep editing. No real person, family, troupe, venue or trademark is named; the magician company is the fictional Veranda Marvelli Company with a fictional lead Aldo Marvelli, and the Fernwood family, Walter Fernwood and the Allsop and Vance funeral home are invented for this benchmark. Verdict STRENGTHEN: the ledger concept was a restoration pass plus a book, which sat on one surface and promised repairs the tools cannot make.

price_band_and_audience: Heritage and memorial commission, 300 to 600 dollars, family and mourners aged 45 to 75, most of them reading printed pages rather than screens. The band is load-bearing in both directions. This is not a luxury commemorative volume, so gilt edges, foil rules, full bleed dramatic plates and a designer typographic conceit read as expensive theatre at a Congregational hall and against the mother's 2019 card on the same shelf. Nor is it a discount photo book, so a dense grid of small plates, drop shadows, decorative corners, script headings and a bright cheerful palette cheapen the keepsake and are exactly what the client says was done badly last time. What the money buys at this band is restraint: generous white space, a quiet classical text face at a size a seventy year old reads without glasses, plates given room, captions that are plain, and an unbroken calm from the contents page to the colophon. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the occasion even if every plate is technically clean. A real posting of this shape runs 350 to 900 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: A private heritage and memorial keepsake commissioned by a family for a service and to keep afterwards.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Commissioned 2024 by the Fernwood family, Brattleboro, Vermont, for a service of around sixty people at the Congregational hall.
brand_identity.about: This is a family memorial keepsake for Walter Fernwood, who died at ninety four. It is a book, not a photo album: plates with captions, a contents page, and the granddaughter's eulogy laid out in the middle, alongside a framed page and a small card for mourners to take home. The visual voice is set by two things: the family's wish that nothing be brightened or invented, and the funeral home pieces made for Walter's late wife in 2019, which the new work should sit beside on the shelf.
brand_identity.audience: The family and around sixty mourners aged 45 to 75, most of them reading printed pages rather than screens, many of whom remember the people in the photographs.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Heritage and memorial commission, 300 to 600 dollars. Neither a luxury commemorative volume with gilt and foil, nor a discount photo book with grids and script headings. What the money buys is restraint.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet classical text face set large enough for a seventy year old to read without glasses, paired with a modest sans for captions and contents. Generous white space, plates given room, plain captions, one unbroken calm from the contents page to the colophon. No script, no decorative corners.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, gentle, unsentimental. Lets the photographs and the family's own words carry. Example line the book would write: The company toured for eleven seasons, and this is his father's hand on the back of the card. No cheerfulness, no exclamation points.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no brand file. The look is inherited from the funeral home's two 2019 press files (a keepsake card and a framed page) that the family wants matched so the pieces sit together on the shelf, and from the family's own scans, eulogy and typed transcriptions. The funeral home's designer has retired and left only flat press files. Damage in the scans is to be shown honestly, handled by crop and placement rather than painted over.
brand_identity.values: Nothing invented and nothing brightened. Honesty to the photographs as they are, and a keepsake the family can keep editing until the day of the service.

assets_supplied.name: shoebox_scans/ (26 files, mixed 1200 to 4800 px)
assets_supplied.kind: Flatbed and phone scans spanning four eras: 1910 postcard photographs of a touring company with handwriting on the reverse, 1930s studio portraits on mount card, a 1968 colour run, 1990s drugstore prints and recent phone frames.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything my brother could scan. Some of them are damaged and we would rather see the damage than see it painted over."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the 1968 colour prints have shifted so far in their dye layers that no correction within reach brings them to the same neutral as the rest without taking the skin green, which is discoverable only by running the correction and looking at the result beside the others. Separately, four scans are photographs of framed prints rather than scans of prints, carrying glass reflection and keystone, and the postcard reverses are pencil on cream card sitting in so narrow a tonal band that the move which makes them legible also greys the card unless it is confined.

assets_supplied.name: keepsake_card_2019_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The funeral home's flat press file for the A6 keepsake card handed to mourners at the 2019 service, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout. Carries a name line, a relationship line, a date line and a placed photograph.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What they printed for my mother. We would like the same shape of thing so the two sit together on the shelf."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The relationship line sits in a fixed measure frame sized for the two and three word entries the 2019 list happened to hold. Longer entries do not spill and do not error, they simply stop rendering at the frame's last line, so a merged card looks finished and complete at thumbnail while a mourner's line is cut mid phrase at trim. The frame's true capacity depends on the applied face and size the retired designer set, which no readout states.

assets_supplied.name: framed_page_2019_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The funeral home's flat press file for the A4 framed memorial page from the 2019 service, with a large plate area, a name and dates, and a short verse block.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The page we framed for my mother. Same size, same place on the wall."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The plate area is a portrait proportion graphic frame while most of the scans worth framing are landscape, and how the merge fits or fills a placed image into that frame, whether it centres and what it clips, appears in no readout and is visible only on the rendered page. assets_supplied.name: guest_list.xlsx export

assets_supplied.visible_description: "Who is coming, and one line about how they knew him. My sister wrote the lines."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The list runs longer than the number of cards actually needed because several couples appear as two rows sharing one household and one line, and a handful of relationship lines run to a full sentence while most are two words. emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the 1968 run can join the book at all in colour. The correction that brings the rest of the colour era to the house neutral is applied to those prints and reports success, and each one looks better on its own than it did. What only appears when they are laid beside the corrected 1930s and 1990s plates is that the two worst have not arrived: their dye layers have shifted far enough that the move which neutralises the cast takes the skin toward green, and pushing further does not converge because the hue range available is moderate rather than complementary. There is no readout for how far an emulsion will travel; it is a property of that print, and the evidence is the set, not the file.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the only way to learn how far a shifted print will move is to move it and look at it beside the others, and there is no earlier moment at which the answer exists. Nothing states it: the brief says the 1968 prints have gone strange and pink and asks for a book, while the acceptance line about the plates sitting together is the family's own standard rather than a disclosure. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is an era level treatment decision that changes what the book is, not a re-execution of the same plan.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Lay the corrected colour plates beside the corrected monochrome plates and judge them as a book turns them. For the prints that will not come, stop chasing the neutral and take a deliberate decision instead: carry that era as a monochromatic tint keyed to the book's warmth so it reads as its own chapter rather than as a failure, or place the two worst small and late rather than as full plates. Then re-cut those plates to the sizes the new decision implies, and record the choice in the note so the family is told rather than shown.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A memory book in which the summer of 1968, the only colour record of the man's young family, turns up as two pink faced plates among ninety years of otherwise settled pages, handed round a Congregational hall by people who remember that summer.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cards and the framed page actually carry what they claim. Two things arrive only on the rendered pages. First, the funeral home's relationship line frame is a fixed measure sized for the two and three word entries the 2019 list happened to hold, so the handful of longer lines the sister wrote do not spill and do not error, they simply stop rendering at the frame's last line: the card looks finished, the merge reports success and every file opens. Second, how the merge fits a landscape plate into the framed page's portrait graphic frame, whether it centres and what it clips, appears in no readout at all, so a plate that was cut correctly to its own subject can still arrive with the subject cut by the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it and care does not help, because both failures present as ordinary success in every response and the frame's true text capacity depends on an applied face and size that a retired designer set and that no tool reports. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a card carrying a name and one line, and the acceptance lines about lines in full at trim and a whole subject on the framed page are the family's own standards rather than warnings. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to change what is bound and how, shortening nothing and instead re-cutting plates to the frame's own proportion and taking the long lines back to the sister for her own shorter wording.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Open and read every rendered card at trim against the normalised list, string by string, rather than judging thumbnails. For each line that stops short, do not shorten the sister's words: take them back to the family for their own decision, and meanwhile re-cut every plate destined for the framed page to that graphic frame's own proportion driven by a selection bbox on the subject, re-merge, re-render at print resolution, and read the pages again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Sixty keepsake cards handed to mourners at the door, several of them carrying a sentence about how that person knew Walter Fernwood that stops mid phrase at the paper's edge, beside a framed A4 page on which his head is cropped by the plate frame, discovered at the service.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the importer actually did to the book's plate construct. The obvious way to give a heritage keepsake its feel is to lay each plate as a mounted print: a soft aged paper texture over the ground, a gently softened plate edge, and a two layer shadow that lifts the plate off the page. All of it exports without a single warning. What comes back is not what was authored: the blend that made the paper texture sit in the page is gone and the texture element arrives as an opaque slab, the softened edge arrives hard, and only the first shadow layer survives, so the plate reads as a flat cut out card. None of this is visible in the rendered preview either, because the preview returns the first root only and the plate pages are pages three onward. The returned markup is the only channel through which any of it can be known.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the construct has to be authored and exported before its normalisation exists to be read, and the preview cannot reach the pages where it lives. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a dignified book and never mentions textures, edges or shadows, and the acceptance line about the book reading as one calm is the family's own standard. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to rebuild the plate treatment out of different materials, which pushes work back into the imaging surface rather than re-exporting the same document.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read the returned markup root by root against what was authored, and rebuild everything that did not survive using means that do: carry the paper feel as a tinted ground and as grain applied to the plate itself in the imaging surface before it is inlined, replace the softened edge with a plate that was cut with its own margin, reduce the lift to the single shadow that survives, then re-author, re-run the readiness check and re-export, and reconcile the markup again page by page.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A memory book whose plate pages, from page three to the colophon, carry an opaque grey slab across the photographs where an aged paper texture was intended, delivered to a family five weeks after a death and printed for a service they cannot rerun.

why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and this shoebox into a frontier image model and it returns beautiful restored photographs. IDENTITY: these are Walter Fernwood's actual family, his father's actual hand on the back of an actual postcard, and a regenerated face or a rebuilt torn corner is a fabrication of a dead man's life presented to the people who are burying him. The client says it outright: do not invent anything that is not in the photographs. client_brief:
Restore a weekly property-sheet workflow from our retired printer's PDF

Every Monday, Harborline Realty prints a sheet for each active listing. The printer retired with the working file. We need the process rebuilt so the current list controls the output, while the starter homes and premium properties retain appropriate, distinct image treatments.

This is the pack you will be working from:
listingsheet_2025_press.pdf; hero_selects/ (11 frames, 3600 to 4200 px long edge); weekly_active.csv; officesign_photo.jpg; principal_note.txt.

Please deliver:

One page per genuinely active property, page count equal to the reconciled roster, each page binding address, headline, description, the beds and baths and square feet strip, price, agent and reference code verbatim plus that property's own hero photograph. Delivered as one multi page press file for the print shop, as one named single page file per property verified by opening it, and as a 300 DPI proof of the point estate at sheet trim. Produced by reverse engineering a retired printer's press file into a live merge template, so the template and the record of how it was derived are handed back with it.

Eleven photographs from two sources and two times of day brought to two declared targets, one per tier, with one black point and one warmth and one crop logic inside each tier, and a stated reason for every difference between the tiers. Levelled where needed before any crop, cropped for the frame that actually receives them, every output at or below its source dimensions with the tradeoff record captured per call, and any frame that cannot be brought to its tier named rather than shipped.

Active listings only. The addresses, descriptions, figures, prices, agents and reference codes must survive exactly from the reconciled data into the exported sheets. Please do not treat the flagship proof as evidence that every record is correct; the individual property files also need identity checks.

The two photographic tiers need declared targets and a reason for the difference, not arbitrary colour changes between properties.

Handover: a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record. Include an inventory showing how every supplied file was used or why it was set aside. Keep factual content tied to the approved inputs. Any missing coverage, substituted asset, reconciliation or quality compromise must be declared; a weak source is not permission to invent or silently replace it.

The commission is budgeted at $1,400-$3,800 fixed. We have allowed 7 to 15 business days, including one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

price_band_and_audience: One brokerage, two audiences in one weekly run. The point estate at 4.5 million is bought by buyers over fifty with liquid capital who read restraint as credibility: one photograph, deep margins, quiet type, a price set small. The starter at 320 thousand is bought by first time buyers under thirty five who need price, beds and the open house time to land instantly: brighter, denser, price forward. The band is load bearing because a single blanket treatment fails in both directions at once. Style the whole book like the estate and the starter sheets look empty and evasive; style it like the starter and the estate reads as volume agency work in front of a vendor paying a six figure commission. A weekly production retainer of this shape posts at 700 to 1,600 dollars a month.

assets_supplied.name: listingsheet_2025_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The retired printer's flat press PDF of the office listing sheet, US Letter portrait, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries an address line, a headline, a three line description, a beds and baths and square feet strip, a price, an agent line, a small reference code line, and one placed hero photograph.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The sheet our printer ran last year. It is the only file we have and she has retired."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither announced. What the conversion exposes as editable structure is a property of how she built the 2025 document: the description, the beds and baths strip, the price and the small reference code arrive inside ONE continuous flow while the address and the agent line sit alone, and the mapping readout silently omits the reference code run while keeping its line break, so every offset past it is short by that run's length and the validator still returns VALID. Separately the hero frame's real bounds are close to square rather than the letterbox the printed sheet suggests, and its fitting is a centre anchored proportional fill that is exposed in no readout at all, so the frame re crops whatever image is bound into it from its own centre regardless of how that image was prepared.

assets_supplied.name: hero_selects/ (11 frames, 3600 to 4200 px long edge)
assets_supplied.kind: One chosen hero photograph per active property, arriving from two sources: four shot by the brokerage's hired photographer for the expensive listings, seven shot by agents on phones.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One picture per house. Some ours, some the photographer's. They need to look like one office."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The two sources do not merely differ in quality, they differ in direction: the photographer's four are late afternoon, warm and deep with the interior lights carrying; the agents' seven are flat midday with a cold cast off the ocean and a lifted black point that reads clean alone and grey the moment it sits beside a photographer's frame. Two of the agent frames sit a degree or so off level and straightening them consumes exactly the edge margin any subsequent crop wants. One agent frame is a twilight exterior whose windows are clipped to paper white with no data behind them, so a highlight recovery there returns a file identical to the one it was given.

assets_supplied.name: weekly_active.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Monday export from the office system, one row per active property, with columns for address, headline, description, beds and baths and square feet, price, agent, reference code and a photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This week's eleven. Straight out of the system."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three faults, none stated. One property went under contract on Thursday and the office manager has not pulled it, so the export carries a row that must not print. The point estate's row was typed by the listing agent rather than exported, so its address uses a different abbreviation convention, its price carries a currency symbol the other rows do not, and its description runs roughly three times longer than anything in the 2025 book the sheet was built around. One photo cell names a file that does not match any folder name because the agent renamed the frame after exporting.

assets_supplied.name: officesign_photo.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the brokerage's harbour front office window, the house mark painted on the glass in cream: a rope ring enclosing a lighthouse and the letters H and R.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "That window is the only place our mark still exists. We lost the artwork years ago."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark traces convincingly at the size the trace comes back, and the failure is entirely one of reproduction size: the rope ring is drawn as a repeating gap and twist, and the R carries a small enclosed counter, and neither of those is a property the trace controls. Vectorize takes no options whatsoever, so nothing about the trace can be tuned after the fact. Whether the gaps and the counter survive is decided by how many pixels the mark occupied in the raster that went in, and it can only be seen at the size the mark is actually used, on the ground it is actually used on.

assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we want to look on the point and how we want to look in town."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the sheet's hero frame actually treats an image bound into it. The frame's bounds can be read out of the converted document, but its FITTING cannot: nothing in the conversion result, the mapping readout, the validator or the merge response says whether a bound image is fitted to the frame, filled from its centre, or placed at its own size. On this document it fills from the centre, so the subject aware crops prepared three steps earlier are re cropped again by the frame, and on the properties whose houses were composed off centre for good reasons the frame's centre lands on driveway and hedge and takes the roofline off the top. Every call in the chain reports success and the thumbnail of the prepared hero is still perfect.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it. Reading bounds and preparing to that aspect is exactly what a careful agent does, and it does not help, because the frame re crops a correctly shaped image from its own centre. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for sheets that look like one office and never mentions frames or fitting, and the acceptance line about the whole house still showing is the client's standing requirement, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a changed crop policy for the whole set, decided against a fitting behaviour nobody could have known.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Compare each rendered page's hero against the file that was bound, establish what the frame is doing to it, then return to the imaging surface and re derive the affected heroes with the house placed for the frame's centre rather than for the photograph, re read every tradeoff record so the re crop has not pushed anything into interpolation, rebuild the image map and merge again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A four and a half million dollar estate goes onto a vendor's sheet with its roofline sliced off and a hedge in the middle of the frame, and seven other sheets go out mis framed in the same silent way, while every file the agent prepared looks perfect on disk.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That one merged record does not fit and does not say so. The description frame was built by the retired printer at a fixed measure for a 2025 book whose entries were short. The point estate's description, typed by the listing agent rather than exported, is roughly three times that length. Overset text in a fixed frame does not spill and does not error: it simply stops rendering, so the page comes back looking finished with the description ending mid sentence at the trim edge. No tool reports overset anywhere in the chain, the merge returns success, and the page count is right.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot settle it: the frame's real capacity for a specific string at that document's point size and leading is not computable from anything the connector exposes, and there is no overset readout to query. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says prices went out wrong once and asks for a clean weekly run; no asset note, deliverable or earlier step mentions copy length. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is editorial: decide which facts a four and a half million dollar listing cannot lose and which are decoration, rewrite in the office's voice, and only then merge again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every rendered page at trim rather than at proof scale, identify each record that stops rather than ends, cut the offending copy to the measure the frame actually holds while keeping the estate's selling facts and the office's voice, raise the rewrite with the listing agent because it is his copy, then re normalise the data file and re run the merge and the per property branch.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The single most expensive listing in the book goes to every open house on a sheet whose description stops mid sentence, in front of the buyers the vendor's commission depends on, and the office's stated reason for hiring a designer was that the sheets keep going out wrong.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered house mark holds at the size it is actually used. The trace comes back at the size of the raster that went in, and at that size it is clean: the rope ring reads as rope, the R has a counter, the lighthouse has a door. Placed at the size a corner mark actually occupies on a square post and a tall story, and rendered on the cream ground the set uses rather than on white, the rope's gaps and the R's counter can close into solid shapes. Vectorize takes no options at all, so nothing about the trace can be tuned afterwards, and whether this particular mark survives is decided by how many pixels it occupied in the raster and by the ground it lands on.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it, because the judgement needs the mark at final size on the final ground, which exists only after the set is authored and exported. Care cannot settle it either: the trace looks correct at every scale before that one. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that the mark on the posts has to be the office's own mark rather than something close to it, which is a provenance requirement, not a warning that a trace can fill in. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The fix lives two surfaces back in raster preparation: re crop the window photograph so the mark occupies far more pixels, re select at ink level and trace again, which is new imaging work and a new judgement.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Inspect the exported canvases through the returned markup and the rendition rather than trusting the export, and where the mark has filled in, return to the window photograph, re crop tightly so the mark carries more pixels, re run the ink level selection and the trace, strip the background path and re inject a viewBox, then re author and re export the set and check the mark on the actual ground again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The office's only surviving mark goes out on public posts as a solid blob with no rope and no letterform, next to printed sheets carrying the real thing, which is the precise brand drift the principal hired a designer to stop.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the folders into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome picture of a flyer. IDENTITY: these are eleven actual properties at actual addresses with actual prices, and the mark is the office's own painted mark, which has to be RECOVERED from the window rather than redrawn, because a brokerage cannot put an invented house or an approximated logo in front of a vendor. client_brief:
Two credential registers rebuilt into a checked autumn graduation run

Cedarline Institute needs credentials for completing candidates across two registers. We have press files from two closed print shops, and they may not convert into the same kind of working document.

Please assess each on its own merits. What matters is a live, usable route that preserves the proper credential, programme, date, number and honours for every candidate, with the institutional seal correctly placed.

Credentials and signature proofs: One credential per completing candidate across two registers, page count equal to the reconciled roster, each binding name, programme title, completion date, credential number and honours verbatim with the institutional seal in place. Delivered as the printer's multi page file, as one named single page file per candidate verified by opening it, and as one 300 DPI proof per register at credential trim for the registrar's signature. Produced by reverse engineering two closed print shops' press files into whatever live route each can actually carry, with the templates and the reasoning handed back.

Campus imagery: Six staff photographs of the hall and the two buildings brought to one declared black point so they read as one set rather than as two afternoons, levelled where needed before any crop, cropped for the canvases that receive them, plus one licensed camera-scale establishing frame graded into the same set. Every output at or below its source dimensions with the tradeoff record captured per call, and any frame that cannot join named rather than shipped.

The campus photographs should read as one set despite being taken on different afternoons. Name any frame that cannot join it rather than enlarging or forcing it into place.

We supply adulted_2024_press.pdf; exec_diploma_2019_press.pdf; cohort_export.csv; seal_impression.jpg; campus_frames/ (6 staff photographs); registrar_note.txt.

Our registrar needs to understand what each recovered template can actually support. Include the derivation notes and inspect the individual candidate files before calling the run complete.

Budget: $3,000-$7,000 fixed. Target: 2 to 4 weeks. Reviews: One direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

The final package should contain a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record, with every source file accounted for, including references and rejected or superseded material. Use the approved information without inventing missing facts. Only the stated stock or concept exceptions permit substitution; document every omission, replacement, reconciliation and material quality compromise.

price_band_and_audience: Two credentials, one cohort, an order of magnitude apart. The community certificate at 180 dollars is earned by evening students in their twenties and thirties and is read by family: plain, warm, legible, honest about what it is. The executive credential at 9,000 dollars is bought by employers and read by that graduate's own clients on an office wall: heavier engraved register, generous margins, restrained colour, the seal given room. The band is load bearing in both directions. Give the community certificate the executive treatment and it becomes pompous about an evening course, which embarrasses the student. Give the executive credential the community treatment and a sponsoring firm sees a printable freebie in a frame, which is the specific failure the registrar says she will hear about within a week. A cohort run of this shape posts at 600 to 1,500 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1978, two campus buildings in Vermont, cohort run by registrar Helen Abbott.
brand_identity.about: Cedarline teaches working adults across two very different registers: an accessible community evening course and a high cost executive programme bought by employers. The Institute trades on being trusted rather than flashy, and on the two credentials reading honestly for what they cost.
brand_identity.audience: Community students in their twenties and thirties whose certificate is read by family at home, and executive candidates whose employer funded credential ends up framed in an office where their own clients see it.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Two credentials an order of magnitude apart: a 180 dollar community certificate and a 9,000 dollar employer funded executive credential. Neither can come off the press looking like the other. Cohort run posts around 600 to 1,500 dollars fixed.
brand_identity.typography: An engraved, higher contrast serif for the executive register, set with generous margins and the seal given room. A warmer, plainly legible serif for the community certificate. The two share bones but never the same weight or spacing.
brand_identity.voice: Measured and earned, never boastful. We state what was completed and who signed it. Example line the brand would write: 'Completed the autumn programme in professional practice. Signed at Cedarline Institute, Vermont.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The seal die went to the printer that closed and cannot be recovered. The only surviving seal is the one blind embossed into an old certificate, plus a raking light photograph of that impression. Two dead press files remain, last year's community certificate and the 2019 executive diploma; there is no digital seal artwork.
brand_identity.values: Each credential must be honest about its price, and every candidate name spelled and accented correctly right up to the ceremony morning.

assets_supplied.name: adulted_2024_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last year's community completion certificate as a flat press PDF, A4 landscape, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries a recipient name, a programme title, a completion date, a small letterspaced credential number, two signature lines and a seal position.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's community certificate. It is what the shop printed from."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The conversion exposes the recipient name, the programme title, the completion date and the credential number inside ONE continuous flow while the two signatory lines sit alone, and the mapping readout omits the letterspaced credential number run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past it is short by that run's length. The validator returns VALID on those offsets, the prepare call reports success, and the fields past the omission are silently absent from the template.

assets_supplied.name: exec_diploma_2019_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The executive diploma as a flat press PDF, produced in 2019 by a different print shop from the community certificate and unchanged since.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The executive diploma. We have not touched it since twenty nineteen."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: How this document was built is nothing like how the printed page reads. Its whole face is one continuous typeset block, so the conversion yields a single text frame holding every line and no graphic frame at all, which means there is no target to bind a per record seal into and every field has to be driven by offset arithmetic inside one story. Nothing about the printed diploma suggests this, and it is not visible until the document has actually been converted and its interchange file read.

assets_supplied.name: cohort_export.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The registrar's export for the autumn cohort, one row per candidate, with columns for name, programme code, programme title, completion date, credential number and an honours field.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The full cohort straight out of the student system."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Four faults, none stated. Which register a candidate belongs to is carried only inside the programme code, so the two tiers have to be inferred rather than filtered. One candidate withdrew in week three and was never removed. Two rows carry the same credential number, a clerical duplicate that would put an identical number on two different people's credentials. And several names carry European diacritics typed in a convention the rest of the file does not use, while the honours column is empty for the entire community register even though the certificate face carries an honours line.

assets_supplied.name: seal_impression.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A raking light photograph of the institutional seal blind embossed into cream certificate stock: a rope bordered ring enclosing a cedar device and the institute's founding year.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The die went with the shop. This is the only seal we have left, pressed into an old certificate."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The impression is colourless: relief and paper are the same cream, and the seal reads only as shadow. Where the raking light falls away along one side of the ring the relief and the stock sit at the same luminance, so a selection there has nothing to hold on to. The mask still comes back looking like a seal, the trace still succeeds, and what is missing is an arc of the rope border and part of the year, which is invisible against cream at preview scale.

assets_supplied.name: campus_frames/ (6 staff photographs)
assets_supplied.kind: Six photographs of the ceremony hall and the two campus buildings, shot on staff phones across two afternoons for the programme cover and the credential card.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our own pictures of the hall and the buildings."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three were shot with the phone's high dynamic range mode on and carry a milky lifted black point that looks perfectly clean alone and turns visibly grey the moment it sits next to one of the other three. One hall interior sits a degree off level, and straightening it consumes exactly the edge margin the programme cover's crop wants.

assets_supplied.name: registrar_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: A page from Helen Abbott on how the two programmes are described, who signs which credential, and what the sponsoring firms have complained about before.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How we talk about the two programmes and who signs what."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether this photograph of a blind embossed seal will give up the whole device. The impression is colourless, so relief and paper are the same cream and the seal exists only as shadow. Along the side where the raking light falls away the relief and the stock sit at the same luminance and the selection has nothing to hold, so the mask silently loses an arc of the rope border and part of the founding year. Nothing reports it: the selection succeeds, the mask thumbnail still looks like a seal, the trace succeeds, and the gap is invisible against cream at preview scale. It becomes visible only with the traced seal placed at credential size on the cream ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot prevent it: the failure is a property of where the light fell on this one photograph, and there is no measurement anywhere in the family, no histogram and no eyedropper, so no read ahead exists. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that the die is gone and the seal must come back as usable artwork; no asset note or acceptance line discloses that part of it will not select. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different instrument, either compositing per element selections or abandoning the impression for the flat printed seal on the old certificate face.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Confirm the loss by reading the traced seal round the whole ring at reproduction size rather than glancing at the thumbnail, then re attack it: name the rope border and the year as their own selections and composite them with the ring, or crop far tighter so the shadowed side carries more pixels, or fall back to the seal printed on the 2024 certificate face and accept that it is a different generation of the same device, which is a provenance decision the registrar has to be told about.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Every credential in the cohort, community and executive alike, carries an institutional seal with a broken rope border and half a founding year, on a document that hangs on a wall for twenty years and whose whole function is to look unforgeable.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What each of the two press files can actually carry. The community certificate converts into a usable structure with a graphic frame that can receive a per record seal. The 2019 executive diploma, built by a different shop as one continuous typeset block, converts into a SINGLE text frame holding every line and NO graphic frame at all, so there is no target to bind a seal into and all four fields must be driven by offset arithmetic inside one story. Nothing about the printed diploma suggests this: it looks like the more carefully made of the two documents. Frame granularity from a PDF is not under anyone's control and is exposed only by converting and reading the interchange file.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it. Converting both and looking IS the correct move, and what it returns is not knowable in advance from the printed pages, the file sizes or anything the client said. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that there are two files and to use whichever still works, which is the client's ignorance, not a disclosure of which one fails or how. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is an architecture decision that changes what the executive register can be, how its seal is placed, and what the agent has to tell the registrar.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re plan the executive register around what its file can hold: drive its fields by offsets inside the one story, decide whether its seal can be placed at all through the merge or whether that register has to ride the community derived template at a corrected type register, weigh what a 9,000 dollar credential loses either way against the registrar's stated fear of looking like a printable freebie, then rebuild the mapping and re verify the placeholders for that register from scratch.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The executive register either merges with no seal at all, or is quietly run off the community template, and the employer funded credential arrives at the ceremony looking exactly like the 180 dollar evening certificate in front of the sponsoring firms the registrar named.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the importer does with the cohort roster once the table is taller than the artboard it sits on. A table survives as a live table, but nothing anywhere documents what happens past the canvas edge: whether rows are clipped, reflowed, hoisted or dropped. The export returns success either way with no warning of any kind, and because the roster sits on a canvas after the first, the rendition cannot show it, so the returned per canvas markup is the only channel through which the roster's actual state exists. Counting rows in the markup is the only way to learn whether the whole cohort is in the programme.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot settle it, because how many rows the artboard holds at a chosen size and leading is not computable from anything the connector exposes, and the check itself only exists after an export. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for the programme with the full cohort listed and for it to be editable; no asset note, deliverable or earlier step says anything about roster length or canvas behaviour. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is an authoring decision about how a cohort is broken across pages and set in two registers.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Count the roster rows present in the returned markup against the reconciled register files rather than trusting slide_count, and where rows are missing, re author the programme: split the roster across additional canvases, decide where the two registers break and whether they are listed together or apart, re set the measure and leading so the names with diacritics still fit their cells, then re run the readiness check and export again and re count.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The ceremony programme handed to every family in the hall silently omits the last dozen graduates, whose relatives are sitting there, and the office finds out during the ceremony rather than before it.

decision_gates: Which deliverables go to the merge surface and which to authored canvases, given credential faces the institute wants kept and names that get corrected on the ceremony morning.
How the cohort is split into registers when no column carries the tier and the boundary lives inside the programme code.

The export: a withdrawn candidate still listed, a credential number appearing on two people, a diacritic convention the file does not hold consistently, and an honours column empty for a whole register. Which are the agent's to fix and which are the registrar's.
How to select a device that exists only as shadow, and whether to composite per element selections or fall back to a printed seal from a different generation.
Which press file carries which register once both conversions have been read, and what a nine thousand dollar credential loses on each route.
Whether to trust the mapping tool's readout of either printer's text or to reconstruct each story independently from the exported document.

client_brief:
Eighteen conference badges with portraits that match and records that do not drift

The Meridian Summit registration desk needs a correct badge for every attending delegate. We have eighteen self-submitted photographs and last year's venue-bureau PDF, but not its working file.

The photographic problem and the record problem are equally important. Please align the portrait framing while keeping individual skin faithful, then bind each person to their own complete registration details, including post-nominals.

Badge run
One page per attending delegate in registration order at true badge trim, rendered at 300 ppi, every field the 2026 badge carried present on every badge and bound verbatim from the registration export including post-nominals, with each delegate's own portrait in the correct graphic frame. Accompanied by one single-badge file per delegate named to that delegate and identity-verified by opening it, plus 300 ppi proofs. Produced by reverse-engineering the bureau's flat PDF into a live merge template, which is handed back with the record of how it was derived and of what it cannot carry.

Portrait set
Eighteen self-submitted portraits of wildly different provenance brought to one house treatment with individual skin held faithful rather than averaged, delivered at a consistent badge framing with the same eye line and head size across the set, plus one licensed venue context frame graded into the same neutral. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-portrait parameter log, one line per portrait on why it differs from its neighbours, and every crop and resize response's reported metadata transcribed.

Preflight evidence
A client-facing preflight package showing representative first, middle, last, longest, and exception records at true output size, with page count, dimensions, overflow, image binding, naming, and record identity checks.

Attached: delegate_headshots/ (18 files, 900 x 1200 to 4200 x 5600); registration_export.csv (21 rows); badge_2026_PRINT.pdf; lectern_plate.jpg (3900 x 2600); tracks_note.txt.

We expect true-size proofs of representative and difficult records, including the longest and exception entries. A successful merge message is not a substitute for checking the exported badges and their individual filenames.

Alongside the finished work, we need a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record. Keep a clear record of the supplied files used, retained for reference, superseded and rejected. Approved source information remains authoritative. Record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and quality limits, and do not use an undeclared replacement or invented fact to conceal a source problem.

This is a fixed-price commission at $6,000-$12,000, with a target of 4 to 6 weeks. The agreed review allowance is direction approval, first-production proof, and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Twenty-one rows for eighteen badges.
