emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the isolation held its edge on this particular person. Five of the eighteen delegates sit within a whisker of their own background in value: a light grey jacket on a pale grey sweep, platinum hair against cream, a white shirt against a white wall. On those frames the automatic isolation returns a clean, confident, entirely plausible cut-out and has quietly taken the shoulder line, the collar or the hair edge away with the background, because there was no value difference for it to find. Which portraits behave this way is a property of these specific photographs (this person, wearing this, in front of that) and cannot be read off the roster, the filenames or the source previews. The damage is also invisible against transparency: it appears only once the cut is placed on the badge's own ground, where a missing shoulder reads as a printing fault rather than as a bad cut.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it and care alone does not either, because the tool reports success either way and the returned cut-out looks correct until it is composited against the ground the badge actually uses. Nothing states it: the brief says the portraits are a mixed bag and asks for one consistent wall, which is an ordinary client requirement, and no asset description names the five delegates at risk. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to abandon the automatic route for those portraits in favour of an explicit selection of the person, inverted and filled to the chosen ground, and then to re-take the ground decision for the whole set, since a ground that rescues a platinum-haired delegate may bury a dark-suited one.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-isolate the affected portraits by selecting the person explicitly, inverting and filling to the ground rather than asking for an automatic knockout, then re-place all eighteen on the ground together and re-decide the ground, because five portraits produced by a different route will not sit with the other thirteen unless the ground choice is re-made across the set. Record the route per delegate in the handover so the reprint desk knows which files were produced how.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A registration wall at a twenty-four-hundred-dollar summit on which five delegates have no left shoulder and one has a hole in her hairline, printed, laminated and hung, with every tool in the chain having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That the per-delegate check-in code the client asked for cannot actually be produced on this surface, and that the tools say the opposite at every step. The code mapping is documented, is accepted and normalised by the validator, and the template preparation returns a clean success message. Nothing is created. The round-tripped document shows the code frame keeping its original static link with none of the markers a live code would carry, and a rendered badge shows the same flat grey rectangle it always had. There is no error, no warning and no diagnostic anywhere in the chain, and the printed badge looks finished.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, and reading the documentation makes it worse rather than better, because the documentation describes the capability as working and the validator agrees, so a diligent agent has every reason to believe it landed. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a scan code because the desk scans people in, which is an ordinary organiser requirement, and the acceptance bar asks only that anything the badge cannot carry be named before print. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to drop a requested feature, re-scope it with the client and propose a different route to check-in, which changes what is delivered rather than re-running what was.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Verify by round-tripping the prepared template and reading the code frame directly rather than trusting the success message, confirm the same on a single rendered badge, then remove the dead mapping so it is not carried silently into the run, and raise it with the client before print with a workable alternative: one static event code on every badge with check-in done against the printed delegate number, or per-delegate code artwork produced by the registration platform and bound through the image column exactly as the portraits are. Nothing else in the badge changes, which is precisely why it is easy to leave broken.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eighteen badges printed and laminated with a grey rectangle where the code should be, discovered by a scanner at seven in the morning at a summit where the first delegate through the door runs a transmission network.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each delegate's organisation and name actually fit the badge. The name and organisation came out of the bureau's system inside one continuous story sitting in a fixed-measure frame, and a fixed frame in this layout does not spill: a string longer than the measure simply stops rendering at the frame edge. The page renders, the page count is right, the merge reports success, the proof looks composed, and one delegate's employer reads as a plausible shorter name with nothing anywhere to indicate that anything is missing. Which records overflow depends on the measure the conversion happened to produce, which is not a parameter and is not under anyone's control, so it can only be learned by merging the real roster and reading each rendered page at true trim.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it: the frame's real measure exists only after the conversion, and the truncation exists only after the real strings are bound into it, so no amount of planning reaches it earlier. Nothing states it: the brief says nothing may be shortened or abbreviated, which is the client's standing requirement rather than a warning, and no asset description tells the agent which three organisations are long. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a scope conversation and a layout decision rather than another merge of the same thing.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every rendered badge at true trim against its export row, identify which records are being cut and where, then take the decision the client asked for: raise it in writing before print rather than abbreviating, and propose what is actually available, which is a second badge variant for the long-organisation records merged as a record-range subset, or the organisation carried across a second line, never a shortened string. Re-run only the affected subset and read it at trim again rather than assuming the second attempt took.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Badges handed to three senior delegates on which their employer's name is cut off mid-word, from an organiser whose entire proposition is that this room is worth twenty-four hundred dollars a seat.

decision_gates: The surface split: badges to the merge surface because the layout is fixed client property and the run is one record per page, room set to HTML authoring because it needs three canvas sizes and must stay editable.
Which portraits set the house treatment, knowing a studio headshot and a hotel-corridor phone picture cannot both be the reference.
How far to correct an individual portrait before the correction stops matching the wall and starts changing the person.
The badge crop policy across eighteen faces, decided as a set, and constrained by the four sources that are a fraction of the size of the rest.
The badge ground, chosen against eighteen different jackets, shirts and hair colours rather than against the best-looking single portrait.
Isolation route per delegate: the one-call knockout is right for a dark suit on a mid grey and wrong for a light jacket on a pale sweep, and the wrong route reports success either way.

client_brief:
A reusable A4 trade catalogue for Halden & Roe's Marlow range

Sixteen pieces need to reach the trade show as one coherent Marlow range. Our studio photography covers two days, and the only page artwork is the flat PDF the printer made three seasons ago.

We need the page rebuilt into a reusable merge document and the photographs prepared for its actual picture frame. Please keep the three glazes distinguishable on the shared page white.

A4 portrait, one piece per page in line order, page count equal to the current piece count, rendered at 300 ppi at trim. Every page binds the caption, the eight spec parameters, the firing and care line, the lead time and the trade price verbatim from the price file in one consistent money format, plus that piece's own photograph in the correct graphic frame and the recovered stamp in the footer. Accompanied by one single-page sheet per piece named to the piece code and identity-verified by opening it, and by 300 ppi proofs. Produced by reverse-engineering the printer's flat PDF into a live merge template, handed back with the record of how it was derived.

Sixteen in-house frames from two days brought to one page white with the three glazes still clearly distinguishable from one another, delivered at a consistent piece scale on the agreed ground, plus one licensed context frame graded into the same neutral. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log, one line per-frame on why it differs from its neighbours, every crop and resize response's reported metadata transcribed, and an explicit record of the four frames whose highlights cannot be recovered.

The eight specification parameters, firing and care copy, lead time and trade price all need to fit in full. Use one money format and keep each piece's image and code correctly bound. Record the four frames whose highlights cannot be recovered rather than claiming that a successful adjustment restored absent detail.

Inputs: marlow_shots/ (16 frames, 4000 x 5000); trade_price_file.csv (19 rows); catalog_page_2026_PRINT.pdf; pot_base_stamp.jpg (3600 x 3600); glaze_note.txt.

Please include individual sheets that have been opened and identity-checked, alongside the combined catalogue and retained template.

price_band_and_audience: Trade 38 to 410 dollars a piece, retailing 100 to 900. The buyer is an independent homeware shop owner or an interior stylist, 30 to 55, who buys forty lines a season across a dozen makers and can tell a thrown piece from a cast one across a room. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the correct book is airy and slow: one piece to a page with real space around it, deep quiet neutrals, the glaze given room to be the subject, type set small and calm, the trade price stated plainly and once, no starbursts and no density. A real posted job of this shape runs 2,000 to 4,000 dollars fixed, or 45 to 70 dollars an hour across 40 to 55 hours.

assets_supplied.name: marlow_shots/ (16 frames, 4000 x 5000)
assets_supplied.kind: In-house product photography of the sixteen Marlow pieces on the paper sweep in the back room, shot across two days in three glazes: reactive oatmeal, gloss celadon and matte slate.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Two days on the sweep, same camera, same corner. Looking at them now they do not hold together, and the glazes are the whole product."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. Four of the gloss celadon pieces were exposed for the body of the glaze, so the specular band along each rim is clipped flat with no data left in it, and a highlight recovery on those frames returns a result in which nothing moves at all, leaving the rim with no edge to hold against a pale page. assets_supplied.name: trade_price_file.csv (19 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the house's order book, one row per line item, with columns for piece code, name, dimensions, capacity, glaze, firing note, care note, lead time, carton quantity, trade price, retail guide, last order date and a photograph column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our price file. The numbers are ours and they are what the shop holds us to."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Nineteen rows for sixteen pages. Two pieces were retired last season and are flagged only by a last order date already in the past, and one row is a mixed carton rather than a piece. Trade prices are formatted three different ways across the column (bare integers, one decimal place, and a currency symbol on some cells only), the two made-to-order pieces carry an empty trade price that reads on a printed page as free, two care strings run four times the length of the rest, and the photograph column holds full local paths without the prefix the merge's own image contract requires.

assets_supplied.name: catalog_page_2026_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF of the existing trade book page, A4 portrait, one piece per page, fonts embedded, produced through a full print engine so it converts cleanly. Carries a piece name, a caption, an eight-row spec block, a trade price line, a product photograph and a footer mark.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer printed from three seasons ago. We do not have the working file and nobody here understands how it was made. Keep the page."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two facts nobody at Halden and Roe could tell you. What the printed page shows as four separate blocks (caption, an eight-row spec block set in two columns, a price line and a footer) is not what the conversion exposes: the spec block and the price line came out of the printer's system as ONE continuous story with tab characters between each parameter and its value, so there are no per-parameter frames to map and everything must be driven by ordered offsets inside a single story. The mapping readout of that story silently omits the run holding the firing and care line while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well-formed, every character offset past it is short by exactly that run's length, the validator returns valid on the resulting arithmetic, the placeholder step reports success, and the two fields sitting past the omission never become placeholders at all.

assets_supplied.name: pot_base_stamp.jpg (3600 x 3600)
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of the impressed maker's stamp on the unglazed foot of a Marlow bowl, shot square on under a raking studio light.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The stamp on the base. It is the only mark we own and there is no drawing of it anywhere."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The stamp is impressed into clay rather than printed, so it reads as shadow in a raking light rather than as ink, and glaze has pooled into part of one letter, thickening that stroke well beyond the others. A prompt naming the pot or the base pulls the selection to the whole unglazed foot, and the wordmark carries two enclosed counters and a hairline connecting stroke that survive a trace at inspection size but have nothing like the same margin at the size the page footer actually uses.

assets_supplied.kind: Half a page from the studio manager describing the three glazes in plain language, with no numbers and no colour values.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Oatmeal breaks pale over the edges and pools brown in the throwing rings. Celadon is glassy and green-grey and shows every highlight. Slate is dead matte and drinks light."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That there is nothing left in the celadon rims to recover. Four of the gloss celadon pieces were exposed for the body of the glaze and the specular band along each rim is clipped flat, so when the highlight and light-portion corrections are applied to bring the rim back the readout is that nothing moves at all: the parameters take, the call succeeds, the returned frame is indistinguishable from the one that went in along that edge. Whether a given frame still holds data in its highlights is not stated anywhere, is not visible from the glaze note or the piece list, and cannot be inferred from the other frames of the same glaze, because it depends on how each piece was exposed on the day. The consequence only becomes concrete once the page ground is chosen: on a pale page a rim with no edge means the piece has no top, which the buyer reads as a photography fault and the shop reads as a glaze that does not exist.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the only way to learn that a highlight has no data behind it is to try to move it and see that it does not move, and there is no readout in the family that reports clipping before the fact. Nothing states it: the brief says the glazes are the whole product and that the pictures must tell them apart, which is the client's commercial requirement rather than a warning, and no asset description names which four frames are affected. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to change the page ground for the whole book so a blown rim has something to sit against, which re-opens the ground decision for all sixteen pieces and every isolation derived from it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Confirm on each affected frame that the recovery genuinely moves nothing rather than assuming a parameter was too small, then take the set-level decision instead of the per-frame one: re-choose the page ground toward the stone neutral so the clipped rims have an edge, re-grade the whole range's white point against that ground rather than against paper white, and re-derive every isolation on the new ground. Record in the handover which four frames cannot be recovered and recommend they be reshot before next season.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A trade book in which four gloss celadon pieces have no rim at all against a pale page, sent to independent shop buyers who are being asked for four hundred and ten dollars a piece on the strength of the glaze.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's page actually exposes, and then whether the mapping built against it landed. Two things arrive only by running. First the granularity: what the printed page shows as a caption, an eight-row spec block and a price line is not three mappable regions, because the printer's system emitted the spec block and the price line as one continuous story with tab characters between each parameter and its value, so there are no per-parameter frames and everything must be driven by ordered offsets inside a single story. Second the yield: the mapping readout of that story omits the run holding the firing and care line while keeping its line break, so the string still parses as well-formed, every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length, the validator returns valid on internally consistent wrong arithmetic, the placeholder step reports success, and the two fields past the omission never become placeholders at all.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Granularity is not a parameter, is not reported before the conversion and has no read-ahead, so the only route to it is to convert, export and read. The yield failure is worse, because it is produced by a convenience readout that presents as complete, so an agent that reads carefully and computes offsets diligently from the readout it was handed produces arithmetic that is internally consistent and wrong, and every downstream tool agrees with it; the only defence is an independent reconstruction of the same text from the document itself, which nothing prompts and whose necessity is invisible until the two disagree. Nothing in the brief states either fact, and it is not a propagation re-run, because the source of truth behind the mapping changes and the whole mapping is re-authored with re-ordered same-uid rows.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story by concatenating the IDML content runs, recompute every offset against that string, re-order rows sharing a uid so their positions hold against the original text, rebuild and re-validate the mapping, re-run the template preparation, and re-verify by round-tripping IDML and grepping for every placeholder before a single page is merged. Settle which graphic frame holds the piece photograph rather than the footer mark by rendering one page and reading it against the printed reference rather than by assuming the larger frame is the product.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Sixteen trade pages that bind the piece name, the dimensions and most of the spec block correctly while the firing and care line and the field after it are silently absent from every page, printed and sent to shops who order to exactly those values, with every tool in the chain having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered maker's stamp is still the maker's stamp at the size the page actually prints it. Traced and inspected at its own canvas size the mark is clean, with its two counters open and its connecting hairline intact. The footer frame's real dimensions only exist once the page has been converted, and once the mark is placed in that frame on the book's own warm paper ground and the page is rendered at trim, the counters close into solid blobs and the hairline drops out, so the wordmark reads as a smudge rather than as a name. Neither the frame size nor the ground colour was knowable while the trace was being made, and neither the trace nor the placement reports anything wrong: the mark is present, the page renders, the proof at reduced scale looks entirely acceptable.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the trace has to exist before it can be placed, the frame size only exists after the conversion, and the ground colour is a decision taken elsewhere in the job, so the three facts that determine the answer are never available at the same time until the page is rendered. Nothing states it: the brief says the stamp goes in the footer of every page, which is an ordinary placement instruction, and the acceptance bar states the client's standing requirement that the mark still read as the stamp, not a warning that it will not. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to derive a different artwork rather than to re-place the same one.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive the mark for the footer from a differently prepared raster, taking a filled plate of the impression rather than the raw binary mask so the strokes carry weight, and even out the stroke the pooled glaze thickened, then re-render one page at trim on the real ground and look again. Where the counters still will not hold, deliver two artworks and say so: a simplified single-weight version for the footer size and the full trace for the stand panel and the slides, with the handover naming which is used where and below what size the full trace should never be set.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A sixteen-page trade book whose footer carries an illegible smudge on every page, from a house whose only owned mark is that stamp, discovered by the studio manager when the printed books arrive nine weeks later.

decision_gates: The surface split: the book to the merge surface because the layout is fixed client property and the run is one piece per page, the trade-show set to HTML authoring because it needs three canvas sizes and must stay editable.

Whether to trust the mapping readout of the printer's spec story or to reconstruct it independently from the document.

client_brief:
Personalised renewal postcards, including eleven correctly separated producer files

For Aldervale Mutual's autumn renewal drop, each household must receive its own address, offer band and assigned producer's photograph. The starting point is the printer's PDF and our spreadsheet.

Please treat the split files as part of the main job, not an afterthought. Each of the eleven producers must receive only their own households, and the record-selection method must guarantee that identity.

Mail-house and producer files
One press file for the mail house with page count exactly equal to the drop list's row count, one household per page in the order the file was merged, every page carrying that household's own address complete to its final line, its own offer band and its assigned producer's own photograph. Plus eleven per producer files, each named for its producer, each containing only that producer's households, with identity guaranteed by how the subset was requested.

Portrait preparation
Eleven producer portraits brought to one look across two shooting situations (one white point, one contrast, one head size in frame), knocked out onto the card's own ground with an edge that holds on the green rather than only against white, cropped to the template's real portrait proportion, named to the values the drop list binds by, and no output above its source frame's pixel dimensions. Delivered with a per-frame parameter log and the file to producer reconciliation.

Source material: aldervale_renewal_card_2025.pdf; aldervale_producers/ (11 portraits, 6000 x 4000); aldervale_households.csv; aldervale_producer_card.jpg; aldervale_brand_sheet.pdf; aldervale_offer_copy.txt.

Check the portrait edges on the card's green ground and crop to the real template proportion. Complete addresses must survive to their final line. We need a file-to-producer reconciliation and a clear explanation of any source limitation before the files are treated as ready for mailing.

Handover: a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record. Include an inventory showing how every supplied file was used or why it was set aside. Keep factual content tied to the approved inputs. Any missing coverage, substituted asset, reconciliation or quality compromise must be declared; a weak source is not permission to invent or silently replace it.

Please work within $1,400-$3,800 fixed and the 7 to 15 business days target. Allow for one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

source_provenance.original_anchor: Anchored to the Freelancer.com brand-collateral post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note: a regional broker asking for a fixed brand-locked template populated from a structured roster into a press-ready PDF plus an editable source, insisting that 'the colors, fonts and overall layout from the brand style guide' come through clearly and that 'I don't want to hunt for missing fonts or mismatched data'. The real post names no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional carrier Aldervale Mutual Assurance; no real company, carrier, agency, person, product or trademark appears anywhere, and the earlier working name that collided with a live Rhode Island carrier is fully removed. The prior version of this engagement sat on the data merge alone, which is what the REBUILD verdict is about. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is: a bare printer's PDF can now be reverse engineered into a live merge template headlessly, a per row image column genuinely binds a different photograph to every record, and an ink level trace off a photographed printed card recovers a real mark. So this is that broker's actual job, end to end: the template is recovered rather than assumed, the producers' faces are real faces, and the editable source they asked for exists.

price_band_and_audience: A mutual whose average home policy runs 1,100 to 1,900 dollars a year, sold face to face by a producer the household knows by name, to owners aged forty to seventy in towns under four thousand people. The band is load-bearing. At this register the card is restrained: one photograph, a serif voice, generous margins, the offer stated once and quietly, the producer's name larger than the offer. Push it down into the mass renewal blast register (bright panel, a percentage in the largest type on the card, three benefit bullets, a starburst) and a household insured here for thirty years reads it as churn marketing from a carrier that has stopped knowing them, which is exactly the retention the drop exists to protect. Push it up into private wealth register (cream stock feel, all small caps, no photograph, almost no offer) and it stops being a renewal reminder for a farmhouse policy. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even when every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Cover from people who know your town
brand_identity.sector: A regional mutual carrier writing home and farm cover, sold face to face through local producers across rural Vermont.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: central Vermont; canonical context for the repeat-client series.
brand_identity.about: Aldervale Mutual Assurance is the repeat client for this benchmark series. The canonical client context is central Vermont, and this commission covers phase 2: personalised renewal mailer.
brand_identity.audience: Homeowners and farm owners aged forty to seventy in small Vermont towns, many insured here for decades, who value a known producer and a fair renewal over the lowest online quote.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Average home policy runs 1,100 to 1,900 dollars a year. Mid market and relationship led, not a discount carrier and not a private wealth boutique. Communications stay restrained: one photograph, generous margins, the offer stated once and quietly, the producer named larger than the offer.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet serif system as set in the 2019 style guide: a text serif for policy copy and addresses, paired with a slightly heavier serif for producer names and headings. Editorial rather than promotional, generous leading, no condensed or display faces.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, direct and adult. We write to the household, never at the market, and we never oversell. Example line the brand would write: "Your renewal is due in October, and your producer, will be glad to walk it through with you."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original design files are gone: the designer retired and took her drive, so the last renewal card survives only as the printer's press PDF. The mark exists cleanly only where it was printed on a producer's business card. One 2019 style guide page (house green, warm grey, the two type families, clear space, and the rule that the mark never sits on a photograph) is all the written guidance that remains.
brand_identity.values: Continuity and knowing the policyholder. Households should feel written to by a carrier that still knows them, and the mark is never placed over a photograph.

assets_supplied.name: aldervale_renewal_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF of last spring's renewal postcard, held by the printer, single page, both sides, real embedded font subsets.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is the card exactly as it printed last spring. It is the only form of the artwork that still exists."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What the printed card visually separates into a salutation, an address block, a producer line and an offer band converts into far fewer frames than that, because the whole left column was set as one continuous flow, so the fields cannot be addressed as separate frames and must be reached by position inside a single story. Worse, the mapping readout of that story omits one run entirely while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length, the validator returns VALID with no warnings, the placeholder step reports success, and the mappings past the omission are silently absent from the template.

assets_supplied.name: aldervale_producers/ (11 portraits, 6000 x 4000)
assets_supplied.kind: Producer headshots, some taken at the regional meeting against the hotel's cream function room wall, some taken later outside an office by a colleague on a full frame body.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our eleven producers. Taken at the regional meeting and afterwards by whoever had a camera, so they are a mixed bag."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The frames are far larger than the one call knockout expects, and that tool silently reduces oversized inputs while reporting it in no message and no error, only as a downscaled entry inside the returned tradeoffs object. Separately, the four shot against the cream function room wall sit at almost the value of that wall at the shoulder and collar, so subject detection has no contrast there and returns a cut edge that looks clean against white and bites visibly once the cutout lands on the card's own green band. Three files are named for the branch office rather than the person, so which face belongs to which producer cannot be settled from the filenames.

assets_supplied.name: aldervale_households.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The cleaned drop list: about sixty rows carrying household name, address lines, town, state, ZIP, assigned producer and renewal offer band.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's list, cleaned. Sixty homes in this drop."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: A dozen or so households carry a materially longer address than the rest: a second line, an apartment or unit designator, a long town name, a rural route. The card's address frame is fixed and does not spill or reflow, so those records do not push the layout, they simply stop rendering partway and lose their last line at trim while the merge reports complete success. Two offer band strings are also much longer than the rest for the same reason. Nothing in the sheet marks these rows.

assets_supplied.name: aldervale_producer_card.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of a printed agency business card lying on a desk, the mark on it in two inks on uncoated stock: an oak leaf inside a shield ring, set beside small caps type and separated by a hairline rule.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only clean version of our mark left. One of the producers still had this card in his wallet."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup photographed on a substrate, which behaves nothing like a flat scan. A prompt naming the card returns the card. A prompt naming the whole lockup returns the type and silently drops the shield ring and the hairline rule while looking entirely plausible. Background removal on the shield returns a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched, and the trace that does work arrives with no viewBox and an opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it. The two inks also run close in value along the shadowed right edge of the card.

assets_supplied.name: aldervale_brand_sheet.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: One page from the 2019 style guide: the house green and the secondary warm grey, the two type families by name, the mark's minimum clear space and the rule that the mark never sits on a photograph.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our style guide page. Please keep to it."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the template the client's own PDF produces can actually hold all of the card's fields. The mapping readout for this document omits one text run entirely while keeping its line break, so the story string it hands back still reads as well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns VALID with zero warnings on those offsets, the placeholder step returns completed successfully, and the fields past the omission are simply absent from the prepared template. Which run is omitted, and therefore which fields fall off the end, is a property of this converted document and appears in no response, warning or error. It is visible only by round tripping the prepared document and reading its story against the card.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the omission is inside the only readout the tools offer and every mapping strategy consumes that readout. Doing it right first time presumes already knowing that this document's readout drops a run, which is document specific. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a card carrying each household's own details and says nothing about how the artwork converts, and the acceptance line about every field landing is the client's requirement rather than a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different derivation of the mapping, computed from reconstructed content runs rather than from the readout.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the round tripped document's own content runs, recompute every offset against that string, rebuild the mapping, prepare again and verify field by field by inspection rather than by response, before any record is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Sixty renewal cards printed and mailed with the producer line and the offer line missing, after a run in which the validator, the preparation step and the merge all reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What this list does to this card. The address frame is fixed and does not spill or reflow, so a household whose address runs longer than last year's typical row does not push the layout or throw an error: the frame stops rendering partway and the record loses its final line at trim, postal code included, while the merge reports every record complete. Which households this happens to depends on the frame's real bounds and set size against each row's actual string, and no readout reports it. It exists only on the rendered pages, and only on some of them.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the frame cannot be resized through this surface at all; the fit is only discoverable once real rows are set in the real frame. (b) Nothing states it: the list is described as cleaned, and the acceptance line about complete address blocks is the standing requirement of any mail run rather than a warning that some will truncate. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a per record copy fit decision, which is different work from merging again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every page rather than the first, name the households that will not set, decide per record whether the address can be legitimately fitted (a combined line, a standard state abbreviation, a dropped unit prefix) or whether the record has to be flagged back to the carrier, apply those decisions to the data, merge again and re-read the affected pages.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A dozen or more cards going to the mail house with the postal line missing, which the mail house will either return or post undeliverable, in the one drop of the year that exists to keep long standing households from leaving.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the one call knockout gives back a portrait the card can use. Two things are reported nowhere except inside the returned tradeoffs object: the tool silently reduces these oversized frames and does not restore the size afterwards, so a plate can come back below what the card's portrait frame needs, and the only route back is interpolation, which the crop tool performs to a hard cap while again saying so only in its own tradeoffs. Separately, the frames shot against the cream function room wall carry almost no value difference at the shoulder and collar, so a cut edge that looks clean against white bites visibly once the plate sits on the card's green band. Which of the eleven behave this way is a property of each frame's own contrast, and neither fact appears in any success message.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it: the defensible sequence is straighten, correct, knock out at source scale and only then crop, precisely so the edge is judged after it exists, and there is no parameter that controls the reduction or reads ahead to it. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the portraits are a mixed bag, and the acceptance line about edges holding on the green is the client's standing quality requirement. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different route per frame, an explicitly selected and inverted ground filled to the house colour rather than a one call knockout.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the knockout route frame by frame, re-derive the affected plates through an explicit selection of the wall by its own material properties, inverted and filled, re-inspect each cut edge on the green rather than on white, and re-read both the reduction and the upscale entries in every tradeoffs object before any plate is bound.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Four producers appearing on their own neighbours' mail with a chewed collar and a halo against the house green, or eleven portraits brought to frame size by interpolation and printed soft at postcard scale.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a picture of an insurance postcard. IDENTITY: these are eleven real producers whose actual faces have to appear on the mail going to their own towns, and the mark has to be RECOVERED off a photographed business card rather than reinvented, because a regenerated mark is a different carrier's mark on a regulated communication. client_brief:
Festival programme production from fourteen artist submissions and two old pages

Lanternwood's programme needs one finished page per act, not fourteen different submission styles. We have the lineup sheet, fourteen artist photographs and two old printed programme pages to work from.

Please choose a defensible running order and write the rule down. The act's stage, day, time and complete biography must stay with its own photograph.

One press file whose page count equals the number of acts on the bill, one act per page, in a defended running order, each page carrying that act's own photograph, its own stage, day and set time, and its own biography ending in a finished sentence at trim. Delivered with a cover proof rendered at true print-resolution, and with the running order rule written down.

Fourteen photographs from fourteen sources brought to one booklet look (one white point, one contrast, one head size in frame), cropped to the chosen template's real portrait proportion with the face placed rather than centred and whole in every frame, named to the values the line up sheet binds by, with no output above the pixel dimensions of the frame it came from. Delivered with a per-frame parameter log naming why each frame differs from its neighbours.

Please place faces thoughtfully in the chosen picture proportion rather than applying a centre crop to everything. The biographies need to end as finished sentences at trim, not stop because a frame ran out of room.

Materials included: lanternwood_programme_2025_pages.pdf; lanternwood_programme_2023_page.pdf; lanternwood_press_photos/ (14 frames, from 14 different sources); lanternwood_banner_photo.jpg; lanternwood_lineup.csv; lanternwood_committee_note.txt.

We need the press booklet and true-resolution cover proof, with the photographs named to the same values used in the lineup. A missing or unsuitable source should be made explicit in the delivery record.

$3,000-$7,000 fixed; 2 to 4 weeks. Review structure: One direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

The final package should contain a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record, with every source file accounted for, including references and rejected or superseded material. Use the approved information without inventing missing facts. price_band_and_audience: A ticketed sixty five pounds a day roots festival with a two thousand capacity, audience broadly thirty to sixty, many of them regulars who keep the programme. The band is load-bearing. At this price the booklet is a keepsake: photographs given real room, editorial type with a proper hierarchy, generous margins, one act per page breathing rather than filled. Take it down to the free town fair register (single colour, dense, photographs shrunk to thumbnails to save a page) and the ticket buyer feels the difference immediately, as the committee already heard about the set times. Push it up into the boutique arts biennale register (near empty pages, tiny type, no set times visible at speed) and it stops working as the thing someone standing in a field uses to find the next act, which is its only functional job. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even when the merge is perfect. A posted job of this shape runs 700 to 1,800 pounds fixed.

brand_identity.typography: A keepsake editorial pairing: a warm serif for act names and headings with a clean, legible sans or serif for set times, stage and biographies. Readable at a glance in a field, generous in a programme, with a clear hierarchy so a reader finds the next act quickly.

The crest has never existed as a file: it lives only as paint on the canvas banner over the main gate, photographed for reference. Fonts and colours must be inferred from the printed pages.
brand_identity.values: The programme is the keepsake, and the crest is how regulars recognise the festival. Both should feel handmade but properly made, worthy of the wall they end up on.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_programme_2025_pages.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Two pages from last year's printed programme, held by the printer: the cover and one performer profile page, real embedded font subsets.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's programme. We like this one better, it looks more like us."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The profile page's portrait was flattened into the page by the old designer rather than placed, so the converted document exposes no graphic frame at all and there is nothing for a per performer photograph to bind to, however obviously the printed page shows a photograph. The stage line, the set time and the biography also sit inside one continuous flow, so they cannot be addressed as separate frames. None of this is visible from the printed page and the conversion reports no problem.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_programme_2023_page.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: One performer profile page from the programme two years ago, a plainer design by the same person before he changed his layout.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The older one. Less handsome, but we included it in case it helps."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: This is the page that actually works, because its portrait is a genuinely placed image and its blocks are separated, but its portrait frame is close to square and considerably smaller than the printed page suggests, while the press photographs are wide stage frames. The biography frame is also set tight to that year's shorter biographies and does not spill or reflow, so a longer biography stops rendering partway and ends mid sentence at trim while the merge reports every record complete.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_press_photos/ (14 frames, from 14 different sources)
assets_supplied.kind: One photograph per act, supplied by the acts themselves: some from a commissioned shoot, some grabbed at a gig on a phone, one saved off a band's own website.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The photographs the acts sent us. They look nothing like each other and we know it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two are stage captures under a heavy magenta wash where a global correction toward the set's neutral takes the skin green rather than neutral. Two more put the performer in a narrow lit band against a black stage, so a subject focused crop locks onto a lit stand or a monitor wedge and returns a confident looking frame that clips the face, reporting its uncertainty only as a detection confidence number and a detection box in the metadata. One arrives already sharpened and heavily saturated by somebody's phone preset, so it fights any correction applied on top of it.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_banner_photo.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of the painted canvas banner over the main gate, the crest on it in two paints on weathered cream canvas: a lantern with glazing bars inside a laurel ring, under an arched wordmark.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our crest. It has only ever existed as paint on that banner."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound painted mark on a weathered substrate. A prompt naming the banner returns the canvas. A prompt naming the whole crest returns the arched wordmark and silently drops the lantern and the laurel ring while looking entirely plausible. Background removal on the laurel ring returns a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched. The paint has also spread into the canvas weave, so the glazing bars and the gaps between the laurel leaves carry far less separation than they appear to at full frame.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_lineup.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Fourteen rows: act name, stage, day, set time, the biography the act sent in, and an image column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everyone's stage, day, time and the words they sent us."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The rows sit in the order the acts were booked, which is neither day order nor set time order, and row order is exactly what determines page order in the finished booklet. The biographies are also wildly uneven because each act wrote its own: the shortest is two sentences and three of them run to nearly double the longest of last year's.

assets_supplied.name: lanternwood_committee_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text from the committee: ticket price, the two stage names, which two acts are the headliners and must not be sequenced as though they are not, the licence line that must appear, and the printer's deadline.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything else you need to know from us."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the committee's two printed pages can actually carry this job. Both plainly show a performer photograph. What one of them exposes on conversion is no graphic frame at all, because that photograph was flattened into the page rather than placed, so there is nothing for a per act photograph to bind to, and its text was set as one continuous flow so stage, time and biography cannot be addressed separately. The other, which the committee likes less, exposes a genuinely placed image frame and separated blocks, but at a portrait proportion that has nothing to do with what the printed page suggests. Frame granularity from a converted PDF is not under anyone's control, appears in no error, and the unusable page converts exactly as cleanly as the usable one.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it: the inventory does not exist until the conversion has run, and there is no parameter that requests placed images or separated blocks. Doing it right first time would mean already knowing which of two visually similar pages hides a flattened photograph. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the committee prefers the newer page and is not precious, which is an aesthetic preference rather than a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the outcome is a different template, a different mapping strategy and a different portrait proportion for all fourteen photographs.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Convert and inspect the second candidate rather than proceeding on the preferred one, choose on structural grounds, tell the committee why the page they liked cannot carry a per act photograph, and re-derive the portrait crop specification for all fourteen frames from the chosen template's real bounds.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A fourteen page booklet in which every act's page shows the same flattened face from last year's programme, delivered after a conversion, a validation, a preparation and a merge that all reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered crest survives at the size it is actually printed. The trace looks correct at full canvas, with lantern, glazing bars, laurel ring and arched wordmark all present and separated. On the profile page the crest sits small on a cream ground, and the paint's spread into the banner's weave means the glazing bars and the gaps between the laurel leaves carry far less separation than they appear to at full frame, so at reproduction size the counters close and the mark reads as a dark blob with a ring around it. The tracing tool takes no options at all, so nothing can be tuned after the fact, and no readout reports path density against reproduction size. It exists only once the page is rendered at print resolution and looked at at true size on the real ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it: all tuning has to happen in the raster preparation before the trace, and whether this particular painted mark on this particular weave holds at this particular size cannot be known before both the trace and the page exist. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for the crest on every page and big on the boards, which is a placement wish rather than a warning about small reproduction. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different upstream chain, a re-selected and re-cropped raster or a deliberately simplified single weight variant for small use.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster preparation, re-select the paint at a tighter crop and cleaner polarity, re-trace, and judge at printed size on the cream ground rather than at full canvas; where it still closes, produce a distinct small use variant and state which variant is for which size. The boards are then re-authored around whichever crest is now correct.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen keepsake pages and two stage boards carrying a crest that is a dark blob at page size, on a festival whose crest has only ever existed as paint and is the thing regulars recognise it by.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the constructions the day boards are built on. A stage entrance board is a schedule read at distance, and the natural authoring of that is a multi column running order with the crest lifted off a photographic band. The importer silently discards multi column text and reflows it into a single column, and it discards the effects that separate a mark from a photograph behind it, all at full success with no warning of any kind. The document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so the second board cannot be checked that way at all, and the returned per root markup is the only channel that reports what survived. Whether the board still reads as a schedule at twenty paces exists only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for boards the committee can edit and that read at a stage entrance, which is a functional wish. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a structurally different authoring of the same board, explicitly laid out sibling containers rather than a flowed one, and a crest separated from its band by a solid panel rather than by an effect.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Audit the returned markup for both roots rather than looking at the first board, re-author the schedule as explicitly positioned sibling blocks, re-seat the crest on a construct that survives, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export and audit both roots again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Two stage entrance boards delivered as an editable file in which the running order has collapsed into one column and the crest has disappeared into the photograph, on the one deliverable nobody can check by opening the first page.

client_brief:
Technical sheets and bin labels from two separate legacy PDFs

Production request: Girdermark Components

Active range: sixteen parts
Document A: US Letter data sheet
Document B: 100 x 62 mm bin label

We need both production documents recovered from their separate legacy PDFs. Please do not assume they can be converted or merged in the same way.

The data-sheet library
US Letter portrait, one page per active part in roster order, page count equal to the current part count, rendered at 300 ppi at trim. Every page binds every spec parameter, the ordering code, both prices and the unpacked attribute values verbatim from the stock export and paired with the parameter each belongs to, plus that part's own photograph in the photograph's frame. Accompanied by one single-page file per part named to the part number and identity-verified by opening it. Produced by reverse-engineering the printer's flat PDF into a live merge template, which is handed back with the record of how it was derived.

The label run
100 x 62 mm trim, one label per active part, rendered at 300 ppi, each carrying the recovered mark at a cut proved to hold at that size on the label ground, the part number, the composed description reaching its end rather than stopping at a frame edge, the ordering code and the small part picture. Produced from a second, independent reverse-engineering of the label house's flat PDF, handed back as a live template with its own derivation record and an explicit statement that no bleed can be introduced into it.

The prepared component images
Sixteen in-house frames shot across two different bench mats brought to one neutral with one white point and one black point, delivered as a sheet picture and a label picture per part at consistent subject scale, plus one licensed context frame graded into the same neutral. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Each unpacked attribute belongs with a specific parameter. The ordering code, both prices and the complete descriptions must remain accurate through the merge. Please state the label template's lack of bleed plainly rather than calling it a capability it does not have.

We provide sheet_2026_PRESS.pdf; label_2026_PRESS.pdf; range_export.csv; nameplate/ (4 frames, 4200 x 2800); bench_photos/ (16 frames, 4800 x 3200).

The printer's combined files and the part-numbered individual files must agree. Include the independent derivation record for each reusable template and the mark's small-label proof.

Alongside the finished work, we need a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record. Keep a clear record of the supplied files used, retained for reference, superseded and rejected. Approved source information remains authoritative. Record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and quality limits, and do not use an undeclared replacement or invented fact to conceal a source problem.

The commission is budgeted at $6,000-$12,000 fixed. We have allowed 4 to 6 weeks, including direction approval, first-production proof, and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

price_band_and_audience: Components from 400 dollars (relay sockets, restrictor brackets, contactor blocks) to 9,000 dollars (governor sheave assemblies, door operator arm assemblies). The buyer is 35 to 60, a working service technician, a building maintenance supervisor or an electrical contractor who judges a supplier by whether the photograph and the spec table agree. The band is load-bearing in both directions. At this tier the sheet is flat, even and technical: one neutral ground, the whole part in frame, generous spec setting, prices plain in the run of the page, no atmosphere. Push it toward bright consumer-tool photography with warm light and shallow depth and the buyer reads a 15 dollar hardware brand and stops trusting the load ratings printed beside it. Push it the other way into dark cinematic hero work and it reads as marketing rather than a parts catalogue. The bin label answers to a different reader again: a picker at arm's length under warehouse light, so it is bigger, blunter and carries less. A posted job of this shape runs 2,200 to 4,000 dollars fixed, or 45 to 75 dollars an hour across 40 to 60 hours.

assets_supplied.name: sheet_2026_PRESS.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF of the current per-part data sheet, US Letter portrait, one part per page, fonts embedded, produced through a full print engine so it converts cleanly. Carries a header block with the house mark, a two-column spec table, a part photograph, a certification strip and an ordering-code panel.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer sends back to us each season. We have never had the working file. Keep it exactly as it is."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed page sets the spec table as rows reading across two columns, but the file's own content order runs all the way down the left visual column and then all the way down the right, and the ordering-code panel that reads as a separate box belongs to the same continuous story, so the order a human reads off the printed page and the order the story actually holds do not agree at any point past the first row. The two graphic frames, the part photograph and the certification strip, are separable only by their bounds and their existing link, and neither is named for what it holds.

assets_supplied.name: label_2026_PRESS.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The label house's flat press PDF of the bin label, 100 x 62 mm, one label per page, fonts embedded. Carries the house mark, the part number set large, a description line, the ordering code and a small part picture.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The label house designed this for us. It is what the pickers know. Same instruction: keep it, just put this season through it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The description sits in a fixed-measure frame sized to last season's longest string. It does not spill, it does not warn and it does not report anything: it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, so a longer record is cut off mid-word on a label that otherwise renders perfectly at trim. Separately, the die outline is a placed graphic rather than a document bleed, so nothing in the file carries real bleed and none can be introduced into it.

assets_supplied.name: range_export.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the components stock system, one row per active part, with part number, description, spec parameters, ordering code, list and dealer price, a finish column and an image column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Straight out of the system. Those values are ours and they are what the customer holds us to."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The spec columns sit in the stock system's own order, which is not the order the printed sheet prints them in, and three values the sheet carries (certification code, seismic rating, superseded-by code) are not columns at all but are packed into one semicolon-delimited attributes blob. Finishes are internal two-letter codes rather than names, the image column holds full local paths without the prefix the merge's own image contract requires, and two of the rows are revision variants of one part number that the system still emits side by side.

assets_supplied.name: nameplate/ (4 frames, 4200 x 2800)
assets_supplied.kind: Phone and camera frames of the cast aluminium nameplate riveted to the traction machine in the back of the warehouse, shot at different angles under a shop droplight.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place the mark still physically exists apart from the printed sheet. Shot it four ways because I did not know what you would need."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark is raised casting in the same aluminium as the plate, so it reads by shadow rather than by colour and a selection that names the plate returns the plate. Its keyline is a hairline rule and its letterforms carry tight enclosed counters, and a trace that looks immaculate at the size it is traced at does not necessarily hold at the size the mark is actually reproduced at on a bin label, on the amber label stock, once the render comes back at trim.

assets_supplied.name: bench_photos/ (16 frames, 4800 x 3200)
assets_supplied.kind: In-house part photography of the sixteen active components, shot on the bench in the back of the warehouse across several months under shop fluorescents.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Same bench, same camera, different days. The backgrounds do not match and neither does the light."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The bench mat was replaced part way through the shoot, so eight frames sit on a mid grey and eight on a near black, which shifted both the exposure the camera chose and the apparent value of every plated part, in the same direction on every affected frame. Four of the components (the sheave, the restrictor bracket, the cable clamp and the operator arm) enclose through-bores and open frames that a one-call knockout fills with captured mat while reporting complete success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's sheet actually is once it stops being a printed page. The page presents a tidy two-column spec table whose rows plainly read across, plus an ordering-code panel that plainly sits in its own box. What the conversion exposes is a continuous story that runs the whole left visual column and then the whole right one, with the ordering-code panel inside the same story, so from the second row onward the order a person reads off the printed page and the order the document actually holds diverge and never re-converge. Granularity is not a parameter, is not reported before the conversion and has no read-ahead: the only route to the answer is to convert, export and read the runs. A mapping authored against the printed page's reading order validates cleanly, prepares successfully and produces pages that are perfectly typeset with every value present and every value attached to the wrong parameter label.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering and no amount of care changes what the conversion returns, and the page gives no signal at all: it looks like the most ordinary two-column table in the world. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says keep the sheet exactly as it is and put this season's parts through it, and mentions no frames, stories or orders; the acceptance bar states the client's standing requirement that a value be paired with the parameter it belongs to, which is what any client would ask for. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the mapping strategy itself changes: from per-block field mapping to ordered offsets inside one interleaved story, with the ordering-code panel folded in and same-frame rows re-sequenced.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping against the reconstructed story rather than the printed page, re-sequence the rows sharing that frame so their positions hold against the untouched text, re-validate, re-prepare, and confirm the placeholders by round-tripping the template before any page is merged. Then settle which of the two graphic frames is the photograph well by rendering one page and reading it against the printed reference, rather than assuming the larger frame is the photograph.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Sixteen data sheets on a dealer portal on which the bore diameter is printed against the duty rating, the seismic rating against the certification code, and so on down every page, all correctly typeset, all bound verbatim from the client's own export, sold to technicians who order to those exact values from a supplier whose entire pitch is that the picture and the numbers agree.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives its real reproduction size. Traced off the nameplate it is immaculate: the keyline is crisp, the counters are open, it sits cleanly on white at the size it was traced at, and it looks right in the sheet header. On the bin label it prints about fourteen millimetres wide on amber stock, and only when the label comes back rendered at true trim does it become visible that the hairline keyline has thinned to nothing in places and the tight counters have filled in, so the mark reads as a dark lozenge at picking distance. Nothing measured this, nothing warned, and every prior artefact was genuinely correct at the size it was made at. Which parts of the mark close, and at what point, are properties of this particular casting under this particular droplight and cannot be predicted from the frames or from the trace.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it. The trace can only be judged at its reproduction size on its real ground, which does not exist until a template has been built and a label rendered at trim, and up to that moment every check the agent can run passes. Tracing more carefully does not help, because the failure is a reduction failure rather than a tracing failure. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the mark goes on every sheet and every label and asks for it back as real artwork; it asks no question about size, sets no minimum, and names no risk. No earlier step claims the mark was verified small, because no earlier step had anything to look at. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a new piece of artwork. A second cut of the mark has to be derived for small reproduction, which means re-taking the trace from a different route or re-authoring the keyline as drawn vector rather than traced ink, and then deciding whether the sheet and the label may legitimately carry different cuts of one mark at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Go back to the imaging surface and derive a small-size cut: re-select the lettering with a different prompt on a different nameplate frame, or produce the plate as a filled colour version rather than a two-value trace, and rebuild the keyline as authored vector at a weight that holds. Re-repair the SVG (viewBox and background path) for the new cut, decide and document which cut is used where, re-bind it into the label template and re-render at trim to look again. The portal mark sheet then has to carry both cuts and say where each is used, which is a change to a deliverable that was already authored.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Every bin label on a brand new mezzanine racking system carrying a dark blob where the company mark should be, printed once for the whole active range, discovered by the operations manager at arm's length in warehouse light on the day the racking is signed off.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which records the bin label physically cannot hold. The description frame is a fixed measure sized to last season's longest string, and it neither spills nor reports: it stops rendering at the frame edge. The merge reports success, the render reports success, the placeholder verification passed, and the label comes back looking completely normal, with a description that simply ends. Which records are affected depends on the description field the agent itself composed in the data-preparation step out of the export's description, its expanded finish name and its revision marker, so it cannot be read off the roster in advance and it is different for a different composition decision. At proof scale on screen a truncated line and a short line are indistinguishable; the only way to know is to read every rendered label at trim against the roster row it came from.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and neither can care: the overflow is a silent geometric fact of a frame the agent did not draw and cannot redraw, and no tool in the chain surfaces overset. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says nothing is reworded or shortened to fit and that anything that will not fit must be escalated before it prints, which is the client's standing instruction rather than a warning, and no asset description names a frame width or a longest string. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a composition decision taken again for the whole roster: what the description field is made of, whether the finish name and revision marker belong on the label at all, whether the policy changes for every part or only the offenders (which would leave the rack inconsistent), and what has to be escalated because the client has forbidden shortening. The sheet run carries the same composed field, so changing it changes both runs.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-compose the label description field across the whole roster, re-merge and re-render both runs because the sheet carries the same field, then re-read every label at trim rather than assuming the second pass took. Where a description still cannot fit without shortening, escalate it in writing with the exact records named and an alternative offered (a shorter house description supplied by the client, or that part running a second line), rather than trimming it quietly.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Bin labels going onto the racking with descriptions cut off mid-word on the longest and most easily confused parts, on a rack where the description is what the picker reads, from a client who asked in writing to be told before it printed.

client_brief:
Nineteen cosmetic labels with exact ingredient copy and per-shade imagery

SEVE Botanicals needs a launch-label run across two price tiers. We have one physical sample photographed on a phone, nineteen drawdown images and a printer's flat PDF. The imagery needs careful preparation; the compliance copy is not open for creative rewriting.

Label production: One label per current SKU at true label trim, one record per page, page count equal to the reconciled SKU count, rendered at 300 ppi with a proof label per tier for regulatory sign-off. Every label binds shade name, the complete compliance ingredient line in its written order with the may-contain clause set as the reference sets it, net weight, the batch field and both per-row images (the packshot and that SKU's own swatch chip) in their own frames. Accompanied by one named single file per SKU, identity-verified by opening it, and by the live merge template reverse-engineered from the printer's flat PDF with its derivation record and an explicit statement that no bleed can be introduced into it.

Photographic preparation: The chosen sample frames and all nineteen drawdown frames brought to one light with one white point, delivered as the hero and secondary packshot plus nineteen swatch chips derived under one stated policy, with one licensed context frame graded to match. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log, the swatch-derivation policy written down, and every crop's reported detection and tradeoff metadata transcribed.

Each row has two image bindings: the packshot and that SKU's own swatch chip. Please check both, including the longest ingredient line and the may-contain clause. Set a clear swatch-derivation policy rather than correcting each chip until it simply looks attractive.

Files supplied: sample_packshots/ (11 frames, 4032 x 3024); drawdowns/ (19 frames, 4032 x 3024); serum_label_PRESS.pdf; launch_roster.csv; carton_foil.jpg (3600 x 2700).

The proof per tier is for regulatory sign-off, not a claim that the designer has approved the product. Hand back the reusable template with its derivation and the explicit no-bleed limitation.

Budget: $1,400-$3,800 fixed. Target: 7 to 15 business days. Reviews: One technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.
