emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the two palest Atelier shades can be told apart at all. They were drawn thin and caught direct window light, so their swatch areas are clipped with nothing left in them, and the honest signal is the strangest one available: a highlight recovery accepts its parameters, returns success and moves nothing whatsoever. The picture that comes back is byte-for-byte as pale as the one that went in. Which shades behave this way is a property of these particular cards under that particular afternoon's light and cannot be read off the roster, off the shade names or off a single card previewed on its own, because on its own each of the two looks like a plausible pale shade. It only becomes a problem when all nineteen chips are laid out together and two SKUs are visibly sharing one near-white square.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot either: the tool succeeds, the parameters are accepted, no warning is emitted, and the only tell is a nil result that an agent reading a success line will not notice. (b) Nothing states it. The client says two of the Atelier shades are very close to each other, which is a fact about the products and a reason for care, not a statement that two photographs are clipped and unrecoverable; nothing in the brief, the roster or the asset descriptions mentions exposure, clipping or which cards are affected. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to change where the swatch comes from, which is a different operation on a different region of the card, and then to re-take the derivation policy across all nineteen, because two chips pulled from the heavy end of a draw will not sit with seventeen pulled from the middle unless the policy is re-decided for the whole set.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon recovery on the affected cards and re-derive their chips from a denser part of the draw, then re-derive the other seventeen under the same revised policy so the set stays internally honest, and re-lay all nineteen together to judge again. Where the two shades still cannot be distinguished at chip size, escalate it to the founder in writing with both chips shown, because a shade card that implies two SKUs are the same colour is a commercial problem the client has to decide on rather than a problem the agent may quietly resolve by pushing one of them.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A counter shade card and two labels on which two separately formulated, separately priced Atelier shades appear as the same near-white square, printed for a launch, in front of the exact buyer who is paying 85 dollars to be able to tell them apart.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the label printer's file actually yields, and then whether the mapping built against it landed. Two things arrive only by running. First, the granularity: the ingredient paragraph, the net weight and the batch line all live in one continuous story with no separate frames, so everything must be driven by ordered offsets inside a single story, and the packshot well and the swatch chip are distinguishable only by bounds and link. Second, the yield: the readout of that story omits the run holding the net weight while keeping its line break, so the string still parses as well-formed and every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on arithmetic that is internally consistent and wrong, the placeholder step reports success, and the net weight and the batch field never become placeholders at all.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and diligence alone cannot either. Granularity is not a parameter, is not reported before the conversion and has no read-ahead. The yield failure is worse: it is produced by a convenience readout that presents as complete, so an agent that reads carefully and computes offsets diligently from the readout it was handed produces arithmetic every downstream tool agrees with. The only defence is an independent reconstruction of the same text from a different channel, which nothing prompts and whose necessity is invisible until the two disagree. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says work from last season's label and that nothing may be reworded or dropped, and the acceptance bar states the client's standing requirement that net weight and batch appear on every label, which is a regulatory fact rather than a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the source of truth behind the mapping changes, from a tool readout to a reconstructed story, and the whole mapping is re-authored with re-ordered same-frame rows and re-computed positions.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story by concatenating the document's content runs, recompute every offset against that string, re-order the rows sharing that frame so their positions hold against the original text, rebuild and re-validate the mapping, re-run the template preparation, and re-verify by round-tripping the template and grepping for every placeholder before a single label is merged. Settle which of the two graphic frames is the swatch chip by rendering one label and reading it against the printed reference rather than by assuming the larger frame is the packshot.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Nineteen product labels bound correctly for shade name and ingredient line while the net weight and the batch field are silently absent from every one of them, sent to a label printer for a retail launch, with every tool in the chain having reported success and a regulatory proof that looks finished.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the bottle cutout is actually clean. Along the left shoulder of the frosted body and across the top arc of the gold collar, the subject sits at the same value as the marble it was shot on, so the knockout reports success and returns something that looks immaculate on white and immaculate against a transparency checker, having quietly bitten away the shoulder edge and the top of the collar. Which parts fail is a property of this one bottle on this one kitchen counter at that hour and cannot be predicted from the frame preview, from the tool's response, or from any check performed against a light ground. The loss only becomes visible when the cutout is finally placed on the deep Atelier label ground, which does not happen until the merge template exists and a label has been rendered at trim.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it. The check that would reveal it (looking at the cutout on a dark ground at real size) is exactly the thing that does not exist until the layout surface has been built, and every check available before then, including the tool's own output preview, is performed against a ground that hides it. Choosing a better frame does not help either, because the frames that show the collar best are the frames where the shoulder disappears into the marble. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for the bottle to sit on the label ground rather than on a kitchen counter, which is an ordinary client requirement, and mentions no edge, no value match and no risk. No earlier step claims the cutout was verified, because no earlier step had the ground to verify it against. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different isolation strategy: routing the frosted body and the polished collar separately, selecting by material rather than by subject, and possibly moving to a different source frame entirely, which changes the hero photograph the whole launch is built on and therefore the light every other picture was matched to.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-isolate the bottle with the body and the collar routed separately, selecting each by naming its own material rather than asking for the subject, inverting and filling to the label ground so the edge is decided by the selection rather than by a detector. If no route holds the collar on the chosen frame, move to the secondary frame and re-run the light correction so the new hero still matches the swatch chips, then re-bind and re-render a label to look at it on the dark ground again rather than assuming the second attempt took.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An 85 dollar counter serum whose label carries a photograph of its own bottle with a slice missing from the shoulder and the top of the gold collar shaved off, printed across the entire Atelier tier, on the one product where the buyer is paying for exactly that kind of care.

decision_gates: The surface split: nineteen labels to the merge surface because the layout is fixed client property and the run is record per page, shade card and system page to HTML authoring because they must stay editable.

Whether the mark is selected by naming the carton or by naming the foil, where naming the substrate returns the carton and every downstream step accepts it.

client_one_liner: Every December we thank everyone who gave and send them the receipt they need for their taxes, it is done by hand one document at a time, it took our office manager three weeks last year, and two donors were missed entirely.
client_brief:
Replace our manual year-end donor letters with a dependable reusable system

Rivermeadow Trust's office manager spent three weeks preparing acknowledgements last year, and two donors were still missed. We need this December's letters and receipts produced correctly, plus templates the office can reuse next year by changing the data.

There are three output streams. They must reconcile to the delivered household records, not blindly to every line of the raw export.

The current-year run
Three press PDFs, community letters, leadership letters and receipts, one delivered record per page in data order, page count reconciling to the delivered record set rather than to the raw export. Every promised field present on every page, money formatted consistently, giving level agreeing with total and threshold, and nothing truncated at trim. Delivered alongside the per donor single page files named to the roster, one letter and one receipt per household, produced through the route whose record identity is guaranteed.

The retained working templates
Three working merge documents reverse engineered from the supplied press files, each carrying live placeholders for its own fields, each built on the strategy its own converted structure permits rather than on one assumed strategy, and each read back to prove what it contains. These are the half the trust keeps: next December they change the data, not the design.

The preserve photographs
The usable volunteer frames straightened, brought to one target with a per-frame parameter log, and cropped to the letter's photo frame without any output exceeding its source pixel dimensions, one picture per preserve with none standing in for two, plus one licensed camera-scale valley frame graded into the same world. Frames that cannot honestly fill their place are named and excluded rather than enlarged.

Please check that giving level agrees with totals and thresholds, and that each household gets one letter and one receipt. One preserve's picture must not stand in for another's.

Our pack: rivermeadow_giving_2026.csv (18 rows); rivermeadow_letter_community.pdf; rivermeadow_letter_leadership.pdf; rivermeadow_receipt.pdf; rivermeadow_plaque_fennhollow.jpg; rivermeadow_volunteer_photos/ (9 frames); rivermeadow_copy.txt.

Include an inventory showing how every supplied file was used or why it was set aside. Keep factual content tied to the approved inputs. The rebuild is anchored instead to the standing posted archetype this entry was carved from, which recurs on Upwork and Freelancer in near identical wording every autumn: a small nonprofit with an existing printed letter and receipt, a giving export out of its donor database, and a request for a designer who can set up a personalised year end acknowledgement run in InDesign, deliver print ready files plus a separate file per donor for emailing, and hand back something the office can run itself the following year. The nearest quoted sibling in this same batch is the Upwork brief anchoring LAYOUT-30, which asks for 'Proficiency in Adobe InDesign', a 'Strong sense of typography, layout, and print design', print ready files and editable source, and it is cited here only for the shape of the deliverable list, not for its content. The verdict on this entry is REBUILD because the prior draft sat almost entirely on one surface, the merge, with the mark and the stewardship page bolted on as prose. This build re carves it as the commission the archetype client actually needs: the identity is RECOVERED off a photographed bronze plaque rather than assumed to exist, two genuinely different printed letters are reverse engineered into two live templates whose internal structure is not under the agent's control, and the one page the trust wanted for the annual meeting is authored as a native editable document instead of promised as a PDF the connector cannot produce. Client, persons and place names are coined and Western. No real charity, person or trademark is named.

price_band_and_audience: A small accredited land trust with a genuinely split base: gifts from 25 dollars to 25,000 dollars, median 85, roughly two thirds of the money arriving from under a tenth of the households. Donors are 45 to 78, local, land literate, and many are easement grantors who know the fields in the photographs by name. The band is load bearing in an unusual way here, because BOTH ends of it ship in the same run. The community register is warm, photographed, generously set, and it may read as produced, because a 60 dollar donor who receives a hand set personal note reads it as money spent on them rather than on land. The leadership register at four and five figures must read restrained and personal: no photograph, quiet rules, a signature that sits like a signature, wide margins, the gift figure set without emphasis. Ship the leadership register at community warmth and a 15,000 dollar donor feels processed. Ship the community register at leadership austerity and an 85 dollar donor feels held at arm's length by a charity that is supposed to be their neighbour. An agent that finds one house look and applies it to both has misread the commission even if every field lands correctly. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Land held in common, kept for good
brand_identity.sector: A small accredited land trust that holds conservation easements and stewards preserves in one Connecticut valley, funded by a few hundred local giving households.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1994, based in the Sedgewater valley, Litchfield County, Connecticut. Four staff, roughly nine hundred acres under easement, a few hundred giving households.
brand_identity.about: Rivermeadow protects the meadows, hollows and river bends of one valley by holding easements and caring for a handful of small preserves. Many of our donors granted the land we now steward, so the relationship is personal and long. We exist so the fields stay fields for the people who walk them.
brand_identity.audience: Local giving households aged 45 to 78, land literate, many of them easement grantors who know the fields by name. Gifts run from 25 dollars to 25,000, a broad community base plus a small leadership circle that carries most of the campaign.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A community land trust, not a national charity. Two registers live in one base: a warm community of small and mid gifts, and a leadership circle giving four and five figures. Every dollar should read as spent on the land, not on ourselves.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet transitional serif for headings and running text, set generously with wide margins, paired with a restrained humanist sans for labels and figures. Type should feel like a well kept letter, never like a campaign.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, grateful and specific, the voice of a neighbour rather than an institution. It names the field, not the fund. Example: We kept forty more acres in hay this year because you asked us to.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original logo files left with our first designer and are gone. The mark now survives only on the cast bronze donor plaque at the Fenn Hollow trailhead, of which we hold one photograph. Approved letter copy, giving level names and thresholds, and the statutory receipt wording still exist as plain text.
brand_identity.values: Permanence of the land, and a personal duty of thanks to every household that gives, whatever the size of the gift.

assets_supplied.name: rivermeadow_giving_2026.csv (18 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: The year to date giving export straight out of the donor database, one row per constituent record, with name, salutation, address, year total, gift count, and a giving level column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is what the database gives us. It has everything on it, we think."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two rows are one household entered twice, because a joint gift was split across both spouses at data entry, and only the identical mailing address reveals it, so the row count is not the household count and the page count gate moves with it. The giving level column is empty on the records whose December gift pushed them across a threshold after the field was last written, the year totals are raw unformatted numbers with inconsistent decimal places, and the salutation column is blank on every household record.

assets_supplied.name: rivermeadow_letter_community.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's press file for last year's community letter, one page, photographed, carrying a placed preserve picture and the trust mark as printed artwork.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The warm one. Most of our donors get this."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Because it carries placed images it converts into several text frames plus real graphic frames, which is workable, but the readout of one frame's story text silently omits a styled run, so every character offset computed past that point is short by exactly that run's length while the validator still reports the mapping VALID and the placeholder step still reports completed successfully. The mappings that land are the early ones and the ones that vanish leave no trace anywhere in any tool response.

assets_supplied.name: rivermeadow_letter_leadership.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's press file for last year's leadership letter, one page, cream stock, typographic, no photograph anywhere on it.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The quiet one. Our biggest supporters get this."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It looks on the printed page like a salutation block, a body, a gift acknowledgement line and a signature block set as four separate elements, but with no images anywhere in the file the whole page converts to exactly ONE continuous text frame and ZERO graphic frames, so the per frame mapping strategy that works on its sibling is not available on it at all and there is nowhere to bind the recovered mark as a graphic.

assets_supplied.name: rivermeadow_receipt.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's press file for the statutory gift receipt, identical for every donor, carrying the trust's registration line and the acknowledgement wording the trust cannot alter.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Same for everyone. The legal line on it is not ours to change."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Its name and address block is a fixed measure frame, so an overset line does not spill, does not warn and does not error: it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, which at trim truncates the longest household names mid word while the page count stays exactly right and every tool in the chain reports success.

assets_supplied.name: rivermeadow_plaque_fennhollow.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the cast bronze donor plaque at the Fenn Hollow trailhead, the mark raised in relief: a heron over a river bend, enclosed in a ring of small caps type broken by a hairline rule.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place our mark still exists. The original file went with our first designer."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup in relief on a photographed metal substrate, so a prompt naming the plaque returns the plaque rather than the mark, a prompt naming the whole emblem returns the type ring and silently drops the heron and the hairline rule while looking entirely complete, and background removal on the ring returns a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched. The raised bronze and its green patina also run close in value along the weathered left third of the casting.

assets_supplied.name: rivermeadow_volunteer_photos/ (9 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Volunteer snapshots of the four preserves taken across the year, intended one per region so each donor sees the land nearest to them.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our stewardship volunteers took these. There should be one for each preserve."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three are phone captures far below the pixel scale the letter's photo frame needs at print resolution, and no filename or column says so, so they can only be brought to the frame by interpolation. Two others are the same footbridge from slightly different angles, which leaves one of the four preserves with no frame of its own at all, and one frame sits noticeably off level.

assets_supplied.name: rivermeadow_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the approved letter copy in both registers, the giving level names and their thresholds, the executive director's sign off line, and the statutory receipt wording.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The wording as the board approved it. The receipt paragraph is fixed."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the mapping that validated and prepared successfully actually wrote every placeholder into the template. The readout of the community letter's story omits one styled run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every character offset computed past that point is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid with zero warnings on those offsets and the placeholder step reports completed successfully, so the early mappings land and the later ones vanish leaving no trace in any tool response. Whether this document has a droppable run at all, and where in the story it sits, is a property of how this particular PDF was produced and cannot be known before conversion.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the omission happens inside the readout the mapping must be built from. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for each donor's own name, salutation, total and level, which is a goal, and the acceptance line about every promised field appearing is the client's standing requirement rather than a disclosure that a readout is lossy. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is to rebuild offsets against a different source of truth, the document's own reconstructed story text, and then re prepare and read back again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the document itself, recompute every offset from that string, rebuild the mapping, prepare the template again, read the placeholders back a second time, and apply the same discipline to the two templates not yet built.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A run that assembles cleanly with the right page count in which the gift figure and the giving level are simply missing from every community letter, discovered by the client rather than the agent, on the one mailing of the year that asks people for money.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every donor's name and address survives onto the page. The receipt's name and address block is a fixed measure frame, so an overset line does not spill into another frame, does not warn and does not error. It stops rendering at the frame edge, which truncates the longest household salutations mid word at trim while the page count stays exactly right and every response in the chain reports success. Which records overflow depends on the frame's real measure and on the salutations written into the data in step 3, so it exists only once the data and the converted frame meet on a rendered page.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) It cannot be ordered around, because it only exists after data meets template, and it cannot be prevented by doing it right the first time without knowing a measure the document does not report until rendered. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the receipt is the same for everyone and its wording is fixed. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a decision about the DATA, shortening or restructuring the household salutation for the affected records, or moving the field to a frame that can carry it, followed by a re merge.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify every record whose block overflows, decide a salutation rule that holds for the longest households without making the shortest ones read oddly, rewrite those rows, re merge the receipt run, and read the affected pages at trim again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Tax receipts going out with a household's name cut off mid word, which for a receipt is not only an embarrassment but a document a donor cannot use, on the exact deliverable whose wording the trust is not permitted to alter.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark still reads as the trust's mark where it actually reproduces. The trace is judged at canvas size, where it looks clean, but on the letterhead it prints small on cream, and a trace taken off raised bronze carries the weight of the relief edge rather than the weight of the original drawing. At true reproduction size the hairline rule can disappear into the ring and the counters inside the small caps can close up into solid marks, and on cream rather than on white the whole lockup can go heavy. None of that is visible at any stage before a page is rendered at print resolution and looked at at trim.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering shows it earlier, because the mark's reproduction size only exists once it sits in the template on a rendered page, and the tracing tool takes no options at all so there is no parameter that could have prevented it. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for the mark back as artwork we can use, which is a goal. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different recovery route, a differently prepared raster before the trace or the colour accurate plate instead of the two colour trace, or a decision to carry the mark larger and set the ring separately.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re prepare the plaque selection and retrace, or switch to the colour accurate plate, re derive the placement raster, rebind it into the templates, re merge and re render, then judge it again at trim on cream rather than at full canvas.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An acknowledgement run going to the trust's entire giving base with a logo that is legible on the designer's screen and a dark blot on the paper, on the one piece of print the organisation is judged by.

Whether eighteen rows are eighteen households, and how to say so in the handover when they are not.
How to derive a giving level for the records whose level column is silent, and how to state the rule so next December's run reproduces it.
How money should be formatted so it reads the same on a twenty five dollar receipt and a twenty five thousand dollar one.

Selection wording on the plaque: naming the casting takes the bronze, naming the relief's own visual properties takes the mark, and background removal on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which mark variant carries the letterhead, judged at reproduction size on cream rather than at full canvas.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a picture of a charity letter. IDENTITY: these are this trust's real donors with their real gift totals and their real giving levels, printed on this trust's own approved copy and statutory receipt wording, under a mark that must be RECOVERED off a bronze casting rather than reinvented, because a regenerated heron is a different organisation's logo. client_brief:
Two reusable menu templates for fourteen locations, not fourteen manual edits

Our managers have been retyping the same Emberwell insert in a word processor. That led to a customer finding a different flat-white price twenty minutes down the road. We need two controlled templates that take their local details and prices from the data.

The two operating groups are:
- Ten kitchen rooms: the plates-tier insert with a featured-dish image.
- Four kitchenless rooms: the counter card, with no photograph.

price_band_and_audience: Upper middle independent: plates 14 to 26 dollars, drinks 4.50 to 7, guest 30 to 55, morning trade that lingers, in secondary New England towns where this is the good room rather than the cheap one. The band is load bearing on this task specifically because the whole estate runs through one template, so the register is set once and either fits or does not. At this band the insert is type led and generous, the dish photograph is a single silhouetted plate given air rather than a grid of tiles, prices sit small and quiet at the end of a line, and there are no combos, no starbursts and no value language anywhere. An agent that finds a look before it reads the price sheet will land on one of the two extremes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,100 to 2,400 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2013, first room in Portsmouth, New Hampshire. Fourteen rooms across New England, two flagship kitchens, four counter service rooms, one shared coffee program.
brand_identity.about: Emberwell runs fourteen rooms under one name and one coffee program, each in a secondary New England town where it is the good room rather than the cheap one. Same room, same welcome, but every store pays its own rent, so the estate is one brand at fourteen prices.
brand_identity.audience: Morning trade aged 30 to 55 that comes in early and lingers for two hours. Guests who read a menu the way they read a good book and treat loud pricing as a sign they are in the wrong kind of room.

brand_identity.typography: A warm high contrast serif for dish names and headings, generously leaded, paired with a quiet humanist sans for descriptions and prices. Between the rustic chalkboard cliche and the cold Swiss default: elevated, never shouting.
brand_identity.voice: Warm and plainspoken, a room talking rather than a brand selling. Short lines, no adjectives stacked for effect. Example: The stout is on until the barrel is done, then it is not.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the licensed frames actually look like. Selection happens against a small catalogue thumbnail, and the frame's real colour, its real white balance and everything living at the edges of it exist only once the full resolution file has been licensed and pulled down. Two frames that were indistinguishable at thumbnail scale can sit a long way apart from a set shot on one walnut counter in one window's light, and one of them can carry a cast, a competing surface or a second dish at its edge that the thumbnail simply did not resolve. Whether the chosen frame can be brought to the house target at all, rather than merely adjusted toward it, is only answerable with the downloaded file placed beside the graded house frames.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because there is no higher resolution view before licensing and no metadata field that reports colour or content at the edges. Licensing first and looking after IS the correct order, which is exactly what makes the finding arrive after a commitment. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that two seasonal items were never photographed. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is either a different licensed frame chosen on different grounds, or a masked correction route the house frames never needed, and both change what the graded set contains.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Put the downloaded frames beside the graded house set, judge them there rather than in isolation, and either license an alternative and grade it from scratch or build a confined correction for the bought frame alone, then re judge the whole set as a set.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Two of fourteen stores printing a featured dish that visibly comes from somebody else's kitchen, on an insert whose entire claim is that this is an independent room and not a chain.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the two template estate run actually assembles into once both tiers are merged and combined. Three things surface only here. The counter rooms come back correctly ordered within their own four page run and the kitchen rooms within theirs, so a combine that stacks the tiers passes page count and uniqueness while sitting the four counter rooms at the back instead of at roster positions nine to twelve. The directory join, done on a store name the raw sheet spells with trailing spaces, silently produced empty address and hours for the unreconciled rooms, and an empty joined field merges as a blank footer with no error, exactly as an unavailable price merges as a blank line. And the footer and on now frames, inherited at the size of one short sample store, overset on the rooms whose address or feature runs long, pushing the tail out of the frame where the merge reports success and only the document's overset state or the trim render shows it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because each merge can only order its own subset, an empty joined value is indistinguishable from any other empty field to the merge, and overset is a property of a fixed frame meeting a variable length string that exists only once real records flow through it. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for one file for the estate and for each room's own address and hours, not for how a two template run concatenates or how long a given room's address is. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a re interleave of the combined run to roster order, a re clean of the join keys so the missing footers fill, and a frame that auto sizes or a value shortened in the data, all different operations from running the same merge again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re interleave the two tier runs to true roster order, clean the join keys and re join so no room merges with a blank footer, auto size or enlarge the footer and feature frames or shorten the offending values in the data, then re merge, re combine and re read the affected pages at trim.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An estate PDF in which the four counter rooms sit out of sequence at the back, two kitchen rooms print with no address or hours at the foot, and the flagship room's on now line is clipped mid sentence at trim, shipped as the one file the whole system was bought to produce.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cutout edges hold where they are actually placed. The pours were shot on dark walnut and the stout and the cortado sit at almost the value of the counter at the glass shoulder, so the one call knockout has no contrast to work from at exactly that boundary. It returns a clean, complete, correct looking cutout and reports full success, and against a dark ground the result is genuinely indistinguishable from a good one. The bite only becomes visible when the silhouette lands on cream at trim, which is the register's whole reason for silhouetting in the first place. Which frames are affected is a property of each photograph's own local contrast and cannot be read off the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the knockout has to happen before placement and the evidence only exists after placement. Doing it right the first time would require knowing which of six frames shares luminance with the counter at the subject boundary, which nothing reports. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the photographs were not all shot on the same day, which is about grading, not edges, and the acceptance line about edges holding on cream is the client's standing quality requirement rather than a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the affected frames go through a different chain, a material named selection of the counter surface inverted and filled, rather than the same chain again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re cut the affected frames through an explicit selection worded to the counter's own material properties, inverted and filled, inspect each new edge against cream rather than against the original ground, re bind them, re merge and read the affected pages at trim again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Featured plates on the flagship pages sitting on cream with a chewed rim along one shoulder, at press, across an estate wide print run.

client_brief:
Autumn shelf talkers that match the bottles and the sellable wine list

Cellar & Cru's autumn selection goes onto the shelf as a collection. We have sixteen photographs covering fourteen wines, taken on two evenings, and an old printer's PDF for the shelf talker.

Please reconcile the captures to the wines and the till export to the sellable list. Allocation-only lines are not part of this shelf run.

A6 portrait, one wine per page in list order, page count equal to the sellable wine count with the allocation-only lines excluded by record range, rendered at 300 ppi at trim. Every card binds grower, region, vintage, style, buyer's note, score, score source and price verbatim from the till export, plus that wine's own bottle in the card's graphic frame. Produced by reverse-engineering the printer's flat PDF into a live merge template, which is handed back with the record of how it was derived so next season is a data change rather than a re-commission.

Sixteen supplied frames reconciled to fourteen wines and brought to one shelf white and one black point across two shooting evenings, with labels, capsules and glass colour honest to the bottle, delivered as one whole-bottle picture per wine at a settled bottle scale, plus one licensed context frame graded into the same neutral. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log, one line per-frame on why it differs from its neighbours, and every crop's reported detection and tradeoff metadata transcribed.

The buyer's note, score and score source must remain verbatim alongside the grower, region, vintage, style and price. Please keep bottle labels, capsule colour and glass honest while establishing one scale and shelf white.

The supplied files are bottle_shots/ (16 frames, 4200 x 2800); talker_2025_PRINT.pdf; autumn_list.csv; mark_card.jpg (3600 x 2400); buyer_notes.txt; bay_photo.jpg.

We want next season to be a data update, not another reconstruction. Leave a live merge template and the derivation record with the press file and true-size proofs.

Alongside the finished work, we need a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record. Keep a clear record of the supplied files used, retained for reference, superseded and rejected. Approved source information remains authoritative. Record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and quality limits, and do not use an undeclared replacement or invented fact to conceal a source problem.

Please work within $3,000-$7,000 fixed and the 2 to 4 weeks target. Allow for one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

No real merchant, producer, critic or publication appears; the house, its wines and its growers are coined.

price_band_and_audience: Bottles from 14 pounds (an entry Loire white, a co-op red) to 220 pounds (a single-vineyard northern Rhone syrah, a mature Piedmontese nebbiolo). Buyer 40 to 65, a confident domestic drinker or a restaurant buyer building a by-the-glass list, who reads a shelf card the way a reader reads a review and who treats visual noise as a signal about the wine behind it. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the correct artefact is restrained and led by grower, region and vintage: generous white space, one quiet type system, the score present but small, the price plain in the run of the card, the bottle photographed straight and lifted onto a calm pale ground so the label carries. Push it toward the supermarket aisle register, price set huge, a shouting discount badge, saturated bottle photography on a dark dramatic ground, and a 220 pound bottle reads as a 6 pound bottle with an inflated ticket, which is precisely the commercial failure this merchant is paying to avoid. Push it the other way into fashion-brand minimalism where the vintage and the region are hard to find and the shop loses the one thing the card is for, which is selling wine when nobody is free to talk. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,400 to 3,000 pounds fixed, or 40 to 65 pounds an hour across 30 to 45 hours.

brand_identity.tagline: Wine worth the walk down the side street
brand_identity.sector: An independent fine wine merchant selling across the counter to retail customers and to restaurant buyers building by the glass lists.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Established 2009, on a side street off the main shopping run in Edinburgh, Scotland. A small counter operation, one or two on the floor, an owner who buys the list himself.
brand_identity.about: Cellar & Cru is a merchant, not a shop that happens to sell wine. The owner tastes and chooses every line, and the selection changes with the season. When there is one of us on the floor and eleven people in, the shelf card is how a wine sells itself, so the card carries the grower, the region, the vintage, our note, the score and the price.

brand_identity.price_positioning: Independent fine wine. Bottles from 14 pounds to 220. The card is restrained and led by grower, region and vintage: generous white space, the score present but small, the price plain in the run of the line. Never the supermarket aisle, never fashion brand minimalism that hides the vintage.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet oldstyle serif for wine names and running notes, set with air, paired with a plain grotesque for regions, vintages and figures. Readable at 40 to 65, restrained rather than loud or fashionable.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, measured and honest, the owner describing a wine as if standing beside you. It says what a wine is and is not, without hyperbole. Example: A co-op red that drinks well above its price, so long as you open it an hour before.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original mark artwork went with the designer who moved abroad. The only clean version we hold is a photograph of the letterpressed compliments card he had made for us, carrying the mark at about 45mm. The autumn list, buyer's notes, scores and prices arrive from the till export.
brand_identity.values: A selection chosen by one buyer with a point of view, and a shop floor that sells wine honestly even when nobody is free to talk.

assets_supplied.name: bottle_shots/ (16 frames, 4200 x 2800)
assets_supplied.kind: The merchant's own bottle photography, shot on the shop counter after closing on two separate evenings, available light plus a counter lamp.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Most of them one evening, the rest the week after. Same counter, same camera. Together they do not look like one shelf."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. The counter lamp was moved between the evenings, so seven frames sit a full step warmer and read as a different glass colour rather than a different light, and six of the wines are in near-black Burgundy or Rhone glass photographed against the dark oak counter, so a one-call knockout finds almost no luminance difference along the shoulder and bites into it, returning a clean, plausible, well-feathered cutout whose shoulder line has been cut flat and whose capsule carries a soft halo. Sixteen frames cover fourteen wines: one wine was reshot and the duplicate is not marked, and one listed wine has no frame at all.

assets_supplied.name: talker_2025_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF of last season's shelf-talker, A6 portrait, one wine per page, fonts embedded, produced from the merchant's old list through a full print engine so it converts cleanly. Carries the mark, a bottle image, the wine block and a score badge.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer sent us last year. We do not have the working file and nobody here knows how it was built. Keep it as it is."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two facts nobody at the shop could tell you. The system that produced the card set the entire body, grower, region, vintage, score, buyer's note, stockist code and price, as ONE continuous story with tab characters between each label and its value, so there are no per-field frames to map and every value must be driven by ordered offsets inside a single story, and the mapping readout of that story silently omits the run holding the stockist code while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well-formed, every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length, the validator returns valid on the resulting arithmetic and the two fields sitting past the omission never become placeholders at all. Separately, the buyer's note sits in a fixed-measure frame sized to last year's notes. And the card ground, named Chalk White in the palette, is a placed warm laid stock rather than a flat process fill: rendered at trim it reproduces a measurable step warmer and slightly darker than a flat #F1ECE1 fill, so a bottle lifted onto a ground matched to the nominal swatch sits in a visible cool rectangular patch on every rendered card, a mismatch that appears only where the cutout ground meets the card ground on the rendered page and only after a card has been rendered.

assets_supplied.name: autumn_list.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the shop's till and stock system, one row per line, with columns for wine, grower, region, vintage, style, buyer's note, score, score source, bottle price, case price, status and an image column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our list, straight out of the till system. The notes and the scores are ours and the prices are current as of Monday."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Sixteen rows for fourteen sellable wines: two allocation-only lines the till still emits, flagged only by a status column the merchant never mentions. Vintages carry a leading apostrophe from the spreadsheet that exported them, the buyer's notes run from 90 to 340 characters because three were written by the owner and the rest by the part-time buyer, and the image column holds full local paths rather than bare filenames and lacks the prefix the merge's own image contract requires, so a naive run binds one bottle to every card or binds no bottles at all.

assets_supplied.name: mark_card.jpg (3600 x 2400)
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the shop's letterpressed compliments card lying on the counter, carrying the merchant's mark at about 45mm wide, shot in daylight.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only clean version of our mark we have left. The original artwork went with the designer."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark is a monoline vine-and-key device with an enclosed counter inside the key bow and a hairline rule beneath the wordmark, pressed into soft cotton paper so the strokes sit close to the paper's own texture. A knockout cannot punch that enclosed counter and collapses on the disjoint lettering, and a trace taken from a selection reads immaculately at screen scale while carrying the paper's tooth as broken edges in the hairline.

assets_supplied.name: buyer_notes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: A page from the owner describing the selection in plain language: which wines are the anchors of the bay, which two are the ones he wants people to try, and how he talks about the scores.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "How I would describe the selection if I were standing there."

assets_supplied.name: bay_photo.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Phone snap of the shelf bay with last season's talkers in place, supplied as a feel reference.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is the bay. The cards sit in wooden fins in front of the bottles."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the lift actually followed the bottle. Six wines are in near-black Burgundy and Rhone glass photographed on dark oak, so along the shoulder and around the capsule the bottle and the counter carry almost the same luminance, and the knockout returns a clean, feathered, entirely plausible cutout whose shoulder has been cut flat and whose capsule drags a soft halo of counter with it. On the dark original that edge is invisible. Which frames behave that way is a property of these particular bottles under this particular lamp and cannot be read off the list, the frame previews or the glass colour alone, because two equally dark bottles separated well and four did not.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it and care alone does not either, because the tool reports success either way and the artefact it returns looks like a competent cutout until it is placed on the pale card ground and looked at. Nothing states it: the brief says dark glass on a dark counter as a description of the shooting conditions and asks for bottles lifted onto a clean pale ground, which is an ordinary client requirement, and no asset description names which six wines are at risk. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to abandon the one-call route for those frames and lift them instead by selecting the bottle's own material, inverting and filling to the ground, which is a different operation with a different failure mode of its own.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-lift the affected bottles through a material-named selection, inverted and filled to the chosen ground, checking each result on the pale ground rather than on the original. Then re-judge the whole set together, because bottles lifted by two different routes carry different edge softness and will not sit as one shelf unless the edge treatment is re-decided across all fourteen, which in practice means re-lifting some of the eight that first succeeded.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen shelf cards in a bay where six of the most expensive bottles have a flattened shoulder and a grey halo, printed and stood in front of the actual bottles, in a shop whose whole proposition is that the card and the wine agree.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card actually exposes, and then whether the mapping built against it landed. Two things arrive only by running. First the granularity: the entire card body came out of the merchant's old system as one continuous tab-delimited story, so there are no per-field frames to map and everything must be driven by ordered offsets inside a single story. Second the yield: the mapping readout of that story omits the run holding the stockist code while keeping its line break, so the string still parses as well-formed, every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length, the validator returns valid on internally consistent wrong arithmetic, the placeholder step reports complete success, and the two fields sitting past the omission never become placeholders at all.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Granularity is not a parameter, is not reported before conversion and has no read-ahead, so the only route to it is to convert, export and read. The yield failure is worse, because it is produced by a convenience readout that presents as complete, so an agent that reads carefully and computes offsets diligently from the readout it was handed produces arithmetic that is internally consistent and wrong, and every tool downstream agrees with it. Nothing states it, since the brief says only to keep the card as it is and put this autumn's wines through it, and it is not a propagation re-run because the source of truth behind the mapping changes from a tool readout to a reconstructed story and the mapping is re-authored against it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story by concatenating the IDML content runs, recompute every offset against that string, re-order any rows sharing a uid so their positions hold against the original text, rebuild and re-validate the mapping, re-run the template preparation, and re-verify by round-tripping IDML and grepping for every placeholder before a single card is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen shelf cards that bind the wine, the grower and most of the block correctly while the score and the price are silently absent from every card, printed and stood on a shelf where the price is the one field the customer is looking for, with every tool in the chain having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every buyer's note actually reaches the card. The note frame in the printer's card is a fixed measure sized to last season's shorter copy, and this autumn's notes run from 90 to 340 characters because two hands wrote them. A frame like that does not spill and does not warn: the text that does not fit simply stops rendering, so an over-long note ends mid sentence at trim and the card still looks like a finished card. Which notes are affected depends on the merged output at true trim in the printer's own type at the printer's own measure, and cannot be worked out from character counts, because the field carries a mix of wide and narrow characters and the frame's real capacity is a property of the converted document rather than of the data.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because nothing in the merge or the render reports an overset condition and both return success, and the truncated card is visually indistinguishable from a card whose note was simply short. Nothing states it: the brief says the notes are ours and the acceptance bar says nothing may be shortened or reworded, which is the merchant's standing requirement rather than a warning, and no earlier step measures a frame or claims to have fitted anything. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is an escalation decision plus a change of what is bound rather than a re-run of the same binding.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify every truncated card by reading the rendered pages at true trim against the source note, not by counting characters. Then decide and disclose: the frame cannot be enlarged through this route and the merchant has forbidden rewriting, so the affected notes are escalated in writing before the file goes to the printer, with the shortest honest option offered (the merchant supplies a cut) and the cards re-merged and re-rendered once he answers.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A shelf of cards in which the four wines carrying the owner's own tasting notes, including the two he most wants people to try, break off mid sentence at the bottom of the frame, printed, cut and stood on the shelf for a customer base that reads the card the way it reads a review.

decision_gates: The surface split: talkers to the merge surface because the layout is fixed client property and the run is record per page, bay set to HTML authoring because it needs three canvas sizes and must stay editable.
Which evening sets the shelf white, knowing a warm reference makes every white wine look oxidised across the whole bay.
How far to correct the warm evening before the correction itself becomes a glass or capsule colour the bottle is not.
Lift route per bottle: the one-call knockout is right for a pale flute and wrong for near-black glass on dark oak, and the wrong route returns a plausible cutout that reports success.
Bottle scale across the set, decided as a bay rather than per picture, and re-decided once any bottle is lifted a different way.
How to name the selection that recovers the mark: naming the card pulls the paper, naming the ink's own colour and medium pulls the mark.
Whether the traced mark is artwork or merely output, including the backing path that rides along and the size below which the hairline rule stops holding.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the printer's own card body or to reconstruct the story independently from the document.

why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and this folder into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of wine bottles. IDENTITY: these are fourteen specific wines whose labels the customer recognises before reading a word, and a generated bottle fabricates a label, which on a card that also carries a grower, a vintage and a score is a false claim about what is in the bottle. The merchant's mark is a specific letterpressed device that must come back as the same mark, not a redrawn one, because it is already on the shop's door. client_brief:
Forecourt cards for current stock, with honest paint and highlight handling

Vanguard Motors has fourteen cars on the forecourt, but the feed still includes vehicles sold or reserved. Please reconcile the stock before producing the A4 window cards. The photography also needs care: some panels were overexposed during the shoot.

This is the required package:

A4 portrait, one vehicle per page in feed order, page count equal to the count of cars actually on the forecourt with sold and reserved units excluded by record range, rendered at 300 ppi at trim. Every card binds year, marque, model, derivative, mileage, colour, the nine-item spec block, price and the finance wording verbatim from the feed, plus that car's own photograph in the correct graphic frame. Accompanied by one single-vehicle file per car named to its stock number and identity-verified by opening it, and by 300 ppi proofs. Produced by reverse-engineering the printer's flat PDF into a live merge template, which is handed back with the record of how it was derived.

Eighteen supplied frames reconciled to fourteen vehicles and brought to one house white and one black point across two lighting sessions, paint colour honest on every car, delivered as one card window and one wider lot picture per vehicle at a consistent vehicle scale, plus one licensed context frame graded into the same neutral. No bodywork invented anywhere. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log, the outcome of every highlight recovery attempt recorded, and every crop's reported detection and tradeoff metadata transcribed.

Finance wording and the nine-item specification block must come through exactly as supplied. Keep the car's actual paint colour, and record the outcome of each highlight-recovery attempt. Do not invent bodywork where the exposure contains no detail.

Available: lot_photos/ (18 frames, 5200 x 3400); windowcard_2025_PRINT.pdf; stock_feed.csv; forecourt_plate.jpg (3800 x 2600); finance_wording.txt; forecourt_photo.jpg.

Please check the individual stock-number files by opening them, and leave the recovered live template with its derivation notes. We need to trust both the printed card and the reusable process.

$3,000-$7,000 fixed; 2 to 4 weeks. Review structure: One direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

Please deliver a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record. Account for every supplied file and identify anything used only as reference, superseded or rejected. Stay with approved facts and copy. Do not silently replace weak assets; use only the stated stock or concept allowances, and record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and material compromises.

price_band_and_audience: Vehicles from 18,000 pounds (a low-mileage compact estate, a four-year-old hatchback) to 95,000 pounds (a two-year-old grand tourer, a specification-heavy performance saloon). Buyer 35 to 60, a private retail buyer who has already narrowed the choice online, has driven a distance to see one specific car, and is deciding whether this dealer is careful. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the correct artefact is photograph forward and quiet: one large honest picture of the actual car, a short specification of the things that differ between examples, the price present and plainly set rather than shouted, the finance line legible and secondary, and generous space. Push it toward the budget lot register, the monthly payment set enormous, a burst badge, a saturated red price flash, three exclamation points of specification, and a 95,000 pound car reads as a car with something wrong with it, which is the exact commercial failure this dealer is paying to avoid. Push it the other way into a manufacturer-style brochure with no price and no mileage and the card stops doing the one job it has, which is answering the two questions a buyer has while standing in the rain. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,600 to 3,200 pounds fixed, or 45 to 70 pounds an hour across 30 to 45 hours.

brand_identity.about: Vanguard holds around fourteen carefully bought cars at a time and sells to people who have already decided roughly what they want and are choosing where to buy it. The card in the windscreen is the first thing a buyer meets, before anyone walks out, so it has to answer their two questions honestly: what is this car, and what does it cost.

brand_identity.typography: A confident low contrast serif or sturdy grotesque for the marque and headline, paired with a clean neutral sans for the spec block, price and finance footer. Careful and quiet, neither discount loud nor brochure sparse.
brand_identity.voice: Factual, unhurried and confident, a dealer who lets the car and the spec do the talking. No exclamation, no urgency. Example: One owner, full history, the colour it says on the card and the colour it is on the forecourt.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The shield artwork is long gone. The only clean version we hold is a photograph of the pressed and painted aluminium plate above the office door, weathered by several winters, carrying the shield at about 180mm. The current stock, specs and prices arrive from the stock feed, and the finance wording is fixed by the broker.
brand_identity.values: Cars bought with care and sold without spin, and a forecourt where the card and the vehicle always agree.

assets_supplied.name: lot_photos/ (18 frames, 5200 x 3400)
assets_supplied.kind: The dealer's own photography of fourteen vehicles taken on the forecourt across one bright overcast morning and one late afternoon, handheld, with a few alternate wider frames.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The whole lot in one morning, the last few late on. The silver and white ones have gone to nothing on the screen."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. The white and silver cars' bonnets and roofs and the sky behind them are genuinely clipped rather than merely bright, so a highlight recovery on those frames returns an image visually identical to the one that went in while reporting complete success, and no response says the data was not there. Separately, three vehicles were shot so tight that the card's landscape window cannot be taken from them without cutting the front wing, and the crop tool responds by offering an expand chain that would fabricate bodywork on a car a buyer will stand in front of.

assets_supplied.name: windowcard_2025_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF of the current window card, A4 portrait, one vehicle per page, fonts embedded, produced from the dealer's old system through a full print engine so it converts cleanly. Carries the shield, a vehicle photograph, a headline, a two-column spec block, the price and the finance footer.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer sent us two seasons ago. We do not have the working file and nobody here knows how it was built. Keep it as it is."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The conversion returns nothing like the structure the printed page suggests. The tidy two-column spec block, the price line and the finance footer all arrive as ONE continuous tab-delimited story that has to be driven by ordered offsets, while the single-looking headline splits into three separate frames because year, marque and model were placed as separate runs, and the two graphic frames (the vehicle photograph and the shield) are distinguishable only by their bounds and their link, neither being named for what it holds.

assets_supplied.name: stock_feed.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the dealership's stock management system, one row per unit, with columns for stock number, registration, marque, model, derivative, year, mileage, colour, transmission, fuel, a nine-item spec block, price, monthly figure, status and an image column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Straight out of the system on Monday morning. The prices are what we are asking today."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Seventeen rows for fourteen cars actually on the forecourt: three sold or reserved units the system still emits, flagged only by a status column the dealer never mentions. Stock numbers have lost their leading zeros to the spreadsheet that exported them, one car's mileage cell is empty, two derivative names run four times the length of the rest because the clerk pasted the full factory description, prices sit as raw integers with no separators or currency, and the image column holds full local paths without the prefix the merge's own image contract requires, so a naive run binds one car's photograph to every card or binds none at all.

assets_supplied.name: forecourt_plate.jpg (3800 x 2600)
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the pressed and painted aluminium plate above the office door carrying the Vanguard Motors shield at about 180mm wide, weathered by several winters, shot in flat daylight.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only clean version of the shield we have. The artwork went years ago."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The shield is a bordered device with an enclosed chevron counter and a hairline keyline inside the outer edge, and the plate's weathering means the trace comes back carrying near-identical greys as separate fills and slightly broken edges along that keyline. It reads perfectly at inspection scale and on white, and the card reproduces it at roughly a fifth of the plate's size on a deep midnight ground.

assets_supplied.name: finance_wording.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The wording the dealership's finance broker requires on any printed material carrying a monthly figure, 310 characters, supplied as plain text.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This has to appear on every card that shows a monthly payment, word for word, and it is not ours to change."

assets_supplied.kind: Phone snap of the forecourt and the entrance board, supplied as a feel reference.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is the forecourt. The board is by the gate."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether there is anything left to recover in the blown areas. The dealer describes the bonnets and roofs of the white and silver cars as gone, which reads as an exposure complaint, and the natural response is a highlight recovery pass. On these particular frames the readout is that nothing moves: the call succeeds, returns an image, and the recovered file is visually indistinguishable from the one that went in, because those pixels are genuinely clipped rather than merely bright. Nothing in any response says so. Which frames are recoverable and which are not is a property of these exposures and cannot be known from the dealer's description, from the previews (a bright roof and a clipped roof look the same on screen) or from the session split, because two afternoon frames recover fully and three morning frames do not.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the only way to learn whether the data survived is to attempt the recovery and compare the result against the input, and the tool reports success in both cases. Nothing states it: the brief says the panels have gone to nothing, which is a client describing a symptom, and no asset description names which vehicles are unrecoverable. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to change what the picture is rather than to redo the correction, which reopens the crop policy and the treatment decision for the affected cars.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Compare each recovery result against its input rather than accepting the call, then handle the unrecoverable frames a different way: re-frame from an alternate wider frame where one exists so less clipped sky is carried, re-decide the card window crop so the blown roof sits outside it, or, where neither works, escalate that the car needs rephotographing rather than shipping a card with a hole in the bodywork. Then re-judge white point and vehicle scale across all fourteen, because cars re-framed for a different reason will not sit with the rest unless the policy is re-taken as a set.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A forecourt of cards on which the most expensive white and silver cars have a featureless white hole where the bonnet and roof should be, printed and put in the windscreens of the actual vehicles, by a dealer whose entire pitch is that he is careful.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card actually is underneath. The printed page shows a tidy two-column spec block, one price line, one footer, one headline and one photograph, and every sensible plan maps those as separate frames. The conversion returns the opposite shape: the spec block, the price and the finance footer arrive as one continuous tab-delimited story that can only be driven by ordered offsets, while the single-looking headline splits into three separate frames because year, marque and model were placed as separate runs, and the two graphic frames carry no name, only bounds and a link, so which one holds the vehicle photograph and which holds the shield is not stated anywhere in the response.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Frame granularity from a PDF is not a parameter, is not reported before conversion and has no read-ahead, so the only route to it is to convert, export IDML and read, and the shape it returns is the inverse of the one the printed page implies. Nothing states it: the brief says only to keep the card as it is and put the current stock through it, and names no frames, stories or fields. It is not a propagation re-run, because the mapping strategy itself changes, from per-field frames to two different strategies inside one card, and the image binding has to be settled by rendering a page rather than by reading the response.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Discard the planned per-field map. Reconstruct the true story from the IDML content runs, compute offsets against that string for everything in the body, map the three headline frames individually by their integer page-item ids, and settle the photograph's frame by rendering one record and reading it against the printed reference rather than by assuming the larger frame is the photograph. Then rebuild, re-validate, re-prepare and re-verify the placeholders before any card is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A template that validates and reports success while binding the model into the year's frame and the vehicle photograph into the shield's frame, producing fourteen cards that are confidently wrong in the two places a buyer looks first.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered shield survives its own reproduction. Traced off a 180mm pressed plate it is immaculate at inspection scale and on a white ground, and it carries perfectly onto the A1 entrance panel. The window card reproduces it at roughly a fifth of that size on the card's deep midnight ground, and at that size on that ground the hairline keyline and the enclosed chevron counter fill in and the shield reads as a solid lozenge, while the plate's weathering, which was invisible as texture, shows as broken edges. This cannot be judged from the trace, from the SVG on screen or from the A1, because it is a product of the reproduction size, the ink behaviour of the card's dark ground and the specific edge quality this particular trace inherited from a weathered plate.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the artwork is genuinely correct at every size it is inspected at until it is rendered at true trim on the real ground, and no tool reports a reproduction limit. Nothing states it: the brief says the shield is on the cards and the board, and never asks how small it can go, so nothing has already discovered it. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to author a different piece of artwork for the small dark application rather than to re-place the same one.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Produce a reproduction cut of the shield for the card: reduce the trace to the marks that survive at card size, open or drop the hairline keyline, keep the chevron counter open, and consolidate the weathering greys into flat fills, then re-generate the raster plate the merge binds, re-merge and re-render, and check it again at true trim on the dark ground rather than on screen. Keep the full-detail artwork for the A1 panel and record in the handover which version belongs where and below what size the detailed one stops holding.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen window cards and every sold slip carrying a shield that has closed into an unreadable dark blob, on the one element that appears on every printed thing this dealership owns, delivered as a recovered brand asset.

why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and this folder into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of cars. IDENTITY: these are fourteen specific vehicles, each with a registration, a stock number, a mileage and a paint colour that a buyer has driven forty miles to see, and a generated car fabricates a wheel, a badge, a trim level or a colour, which on a card that also carries a price is a false claim about the goods. The dealership shield is a specific pressed device that must come back as the same shield, because it is already on the board at the gate. SPEC: the dealer needs one card per car actually on the forecourt at A4 and 300 ppi with every value bound verbatim from their own stock feed, sold and reserved units absent, the full finance wording present word for word, each card carrying its own photograph, and one separately named file per stock number containing the car its filename claims. None of that can be produced or checked by generation. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next week's stock is a data change, and a native document with live text, a real table and real vector artwork so prices can move every week. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did anything survive in that blown roof, did this placeholder get created, is this photograph in the photograph's frame, does this shield still read at card size. That is not a generation problem.

client_brief:
Expand our licensed player-card production to the full stocked squad

The licensing partner has taken the full Continental Cup squad. We now need the eighteen-player material reconciled against the stock roster and produced from last season's printer PDF.

Please keep player identity correct through the entire job: portrait preparation, image binding, page order and individual partner-file naming. A correct-looking card with the wrong name on the file is not a usable delivery.

One press file carrying the whole stocked squad at the printer's trim, one record per page, page count equal to stocked row count and page order equal to squad order, every card carrying its own player photograph and the bound mark plate. Plus one named single card file per player for the licensing partner, each name verified against the card inside it rather than against its position in a list.

Eighteen portraits brought to one pitch side target (one white point, one black point, one player height in frame) across three evenings and a corridor, with the kit held to the licensed shade rather than dragged along by the skin correction, plus one licensed camera-scale stadium frame graded into the same world. Per frame parameter log including one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours.

A client-facing preflight package showing representative first, middle, last, longest, and exception records at true output size, with page count, dimensions, overflow, image binding, naming, and record identity checks.

The portraits span three evenings and a corridor. Bring them into one pitch-side look, but protect the kit's licensed shade while correcting skin. The stadium context frame needs to belong to that same treatment.

Pack contents: cup26_squad_portraits/ (18 frames); cup26_teamset_2025_PRINTER.pdf; cup26_squad.csv; cup26_sponsorboard.jpg; cup26_printer_spec.txt.

Please include the representative and exception-record proof package at actual output size, not just a collage of the easiest cards.

Handover: a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record. Include an inventory showing how every supplied file was used or why it was set aside. Keep factual content tied to the approved inputs. Any missing coverage, substituted asset, reconciliation or quality compromise must be declared; a weak source is not permission to invent or silently replace it.

The commission is budgeted at $6,000-$12,000 fixed. We have allowed 4 to 6 weeks, including direction approval, first-production proof, and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.
