Every real element is laundered: the competition is the coined fictional Continental Cup 2026, the athletes are clearly fictional (Diego Solano, Marco Ferraz, Theo Rocher, Luka Petrov, Andre Mensah, Rafael Duarte, Nikolai Ivanic, Samuel Okoye and the rest of the coined squad), and no real club, nation, flag, emblem, competition, sponsor, camera, editing product or social platform is named anywhere. The ledger's own repositioning note concedes that the poster as posted sat on a single surface and was not the fuller commission. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest job is: a printer's flat press PDF can be reverse engineered into a live InDesign merge template headlessly, one record per page is confirmed behaviour, per record named single card files are producible by two verified routes, and an authored HTML page becomes a native editable Express document. So this is the commission that client genuinely needed once the licensing partner bought the whole squad rather than one hero: a variable data print run off photography that has to be brought to one look first, with the identity recovered rather than reinvented, and the trade stand chart handed back editable.

The band is load bearing: a marquee cup set reads dramatic, saturated and high contrast, dark card field, heavy metallic feeling type, the player large in frame. The same eighteen players treated for a community league programme (flat, bright, cheap, small pictures, generic sans) undersells the licence and the licensing partner will not sign it off. brand_identity.audience: Collectors aged sixteen to forty five who buy officially licensed sets beside other marquee cards, in grocery aisles, at newsstands and in hobby shops. They notice when a card in the pack looks like it came from somewhere else.

brand_identity.typography: A heavy, near-metallic display face for the player name and squad number, set large and confident, paired with a clean condensed sans for the position, club line and set year. The type should feel like a stadium scoreboard, not a school sports day.

brand_identity.values: A licensed set is a promise: every player is who the card says, and the look holds across the whole squad rather than favouring a hero. Consistency in the sleeve is the product.

assets_supplied.name: cup26_squad_portraits/ (18 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Squad photography: fourteen frames shot pitch side across three evenings at the same ground, four shot later in a service corridor under the venue's own house lighting.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The whole squad, one player per frame. Fourteen at the ground, four in the corridor because those lads missed the shoot. They do not match and we need them to."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The corridor lighting is sodium vapour, so a whole frame warmth correction that fixes the skin drags the kit colour off the licensed shade at the same time and a confined correction is the only route that holds both. Separately those four frames came off a second body and were already cropped in camera, so several of them cannot reach the card photo frame's placement geometry at native scale.

assets_supplied.name: cup26_teamset_2025_PRINTER.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF the printer ran for last season's team set card, at trading card trim, fonts embedded, produced from a genuine page layout so it converts cleanly.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card file the printer ran last year. The layout is right, keep it." Carries the player name, squad number, position, club line and set year plus the photograph and a small placed tournament mark.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark sits in a frame far smaller than the printed card leads you to expect, so the mark's real reproduction size is geometry inherited from a printer nobody can ask, and it lands reversed on a near black field rather than on the pale board the mark was photographed from. The document also carries no bleed at all and no bleed can be introduced into it later, although the printer's own spec sheet asks for it.

assets_supplied.name: cup26_squad.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Roster export straight out of the licensing database: player, squad number, position, club line, set year and a photo column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Contractual copy. It goes on the card exactly as written."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Twenty rows for eighteen squad players, because two players who were loaned out before the squad was confirmed are still emitted, each with a blank squad number. The export is sorted alphabetically by surname while the client asked for squad order, the merge honours row order and nothing about the finished file announces that the order is wrong. The photo column is a plain header holding bare filenames, which is not the shape a variable image binding accepts, and two players share a surname so their filenames collide.

assets_supplied.name: cup26_sponsorboard.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of a pitch side sponsor board carrying the tournament mark, printed in one deep ink on a pale board, under floodlight.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place our mark still lives. It is on the board at the ground."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark is a compound lockup, a wordmark set inside a ring with a hairline rule between them, and a single compound selection returns the ring and silently drops the hairline while looking entirely plausible. The floodlight also runs the ink and the board close in value across the right third of the board face.

assets_supplied.name: cup26_printer_spec.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text from the card printer: trim, the photo frame and mark frame placement geometry as the printer holds it, the proof resolution the licensing people sign off from, and the file naming the partner expects.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer and the partner need from us. The naming matters to them."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives at the size it actually reproduces on the card, on the ground it actually lands on. The trace is clean, complete and convincing at its own canvas: ring, wordmark and the hairline rule between them all present. The mark frame inherited from the printer is a fraction of what the printed card suggests, and the field behind it is near black rather than the pale board the mark was photographed from. Whether the counters inside the wordmark and the hairline stay open at that reduction, or close into a solid lozenge that reads as a dark smudge reversed on a dark field, is a property of this particular trace at this particular size and is invisible at any larger view.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the mark cannot be judged at reproduction size until both the frame geometry and the card field exist, and the tracing tool takes no options at all, so there is no parameter to set correctly the first time. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for the mark back as artwork usable at any size, which is the client's requirement rather than a disclosure that this trace will not meet it. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different upstream chain, since the only lever the tracer has is the raster prep that feeds it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster preparation and build a different plate: re-select at ink level with a prompt naming a single element rather than the compound lockup, composite the elements taken separately, thicken or drop the hairline rule for the card size, and produce a reduction cut for the card while the full lockup carries the chart. Then re-rasterise, re-bind to every record and re-merge.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eighteen licensed cards going to press with the tournament's own mark printing as an unreadable dark blot on every one of them, having looked perfect in every view anybody actually opened.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the per player files the partner distributes contain the player their filename claims. The named file route that looks cheapest returns a labelled list of outputs, one per record, in what presents as record order. The labels are generated rather than read, and on this route the outputs come back against the wrong records while every label still reads correctly and every card is individually perfect. Nothing in the response distinguishes a correct list from a reversed one, and the only evidence that exists is opening the files and reading the name on each card against the roster.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it and there is no parameter that makes the labels truthful; an agent that simply believed the labels would have done nothing wrong by any published rule. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for one file per player named to the player, which is the requirement, not a warning that a route exists which satisfies it falsely. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the correct response is to abandon that route entirely for one whose record identity is guaranteed, either rendering separate files off the merged document or driving the merge one record at a time, which is a structurally different chain rather than the same chain again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Discard the whole named set, re-derive it through a route where identity is guaranteed per file, and verify every file by reading the card inside it against the roster before naming it. The press file and the proofs then have to be re-checked for order against the same reading, since the same assumption was in play.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A licensing partner distributing eighteen individually named player files in which the names and the players do not correspond, on contractual copy, which is the single failure a licensed set cannot survive.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer treats the construction the squad chart is built on. A chart of eighteen players is naturally authored as a grid of fixed size cells each carrying its player as a covering background image, which is exactly the construction the importer discards: the cell arrives with its geometry, its border and its caption intact and no picture in it at all, at full success and with no warning anywhere in the response. Only a photograph carried as its own element survives. Compounding it, the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so the partner tile cannot be checked that way at all and the returned per canvas markup is the sole channel that reports what happened.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the drop happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of two equally ordinary constructions survives, which no tool reports. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a chart the client can edit and for the players to be on it. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix is to re-author the chart's entire photo mechanism as a different construction and re-verify both canvases from the markup rather than from the preview.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-author every player cell around an element carried image with explicit dimensions, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, then audit both canvases from the returned markup for placeholder images and for the mark arriving as path shapes rather than as one picture.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A trade stand chart delivered as an editable document that is eighteen empty grey boxes with names under them, on the canvas nobody looked at, with the export having reported success throughout.

client_one_liner: Our spring list is eighteen varieties, the tag printer wants one file by the end of the month, and all we have is last year's printed tags and a spreadsheet the growers keep in their own shorthand.
client_brief:
Spring plant tags with four complete, non-overlapping department files

Ferncroft Nursery needs the spring tag run rebuilt from last year's printed artwork and the growers' spreadsheet. There are eighteen varieties in the source material, but only stocked varieties should reach the final run.

The printer wants the full file. Our departments need their own subsets from that same template and data, with no variety missing and none accidentally appearing in two departments.

Tag files: One press file for the tag printer covering every stocked variety and nothing cut from the season, one record per page, page count equal to stocked row count and page order equal to department order, every field variable where the season list says it varies and every tag carrying its own variety photograph. Plus four department subsets, complete and disjoint, cut off the same template and data.

Variety photographs: Eighteen phone frames shot across weeks of changing weather brought to one bench target (one white point, one crop logic, one distance from the plant), foliage held true rather than dragged along by the ground correction, plus one licensed camera-scale potting bench frame graded into the same world. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with the returned tradeoff record for each, and a per-frame parameter log.

The photographs were taken over weeks of changing weather. Please align the bench treatment and plant distance while keeping the foliage true. A ground correction must not turn one plant's leaves into another colour.

We have ferncroft_season_list.csv; ferncroft_hangtag_2025_PRINTER.pdf; ferncroft_benchtag_2025_PRINTER.pdf; ferncroft_variety_photos/ (18 frames); ferncroft_slate_sign.jpg.

Please reconcile the growers' shorthand before merging, and make the department order and final record counts easy to check in the handover.

Budget: $3,000-$7,000 fixed. Target: 2 to 4 weeks. Reviews: One direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

The final package should contain a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record, with every source file accounted for, including references and rejected or superseded material. Use the approved information without inventing missing facts. Only the stated stock or concept exceptions permit substitution; document every omission, replacement, reconciliation and material quality compromise.

The recurring Upwork and Freelancer.com listing of exactly this shape is a garden centre or nursery asking for a variable data tag or label run: a season spreadsheet of varieties plus a folder of variety photographs plus last year's printed tag as the only surviving artwork, with the deliverable named as one print ready file for the tag printer and, very often, separate files per department or per bench. Those posts consistently arrive without a native layout file, with the spreadsheet kept in the growers' own shorthand, and with the request phrased as goals (get the tags printed, keep last year's look, make the prices right) rather than as method. price_band_and_audience: An heirloom specialty grower at eighteen to ninety five dollars a plant, buyer thirty five to sixty five, who reads the botanical name and asks where the stock came from. The band is load bearing: at this price the tag is provenance led and botanical forward, the Latin sits with real presence, the care information is set quietly, the price is small and the photograph is a supporting note rather than the headline. The same eighteen varieties at a six dollar big box band would correctly be tagged the other way round, price loud, photograph filling the tag, care icons oversized, common name only, and shipping that treatment here makes a ninety five dollar specimen shrub read as clearance stock. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Grown for the people who ask where it came from.
brand_identity.sector: Retail horticulture: an heirloom specialty nursery and garden centre selling perennials, herbs, shrubs and a short specimen list from its own benches across four planting departments.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A small heirloom grower in Litchfield County, Connecticut, selling from its own benches, with a growing office and four department benches each tended by a different person.
brand_identity.about: Ferncroft Nursery grows heirloom and specialty stock for gardeners who read the botanical name first. Everything is sold off the bench with a tag that reads like a plant person wrote it. Spring opening is the last Saturday of April, and every plant on the rack needs its tag by then.
brand_identity.audience: Gardeners aged thirty five to sixty five who buy for provenance, read the Latin name, and ask where the stock was grown. They distrust a rack where one tag looks like a different shop.
brand_identity.price_positioning: An heirloom specialty grower at eighteen to ninety five dollars a plant, above the six dollar big-box rack and below a fine-press botanical print. The tag is provenance-led and botanical-forward: the Latin carries, the price sits small, the photograph is a supporting note.
brand_identity.typography: A humanist serif with real presence for the common and botanical names, the Latin set in italic beneath, paired with a quiet, small sans for the care line, pot size and price. Restraint is the point: the price should never shout.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, knowledgeable, unhurried, the voice of a grower. Example line the brand would write: 'Slow to establish, then generous for decades. Give it morning sun and patience.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There are no design files. The two tags the printer ran last spring survive only as press PDFs, and the nursery mark exists only routed and painted into the slate sign at the gate, captured in one handheld photograph. The mark and the printed care icons have to be recovered before they can go anywhere new.
brand_identity.values: Provenance and honesty on the bench: the name on the tag is the right name, and the whole rack reads as one careful hand. Restraint signals quality here.

assets_supplied.name: ferncroft_season_list.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Season list exported from the growing office: common name, botanical name, department, care line, pot size, price and a photo column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our season list. The growers keep it the way they like it. Everything we are stocking should be in there."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Twenty one rows for eighteen stocked varieties, because three plants cut from the season after the list was written are still in it and nothing in the row says so except a pot size that never got filled in. It is sorted in bench walking order rather than by department, the merge honours row order and a finished file gives no sign that its order is wrong, and the photo column is a plain header holding bare filenames, which is not the shape a variable image binding accepts.

assets_supplied.name: ferncroft_hangtag_2025_PRINTER.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF the printer ran for last spring's small hanging tag, at its proper trim, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The tag that goes in the pot. It is the right look, keep it." Prints the common name, the botanical name in italic underneath, the care line, the pot size, the price and a variety photograph, plus a row of small care icons along the foot.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed face reads as six separately labelled fields but the placed photograph splits the flow into only two text frames, so most of those lines share one continuous story and can only be driven by ordered offset arithmetic inside it. The readout of that story silently omits the run holding the italic botanical name while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length.

assets_supplied.name: ferncroft_benchtag_2025_PRINTER.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF for the larger bench tag that stands beside the specimen shrubs, same house look, same faces, at a much larger trim.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The big one we stand next to the specimens. Same look, bigger. We want both formats."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What prints as a photograph panel on this format was a flat tinted panel in the original artwork rather than a placed image, so nothing about the printed tag distinguishes it from the hanging tag's real photo frame.

assets_supplied.name: ferncroft_variety_photos/ (18 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Phone photographs of each variety taken at the growing benches across several weeks, at whatever distance the grower happened to be standing.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One picture of every variety. Different days, different weather, but they are all there."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: They were shot across weeks of changing light and at wildly different distances, so several frames are already tight and small and cannot reach the tag's photo frame placement geometry at native scale, while the crop tool will interpolate up to a hard cap and report having done so only inside its own tradeoff record. Two of the eighteen turn out to be the same plant photographed at two stages, and one stocked variety has no photograph at all, which no filename reveals.

assets_supplied.name: ferncroft_slate_sign.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the painted slate sign at the nursery gate, the mark routed into the slate and filled with a pale paint.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our mark. It only exists on the gate now."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark is paint sitting inside a routed groove, so its own edge carries a cast shadow line all the way round, and a prompt naming the sign returns the slate rather than the paint.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether these particular phone frames can reach the tag's photo frame geometry at one crop logic without being enlarged. The frames were taken at whatever distance the grower happened to be standing, so occupancy varies wildly, and the ones where the grower stood close are already tight. A crop to the tag's geometry on those returns a clean, correctly sized, entirely plausible looking picture while having interpolated up to a hard cap, and it says so nowhere in its message, its warnings or its errors: the only trace is an entry inside the returned tradeoff record. Which of the eighteen this happens to is a property of each file and is not visible by looking at the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the tag's placement geometry is only known once the printer's document has been converted and read, and there is no parameter that forbids the enlargement. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the pictures were taken at the benches on a phone over several weeks, which is the client describing their photographs rather than a disclosure about resolution. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a per frame decision about a different crop logic for the set, not the same crop again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read the tradeoff record on every crop, then re-plan the crop logic for the whole set around what the tightest usable frame can actually give at native scale, re-cut all eighteen to that logic so the rack still reads as one rack, and name any frame that cannot be brought to it rather than shipping it enlarged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A rack of tags where several varieties are represented by soft interpolated pictures at ninety five dollars a plant, and a set that no longer reads as one set because the affected frames were the only ones cropped differently.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the second tag format actually is as an editable document. Both printed tags carry what reads as a variety photograph in the same house layout at two sizes, and nothing about the printed artwork, the file, or the client's description separates them. The conversion is where they diverge: what looks like a photograph panel on the larger format was never a placed image, so that document comes across as a continuous text flow with no graphic frame anywhere in it, and there is nowhere for a per variety photograph to bind at all. The mapping strategies the two formats need are therefore different in kind, not in degree, and the difference exists only inside the converted structure.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no care in the mapping prevents it; frame granularity out of a PDF is not under the agent's control, and an agent that promised the same treatment on both formats would have been reading the same evidence the client was. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the two tags are the same look at two sizes and asks for both, which is true of what prints. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the second format needs a structurally different plan, and the photograph it cannot carry has to be dealt with somewhere else entirely.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the specimen format around what its own document can carry, drive its lines by ordered offset arithmetic inside the single story it exposes, decide honestly whether the specimen varieties get a photograph on a different surface instead, and rewrite the department subsets so the specimen department is not silently promised something the format cannot do.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A specimen bench of ninety five dollar shrubs tagged with an empty tinted panel where the customer expects to see the plant, discovered by the owner on opening Saturday.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the mapping built against the hanging tag actually landed on every field. The tag's printed face reads as six labelled fields, the readout of its story looks well formed, the validator returns valid with no warnings and the placeholder step reports completing successfully. The readout silently omits one run while keeping its line break, so every offset computed past it is short by exactly that run's length and two of the mappings never become placeholders at all. The merged tags then carry the template's own static text in those positions, and because that static text is a perfectly ordinary care line and a plausible price, a merged tag read on its own looks completely correct. Only reading tag against tag against the season list, variety by variety, shows that those two fields never change.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and there is no parameter that makes the readout complete; an agent that computed its offsets from the readout the tool handed it would have followed the documented chain exactly. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the growers' list has never been tidied, which is about the data, not about the template's story. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix is to reconstruct the true story text from the round tripped document and recompute every offset against that string, which is a different source of truth rather than the same computation again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the offsets from the reconstructed story, rebuild the mapping, prepare the template again, confirm every expected placeholder by inspecting the round tripped document rather than by reading the response, then re-merge the whole run and re-read sample tags against the list before any subset is cut.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eighteen tags printed with the same care line and the same price on every one of them, which on a nursery bench means a shrub priced like a herb and a shade plant sold to somebody who will put it in full sun.

Which fields can be addressed as frames and which have to be driven by ordered arithmetic inside one story, decided per format rather than once.

IDENTITY: these are this nursery's own eighteen varieties with their own botanical names, care lines and prices, their own mark recovered off the gate sign rather than reinvented, and their own care icons recovered off the tag their customers already read; a regenerated mark is a different nursery's mark and a regenerated icon means nothing to anybody. Exhibition wall labels and artwork records, with installer files by room

Marrow & Vane is hanging forty-one works. We need the spring printer's label artwork reused, not redesigned, and a reconciled photographic record from the interns' two shoots.

There are forty artwork photographs. One missing photograph must remain a documented gap, not a substituted image. The labels still need to cover all forty-one works in the supplied list.

Labels and room files
One press PDF of forty one wall labels, one work per page in works list order, built from the printer's own spring artwork rather than a new design, every field present including the credit line on the two works that carry one and the accession number at the foot, and no record truncated at trim. Artwork records
Forty normalised artwork records brought to one standard across storeroom and gallery lighting: one white point, one black point, each work square and cropped to its own edge with the wall, the floor and the frame shadow out, the three glazed works corrected without lifting their reflections, none enlarged beyond its source frame. Delivered with a per-frame parameter log, the folder to works list reconciliation, and the one work with no photograph named rather than substituted.

Preflight package
A client-facing preflight package showing representative first, middle, last, longest, and exception records at true output size, with page count, dimensions, overflow, image binding, naming, and record identity checks.

Please retain the two credit lines and every accession number. Square the artwork and crop to its own edge, with the room and frame shadow removed; glazed works need careful treatment without lifting their reflections.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Anchored to the posted freelance commission this concept sits on: a gallery job asking for printed exhibition wall labels and an accompanying exhibition checklist produced from a works list and a folder of artwork images, one label per hung piece carrying title, artist, medium, dimensions and year, all consistent across the show, with the previous season's printed piece supplied as the look to keep. The real posting names its gallery, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional house Marrow and Vane. The ledger verdict is STRENGTHEN: the concept and its collateral are right, but the original sat almost entirely on one surface (drop the rows into a template and merge). CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is, because a bare press PDF can now be reverse engineered into a live merge template headlessly, a checklist with real tables and real type can be authored into a native editable Express document, and a mark can be recovered at ink level off a photograph of the brass fascia. So this is the gallery's actual job: the printer's spring artwork becomes a live run, the interns' photography becomes a record set, and the checklist the desk updates next week is genuinely editable.

So this is the gallery's actual job: the printer's spring artwork becomes a live run, the interns' photography becomes a record set, and the checklist the desk updates next week is genuinely editable.
price_band_and_audience: Works at six thousand to eighty five thousand dollars, audience collectors and two institutional curators, plus a press list. The band is load-bearing: at this level the label is austere and generously spaced, a small quiet type size sitting high on a large card with a lot of unprinted stock under it, no rules, no colour, no logo on the label at all, because typographic restraint is how the institution signals that the work carries the room. Drop the same show to a two hundred dollar community group show and the correct label is warmer and denser: bigger type, the gallery mark on every card, a price line, a QR to the artist's page, all of which would read here as a market stall. Push the other way into a museum's editorial house style with a wall text paragraph per work and the labels start competing with the art and misrepresent a selling show as a survey. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every field maps correctly. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

assets_supplied.name: mv_spring_labels_press.pdf

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the fields the mapping claimed to write are actually in the prepared template. The spring card presents as four separated blocks, but what the conversion exposes is a continuous story in which the credit line is its own run, and the mapping readout omits that run while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed. Every offset computed past that point is short by exactly the omitted run's length. The validator returns VALID with zero warnings on those offsets, and the preparation step returns a completed successfully message, and only some of the fields are present in the document afterwards. Which fields survived is visible in no response at all, only in the prepared template's own stories.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it and care does not either, because the readout looks correct and the validator confirms it; the mitigation (rebuild the story from the document's own runs and recompute every offset against that) is only obviously worth its cost once the round trip has shown fields missing. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that there is no layout file and the spring PDF is the look to keep. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different derivation of the offsets from a different source string, and on this template the credit line may have to be mapped by a different action entirely.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild each frame's true story from the document's content runs, recompute the whole offset table against it, remap the credit line by an action that suits a field only two of forty one records carry, prepare the template again and round trip it again before any record is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Forty one wall labels that go to press missing the credit line and the accession foot, with the page count correct, every response reporting success, and the omission first visible on the wall on opening night.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the three long medium lines and the two part dimensions actually do inside a fixed label frame at true trim. They do not spill and they do not report an overset anywhere in the merge response: the text simply stops rendering at the frame's bottom, mid phrase, and the merged document still has one page per record and the page count still equals the row count. Where a proportional string of that length breaks, inside that measure at that point size, is not computable from the frame bounds and the typography the template reports, and the rendered page is the only channel that shows it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it. The defensible order is exactly this one, prepare then merge then render then read, and there is no capacity readout anywhere in the chain and no overset flag in a merged output. (b) Nothing states it: the client says the medium lines are the artists' own wording and cannot be edited without asking, which is a permissions statement about the copy, not a warning that a frame will silently truncate it. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a set wide decision rather than a repeat: the run is one typographic system, so a single label cannot be rescued by being set smaller, and the choice is between a smaller size across all forty one, a wider measure on every card that changes the spring look the client asked to keep exactly, an abbreviation convention applied consistently and cleared with the registrar, or going back to the gallery on three specific works.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Decide the treatment for the whole run rather than the three offending records, change the template or the copy convention accordingly, prepare again if the frame changed, merge all forty one again, render at trim again and read every page rather than the three that were known to be long.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Three works hung with labels that stop mid phrase, on a selling show where the medium line is the collector's provenance, with the page count, the field mapping and every tool response all reporting a clean run.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives at the size the checklist actually reproduces it, on the ground the checklist actually uses. The trace is judged at full canvas against the plate, where it is clean, complete and correct: the ampersand's counters open, the hairline rule present. Placed at its real size on the checklist's warm grey ground, and rendered by the importer rather than by a browser, the thinnest parts are where the etched line and the brushed brass ran closest in value, and the counters can close into solid shapes while the rule thins to nothing. Nothing in the trace, the markup or the export response reports it. The rendered page is the only place it exists, and the rendition only returns the first page.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it: the mark cannot be judged at its reproduction size before there is a page that reproduces it at that size, and no tool in the connector reports stroke weight, counter area or contrast against a ground. (b) Nothing states it: the client asks only for the mark placed properly rather than as a picture of brass, which is a request about medium, not a warning about size. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different asset produced by a different route, either a re trace from a selection made on the unlit half of the plate where ink and ground separate, or a colour accurate plate rather than the two colour trace, or a decision to reproduce the mark larger and re compose the checklist masthead around it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re derive the mark by a different selection and polarity, or accept a larger reproduction size and re author the masthead around it, re inject the viewBox and strip the ground path again, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every page from the returned markup rather than from the first page alone.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A checklist going out with the press list carrying a gallery mark that has filled in and lost its rule, which is the one element on the document that is the institution rather than the exhibition.

price_band_and_audience: A casual premium wood fired grill, mains around thirty four dollars, walk in diners deciding in the time it takes to scroll past. The band is load bearing: at thirty four dollars the grade is warm, the cut is fast, the food fills the frame and the type is bold and immediate, because the job of the reel is appetite in two seconds. The same footage cut for a two hundred dollar tasting menu would correctly be slow, cool, quiet, sparse and hands only, with type set small and set back, and shipping that treatment here reads as a room this restaurant is not and empties it. Push the other way into a value grill and the correct treatment is price led, saturated and busy with a deal burned across the frame, which at thirty four dollars reads as a discount and undercuts the room. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 600 to 1,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: What fire does to good meat.
brand_identity.sector: Food and beverage: a wood fired neighbourhood grill serving walk-in trade and delivery, opening a second room.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A single-room wood fired grill on the west side of Providence, Rhode Island, opening its second room in launch week, run by a small owner-operator team.
brand_identity.about: Ember and Oak is a wood fired grill on the west side of Providence, one hearth you can see from every table, mains around thirty four dollars. Launch week opens the second room. The brand is fire, char and appetite: warm, loud and alive, built to make somebody hungry in the first two seconds.
brand_identity.audience: Walk-in diners on the west side deciding in the time it takes to scroll past, plus delivery orders. Neighbourhood people who want a room that feels alive, not a tasting menu and not a value grill.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A casual premium wood fired grill, mains around thirty four dollars. The grade runs warm, the cut is fast, the food fills the frame and the type is bold and immediate. Never moody fine dining, never a discount grill with a deal burned across the frame.
brand_identity.typography: A bold, warm display face for dish names and the end card, set large and immediate, paired with a sturdy sans for the one-line description and price. The type has to carry over fire behind it: confident, appetite-first, never a restrained editorial serif.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, direct, hungry. Short lines with heat in them. Example line the brand would write: 'The chop, the char, the fire you can see from your table. Second room now open.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The mark survives only as a small raster: a two word lockup inside a thin ring, sitting on a cream square baked into the picture rather than behind it. It has to be recovered as clean, placeable artwork before it can go on the end card or the window poster.
brand_identity.values: Appetite and honesty: show the real food from the real service, and make the room feel like what it is. The reel should read like the room smells.

Four-second product launch edit and a consistent eight-bowl photo set

Ironwood Kitchen has one short product clip available for this commission. Please build a deliberate edit of no more than four seconds, not a longer launch film assembled from material we have not supplied.

The photographic side is equally important: eight bowls need a shared bright treatment and usable crops for both the tiles and the line sheet. Removing a reference card must not clip the bowl itself.

A deliberate 4-second-or-shorter edit assembled from the 1 supplied short clip using an explicit timeline, plus one platform reframe and three checked poster frames. Source time ranges must come from motion_source_metadata.json and a task-specific edit decision list. The supplied video files contain no audio streams; use a separate supplied WAV only where one exists and never infer dialogue from silent footage.

Eight bowl masters brought to one bright house target, one white point, one black point, one brightness and one crop logic, delivered at both the tile ratio and the line sheet picture ratio, with no grey card anywhere in frame and no bowl clipped by the crop that removed it. Per frame parameter log, including one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours and which cards could not be trusted.

The inputs are source_video_files/ (1 measured short file); motion_source_metadata.json; ironwood_bowls/ (8 stills, 6000 x 4000); ironwood_linesheet_2027.pdf; ironwood_skus.csv; ironwood_wordmark.png; ironwood_notes.txt.

Handover: a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the final edit decision list and measured source metadata. source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork recurring role posting for a creative partner serving meal prep and caterer businesses, quoted in the ledger grounding_note, whose listed deliverable scope was short form video ads, vertical short form and feed video content, product showcase videos and video resizing or adaptation, plus the graphic design line items paid social ads, website banners and assets, branding assets and promotional creatives, with turnaround weighted as the success metric. That posting is a retainer shaped list rather than one job, so the honest fuller commission is the launch it exists to service: one product line going live at once on the counter, on the delivery tiles, in the drivers' printed sheet and in paid social. The post names no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional brand Ironwood Kitchen. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes the printed half real rather than asserted: a printer's press PDF converts into a live InDesign merge template headlessly, so the client's own last season artwork becomes the template rather than something invented, and HTML authoring returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, which is what the weekly rotating caption card actually needs.

The post names no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional brand Ironwood Kitchen. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes the printed half real rather than asserted: a printer's press PDF converts into a live InDesign merge template headlessly, so the client's own last season artwork becomes the template rather than something invented, and HTML authoring returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, which is what the weekly rotating caption card actually needs.
price_band_and_audience: Twelve dollar grab and go bowls, buyer 24 to 45 on an office lunch run with about eleven minutes to spend. The band is load bearing: at this price the work has to read bright, high key, clean and fast, food photographed close to how it looks in the case under fridge light, type large and plain, one claim per card. The same eight bowls at a thirty two dollar chef counter band would correctly be graded down, shot warmer and darker with negative space and small quiet type, and shipping that treatment here reads slow and expensive and empties a lunch rush. Push the other way into saturated primaries, drop shadows and burst badges and it becomes a mall food court, which contradicts the macro led claim the whole line is sold on. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Real lunch, in the case by half ten
brand_identity.sector: Fast casual grab and go: high protein meal prep bowls sold from a counter case and by office park delivery.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019, Providence, Rhode Island, two counters and three office park delivery routes run by a small kitchen crew.
brand_identity.about: Ironwood Kitchen builds honest, high protein bowls for the office lunch run, in the fridge case by mid morning and gone by early afternoon. We are a working kitchen, not a tasting room. The promise is simple: food you would actually eat at your desk, twelve dollars, nothing invented and nothing dressed up.
brand_identity.audience: Office workers 24 to 45 on a weekday lunch run with roughly eleven minutes to spend, buying on macros, speed and trust rather than on spectacle.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Twelve dollars a bowl, the everyday middle of grab and go. Above a supermarket meal deal, well below a chef counter. We are not a tasting menu and never pretend to be one.
brand_identity.typography: One plain, high legibility grotesque sans carries everything, set large and tight. Names and prices sit big and quiet, one claim per card, no scripts and no display flourish. The type should read from arm's length in a fridge case.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, warm, counter honest, one thought per line. Example: "Twelve bucks, in the case by half ten, gone by two. That is the whole promise."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No brand kit survives. The wordmark exists only as a flat picture on a white ground, exported by a designer who has since left, with no vector file and no source anywhere. Everything else is a photograph or a spreadsheet.
brand_identity.values: Feed people well and tell the truth about what is in the bowl. The allergen line and the macros are not marketing, they are the deal.

price_band_and_audience: Fifty nine dollars a month on subscription, buyer 25 to 40, health literate and specifically sceptical of polish. The band is load bearing in an unusual direction: the money is real but the look must be cheap, because at subscription economics the acquisition cost is decided by whether the ad survives being recognised as an ad. Grade lightly, keep the phone framing, keep the room noise short of unintelligible, set the hooks in plain type at conversational length. The same product at a hundred and forty dollars a month would correctly be shot in a studio, graded cool and clean, with restrained type and generous space, and shipping that treatment here reads as a company pretending to be a person, which is the single most expensive mistake available on this brief. Push the other way into flashing text, countdowns and stacked badges and it reads as a fifteen dollar tub, which contradicts the subscription price. A posted job of this shape runs 700 to 1,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Direct to consumer daily greens powder sold online on a monthly subscription, creator seeded.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2023, Portland, Oregon, online only, a small founder led team with a growth lead and three seeded creators.
brand_identity.about: Halden Greens is a daily greens powder people actually keep drinking, sold by subscription to buyers who have already been let down by a supplement that promised too much. We grow by putting the product in real kitchens and letting real people talk, not by looking like an advert. That distrust of polish is the brand.
brand_identity.audience: Health literate adults 25 to 40 who are specifically wary of supplement marketing and trust a friend's recommendation over a glossy campaign.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Fifty nine dollars a month on subscription. Priced as a considered daily habit, above the fifteen dollar tub and below the studio shot premium brands. The money is real, so the look must never be.
brand_identity.typography: One friendly, near neutral sans set at conversational size, plain weights only. Type should look unconsidered while being entirely considered: no countdowns, no stacked badges, no burst text. Hooks read like a caption a person typed, not a headline.
brand_identity.voice: Conversational, honest to a fault, a little self aware, never hype. Example: "We are not going to tell you it changed our life. It is greens. You drink them in the morning."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark exists only as a flat export, dark disjoint letters on white, with no vector source. The brand green panel is fixed and every cutout has to hold against it. Some earlier photography still shows a previous tub label and should not be reused.

A concise property-tour cut, evening stills and the active-listing card run

Sable & Finch needs a tightly scoped listing package: a tour edit from seven short clips, matching evening exterior stills and a twelve-listing open-house card run. Please keep the photographic and video treatment coherent without making one property stand in for another.

Tour and platform reframe
A deliberate 24-second-or-shorter edit assembled from the 7 supplied short clips using an explicit timeline, plus one platform reframe and three checked poster frames. Source time ranges must come from motion_source_metadata.json and a task-specific edit decision list. The supplied video files contain no audio streams; use a separate supplied WAV only where one exists and never infer dialogue from silent footage.

Evening exteriors and covers
The dusk exteriors brought to one warm evening target (one white point, one black point, one treatment of the lit porch against the sky), plus one licensed camera-scale streetscape frame graded into the same world, and from that set the cover still and the listing thumbnail cut without enlargement. Per frame parameter log, including one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours and which frames could not be brought.

Printed cards
One press PDF at one page per listing for all twelve active listings, derived from the team's own printed card, with every mapped field verified present in the template before the merge and every page proofed after it. No record truncated at the measure, the brokerage disclosure line on every page, plus per record proofs for the four agents to check their own listings and a 300 dpi proof raster.

The video is limited to twenty-four seconds and the supplied media. The cards have a separate data requirement: all twelve active listings, complete fields and the brokerage disclosure on every page. Check the converted template before merging and the exported pages afterwards.

price_band_and_audience: A 1.2 million dollar coastal single family listing sold to move up buyers aged roughly 35 to 48 with children, choosing between three or four comparable houses in the same school district. The band is load bearing. At this price the tour has to be slow, warm and near neutral, with long held frames, restrained captioning and an evening cover: the buyer is reassuring herself about a large decision, and calm reads as confidence. Push the same material into a saturated, fast cut, caption heavy treatment with hard cuts on every beat and it reads as a 400,000 dollar starter home listing and the move up buyer stops watching, which is the exact failure the team is paying to avoid. Push the other way into a near silent, near black, no text luxury film and it misprices the house upward and confuses buyers who genuinely need the bed count and the school district on screen. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Residential real estate: a boutique agent team listing coastal single family homes on Massachusetts' North Shore.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, Marblehead, Massachusetts, a four agent residential team running four or five listings a month.
brand_identity.about: Sable and Finch Realty sells character homes along the North Shore to move up families who are choosing carefully between a small number of houses. We present a property the way a buyer wants to feel about it: calm, warm and reassuring. Our work is quiet on purpose, because at this price calm reads as confidence.
brand_identity.audience: Move up buyers roughly 35 to 48 with children, weighing this house against three or four comparable homes in the same school district, who need the facts on screen and the feeling in the frame.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Homes around and above 1.2 million dollars, the established coastal middle of the market. Presentation sits between a fast starter home listing and a near silent luxury film, and must read as neither.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet, warm text serif for names and headings paired with a restrained sans for facts and captions. Type stays small and calm: address, price, beds and baths and school district carried plainly, never loud, never dense. Evening warmth over crisp cool.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, measured, reassuring, never a hard sell. Example: "Two streets back from the water, shingled, and the porch light is already on."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no packaged brand kit. Last season's open house card survives only as the printer's press PDF, and the on screen captions have always been rebuilt by hand each listing. Colour and type live in prior collateral rather than in a guideline anyone can hand over.
brand_identity.values: Honest presentation of a real property. Every figure a buyer relies on, the price, the bed and bath count, the school district and the disclosure line, must be exactly right on every piece.

assets_supplied.kind: Dusk exterior stills of the house shot by the team's photographer across about twenty minutes of falling light.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The dusk exteriors. Our favourite is the one with the porch lights on."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The two frames the team likes best were exposed for the lit porch interior, so the sky across the upper third is clipped flat and a highlight recovery move on those frames returns a result in which nothing visibly changes. Separately one of the two is about two and a half degrees off level, and levelling it eats exactly the roofline that the cover crop needs to keep, so straightening and cropping cannot both be satisfied on that frame.

assets_supplied.name: sablefinch_open_house_card.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The team's existing printed open house card from last season, supplied as the template for the run.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's card. We want the same card for every listing."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Printed, the card shows four clearly separated blocks. Its text was actually set as one continuous flow, so the conversion exposes far coarser frame granularity than the printed page suggests. Worse, the mapping readout omits one run from the middle of that story while keeping its line break, so the readout still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly the length of the dropped run. The validator returns valid on those offsets and the placeholder step reports success, and the fields past the omission simply never land.

assets_supplied.name: sablefinch_listings.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Twelve active listings: address, town, price, beds, baths, square feet, school district, open house window, agent line.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All twelve of our current listings. The open house times are already correct."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three of the twelve addresses are long enough that at trim they run past the card's fixed measure. A fixed text frame does not spill and does not flag: it simply stops rendering, so those records come out truncated in the middle of a street name while the merge reports success and the page count is exactly right. One further row carries a price with a range rather than a single figure, which reads as an error on a printed card.

assets_supplied.name: sablefinch_mark_scan.png
assets_supplied.kind: The Sable and Finch lockup, a small finch perched on a branch emblem beside the SABLE AND FINCH wordmark, the only surviving copy, exported small from the team's old email signature.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our little finch logo. We only have this one small copy of it, off an old email footer."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a low resolution raster with soft anti aliased edges and a faint halo, and the mark is Finch Gold sitting on a Shell ground at low contrast. A default trace reads the halo as edge and returns a furry multi node outline, and at that low contrast a luminance or ink level selection closes the finch's eye counter and merges the fine branch strokes. Nothing shows at screen size: the trace looks clean until it is placed at the card's roughly fourteen millimetre lockup and the end card size, where the eye fills in and the branch gaps close. The mark has to be selected by its own gold hue and thresholded to a clean bi level before the trace, and confirmed at reproduction size rather than on screen.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Adapted from a real Upwork post in which a top producing luxury real estate broker running an online video channel (market insight pieces plus property walkthroughs, three or four a month) asks for a per video content package: a click worthy on brand thumbnail that is explicitly NOT a generic headshot with a text box, a cinematic cold open teaser that is cross postable as a square, and a consistent branded end card, all with luxury brand restraint and a 48 to 72 hour turnaround. The real post named no company, so the brokerage is laundered to the coined fictional wordmark Sterling Row and the broker stays an unnamed figure. REASONABLY ENRICHED into the fuller commission that client genuinely needed rather than three assets per video: the reason every video looks like a different person made it is that the source photography was never brought to one look, so the engagement leads with the eight mixed light hero stills; the reason the end card cannot simply be typeset is that the only surviving version of the wordmark is a photograph of a brass plaque in the lobby; and the same nine residences need a printed card each off the developer's existing spec sheet. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that honest: an ink level trace off photographed printed artwork recovers a real mark, HTML authoring produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, and a real press PDF converts into a live merge template headlessly.

price_band_and_audience: Full floor residences from just over 4 million dollars, sold to ultra high net worth buyers who are typically buying their third or fourth property and who are reassured rather than persuaded. The band is load bearing in a specific direction: at this tier the grade sits near neutral and slightly cool with clean whites and no crushed blacks, motion is slow and largely static, on screen text is minimal and small, and the wordmark reproduces at a size that would look timid on any other listing. Ship the same material with a saturated warm grade, fast cuts, large benefit captions and a price burned across the frame and it reads as a mass market development, and a UHNW buyer reads that as a building that is struggling to sell, which is precisely the impression that ends a 4 million dollar conversation. Push the other way into pure atmosphere with no unit information at all and the broker loses the qualified buyer who needs to know which floor and how many square feet before she will ask for a viewing. A posted job of this shape runs 1,500 to 3,500 dollars fixed, on a 48 to 72 hour cycle.

brand_identity.about: Sterling Row is nine full floor residences in a converted warehouse block, starting just over four million dollars, sold to buyers who are not in a hurry and have seen everything. The channel is where most buyers first meet the broker, so every piece has to feel made by one hand. Restraint is the whole proposition: these buyers are reassured, not persuaded.

brand_identity.price_positioning: Full floor residences from just over four million dollars, the top of the market. Presentation sits near neutral and deliberately small: anything that looks like a promotion reads, at this tier, as a building that is struggling to sell.
brand_identity.typography: One reassuring, near neutral pairing that avoids both extremes: no high contrast display serif that reads as a perfume advert, no heavy grotesque that reads as a development brochure. Text sits small and calm, the wordmark reproduces modestly, on screen copy is minimal by rule.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, composed, confident without pressure. Example: "Nine residences. Full floor. Sold one at a time, to buyers in no hurry."

There is no vector file and no clean scan. The developer's spec sheet exists only as a printed PDF, and the disclosure wording is fixed and cannot be changed.

assets_supplied.kind: Hero photographs of the residences, five from the building's architectural photographer and three taken by the sales team on a phone.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Eight hero rooms. Five are the photographer's and three are ours, which you will notice."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The three sales team frames are substantially smaller than the channel's cover specification, so a cover cut from one of them reaches size only by interpolation, which the crop tool performs up to a hard cap while reporting it solely inside its own returned tradeoffs and never in a message or a warning. Separately two of the photographer's frames were lit tungsten against blue hour glass, so no single white point serves both the room and the window: correcting the room takes the city outside green, and correcting the window takes the room grey.

assets_supplied.name: sterlingrow_lobby_plaque.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the cast brass Sterling Row wordmark mounted on a dark stone lobby wall, lit from one side.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only version of our wordmark anybody can find. It is on the wall in the lobby."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Brass on dark stone runs close in value across the lit half of the plaque, and it is a disjoint wordmark on a photographed substrate rather than a flat scan. A prompt naming the plaque returns the plaque rather than the letters, background removal on lettering keeps only a fragment or two because subject detection needs one coherent blob, and the resulting trace looks clean and open at canvas size while its counters behave differently at the size the mark actually reproduces on a near black end card.

A fixed frame does not spill and does not flag: it stops rendering, so that record comes out cut mid figure while the merge reports success and the page count is exactly right.

A short Lesson 4 excerpt and three purposeful catalogue stills

Meridian Academy teaches operations analytics to working managers. The audience is watching after a working day, so the excerpt should be clear and economical rather than styled like an energetic bootcamp advertisement.

This commission uses six short supplied clips for a maximum twenty-one-second edit. It is not a request to produce a complete lesson or invent missing teaching dialogue.

Source time ranges must come from motion_source_metadata.json and a task-specific edit decision list. source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com 'Online Course / Explainer Video Editor' post carried in the ledger, whose verbatim intent is that an editor is handed a recorded talking head lecture plus slide decks and screen recordings and must cut them into a clean professional lesson video, trimming filler and dead air, cutting between the presenter and the on screen material, adding title cards, lower thirds and on screen key point captions, and exporting a 16:9 course master plus a course catalogue thumbnail. That client wanted a lesson, not a clip. REASONABLY ENRICHED and REPOSITIONED for connector reality, which changes what the honest fuller commission is in three ways. The connector cannot composite a lower third onto a video track, so the key point caption system is delivered as a genuinely editable card set on the HTML to Express surface, which is what the real client actually needed anyway (their previous editor handed back a flattened picture they could not change per cohort). The connector cannot trim to a timestamp, so the tightening is done by the shortening route, which chooses its own retained set and therefore has to be inspected rather than trusted. And the academy's crest survives only on printed certificates, so the identity is recovered off a photograph rather than reinvented. No real academy, person or trademark is named; the line is laundered to the coined fictional Meridian Academy, and Freelancer.com is only the sourcing platform.

price_band_and_audience: A two hundred and ninety dollar self paced professional course sold to working adults aged thirty to fifty who are paying with their own money and watching late at night. The band is load bearing. At this price the learner expects a competent, quiet, adult production: legible screen material, a voice that sounds like a person in a room rather than a podcast studio, restrained type, and a thumbnail that promises a working skill rather than a transformation. The same lesson at a nineteen dollar impulse band would correctly be cut fast and bright with arrows, zooms, high contrast captions and a face reaction thumbnail, and shipping that treatment here reads as content marketing and triggers refunds from managers who bought a tool. Push the other way into a university register, slow pacing, a serif institutional crest and a lecture hall thumbnail, and it misprices a course a person finishes on a laptop in four evenings. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Practical skills for people who already have a job.
brand_identity.sector: Professional education (self-paced online academy)
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2021 in Portland, Oregon. A four person team running one course.
brand_identity.about: Meridian Academy sells a single self-paced program, Operations Analytics for Working Managers, at two hundred and ninety dollars. Our learners are thirty to fifty, mid-career, watching lessons late at night after their own workday. We are not a bootcamp and we are not a university. We teach one useful thing well and we respect the viewer's time and intelligence.
brand_identity.audience: Working managers aged thirty to fifty, paying with their own money, fitting the course around a full-time job. They want a working skill, not a transformation story, and they distrust anything that feels like marketing.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid-market. A two hundred and ninety dollar considered purchase. The register sits between an impulse-priced tutorial and a formal institution: competent, quiet, self-funded professional development.
brand_identity.typography: One restrained type system across every card and still: a plain, legible workhorse for body and captions, paired with a slightly more characterful face for titles. No display gimmicks, generous size for late-night laptop reading.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, warm, matter of fact. Speaks to a peer, not a beginner. Short sentences, no hype, no exclamation. The tone of a good colleague explaining something over coffee.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Brand files are largely gone. When we changed studios the original crest design file was lost, and the mark now survives only on the completion certificates we had printed two years ago: an enclosed laurel ring with small caps type set inside it and a rule beneath, in one deep ink on cream stock. We would like it recovered as artwork we can use at any size. No usable logo vector, colour spec sheet or type licence exists on our side.
brand_identity.values: Respect for the learner's time, honesty about what the course does and does not cover, and production that is clear and quiet rather than loud.

price_band_and_audience: A one hundred and forty dollar per seat per month B2B product bought by a committee of three in finance and operations, with a procurement review in the middle of the cycle. The band is load bearing. At this price the buyer is looking for evidence of seriousness, so the kit has to be quiet, specific and legible: a founder who sounds like she knows the domain, press frames that show the actual product, a printed card that looks like it came from a company with a controller, and type that is plain rather than expressive. The same product at a nine dollar self serve band would correctly be launched loud, bright, animated and benefit led, and shipping that here reads as consumer marketing and lengthens the sales cycle because the committee stops believing the numbers. Push the other way into enterprise grey, stock boardrooms and a dense capability matrix and it misprices a product an operations lead adopts in an afternoon. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Workflow automation for finance and operations.
brand_identity.sector: Technology, B2B SaaS (workflow automation)
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2022 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. An eleven person company with no in-house designer.
brand_identity.about: Norvant is workflow automation built for finance and operations teams. Seats are one hundred and forty dollars a month, and nothing gets bought without three people signing off, so everything we put out has to look like it was made by people who know what they are doing. We are a small team shipping a serious tool, and our March release is the work the whole company has been building toward.
brand_identity.audience: A buying committee of three in finance and operations, with a procurement review mid-cycle. They are looking for evidence of seriousness and real numbers, and they lengthen the cycle the moment something feels like consumer marketing.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Considered B2B mid-market. One hundred and forty dollars per seat per month, committee-approved. Not self-serve impulse software, and not heavyweight enterprise. A tool an operations lead can adopt in an afternoon and defend to a controller.
brand_identity.typography: One quiet, credible type system across the cards, the announcement set and the handover: a plain neutral face for detail and body, a measured companion for headings. Nothing expressive, nothing decorative. Legibility at small print sizes matters more than personality.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, specific, confident without selling. States what the product does and lets the facts carry it. No stock smiles, no superlatives. Tells people directly what is and is not true.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Brand files went with the agency that made them. The mark now survives only as the sign on our reception wall: a hexring glyph beside the wordmark, cut in slate on a brushed metal panel. Last year's regional event card exists only as the print-ready file we sent to the printer. We need the mark recovered as scalable artwork and this year's card run rebuilt from last year's file so it matches. No editable logo source, colour build or master template remains on our side.
brand_identity.values: Seriousness you can verify, restraint over noise, and plain honesty about what we could and could not do.

price_band_and_audience: Enterprise security software at forty to ninety thousand dollars a year, bought by a CISO or IT director with a security engineer reading over their shoulder. The band is load-bearing: at this price the whole treatment has to be restrained, precise and quiet, with the product interface legible at the size a buyer actually watches it, muted neutrals against the platform's own dark navy, one accent, and claims that read as cleared rather than sold. brand_identity.tagline: Catch the risky moment. Coach it away.
brand_identity.sector: Enterprise cybersecurity software (human cyber risk platform, SaaS)
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2022 in Denver, Colorado. Roughly 40 people, venture-backed, entering its first full launch quarter.
brand_identity.about: SentinelMesh reduces human cyber risk for regulated enterprises. The platform watches for the risky moment, runs an adaptive simulation, and coaches the person in real time, closing the gap between security policy and daily behavior. We sell to CISOs and IT directors on annual contracts and we win on trust, precision, and proof that the product does what we say.
brand_identity.audience: CISOs, IT directors, and the security engineers reading over their shoulder at mid-market and enterprise organizations. Technical, skeptical, and short on patience for hype.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Premium enterprise. Annual contracts from 40,000 to 90,000 dollars. Everything we ship has to read as a considered purchase a security leader can defend internally, never as a self-serve consumer app.
brand_identity.typography: A single humanist sans family across headings and body, set with generous spacing and modest weight contrast. No display faces, no condensed heads. Numerals and interface labels stay legible at the size a buyer actually reads them.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, exact, and calm. We state what the product does and let it read as cleared rather than sold. We avoid fear language, exclamation, and buzzwords. One accent, one idea per line.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our designer built the original identity and left the company, and that working file left with him. What survives is a flat export of the mark on white and a phone photo of our trade show banner, neither of which is the source artwork. The mark needs to be rebuilt as usable artwork that sits correctly on our dark navy ground.
brand_identity.values: Trust earned through evidence, restraint over spectacle, clarity for a technical buyer, and claims that are cleared before they are spoken.

A four-second episode short and a clean still set for Voltcast

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, 'Tech Channel Video Editor Needed', from an independent consumer-tech review channel that publishes 'several times a week', needs 'both long-form reviews (8-12 minutes) and short vertical cuts for YouTube Shorts, Reels and TikTok', wants 'a 16:9 master ... plus a reformatted 9:16 or 1:1 version', supplies '4K footage, screen recordings, b-roll and a rough talking-head guide', and asks for thumbnails and channel branding that read on-brand across the grid. The channel, host, episode and every product in it are invented and IP-clean; Voltcast and Voltcast Media are coined. The posted job reads as a cutting job, which is what made the earlier version of this task sit almost entirely on one surface. The fuller commission the same client genuinely needs is the one the post's own last clause implies: the thumbnail and the on-screen furniture are what the grid is judged on, and they have to read as the same channel as the video. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that honest, because HTML authoring now returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, which is the only form in which a channel publishing several times a week can actually reuse a card set instead of rebuilding it.
