The posted job reads as a cutting job, which is what made the earlier version of this task sit almost entirely on one surface. The fuller commission the same client genuinely needs is the one the post's own last clause implies: the thumbnail and the on-screen furniture are what the grid is judged on, and they have to read as the same channel as the video. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that honest, because HTML authoring now returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, which is the only form in which a channel publishing several times a week can actually reuse a card set instead of rebuilding it.
price_band_and_audience: An ad and sponsor-funded independent review channel with a mid six-figure subscriber base, where a sponsor integration is worth a few thousand dollars and renewal depends on how the segment looks. The band is load-bearing: at this level the look has to read as a credible independent reviewer, confident and plain, with real product photography, restrained on-screen furniture and type that sits out of the way of the thing being reviewed. Push it up into broadcast-grade motion design, glossy sweeps and a full lower-third package and the channel stops reading as independent, which is the entire reason its audience trusts a shootout. Push it down into raw phone-shot energy with mismatched cards and the sponsor does not renew, which is the stated commercial risk. The same three products covered by a manufacturer's own marketing channel would correctly look glossier and more produced, and shipping that treatment here reads as an advertorial. A posted job of this shape runs 600 to 1,600 dollars per episode package.

brand_identity.sector: Independent consumer-technology review channel (media, sponsor-funded)
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Started 2020 in Portland, Oregon. A two-person operation with a mid six-figure subscriber base, publishing several times a week.
brand_identity.about: Voltcast is an independent consumer-tech review channel run by two people out of Portland. We buy or borrow the gear, run it hard, and say what we actually think. Episodes go out long-form to the main feed plus vertical and square shorts. About a third of the revenue is sponsor money, so the grid has to look like one channel and the sponsor read has to be exactly right.
brand_identity.audience: Enthusiast buyers and everyday shoppers who want an honest verdict before they spend. They follow us because we are not the manufacturer, and they can tell the difference.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid-tier creator economy. A sponsor integration is worth a few thousand dollars and renewal depends on how the segment looks. The channel has to read as a credible independent reviewer, never as broadcast gloss and never as raw phone-shot filler.
brand_identity.typography: A sturdy grotesque sans for headings and callouts, paired with a clean readable sans for body and specs. Type stays out of the way of the product being reviewed. Spec numbers read cleanly at small sizes.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, dry, and unhyped. We talk like a person who has actually used the thing. Sponsor copy runs as written and the disclosure line is exact. We never oversell.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The channel bug exists only as a flat export on white and we have no editable brand kit. On-screen cards get rebuilt from scratch every episode, which is the problem we want solved. We need the bug prepared as reusable artwork and the card set delivered as a file we can reopen and change each week.
brand_identity.values: Independence from the manufacturers we cover, honesty about what we tested, consistency across the grid, and respect for the audience that trusts the verdict.

assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our bug. It goes on everything. It is always small."

Nothing about the file at full size predicts it.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com YouTube podcast post carried in the ledger, where a two person show hands over raw episode recordings and asks for episodes shaped into something watchable, for light hearted graphics that match a casual fun vibe, for the client's existing logo carried across the channel branding, and for any custom graphic assets created to be delivered separately in transparent PNG or vector form. Two literal asks in that post are not connector work and are re cast honestly rather than faked. A timeline trim of pauses and stumbles has no connector analogue, because the shortening tool works from engagement rather than from timestamps, so the short vertical pieces are produced by that route and the brief asks for short cuts rather than for a re edited episode. Motion graphics composited over the picture are also unavailable, so the caption plate and the end card are delivered as editable canvases the show drops into its own editor, and the brief asks for a plate rather than for burned in captions. Everything else in that post is now genuinely producible: CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) confirms an ink level recovery off photographed printed collateral, a merge template reverse engineered out of a flat press PDF, and a native editable Express document carrying mixed canvas sizes, which is exactly the separately delivered, client editable asset set the poster asked for and never got.

price_band_and_audience: Independent long form podcast, eight dollar monthly membership, one modest renewing sponsor, listeners thirty to fifty. The band is load bearing. At this level the look has to read considered and hand made: warm domestic light, real texture in the room, restrained type, the picture of two people talking rather than a set. Push it toward broadcast, with a hard lit black seamless, a hard geometric grid and a network style lockup, and it misrepresents a two person show to the exact membership that pays for it because it is not that. Push it the other way into a scrappy meme treatment, with heavy outlines, arrows and shouted type, and it reads as the wrong genre entirely for a fifty minute interview and the sponsor renewal argument collapses. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even when every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Independent long form interview podcast with a YouTube channel, one guest per episode, made and recorded in the show's own room.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Started 2021 in Portland, Oregon. A two person show: two hosts, one room, nine episodes a season.
brand_identity.about: DAYDRIFT is a slow, unhurried interview show built around one guest and one real conversation that runs the better part of an hour. It is made by two people in a room they know well, funded by a small paying membership and one renewing sponsor. The promise is intimacy: you are sitting in on a talk between people who like each other, not watching a broadcast.
brand_identity.audience: Regular listeners aged thirty to fifty, most of them listening at work through the day. About two hundred paying members at eight dollars a month, plus a few thousand free listeners who click through to the channel page.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Membership at eight dollars a month with one modest renewing sponsor. Squarely independent: above hobby, well below a network production. The look must read considered and hand made, never broadcast and never scrappy meme.
brand_identity.typography: A warm humanist serif for the show name and episode titles, paired with a quiet humanist sans for credits, dates and body. Generous spacing, restrained weights, nothing condensed or shouted. Type should feel like a good paperback, not a title card.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, warm and a little understated, the way two friends actually talk. We never oversell a guest. Example line the brand would write: "Episode eight. We sat down with her for an hour and did not want it to end."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There are no brand files left. The show name only survives as artwork on the foam flag on the microphone, drawn years ago by a friend who has since moved away and left no source file. Last season's printed episode card exists only as the print file the printer returned. Everything else has to be rebuilt from those.
brand_identity.values: Honesty and warmth over polish. The show would rather be small and real than slick, and it wants a look it can keep running itself next season without re commissioning.

STATIC FOX lives or dies in the feed. We need six thumbnails that read quickly as our channel while still giving each supplied episode title a clear, distinct treatment. The competitor sheet is reference, not a composition or character library to copy.

Thumbnail family
Six platform thumbnails built from the supplied episode titles, mascot render, channel patch, and competitor reference sheet. The family must be recognizably STATIC FOX without copying a competitor's character, claims, composition, or typography; each title must remain readable at feed size.

Mascot and emblem preparation
A clean transparent mascot cutout, a one-color raster proof of the fox emblem recovered only as far as the photographed patch supports, and light/dark application tests. No claim of production vector readiness is permitted.

Animated title/end-card
One 5 to 8 second animated title/end-card treatment adapted from a professionally selected Adobe Express template, using the approved STATIC FOX title, mascot, and palette. Deliver the editable design and final export; no source video or speech is implied.

Please test the titles at feed size, where the real decision happens. The photographed patch only supports a limited raster recovery of the emblem; do not label it a production-ready vector. The mascot needs clean transparency and proof on both light and dark applications.

Assets and titles: motion_source_metadata.json; staticfox_scrap_render.png; staticfox_patch.jpg; staticfox_titles.txt; staticfox_refs.png.

Media inventory: 0 video files, 0 seconds in total; 0 with embedded audio; 0 separate audio files (0 seconds). These measured sources set the production limits.

There is no implied source footage or speech here. The motion piece is a five-to-eight-second template adaptation, and we need its editable design as well as the export.

Budget: $1,000-$3,000 fixed. Target: 7 to 15 business days. Reviews: One technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

The final package should contain a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the final edit decision list and measured source metadata, with every source file accounted for, including references and rejected or superseded material. Use the approved information without inventing missing facts. Only the stated stock or concept exceptions permit substitution; document every omission, replacement, reconciliation and material quality compromise. Keep runtime within measured source duration and the stated cap; do not invent footage or dialogue.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com comedy gameplay post carried in the ledger, where a creator supplies raw captures plus rough notes and their own custom graphics and asks for an entertaining fast paced upload with reaction zooms, on screen text call outs and meme cutaways, a thumbnail, and a reusable project file they can keep working in. Four of the literal asks in that post sit on the connector's not available list and are re cast honestly rather than faked: timeline trims to flagged timestamps, animated reaction zooms, motion graphic call outs composited over the picture, and meme overlays burned into the video. What survives is the part that post was actually paying for and never articulated, which is a channel front that looks like one channel: the reaction zoom becomes a punched in still crop on the thumbnail, the call out becomes a title plate the creator drops into their own editor, the meme cutaway is dropped as undeliverable and said so, and the reusable project file becomes a native editable document carrying every canvas at its own size. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes the rest real: an ink level recovery off a photographed embroidered patch, a knockout that can be inspected and re routed where it bites, and mixed canvas authoring into a document the creator opens and edits themselves.

price_band_and_audience: Mid tier comedy gaming channel, advertising and membership income, audience fifteen to twenty five. The band is load bearing in the opposite direction from most commissions. At this genre and this audience the work has to be loud: saturated, high contrast, faces large in frame, type heavy and unembarrassed, because that is what wins the click in a crowded feed. A restrained, tasteful, low saturation treatment with generous white space is a correct looking wrong answer that signals the wrong channel entirely and suppresses the only metric the creator is paying to move. Push the other way past loud into pure noise, with every element outlined, arrowed, glowing and shouting at once, and the grid stops reading as one channel at all, which is the exact problem the creator hired someone to fix. The judgement is loud AND coherent, and an agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even where every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 700 to 1,600 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Co op disasters and bad decisions.
brand_identity.sector: Mid tier comedy gaming YouTube channel: co op gameplay, reaction humour and a weekly members stream.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Running since 2019 out of Manchester, England. One creator with a home setup, six uploads a month plus a Sunday members stream.
brand_identity.about: STATIC FOX is a loud, fast comedy gaming channel built on co op chaos and the creator's on camera reactions. Around four hundred thousand subscribers watch for the disasters, the bad calls and the running jokes. The videos land once people click, so the whole brand fight happens on the thumbnail, in the feed, at a glance.
brand_identity.audience: Mostly fifteen to twenty five, watching in a crowded feed on phones. They want energy and payoff, not taste. Income comes from advertising and channel memberships.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid tier creator funded by ad revenue and memberships. The work has to be loud, saturated and heavy on the face and the moment, because that is what wins the click at this level. Restrained and tasteful reads as the wrong channel; pure noise stops reading as one channel at all. Loud and coherent is the line.
brand_identity.typography: A heavy condensed display face for titles that has to punch at thumbnail scale and survive both very short and very long titles, paired with a bold grotesque for supporting lines. Big, tight, unembarrassed. No delicate or editorial type anywhere.
brand_identity.voice: Fast, funny, self deprecating and a bit chaotic, always in on the joke. Example line the brand would write: "We had one job. We did not do the job. New one up now."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The mascot, Scrap the fox in a headset, was drawn two years ago and survives only as a flat shaded render on a dark panel, with no clean cutout. The merch fox head emblem's original file is long gone and exists only as a photo of the embroidered patch on the creator's hoodie. There is no brand kit; titles and catchphrases live in a text file.
brand_identity.values: Repeatability and independence. The creator wants a set that looks like one channel and a file they can keep editing themselves, so they never have to pay for a new one when a title changes.

assets_supplied.kind: machine-readable source inventory

assets_supplied.name: staticfox_scrap_render.png
assets_supplied.kind: The channel mascot, a fox in a headset, drawn two years ago and supplied as a flat shaded render sitting on a dark gradient panel.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Scrap. He goes on everything. This is the only file I have of him."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Scrap is outlined in a deep navy that sits close in value to the dark panel he was rendered on, so the one call knockout hands back a complete looking cutout that has quietly bitten the tail tip and one ear. It reads as correct at preview scale and only shows at full resolution against a light ground. The render also carries a soft glow baked into its own pixels, which comes away as a grey fringe wherever the cutout lands on anything pale.

assets_supplied.name: staticfox_patch.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of the channel's merch patch, a fox head emblem embroidered in three thread colours, worn on the creator's hoodie.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The emblem off my merch. The original file is long gone."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The emblem has enclosed shapes inside it, so background removal returns a solid opaque badge rather than a knockout, and the badge looks entirely convincing until it lands on a coloured ground. The embroidery's thread texture also turns a colour accurate trace into hundreds of near identical fills that will not reproduce as a mark at any size. The patch is photographed on folded fabric, so the emblem is neither flat nor square to the camera.

assets_supplied.name: staticfox_titles.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the six upload titles, the creator's recurring catchphrases, the members call to action and the end card copy.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Titles and the lines I always use. The members line has to be on the end card."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the six titles run more than twice the length of the others, so a single type size and a single measure cannot serve the set and the shortest titles will look underset wherever the longest one fits.

assets_supplied.name: staticfox_refs.png
assets_supplied.kind: Screengrab of three channel grids the creator admires, supplied as a direction reference rather than as a spec.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is the energy I want. Not the exact style, the energy."

Low Beam release visuals from a single short night-driving take

NIGHTFORM's next single, Low Beam, needs a small, coherent visual package. The direction is nocturnal and cinematic, but enough roadway should remain legible for the images to feel intentional rather than simply crushed into black.

We have one short take. Please build the release edit within its four-second limit and derive six distinct still beats from that source.

A deliberate 4-second-or-shorter edit assembled from the 1 supplied short clip using an explicit timeline, plus one platform reframe and three checked poster frames. Source time ranges must come from motion_source_metadata.json and a task-specific edit decision list. The supplied video files contain no audio streams; use a separate supplied WAV only where one exists and never infer dialogue from silent footage.

Six frames pulled from the take and brought to one night target: one black point, one warmth, one grain, one sense of how much roadway stays legible, all at or below the take's native frame dimensions. Delivered with a per beat parameter log recording what was applied and why that beat differs from its neighbours. This is one set with one grade, not one frame at several sizes.

The stills should share a black point, warmth and grain with the motion. Six crops of one moment are not six beats. Keep them within the take's native dimensions and note why each moment needed its particular correction.

client_brief:
Today's Emberline package, with a reusable segment-card workflow

TODAY'S PRODUCTION: EMBERLINE

We need the dish, promo and segment cards to feel like the same bright, friendly show. This ships daily, so the next person at the desk must be able to repeat the workflow tomorrow.

Start by resolving the two house-colour values in our notes and explaining the choice. The plate edge should be checked on that chosen colour, not only on white.

Dish plate and thumbnail
Today's dish isolated and set on the show's chosen house colour with nothing behind it, the rim holding where the plate meets the cloth when inspected on that colour rather than against white, plus the thumbnail crop cut from it. The house colour decision between the two values in the client's own notes is made and justified rather than picked.

Short promo
A deliberate 4-second-or-shorter edit assembled from the 1 supplied short clip using an explicit timeline, plus one platform reframe and three checked poster frames. Source time ranges must come from motion_source_metadata.json and a task-specific edit decision list. The supplied video files contain no audio streams; use a separate supplied WAV only where one exists and never infer dialogue from silent footage.

Matched day frames
Eight key frames shot across seven hours of moving daylight brought to one show white point, one brightness and one warmth, plus one licensed establishing frame brought into the same world, all at or below their source pixel dimensions. Delivered with a per-frame parameter log recording what was applied and why that frame differed. This is one set with one target, not eight separately pleasing pictures.

Segment-card run
The office's flat card template reverse engineered into a live merge template with every placeholder confirmed present by inspection of the re-exported document, then run against the day's rundown as one card per segment: the printer's deck with page count equal to the segment count in running order and rendered at 300 ppi at trim, each card binding its own segment's still cut from the graded set, the strap and time set from the rundown, plus per segment proofs named from what is actually inside them rather than from the returned order, with the Market Open segment that has no exported frame handled deliberately rather than left as a blank picture well, and the bleed reality of the supplied template stated. Delivered with the live reusable merge template so tomorrow's deck can be run without repeating the reverse engineering.

Editable caption cards
Emberline caption card set as one editable document plus its source: Choose and adapt an Adobe Express template for these supporting pieces, using the supplied brand, approved copy and imagery. Select the strongest fit, replace the template content and correct its background as needed. Supply the editable design link and the requested export, in addition to the commissioned custom production work.

The rundown controls the card count and order. Handle the Market Open image gap deliberately, and leave the template ready for another day's data. The four-second promo remains limited to its supplied clip and any separate audio actually present.

The same eight frames graded moody and filmic, or styled as a 200 dollar tasting menu with deep shadows, sparse plating and fine type, would be technically excellent and completely wrong for the format, and returning viewers read that drift as the show having changed. Push the other way into hard saturated broadcast punch and the food stops looking edible. A posted job of this shape runs 600 to 1,400 dollars for the first package with a lower daily rate afterwards, which is exactly why the recipe is a deliverable.

brand_identity.sector: Daily food and craft television show on a regional daytime slot, with promos cut for the short video feeds and a same day turnaround.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: On air since 2018, produced in Providence, Rhode Island. A small daily production crew that shoots in the morning, cuts in the afternoon and posts the promo before anyone leaves.
brand_identity.about: Emberline is a bright, friendly daily food and craft show built around one host, a sunny studio kitchen and an accessible dish or make each day. It is free to watch and mainstream in the best sense: warm, unfussy and appetising. Because the promo ships every single day, the brand lives or dies on a look that can be reached again tomorrow by whoever is at the desk.
brand_identity.audience: Mainstream daytime viewers skewing thirty five to sixty five, watching on a mid range television and on their phones. The show is free and the products featured run ten to thirty dollars.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Regional daytime, free to watch, everyday products. The look must be lively, clean and appetising, never moody, filmic or corporate, and never a two hundred dollar tasting menu with deep shadows and fine type. Hard broadcast punch is the other failure: it stops the food looking edible.
brand_identity.typography: A friendly rounded sans for straps and captions with a slightly warmer sans or soft slab for the show name and endboard. Generous, plain and legible on a television and a phone alike. Nothing precious, condensed or editorial.
brand_identity.voice: Upbeat, plain and welcoming, like a host talking to a regular viewer. Example line the brand would write: "Today on Emberline: a white bean and rosemary gratin you can have on the table in under an hour."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no clean brand kit. The typefaces the on air package used survive only as a previous designer's note written from memory, in loose form. The house colour is recorded twice with two different values, one from the on air graphics package and one from the print kit, with nothing saying which governs, so it must be settled before use.
brand_identity.values: Repeatability and warmth. What the show is actually buying is a look and a written recipe a different editor can run tomorrow, so the brand stays consistent day after day without drift.

client_brief:
Season-two recap that still feels like the Halden Diaries

Nate's flat should still feel like Nate's flat. The Halden Diaries has its first sponsor, but the season recap must not suddenly look like a studio campaign. We want a considered edit from eight supplied clips and a coherent image set across the kitchen, window light and evening footage.

A deliberate 24-second-or-shorter edit assembled from the 8 supplied short clips using an explicit timeline, plus one platform reframe and three checked poster frames. Source time ranges must come from motion_source_metadata.json and a task-specific edit decision list. The supplied video files contain no audio streams; use a separate supplied WAV only where one exists and never infer dialogue from silent footage.

Eight episode pictures brought to one channel look across kitchen tungsten, window daylight and evening dusk: one white point, one black point, one warmth, one contrast handling, with the flat still reading as a flat rather than as a studio. Every output at or below its source dimensions with the returned tradeoff record captured, and a per picture parameter log including one line on why each differs from its neighbours.

The hand painted channel name recovered from a photograph of a limewashed pine board as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, its counters open and its painted hairline rule intact, delivered as both a single colour mark and a colour-accurate variant, and holding at the size it actually reproduces on the card foot as well as on the end plate. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. The creator handle is laundered to a fully invented persona, The Halden Diaries, wordmark HALDEN, tagline an ordinary week filmed, run by fictional creator Nate Halden. price_band_and_audience: Sponsorship tier lifestyle vlog, patron subscriptions at 6 dollars a month with a printed card set at season end, audience 24 to 38 and loyal rather than large. The band is load bearing in both directions. Push it up and the work becomes a studio channel: crushed contrast, a cool graded look, a hard geometric plate, a logo that sits large. That look reads as an agency production, it contradicts the whole premise of one man filming his own week, and the audience that pays 6 dollars a month for intimacy reads it as the channel having been bought. Push it down and it becomes a phone edit: no consistent white point, a caption plate in a default system face, a card that looks like a home printer job, which fails the sponsor who is paying for the season and fails the patrons who paid for a physical object. The correct register is domestic warmth held to a professional standard: one white point, one black point, real licensed type, restrained plates, and a wordmark that still looks hand painted because it was. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed with a per season retainer attached.

brand_identity.sector: Independent daily vlog channel, self shot and self edited, patron supported, entering its first sponsored season.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2021, Portland, Maine, a one person channel run entirely by its creator Nate Halden.
brand_identity.about: The Halden Diaries is a self shot, self edited vlog in which Nate Halden films an ordinary week in his own flat and puts out one episode every Sunday. The channel promises intimacy over production: the same rooms, the same face, the same unhurried attention week after week. Season two is its first with a sponsor, and the whole point is that the sponsor changed nothing about how the week feels.
brand_identity.audience: Loyal rather than large, aged 24 to 38, patrons who pay 6 dollars a month for closeness and receive a printed card set at each season end. They buy the feeling of a friend filming his week, not a studio production.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Patron subscriptions at 6 dollars a month with a printed card set mailed at season end, first sponsored season attached. Sits deliberately between a phone edit and a studio channel: domestic warmth held to a professional standard.
brand_identity.typography: Display: a warm humanist serif with a hand set feel that echoes the painted board. Text: a quiet, readable humanist sans. Nothing geometric and nothing slick. The type should feel set by hand at home rather than commissioned from an agency.
brand_identity.voice: First person, plain, unhurried, a little self deprecating. He writes the way he talks to camera. Example line: 'An ordinary week, filmed. Thanks for staying with it.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No brand files have ever existed. The channel name lives only as a board Nate hand painted on limewashed pine before the first episode, one deep ink with a painted hairline rule beneath it, and it survives only as a handheld photograph. The wordmark HALDEN has to be recovered from that photograph as usable artwork. There is no logo file, no colour spec and no prior guideline.
brand_identity.values: Intimacy and honesty: one man filming his own week, kept that way even with a sponsor in the room.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Adapted from the Upwork post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, where a personal training business with a large exercise library wanted a repeatable production pipeline turning raw demo footage into short educational reference clips with reusable branding, muscle group callouts, and a clip naming and organisation convention. Two parts of that literal ask are on the connector's unavailable list and are therefore re carved rather than faked: open timeline editing to timestamps and frame by frame overlay or caption compositing do not exist here, so the callouts become a printed and authored reference card set that lives beside each clip rather than burned into it, which is what a coached library actually ships to subscribers anyway. Everything else in the post is real work and fully doable: shortening long demo takes into per movement highlights, producing the vertical companions the app's short feed needs, bringing a set of poster frames shot across two sessions to one studio white, recovering the studio's own mark and certification seal from the only surviving physical object, and turning the printer's existing exercise card into a live six record run so the library extends itself later. The business is laundered to a fully invented studio, Anvil and Oak Strength, run by fictional coaches Ruth Callaway and Dean Marchetti. No real trainer, gym, certifying body or app is referenced, and the certification seal is a coined in house mark rather than any real credential.

price_band_and_audience: Coached strength subscription at 49 dollars a month, subscriber 30 to 52, home gym or garage gym, already lifting and buying instruction rather than motivation. The band is load bearing in both directions. Drop toward a 9 dollar mass fitness app and the correct treatment is high saturation, hard contrast, big shouty type, bodies as motivation imagery, cards that are mostly a photograph; ship that here and the coaching claim collapses, because the subscriber is paying for someone who knows what a hip hinge is and that person does not shout. Push up toward a clinical or rehabilitation register and it becomes cold, white, diagrammatic and medical, which reads as physiotherapy, is a different product, and is exactly the thing this studio's whole positioning is not. The correct register is a working craftsman's studio: one honest studio white, real bodies doing real work, quiet confident type, cue lists that read as instruction rather than as marketing. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,800 dollars fixed with a per quarter extension attached.

assets_supplied.name: anvil_oak_demo_takes/ (14 files across 6 movements)
assets_supplied.kind: Long single camera demo takes, two or three per movement, filmed in one session in the barn gym.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Every movement, all the takes. They are far too long and there is a lot of setting up at the front."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The takes carry their most visible motion in the setup and in the reset after a failed rep rather than in the working set, so a shortening pass driven by what is happening on screen returns a plausible, well paced clip of the wrong part of the take at exactly the requested length. assets_supplied.name: anvil_oak_poster_stills/ (6 frames plus alternates)
assets_supplied.kind: Studio stills shot by a photographer alongside the filming, across two separate visits a fortnight apart.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The poster frames. She was in twice and the light was not the same both times."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: A ceiling bank was replaced between the two visits, so the second session's frames carry a different illuminant that one identical correction applied across the set cannot resolve, and the difference is small enough per frame to look acceptable alone. In two frames the chrome of the loaded bar sits at almost the luminance of the barn's whitewashed wall, so a subject led cut bites the bar sleeve while returning a clean looking edge everywhere else.

assets_supplied.visible_description: "The file the printer worked from. Same card, six new movements."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The cue list block is a fixed frame that does not spill. Records whose cue list runs longer than last year's simply stop rendering at the frame's edge, mid line and without a mark, while the merge reports success and the page count still matches the record count.

assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our mark and the seal. This patch is the only place either of them still exists."

The thread also raises a visible nap on the wordmark's strokes, which reads as texture at full frame and as broken edges once traced.

price_band_and_audience: A forty dollar monthly subscription supplement bought by a wellness curious thirty to fifty year old who has been burned by overclaiming. The band is load bearing in both directions. Push it up into near black grounds, cold hard light, a slow authored title sequence and a whispered voice and it becomes a two hundred dollar longevity clinic, which misprices a forty dollar bottle and reads as a claim the reviewer never cleared. Push it down into saturated fast cuts, shouted supers, a bright bounce grade and stacked benefit captions and it becomes a discount aisle stack of gummies, which in this category reads as hype and is precisely what makes a cautious buyer close the tab. Around it sits the rest of what a promoter posts the same night and never commissions separately: a cover still that survives being posted small, the venue's painted wall mark recovered as artwork the night can reuse, and the event details handed back as a working file, because the next date changes every month and the promoter is not going to pay a freelancer for a date change.
price_band_and_audience: A twenty to thirty dollar door at an independent monthly warehouse night, with a late teens to twenties crowd who follow the night rather than the venue. The band is load bearing. Push it up into restrained typography, a clean neutral grade, generous white space and a considered logo lockup and it reads as a hundred dollar festival brand or a corporate venue takeover, which is precisely the thing this audience treats as evidence that the night has been bought and is no longer theirs. Push it further down into cluttered stacked promoter text, clip art and drop shadows and it reads as a flyer nobody made, which is a different kind of dead. The correct answer is loud, immediate and slightly rough on purpose: a dark ground, saturated stage colour left in rather than corrected out, display type doing real work, and a mark that looks painted rather than drawn. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even where every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 350 to 900 dollars, and the tight turnaround is the real constraint on how much archaeology is affordable.

brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Pulsevault has never had a logo file. The mark exists only hand painted on the brick beside the entrance and survives as one photograph taken at the end of the night under a single floodlight. The wordmark has to be recovered from that photograph as artwork the night can reuse, and it has to hold on a cover that is close to black. There is no colour spec and no prior guideline. The one thing the night reprints unchanged is a plain lineup card its print shop runs a small batch of each month, supplied as last month's flat press artwork: the running order and the per act details change every date, the layout does not.
brand_identity.values: It belongs to the crowd: made by the people who run the night, not bought in.

The real post named no venue, so the line is laundered to the fictional Velvet Hour monthly night (a moth and lamp mark) with four fictional acts: Junie Ash, The Paper Kestrels, Odette Vann and Cinder and Salt. The ledger's repositioning note stops mid sentence at 'REPOSITIONED for co', and the reposition it was reaching for is the honest one: the real post asked for a recurring package, so the commission is written as the FIRST month of that recurring package, and the parts of it the connector cannot do (assembling a multi angle edit, adding motion graphics, extracting a frame from the take) are replaced by the parts it verifiably can (index, shorten, clean speech, reframe without enlarging; grade a mixed set to one look; recover a lost mark off a photograph; reverse engineer the printer's card into a live merge template). CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes the fuller commission honest, because HTML authoring now yields a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes and prepare_indd_merge_template builds a real merge template from a bare press PDF.

price_band_and_audience: An eighteen to twenty five dollar ticket in a ninety seat back room, audience thirty to sixty and lineup literate. The band is load bearing. At this price the night sells intimacy and musicianship, so the treatment has to be warm, low key, close and unhurried: lamp light left as lamp light, grain left in rather than fought, type quiet and editorial, the act's face doing the work. The same four acts at a fifteen dollar door in a two hundred capacity club would correctly be graded cold and contrasty with hard colour and a loud type scale, and shipping that here misrepresents a room where people sit down and listen, which loses the crowd the venue actually has. Push the other way into black tie restraint and gold foil gestures and it prices itself at a ninety dollar concert hall and reads as pretentious to a bar audience. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 700 to 1,600 dollars a month on retainer.

brand_identity.tagline: One night a month, sit down and listen.
brand_identity.sector: Arts, culture and live music (monthly ticketed jazz and folk night)
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2021 in the back room of a bar, Providence, Rhode Island. Tiny: two organisers, ninety seats, one night a month.
brand_identity.about: Velvet Hour is a monthly ticketed jazz and folk night held in the ninety seat back room of a Providence bar. Two sets, no support, one camera in the same corner every month. The night sells intimacy and musicianship to people who read a lineup carefully, so everything we make should feel like a good room rather than a club or a concert hall.
brand_identity.audience: Lineup literate adults roughly thirty to sixty who pay eighteen to twenty five dollars to sit close and listen. Locals who follow the acts, not a party crowd.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid, intimate. An eighteen to twenty five dollar ticket. Never budget club, never black tie concert hall.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet editorial system: a warm serif for act names and titles, a restrained humanist sans for billing lines, dates and body. Type stays small, generously set and calm. No display gimmicks, no gold foil gestures.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, affectionate, low key. Talks about the room and the players, never hypes. Short sentences, no exclamation, lets the act's face and the music do the work.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our mark, a moth over a lamp inside a hairline arc of small caps type, was made by the designer who set up the night, and the source file went with them when they left. All that survives is the mark painted in one cream ink on the dark green lamp box by the door, which is why it has to be rebuilt from that as real artwork. No brand typeface was ever formally chosen, so the type system is open for you to set.
brand_identity.values: Story first, no gimmicks. Clean, coherent, honest to the room. We would rather look like a place people sit and listen than like a night that is trying too hard.

assets_supplied.name: velvet_hour_house_stills/ (11 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photographs taken from the bar during the same set at very high sensitivity under a single tungsten lamp.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Pictures from the bar on the night. The one of the singer under the lamp might carry a poster."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The lamp throws a heavy warm cast across the singer's face, so a whole frame move toward a neutral room look takes her skin grey while leaving the lamp itself orange, and the frames are noisy in a way no tool here reduces. Two of the eleven are the same moment a third of a second apart, and the sharper of the two is the one where her eyes are closed.

assets_supplied.name: next_month_act_photos/ (4 frames, one per act, supplied by the acts)
assets_supplied.kind: Publicity photographs sent in by Junie Ash, The Paper Kestrels, Odette Vann and Cinder and Salt, each shot by whoever they had.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the four acts sent us. Use them as they are, we cannot go back and ask."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: They are not comparable inputs: two are full scale camera files, one is a screengrab off a phone at roughly nine hundred pixels on the long edge, and one is a photograph of a printed press sheet that carries the printer's screen and grows a moire once it is graded. Nothing in the filenames, the list or the client's description separates them, and the small one binds into the card's photograph frame without any complaint from anything.

assets_supplied.name: velvet_hour_lampbox.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Daylight photograph, taken at an angle, of the venue's mark painted in one cream ink on the dark green lamp box beside the door: a moth over a lamp inside a hairline arc of small caps type.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our mark. It is paint on the lamp box now, that is all that is left of it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound mark on a photographed painted substrate, so a prompt naming the box returns the box, a prompt naming the whole mark returns the moth and the lamp while silently dropping the arc of type, and the wing counters are enclosed so a background knockout hands back a filled slab rather than a see through mark. The paint is also laid on thickest at the wing edges, which is not visible in the photograph and does not show in a trace viewed at canvas size.

assets_supplied.name: velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF the venue's printer has used for the listing card for three seasons, one act to a card, with a photograph well and four blocks of type.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The printer's own file. Same card three seasons running, one act per card."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Printed it reads as four separate blocks (the act name, a one line billing, the date and door time, and a short paragraph) plus a photograph, but the artwork is one continuous flow, so what the conversion actually exposes as editable frames looks nothing like the printed page. The structure readout also omits one run while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed, every offset past it is short, and the validator still calls the mapping valid.

assets_supplied.name: velvet_hour_lineup.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Plain data: the four acts, their billing lines, the date, the door time and the ticket price.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The four acts as our booker keeps them. The billing lines are theirs, do not rewrite them."

source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post for a driving education content system quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, a driver education brand wanting a library of clean, mobile first explainer shorts on lane changes, turns, roundabouts, parking, merging, four way stops and hazard recognition, plus reusable branded templates and vector illustration. The literal ask in that post is from scratch After Effects two dimensional motion graphics animation, which is squarely on the connector's not available list (no text to image, no vector authoring, no After Effects timeline, no compositing), so the ledger's own note concedes the job has to be honestly re cast to the in scope production work this exact system needs. That is what this commission is: the same academy, the same eight scenarios, the same mobile first distribution, but built from what a small academy actually has, which is an instructor with a dash mount, a Saturday of photographs, a photographed sheet of the sign shapes their first designer drew, and the printer's file for the guide they hand every learner. client_brief:
Two client sizzles, two distinct looks, one clear studio service presentation

FOLD & GRAIN is moving from selling shoot days to selling a repeatable product. This commission should show how the same disciplined method can serve two very different clients without making their brands look alike.

Two clients, deliberately different:
- Cobbleway: bright, warm, honest carton photography.
- Lunara: cool, restrained, dark pendant imagery.

Keep the client clips, source choices and final exports separate throughout.

CLIENT FILMS
Two visually led 4-second sizzles, one per supplied client clip, plus one vertical reframe of each. Select the strongest visual span within each short clip; do not combine the two brands or imply speech. Inspect both outputs for product continuity and keep the two client looks deliberately distinct.

CLIENT IMAGE SETS
Six Cobbleway carton masters brought to one bright, warm, honest target and nine Lunara pendant masters brought to a separate cool, restrained, dark target, each set holding one white point, one black point and one product scale within its own cells, plus one licensed camera-scale bench frame graded into the studio's own page. Per frame parameter log including which colour family each Cobbleway grab came from and which Lunara grab index was used for each piece and why. Every output at or below its source dimensions with the returned tradeoff record for each.

STUDIO PRESENTATION
Cobbleway and Lunara shot boards plus the FOLD & GRAIN service page, as one editable document with its source: Choose and adapt an Adobe Express template for these supporting pieces, using the supplied brand, approved copy and imagery. Select the strongest fit, replace the template content and correct its background as needed. Supply the editable design link and the requested export, in addition to the commissioned custom production work.

The films are four-second sizzles, one from each supplied clip, not an expanded shoot. Check product continuity and the vertical reframes, and do not combine the two brands into a single highlight.

The pack contains source_video_files/ (2 measured short files); motion_source_metadata.json; cobbleway_grabs/ (24 frame exports, 3840 x 2160, four per carton); lunara_grabs/ (27 frame exports, three per piece); client_marks/ (two photographs: cobbleway_carton_face.jpg, lunara_bail_stamp.jpg); foldgrain_service_copy.txt.

Media inventory: 2 video files, 10.084 seconds in total; 0 with embedded audio; 0 separate audio files (0 seconds). These measured sources set the production limits.

We need the shot boards and editable service page to demonstrate what the source actually yields. Honest limits and clear file organisation are part of the service being sold.

Alongside the finished work, we need a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the final edit decision list and measured source metadata. Keep a clear record of the supplied files used, retained for reference, superseded and rejected. Approved source information remains authoritative. Record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and quality limits, and do not use an undeclared replacement or invented fact to conceal a source problem. Keep runtime within measured source duration and the stated cap; do not invent footage or dialogue.

Please work within $5,000-$12,000 fixed and the 4 to 6 weeks target. Allow for direction approval, first-production proof, and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post from a small packaging design studio launching a new website, asking for an 'eye-catching sizzle reel to be used as the hero video on my new site' that is 'fast paced and energetic while showcasing my design work in the best way possible', to be built from 'mockups and photographs of packaging projects I have completed'. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com post from a growing direct to consumer sterling silver jewellery brand wanting a freelance editor to 'repurpose existing content into multiple formats and variations' for short form and social. Both posts are laundered: the studio becomes the coined FOLD & GRAIN Studio, its two client runs become the coined Cobbleway Provisions and Lunara Silver, and the ledger's non Western founder persona is replaced by Elodie Marchand. The STRENGTHEN verdict applies because the killed original sat almost entirely on one surface (reframe a clip, ship it) and because the ledger's own repositioning note concedes the original reframed an already vertical clip to vertical, a no operation that would also have enlarged. real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post from a small packaging design studio launching a new website, asking for an 'eye-catching sizzle reel to be used as the hero video on my new site' that is 'fast paced and energetic while showcasing my design work in the best way possible', to be built from 'mockups and photographs of packaging projects I have completed'. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com post from a growing direct to consumer sterling silver jewellery brand wanting a freelance editor to 'repurpose existing content into multiple formats and variations' for short form and social. Both posts are laundered: the studio becomes the coined FOLD & GRAIN Studio, its two client runs become the coined Cobbleway Provisions and Lunara Silver, and the ledger's non Western founder persona is replaced by Elodie Marchand. The STRENGTHEN verdict applies because the killed original sat almost entirely on one surface (reframe a clip, ship it) and because the ledger's own repositioning note concedes the original reframed an already vertical clip to vertical, a no operation that would also have enlarged. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is: HTML authoring now yields a native editable document at mixed canvas sizes, an ink level trace off photographed printed collateral recovers a real mark, and the video family shortens and reframes but never enlarges. So this is the commission both clients genuinely needed, which is not a reel but a repeatable service proven twice at two different price bands.
price_band_and_audience: One engagement, two deliberately opposed client bands, plus the studio's own band. Cobbleway Provisions is pantry goods at roughly eight dollars a carton, bought off a shelf and off a small web store by a shopper aged twenty five to fifty five who decides in under two seconds: bright ground, generous product scale in the cell, warm honest colour, legible price, nothing precious. Lunara Silver is sterling pendants at roughly one hundred and eighty dollars, bought by a woman aged twenty eight to forty five who is buying restraint: dark stone ground, small product in a lot of air, cool restrained colour, no gloss, price set quietly. The band is load bearing twice over. Apply the bright generous treatment to the pendants and a one hundred and eighty dollar piece reads as costume, apply the restrained dark treatment to the cartons and eight dollar pantry goods read as unaffordable and stop selling. And because the whole pitch is a productized service, a single house look applied to both boards is not a stylistic slip, it is the proof failing: it demonstrates the studio cannot price tune, which is the one thing the service claims. FOLD & GRAIN itself bills around fifteen hundred dollars a day today and wants the product at a fixed twenty two hundred to three thousand five hundred dollars per client run. A posted job of this shape runs two thousand to four thousand five hundred dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: One take. Everything you need to sell it.
brand_identity.sector: Product photography studio moving from a day rate practice to a fixed price productized service
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2020 in Portland, Oregon. Three people: Nina (art direction and shooting), plus a retoucher and a studio assistant.
brand_identity.about: FOLD & GRAIN shoots small brands' products the way those brands actually sell them, in a row, as a range, rather than one hero at a time. For six years we sold days. We are now selling a product: one continuous take per client and, out of that single take, the shot board, the short films and the platform cuts a small brand needs to launch. Our work sits behind pantry goods at eight dollars and sterling silver at a hundred and eighty, and the whole point is that the same method tunes to each. Precision, repeatability and honesty about what a shoot can and cannot yield are the studio's stock in trade.
brand_identity.audience: Small and independent product brands (pantry, personal care, jewellery, homeware) launching or refreshing a web store and needing a full range shot to look like one afternoon. Founders who buy a fixed price and a fixed turnaround, not a day rate.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Repositioning from roughly fifteen hundred dollars a day to a fixed twenty two hundred to thirty five hundred dollars per client run. Mid-market, productized, premium to a freelancer but well under an agency.
brand_identity.typography: A clean neo-grotesque for headings and the studio wordmark, paired with a monospaced face for technical specs, parameters and captions on the service page. Type is set tight, quiet and utilitarian.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, specific, no salesmanship. We name what a shoot can deliver and what it cannot, and we write our recipes so an assistant could run them. Sentences are short and concrete.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: FOLD & GRAIN has a consistent working look built up over six years but never a codified system. There is a set wordmark and studio colours in practice, no written guidelines. This engagement, which includes the studio's own service page, is where the identity gets formalized for the first time.
brand_identity.values: Repeatability over one-off flourish, honesty about limits, and price-appropriate craft: a treatment right for one band is wrong for another, and saying so is the service.

client_brief:
Make eight skincare products look like one launch, not eight shoots

Our launch range needs to look as considered online as it does on the shelf. At the moment the eight bottles look as though they belong to different brands.

What needs resolving:
- Different afternoons have produced inconsistent whites and shadows.
- Bottle size wanders across the range.
- The retailer needs both white tiles and convincing transparency, not a background-removal preview.

We are Aurelian Skin. Think clinical and precise, with enough material detail to make the products tangible. We need an experienced product retoucher who can establish a convincing range standard and carry it into the retailer files.

The two sets we need back:

Eight bottle masters brought to one clinical target (one white point, one black point, one height in frame) plus a separately targeted family of ingredient close ups, one per launch product with none standing in for two, plus one licensed camera-scale bench frame graded into the same world. Per frame parameter log, including one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours.

Eight square store tiles at the retailer's tile size of 2048 x 2048 px on a clean white ground, product optically centred with clear air at every edge and a cut edge that holds under close inspection, plus eight genuinely transparent variants for the chain's coloured band. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with the returned tradeoff record for each. This is one set with one cut logic, not one picture at several sizes.

Please judge the cutouts on the retailer's coloured band as well as on white. A tidy thumbnail is not enough if the bottle edge falls apart at the size the buyer will actually use. Keep the ingredient images specific to their products; repeating a convenient macro would misrepresent the range.

In the folder: aurelian_launch_shoot/ (8 frames, 8688 x 5792); aurelian_actives_macros/ (8 frames); aurelian_carton_front.jpg; aurelian_copy.txt; aurelian_reference_page.png; aurelian_speccard_press.pdf.

The ledger's own repositioning note concedes that from-scratch identity art and free-form layout composition are not connector work; CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is, because HTML authoring now produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes and an ink-level trace off photographed printed collateral recovers a real mark. So this is that client's actual job: the identity is RECOVERED rather than invented, and the editable source files they asked for are real.
price_band_and_audience: Prestige-mass clinical actives at 34 to 68 dollars per SKU, buyer 26 to 42 and ingredient literate. The band is load-bearing: at this price the range must sit on a cool near-clinical white, with restrained type, generous white space, no props and no styling that reads as ritual or spa. The same eight products at a 12 dollar mass band would correctly be shot warm, saturated, prop-heavy and tightly cropped to fill the tile, and shipping that treatment here reads downmarket and kills the clinical claim. Push the other way into near-black grounds, extreme sparseness and cosmetic gloss and it becomes a 200 dollar luxury conserve of a skincare line, which misprices a 34 dollar serum. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,200 to 2,600 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Clinical skincare and personal care, actives-led, direct to consumer plus specialty retail
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2024 in Boston, Massachusetts. A two person founder team, sold for a year to a waiting list and through two dermatology practices before the retail season.
brand_identity.about: Aurelian Skin is a small clinical skincare line built on eight actives-led products at thirty four to sixty eight dollars. In March we open our own online store and enter a specialty chain's twelve doors, so everything a customer sees changes at once. The line is meant to read like a laboratory with good taste: cool, quiet, evidence first, generous with white space and free of decoration. Not a spa, not a discount aisle. Our customer reads the ingredient list before the copy, and the brand is built to reward that: honest claims, clear INCI, restraint in place of ritual.
brand_identity.audience: Women roughly twenty six to forty two, ingredient literate, who research formulations and trust plainness over promise. They shop web stores and specialty beauty floors and judge a product by its panel.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Prestige-mass at thirty four to sixty eight dollars per SKU. Above the mass aisle, below luxury conserve pricing. The middle is the position, and the look must not drift warm and cheap or dark and precious.
brand_identity.typography: One restrained type system for all launch collateral: a clean grotesque for names and body copy carrying the ingredient literacy, with a single quiet display cut for the wordmark. Strong typography and whitespace do the work, no decorative faces.
brand_identity.voice: Measured, factual, unhurried. States what a product does and does not claim. Reads like a well-run lab that respects the reader, never breathless and never coy.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original logo file was lost when the first designer's drive failed. All that survives is a handheld photograph of an outer carton showing the mark printed in one deep ink: a small-caps lockup set around a monogram, separated by a hairline rule. Recovering that mark as usable artwork is part of this engagement. No other source brand files remain.
brand_identity.values: Ingredient honesty, precision in every detail from panel to package, and clinical restraint: at this band, quiet and exact is the brand, and overstatement or gloss would undercut the claim.

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_launch_shoot/ (8 frames, 8688 x 5792)
assets_supplied.kind: Product photography shot in-house by a friend across three afternoons, one SKU per frame, pale sweep, fifty megapixel body.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All eight, same sweep, same corner of her studio. Some read cooler than others and one is brighter, but they are good pictures."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The frames are far larger than anything downstream expects, and the one-call background knockout silently reduces oversized inputs and reports it in no message and no error, only as a downscaled entry inside the returned tradeoffs object with output dimensions below source dimensions. The returned cutout is clean, complete and correct looking at preview scale; the shortfall only appears when the square store tile is cut from it, and by then the only route back to the retailer's tile size is interpolation, which the crop tool will perform up to a two times cap while saying so only inside its own tradeoffs. Separately the 30ml frosted-glass SKU sits at almost the luminance of the sweep at its shoulder, so subject detection has no contrast there and hands back a soft rim on that frame alone.

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_actives_macros/ (8 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Macro close ups of the raw actives themselves, shot on a later day: a drop on glass, a pipette tip, a crystal, a powder cone.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The ingredient close ups for the product pages. Tighter, different day."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Each frame is a single small element on a near empty ground. A subject-focused crop on that kind of art returns a confident looking result at a plausible size while reporting its uncertainty only as a numeric detection confidence and a detection bounding box buried in the metadata, and on sparse art it can lock onto a specular highlight or a reflection instead of the subject and hand back a crop that clips most of it, at full success. Which of the eight this happens to is a property of each frame's own contrast. Separately there are eight macros for eight products but two of them are the same active shot twice and one launch product has no macro at all, which no filename or column reveals.

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_carton_front.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of an outer carton standing on a bench, the mark printed in one deep ink on pale board: a compound lockup of small-caps type set around a monogram, separated by a hairline rule.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place our mark still exists. We lost the file when the drive failed."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup on a photographed substrate, which behaves nothing like a flat scan. A prompt naming the substrate returns the carton rather than the ink; a compound prompt returns the type ring and silently drops the monogram and the hairline rule while looking entirely plausible; and background removal on the ring returns a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched. The ink and the board also run close in value on the shadowed right third of the carton face.

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_reference_page.png
assets_supplied.kind: Screengrab of a store page layout the founders like, from a category-neutral retailer, supplied as a proportion reference.

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_speccard_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The flat press PDF the specialty chain's print vendor supplied as the template each per-SKU shelf-edge and tester-station card is struck from: an A6 portrait card carrying the product name, an ingredients (INCI) block, the cleared claim, the price and a square product-image well, 3mm bleed present, fonts embedded.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The chain's card template. Every SKU gets one of these on the shelf edge and at the tester station, so their printer wants a run built off this file. The INCI on it is the approved line and cannot change."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed card reads as five tidy blocks, but the product name, the INCI block and the cleared claim are set as ONE continuous threaded story flowing through three linked frames, so the INCI is an offset inside a continuous flow rather than an addressable field. The mapping readout normalises and shortens that story, so an offset computed from the readout silently drops or misplaces the INCI while validation returns valid and both preparation and render report success; the only evidence the INCI landed is reading the rendered card. The square image well IS a real bindable graphic frame, and a 3mm bleed box IS present in the source PDF; but convert_pdf_to_indd collapses it, setting the converted document's BleedBox equal to its TrimBox, so the connector cannot carry bleed through a PDF-derived merge template and the honest deliverable is trim-only.

assets_supplied.name: aurelian_speccards.csv (8 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: The per-SKU card data the chain wants merged: one row per launch product carrying the product name, its locked INCI line, its cleared claim, its price and a picture reference, derived from the approved copy.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One row per product for the shelf cards. The INCI lines are the approved ones and cannot be edited."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Prices are written inconsistently across the eight rows, dollar sign on some, two decimals on some, bare integers on others, so a naive bind prints mixed formats on a clinical line. The frosted SKU's name carries the internal warehouse parenthetical '(30ml frosted)' that must be kept off the retail card. And the picture column carries an off-by-one copy-down slip on the exfoliating toner row, which points at the cleanser frame rather than the toner's own, so a merge that trusts the column shows the wrong bottle on that card. The INCI and claim cells are comma-bearing and quoted, and none of this is revealed by any header.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the one-call knockout gives back a picture the store tile can still be cut from. The captures are 8688 x 5792 and the knockout silently reduces oversized inputs, reporting it in no message, no warning and no error: the only trace is a downscaled entry inside the returned tradeoffs object with output dimensions below source dimensions. Nothing in the tool's description mentions a size ceiling and nothing states where it sits. The returned cutout is clean, complete and correct at preview scale. The shortfall appears only when the square tile is cut, and the only route back to the retailer's size is interpolation, which the crop tool performs up to a two times cap while reporting it solely inside its own tradeoffs.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it. The defensible order is straighten, grade, knock out at source scale, then choose the crop, precisely so the crop is chosen after the cut edge is visible; there is no read-ahead for the ceiling and no parameter that controls it. An agent that cropped first would be trading away crop choice for a reason nobody has told it. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for square store pictures and says nothing about resolution; the no-enlargement line in the acceptance bar is the client's standing trade requirement, not a disclosure that a tool shrinks things. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different route, decided per frame: crop to the subject's own bounds at native scale so the knockout receives a frame under the ceiling, or abandon the one-call knockout for a material-named sweep selection inverted and filled to white.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the knockout route for all eight frames, re-derive every white-ground plate and every transparent variant through the new route, and re-read both the downscaled and the upscale entries in every returned tradeoffs object before any tile is called delivered.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eight store tiles that are either short of the retailer's required size and bounced at upload, or brought to size by interpolation and shipped soft, on a clinical line whose entire claim is precision.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the thing the launch look is built on. The client asked for the bottles to sit on a surface with a soft shadow rather than float. Authored the natural way that is a blurred element or a layered shadow, and the importer discards a blur filter outright and truncates a layered shadow to its first layer, with no warning and a successful response. The returned per-canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so the square and tall canvases can be checked no other way. Whether what survives still reads as a bottle sitting on a surface, or as a bottle floating beside a grey smudge, is visible only after the export.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the drop happens at import and the import is the last step; and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for a look, and the acceptance line about sitting rather than floating is the client's own art direction, not a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to produce a DIFFERENT upstream asset, a bottle composited onto a solid house ground in a single knockout call so the ground is part of the raster, or to reduce the shadow to the single layer the importer keeps and re-judge whether it still reads, and then re-compose the canvas around whichever it is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the launch masters through a different knockout route or re-cast the shadow as the single surviving layer, re-author the HTML around that decision, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit all three canvases from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A launch set delivered as an editable file in which the bottles float on flat white on the two canvases nobody looked at, with the export having reported success throughout.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a subject-aware crop can find the subject in the ingredient close ups at all. Those frames are one small element on a near empty ground. The crop tool answers a subject-focused request on that kind of art with a confident looking result at a plausible size and reports its uncertainty only as a numeric detection confidence and a detection bounding box buried in the metadata; on sparse art it can lock onto a specular highlight or a reflection and return a crop that clips most of the subject, at full success. Which of the eight this happens to is a property of each frame's own contrast and is not visible by looking at the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) There is no ordering that avoids it and no parameter that prevents it. The safe route, an explicit selection with a returned bounding box driving a bounds crop, costs three calls per frame and is what a competent agent adopts once the cheap route has been seen to fail. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the macros are tighter and were shot on a different day. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the affected frames go through a different chain, not the same chain again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read the detection confidence and bounds on every macro crop, and for each frame below a defensible threshold re-do the crop through an explicit selection of the material by its own visual properties, a returned bounding box and a padded bounds crop, then inspect each result rather than the response.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Ingredient panels showing a third of a droplet and the edge of a pipette, on a line whose customer buys on ingredient literacy and reads that panel before the copy.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of skincare bottles. IDENTITY: these are this line's actual eight products with their actual labels and their actual regulatory-cleared claims, and the mark must be RECOVERED off a photographed carton rather than reinvented, because a regenerated mark is a different company's logo.
