assets_supplied.name: kilnmore_tissue_wrap.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of a sheet of the studio's printed wrapping tissue lying on a table, the mark printed in one ink as a repeating pattern across the whole sheet, a small-caps wordmark beside an enclosed kiln-arch device.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only clean copy of our mark left. It is printed on the tissue we wrap everything in."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Because the mark repeats across the sheet, a selection that correctly takes the ink takes every repeat, and the returned bounding box is therefore the extent of the whole sheet rather than of one mark, so a bounds crop driven by it yields the tissue and a trace of it yields a field of tiny marks that looks plausible at thumbnail size. The tissue is also crinkled, so the ink runs light along the folds, and the arch device is an enclosed form that background removal returns as a solid shape.

assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is the card our printer runs. We just need one per piece with the right words on it."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the knockout actually held on the pale pieces, which cannot be judged on the ground it was first judged against. Four of the fourteen are the bone and oatmeal glazes whose shoulder and rim run within a hair of the pale sweep in value, and on those frames the one-call knockout returns a cutout that is clean, complete and entirely convincing at preview scale while having taken a bite out of the rim. Against the marketplace's plain near-white ground the bite is invisible, because what was removed and what replaced it are both near white, so the primary tile passes inspection. The same cutout on the studio's warm grey shows the piece with a chewed shoulder. Nothing in any response distinguishes the four frames from the ten.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering dodges it, because the defect is a property of this glaze against this sweep and it is only legible on the second ground, which is a deliverable rather than a diagnostic. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says both grounds must exist and that both have to be the same photograph underneath, which is the client's requirement, not a disclosure that one ground hides what the other reveals. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different chain for those frames, selecting the sweep as a material, inverting it, and filling, rather than asking for a subject.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-judge every cutout on the warm grey rather than on the plain ground, re-derive the affected pieces through a material-named sweep selection inverted and filled, and re-cut both the primary and the store tile from the new master so the two grounds do not drift apart.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen marketplace primaries that pass intake and fourteen store tiles showing bitten rims on exactly the four glazes the studio's quietest, most expensive pieces are, on a line whose returns problem is already about colour and truthfulness.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the selection on the tissue actually spans. The mark is printed as a repeat across the whole sheet, so a correctly worded ink level prompt takes the ink faithfully and takes every repeat of it, and the returned bounding box is the extent of that mask, which is the sheet. Driving a bounds crop from it therefore succeeds and yields the tissue; tracing that yields a field of dozens of tiny marks with a viewBox that can be injected and a background path that can be stripped, all of it looking like a legitimate result at thumbnail size and unusable as a placeable mark. Nothing reports that the extent covers many instances rather than one, because a mask extent has no notion of instances.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Doing it right the first time presumes knowing that the returned geometry is an extent rather than an object, and that this particular sheet repeats, which is a fact about the client's wrapping paper. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the mark is printed on the tissue they wrap orders in. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix inverts the order of operations, cutting a single repeat out of the raw photograph by eye first and only then selecting, inverting, tracing and cleaning, which is a different chain rather than the same chain again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Crop one repeat out of the source photograph before any selection is made, choosing a repeat that falls on flat tissue rather than across a crinkle where the ink runs light, then re-run selection, polarity, bounds, trace, viewBox and ground path removal on that crop, and re-judge the arch device at the size it actually reproduces.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A brand mark delivered as a sheet of marks, which reduces to a grey texture the moment it is placed at corner size on a store page, on a studio whose only surviving copy of its identity was this photograph.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card actually is as editable structure, and then whether the mapping built against that structure landed. Two things arrive only by running. First, granularity is not under anyone's control: the four copy lines that read as four blocks on paper can convert as one continuous flow, and the square where the glaze picture sits may or may not survive as a frame anything can bind to, so the shape of the card as a merge is discovered rather than planned. Second, the readout of that flow can omit an entire run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid, the template preparation reports success, and two fields simply never appear on the merged card.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because conversion granularity is a property of the supplied PDF and the readout's omission is invisible in the readout itself. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the printer already runs this card and that one is needed per piece. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is to reconstruct the document's true text from the document rather than from the readout, recompute every offset against that, and re-verify placeholders by inspecting the prepared template, which is a different method rather than a repeat.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping from the document's own reconstructed story text, re-prepare the template, confirm each placeholder by inspecting the result rather than reading the success line, re-merge and re-render the run, and if the picture block turns out not to be bindable, tell the studio and move the glaze picture to a collateral that can carry it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen shelf cards printed and distributed to six shops with the care line and one specification field silently blank on every one of them, having passed a validity check, a success message and a page count.

decision_gates: Where to put the house target, given that the honest target for a glaze led range is fidelity to the piece in the hand rather than the most attractive celadon.
Whether the fourteen frames are one shoot. The studio believes they nearly are; the row is the only place that can be settled.
How far to push a second session frame before it stops being worth saving, versus naming it in the note.
Knockout route per piece: the one-call route for the dark coherent glazes versus a material-named sweep selection inverted and filled for the pale ones whose rim has no contrast against the sweep.

Selection prompt wording on the tissue: naming the sheet takes the sheet, naming the ink's own visual properties takes the mark, and background removal on an enclosed arch is the wrong instrument entirely.
Whether the returned geometry from a selection describes one thing or many, and therefore whether cropping comes before selecting or after.
Whether to trust a confident crop on a near-uniform glaze surface or to spend the extra calls on an explicit selection.
What the supplied press card can structurally carry, and what to tell the studio about the fields it cannot.

client_brief:
Silver jewellery retouching with an honest plan for open centres

Argent & Faith needs ten seasonal pieces prepared as a consistent listing set. The silver should read as silver, with a common light and scale across the range. We do not want the high polish turned into featureless grey.

Some pieces have pierced or open centres. We know those are not equivalent to a solid silhouette, so please follow the intended ground treatment rather than shipping false transparency.

Ten client frames brought to one house neutral (one white point, one warmth in the metal, one black point, one crop logic) plus one licensed camera-scale frame graded into the same set, delivered as listing squares and card-ratio masters, every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame log of the corrections applied and of every reported resize. One set with one look, not ten separately optimised photographs and not the same picture at several sizes.

Ten pieces isolated from their sweep and delivered on the agreed plain ground, with genuinely open band centres and genuinely pierced tracery reading open ON THAT GROUND (the enclosed negative space filled to the delivered ground, because the connector cannot punch an enclosed alpha hole), plus transparent (alpha) versions for layering of the pieces that are single coherent solids. The isolation route is recorded per piece, because the pieces that are single coherent solids and the pieces that enclose negative space cannot be produced the same way: the coherent solids knock out to true transparency, while the open bands and the pierced medallion are filled to the agreed ground so the centre reads open rather than as a casting-fault plug. Each piece must hold when inspected adjacent to the others at listing size, on the ground it ships on.

The approval test is at listing size: do the pieces look like the same collection, and do the open areas sit correctly on their final ground? Supply alpha only for the solid pieces where that route is appropriate, and keep the method for each item in the production notes.

Available references and captures: bench_capsule/ (10 frames, 5472 x 3648); bench_block_mark.jpg (4032 x 3024); capsule_inventory.csv; house_notes.txt; boxed_card_in_hand.jpg.

Also in the archive, for background only: provenance_card_2026_PRINT.pdf. These do not add deliverables to this commission.

Please retain a clear connection between each seasonal piece, its corrected master and its listing export.

Please deliver a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note. Account for every supplied file and identify anything used only as reference, superseded or rejected. Stay with approved facts and copy. Do not silently replace weak assets; use only the stated stock or concept allowances, and record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and material compromises.

Budget: $1,800-$4,500 fixed. Target: 2 to 4 weeks. Reviews: One direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

price_band_and_audience: Retail 180 to 900 dollars (open bands 180 to 260, pierced medallion 420, signet 560, reliquary locket 900). Buyer 28 to 55, Northeast urban and coastal, buys one considered piece for herself or as a milestone gift and reads the metal and dimensions before buying. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the listing tile is mostly ground, the piece sits small and centred, the type is quiet and the provenance line is treated as editorial copy. If the same capsule sold at 25 dollars the correct answer would be the opposite artefact: busy flat-lays, four pieces to a tile, a price flash, and nobody would look at the centre of a band. An agent that ships a dense, price-led, high-saturation set has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,600 to 3,200 dollars fixed, or 50 to 80 dollars an hour for 30 to 45 hours.

assets_supplied.name: bench_capsule/ (10 frames, 5472 x 3648)
assets_supplied.kind: Product photography shot by a friend of the studio across two mornings on the same light grey paper sweep on the finishing bench, one piece per frame.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The whole capsule, shot on the bench under the north window. Three of them were still at the polisher so he came back a second morning. They look fine one at a time."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. (1) The second morning was overcast and a warm work lamp was switched on over the bench, so the three catch-up frames (Quarry Band, Vesper Medallion, Crescent Studs) carry a different illuminant from the other seven. Each looks entirely plausible alone, which is why the client believes they match. (2) The four high-polish pieces are mirrors. The grey sweep and the softbox are reflected in their shanks and bezels as a broad cool band that is part of the metal, not part of the background. While the pieces sit on the sweep they were shot on, this is invisible and correct. The moment a cut-out piece is placed on any other ground, the reflected cool band stays in the silver and the piece reads as lifted off one surface and dropped onto another. No selection, knockout, crop or adjustment reports anything about it, every call returns success, and the failure is only visible with several isolated pieces laid on the chosen ground at listing size.

assets_supplied.name: bench_block_mark.jpg (4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Hand-held phone photograph, shot square-on, of the studio's maker's mark engraved into the face of a polished steel bench block.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our mark, cut into the bench block by Nora's teacher. It is the only version of it that exists. We never had a file and there is nobody to ask."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark is incised into polished metal rather than printed in ink, and the block was lit from the left. Every stroke therefore reads as a bright specular flank on one side and a dark shadow flank on the other, with the true stroke width lying between them. A selection that names the mark as a dark engraved line takes the shadow flank only, so a trace made from it comes back with every stroke at roughly half its true weight and displaced consistently to one side. At canvas size this looks crisp, deliberate and entirely correct. It only declares itself as the wrong mark at the size the card foot and the lookbook cover actually reproduce it, and against the dark ground where the thin side of each stroke drops out. The mark also carries a fine assay-style border ring with an enclosed interior and two small closed counters, and how much of that ring survives this photograph's engraving through a trace is an empirical property of this frame that no tool reports.

assets_supplied.name: provenance_card_2026_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF for last season's boxed provenance card, 105 x 74 mm landscape, one card per piece, font subsets embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer ran last year. We do not have the working file and the woman who made it has retired. Keep the card as it is."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two structural facts nobody at the studio could tell you and nothing in the PDF announces. (1) The mark printed at the foot of the card is not a placed graphic. Prepress flattened it into the card's background artwork, so the conversion exposes exactly ONE graphic frame, the piece photograph, and no frame anywhere that the recovered mark can be bound into. The client has asked for the mark at the foot of every card and there is no place to put it. (2) The piece name, the metal and finish line and the dimensions line came across as one continuous story rather than three addressable frames, so those three fields have to be driven by ordered character offsets inside a single story while the provenance line and the piece number sit alone.

assets_supplied.name: capsule_inventory.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the studio's inventory system, one row per piece, with columns for piece name, metal and finish, dimensions, provenance line, piece number, retail price and a photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Ten pieces straight out of inventory. The provenance lines are Nora's own words and they go on the card as written."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. (1) The photo column points at a folder of web copies the studio made for its old site: 900 px JPEGs, already downscaled and already sharpened. Every filename resolves, every key binds, every card gets a photograph and nothing anywhere reports a problem. The cards simply print soft at trim, and no enlargement can put back what the studio's own export threw away, so the image map has to be rebuilt against the agent's own graded masters. (2) The provenance lines for the Vesper Medallion and the Lattice Pendant are swapped. The clerk copied one cell into the wrong row, so a pierced and hand-sawn medallion is described as cast solid and chased. Both rows are internally well formed, both bind, and only reading the copy against what the photograph actually shows settles it.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the isolated pieces actually belong on the ground that was chosen for them. Four of the ten are high-polish, and the grey sweep and the softbox are reflected in their shanks and bezels as part of the metal. On the sweep this is invisible and correct. Once the pieces are cut out and laid on the warm ivory ground at listing size, those four carry a broad cool band that belongs to a surface that is no longer in the picture, and they read as lifted off one ground and dropped onto another while the six matte and brushed pieces sit perfectly. Nothing reports it: the selections are clean, the knockouts return success, the fills return success, and each piece inspected alone looks entirely finished.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot either. The reflection is not a background to be removed, it is the subject's own surface, so no selection wording, polarity or route avoids it. It cannot be seen before the pieces are cut out, because on their original ground the reflection is the correct reflection. And it cannot be predicted from the frames, because how much of the sweep a given piece mirrors is a function of that piece's curvature and polish. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says a piece must look like it belongs on the ground it is sitting on, which is the client's own standing quality requirement of the same kind as any 'no sloppy masking' clause, and it says nothing about reflections, polish or which ground is at risk. The ground choice at step 8 is presented as an open taste decision with no hint that one option is materially harder than the other. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a design decision that invalidates an earlier one: either the ground pick changes (which changes the listing set, the card masters and the lookbook's ground), or four pieces need masked work confined to the reflected band on the metal itself, which is different work from anything done so far, or those four are re-shot and the client is told. The isolation is not simply re-fed with a different parameter.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Lay the isolated set on both candidate grounds and look at the polished pieces specifically. Then either re-take the ground decision from step 8 toward the neutral that the reflections can live on and re-derive the isolated set and the card masters against it, or go back into the imaging chain and run masked corrections on the reflected band on the four polished pieces before re-isolating them, checking the result adjacent rather than alone. Whichever route is taken, the lookbook's ground and the boxed card's photo treatment inherit it, so both have to be settled before the merge masters are uploaded.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A product page where four of the ten pieces visibly float on a ground they were never photographed on, on a capsule where the whole proposition is that the metal is honest and the photograph is not faked, in front of a buyer paying nine hundred dollars for a locket.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card actually exposes as editable structure. Two facts arrive only by converting and looking, and neither is under anybody's control: how the three copy lines came across (as three addressable frames or as one continuous story that has to be driven by ordered offsets), and whether every element the client asked for has a frame to live in. On this card the mark at the foot was flattened into the background artwork by prepress, so the conversion exposes exactly one graphic frame, the piece photograph, and there is no frame anywhere that the recovered mark can be bound into. The card renders perfectly without it and every tool in the chain reports success.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. Frame granularity and what prepress flattened are properties of a document made by a retired designer and a printer nobody can ask. They are not parameters, they are not reported before the conversion, and there is no read-ahead. The trajectory reaches the answer by converting, exporting and reading, which is the only route there is. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the mark should sit at the foot of the cards and that the card layout should be kept as it is. That is the client's requirement, not a description of the template's internals, and the brief mentions no frames, fields or offsets. The acceptance bar names an output requirement, that every line the old card carried is present on every page, which is the client's standing quality line rather than a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The mapping strategy itself changes shape (offset arithmetic inside one story rather than per-frame replacement), and the mark requirement has to be re-planned rather than re-run: it cannot be bound per record, so the agent must decide between accepting the flattened mark already printed on the card and saying so, rebuilding the card family on the authoring surface at the cost of the layout the client asked to keep, or telling the client the request cannot be met inside their own artwork. That is a different deliverable route, not the same operation on changed input.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping as ordered offsets computed from the reconstructed story rather than per-frame replacement, re-order any rows sharing a uid against the original text, re-validate, re-prepare, and re-verify by round-tripping the IDML and grepping for every placeholder before any page is merged. Then take the mark decision explicitly, carry it into the press file and the per-piece cards consistently, and write it into the handover as something the client is told before the printer sees the file rather than after.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A press run of boxed cards that binds name, dimensions and number correctly on every card while the metal and finish line is silently absent, and where the studio's mark, the one thing the client said had to be at the foot of every card, is quietly whatever the retired designer left baked into the artwork. Every tool in the chain reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives being made and being imported. The mark is an engraving in polished steel lit from one side, so every stroke has a bright flank and a dark flank with the true width between them, and a trace taken from the dark flank comes back at roughly half weight and displaced to one side. At canvas size that trace is crisp and looks correct. Only at the size the card foot and the cover actually reproduce it, and only against the dark ground the cover uses, does it show as a hairline ghost with its border ring broken. Separately, how the importer normalises the trace once it arrives (loose ungrouped geometry rather than one coherent mark) is reported by nothing except the returned markup, and the rendition preview shows canvas one only, so the answer for the other three canvases has to come from the markup rather than from looking.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it. Which flank a selection takes and how much of the border ring survives are functions of this photograph's lighting and this engraving's depth, and the tracing call takes no options at all, so the only lever is the raster preparation and the only way to learn which preparation is needed is to see the failure. There is no first-time-right to aim at, only an empirical answer at real size on the real ground. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for the mark back as artwork usable at any size, including reversed out of dark, and never mentions strokes, weights, flanks or minimum sizes. It does not ask how small the mark can safely go, which would have made this a stated deliverable. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to produce a different asset: re-select on the specular flank or across both flanks, trace the colour-accurate plate instead, or re-cast the cover lockup with the mark larger or demoted. The earlier deliverable changes, and the lookbook composition is re-authored around whichever decision that is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-run the recovery with a selection worded for a different part of the incision or through the colour-accurate plate route, place the result at true card-foot size and at cover size on the dark ground and look at it there rather than at canvas size, re-take the cover lockup decision if the mark will not hold, re-author and re-upload the HTML, re-run the readiness check, re-export and verify again through both channels rather than assuming the second export took. The card foot decision from the earlier checkpoint has to be revisited with whatever mark actually survives.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A stockist lookbook whose cover carries a broken hairline ghost of the studio's mark on a dark ground chosen for a mark that no longer reads, and product pages carrying the same half-weight artwork at every size, delivered as the client's recovered logo with the export having reported success.

decision_gates: Whether the ten frames are one shoot. The client says they are and three of them are not.
Which ground the capsule ships on, decided as a taste question at first and then re-decided against what the polished pieces actually do on it.
Isolation route per piece: the one-call knockout is right for a coherent solid and wrong for anything enclosing negative space, and the wrong route returns a filled centre that reports success.
Whether the inventory copy matches the pictures, when two provenance lines are internally well formed and simply attached to the wrong pieces.

Whether to bind the client's own web-copy photo references or rebuild the image map against the agent's graded masters, and whether repointing a client's data silently is the same act as repointing it and saying so.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the client's text or to reconstruct the story independently from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification, when nothing instructs a re-export and grep of the prepared template and nothing warns if it is skipped.
How to answer a request that the client's own artwork cannot carry, once it is clear there is no frame for the mark on the card.

why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of jewellery. It fails all three gates. IDENTITY: these are ten specific pieces a buyer receives in a box, and the mark is a specific engraving cut by a named teacher into a specific bench block. A regenerated ring is a different object being sold under a photograph of it, and a regenerated mark is another studio's logo. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next season is a data change rather than a re-commission, and a native document with live text and real vector geometry so the studio changes prices itself. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this placeholder exist, is the photograph on this card the piece named on it, does this cutout belong on this ground, does this trace hold its ring at card-foot size. None of that is a generation problem.

client_brief:
Catalogue-ready component photography, including difficult internal openings

Girdermark sells replacement components. A buyer needs to recognise the finish and the shape, not admire a dramatic studio treatment. Our twelve components were photographed over two bench sessions and need a consistent technical presentation.

Please keep all four finishes distinct while aligning scale, neutral balance and the catalogue crops. Through-bores, open frames and handles must be treated as part of the product geometry, not filled in for convenience.

Scope for quotation

Twelve in-house frames from two sessions brought to one technical neutral with the four finishes still distinguishable from one another, delivered as a catalogue grid tile and an in-context bench crop per SKU at consistent subject scale, plus one licensed context frame graded into the same neutral. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Twelve parts isolated onto the agreed neutral ground for the sheets, with through-bores, open frames and enclosed handles genuinely open rather than filled with captured bench, and the isolation route recorded per SKU because parts that are single coherent solids and parts that enclose voids cannot be produced the same way. True finish colour preserved through the isolation, since a buyer specifies from these pictures.

Inputs: bench_sessions/ (12 frames, 4800 x 3200); datasheet_2025_PRINT.pdf; parts_export.csv; finishes_note.txt; counter_2024.jpg.

For each SKU, document the isolation route and check the result on its actual neutral ground. A clean outer silhouette is insufficient if a hole still contains bench background or a thin edge has disappeared.

We need reusable production files and straightforward evidence of the checks, so the catalogue team can place the range with confidence.

This is a fixed-price commission at $1,800-$4,500, with a target of 2 to 4 weeks. The agreed review allowance is one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

Handover: a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note. price_band_and_audience: Parts from 400 dollars (contactor blocks, relay sockets, restrictor brackets) to 9,000 dollars (governor sheave assembly, door operator arm assembly). Buyer 35 to 60, a working service technician, a building maintenance supervisor or an electrical contractor who has specified this class of part for twenty years and judges a supplier's credibility by whether the photography and the spec table agree. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the correct artefact is flat, even, technical: one neutral, true finish colour, the whole part in frame at consistent scale, generous spec tables set for reading, prices plain in the run of the sheet, no styling, no atmosphere, no lifestyle. Push it toward bright consumer-tool photography with shallow depth and warm light and the buyer reads it as a 15 dollar hardware brand and doubts the load ratings printed beside it, which is exactly the failure this client describes. Push it the other way into dark cinematic hero photography and it reads as marketing rather than a parts catalogue. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,500 dollars fixed, or 45 to 70 dollars an hour for 35 to 50 hours.

assets_supplied.name: bench_sessions/ (12 frames, 4800 x 3200)
assets_supplied.kind: In-house product photography of twelve SKUs shot on the stainless bench top in the back of the warehouse under shop fluorescents, across two Saturdays.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Most of them one Saturday, the rest a few weeks later. Same bench, same camera. They do not look like the same catalogue."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. (1) A failed fluorescent tube was replaced between the sessions, so the six later frames carry a green cast that a buyer reads as a finish difference rather than a lighting difference, which is the one thing this client cannot ship. (2) Three of the SKUs are long, thin and made of the same brushed steel as the bench they are lying on: the guide rail section, the door operator arm and the traveling cable clamp. On these frames a subject-aware crop has almost no contrast to find, so it latches onto the one high-contrast feature in the frame (the painted end fitting, the yellow cable jacket) and returns a tight crop of that fitting at low detection confidence while reporting complete success. The resulting grid tile is sharp, well composed and plausible, and it shows a fragment of the part rather than the part. Nothing declares it except the confidence and bounds values buried in the response and the sight of the twelve tiles laid out as the grid they are for.

assets_supplied.name: datasheet_2025_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF of last spring's per-part data sheet, US Letter portrait, one part per page, fonts embedded, produced from the distributor's own system through a full print engine so it converts cleanly. Carries a fourteen-row spec table, a part photograph, a dimensional line drawing and a compliance footnote.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer sent us last spring. We do not have the working file and nobody here knows how it was built. Keep it exactly as it is."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three facts nobody at Girdermark could tell you. (1) The system that generated the sheet set the entire fourteen-row spec table as ONE continuous story with tab characters between each parameter and its value, so there are no per-parameter frames to map and every value has to be driven by ordered offsets inside a single story. (2) The mapping readout of that story silently omits the run holding the compliance footnote while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well-formed and every character offset past it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on the resulting arithmetic, the placeholder step reports success, and the two fields that sit past the omission never become placeholders at all. (3) The two graphic frames are distinguishable only by their bounds and their link, and neither is named for what it holds.

assets_supplied.name: parts_export.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the distributor's stock system, one row per SKU, with columns for part number, description, the fourteen spec parameters, list price, dealer price and an image column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our export, straight out of the system. The spec values are ours and they are what the customer holds us to."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Thirteen rows for twelve parts: a superseded part number the system still emits, flagged only by a discontinued date column the client never mentions. Part numbers carry a leading apostrophe from the spreadsheet that exported them. The image column is a plain header holding full local paths rather than bare filenames and without the prefix the merge's own image contract requires, so a naive run binds no images at all or binds the template's original photograph to every page. And three of the descriptions are full compliance strings running four times the length of the others, written by the compliance clerk, which the client has said are held to as written.

assets_supplied.visible_description: "How to tell them apart: galvanised is the spangled dull one, zinc plate is the bright bluish one, clear anodised is the flat grey one, powder coat is the flat black one."

assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the counter looks like. Nothing fancy."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a subject-aware crop found the part. Three SKUs are long, thin and made of the same brushed steel as the bench beneath them, so the crop has almost no contrast to work with and latches onto the one high-contrast feature in the frame, returning a tight, sharp, well-composed crop of a painted end fitting or a yellow cable jacket, at a detection confidence well under any level worth trusting, while reporting complete success. Which frames behave that way is a property of these particular photographs (this part on this bench under this light) and cannot be predicted from the SKU list, the finishes note or the frame previews. The tile looks like a competent product tile. It is a picture of a fragment.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care alone does not either. The failure is produced by a detection step whose only honest signal is a confidence value and a bounds rectangle buried in a response that otherwise reads as success, and the crop that comes back is genuinely well composed, so there is no visual alarm in the artefact itself. An agent can only learn which frames are affected by running the crop on each of them and either reading the confidence or laying the twelve tiles out together and noticing that three of them are showing the wrong thing. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for a grid tile per part that shows the whole part rather than a corner of it, which is an ordinary client quality requirement, and says nothing about contrast, detection or which parts are at risk. No asset description names the three SKUs, and no earlier step reports subject contrast as a number. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to abandon the subject-aware route for those frames and drive the crop from an explicit selection's own bounds instead, which is a different operation on a different input, and then to re-take the scale policy for the whole grid, because three tiles derived a different way will not sit at the same subject scale as the other nine unless the policy is re-decided across all twelve.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive the affected tiles by making an explicit selection of the part, taking its bounds, and cropping to those bounds with padding, rather than asking the crop to find the subject. Then re-lay all twelve tiles and re-decide the subject scale policy so the re-derived three sit with the nine, which in practice means re-cropping some of the nine as well. Transcribe every crop's reported metadata into the handover so the client can see which tiles were produced by which route.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A catalogue index in which three of twelve parts are represented by a sharp, confident photograph of the wrong end of the part, sent to buyers who order by looking at the picture and then reading the number beside it, from a supplier whose entire pitch is that the picture and the number agree.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's sheet actually exposes, and then whether the mapping built against it landed. Two things arrive only by running. First, the granularity: the fourteen-row spec table came out of the distributor's system as ONE continuous story with tab characters between parameter and value, so there are no per-parameter frames to map and everything must be driven by ordered offsets inside a single story, and the two graphic frames are distinguishable only by bounds and link. Second, the yield: the mapping readout of that story omits the run holding the compliance footnote while keeping its line break, so the string still parses as well-formed and every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on internally consistent wrong arithmetic, the placeholder step reports success, and the two fields past the omission never become placeholders.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and diligence alone cannot either. Granularity is not a parameter, is not reported before the conversion, and has no read-ahead: the only route to the answer is to convert, export and read. The yield failure is worse, because it is produced by a convenience readout that presents as complete, so an agent that reads carefully and computes offsets diligently from the readout it was handed produces arithmetic that is internally consistent and wrong, and every downstream tool agrees with it. The only defence is an independent reconstruction of the same text from a different channel, which nothing in any tool description prompts and whose necessity is invisible until the two disagree. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says keep the sheet exactly as it is and put this year's specs through it, and mentions no frames, fields, stories or offsets. The acceptance bar states an output requirement, that every field the 2025 sheet carried is present on every page, which is the client's standing requirement rather than a warning. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The source of truth behind the mapping changes, from a tool readout to a reconstructed story, and with it the whole mapping is re-authored with re-ordered same-uid rows. If the photograph turns out to have been mapped into the drawing's frame, the image binding is re-planned before the merge rather than after.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story by concatenating the IDML content runs, recompute every offset against that string, re-order rows sharing a uid so their positions hold against the original text, rebuild and re-validate the mapping, re-run the template preparation, and re-verify by round-tripping IDML and grepping for every placeholder before a single page is merged. Settle which of the two graphic frames holds the photograph by rendering a page and reading it against the 2025 printed reference rather than by assuming the larger frame is the photograph.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twelve data sheets that bind part number, description and most of the spec table correctly while the compliance line and the field after it are silently absent from every page, printed and put on a counter for technicians who order to those exact values, with every tool in the chain having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the importer actually did with the two constructs the collateral depends on: the dimensional line drawing carried in as vector, and the spec comparison carried in as a real table. Neither the drawing's leader lines and dash treatment nor the table's per-cell strokes and cell backgrounds can be confirmed to have survived by any means other than reading the markup the import returns, and every drop this importer performs comes back as a success with no warning at all. The A1 poster and the slides compound it: the rendition preview shows the first canvas only, so whatever happened on the poster and the slides is reported by the returned markup and by nothing else.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it. How this importer normalises a given construct is not documented anywhere the agent can read ahead, is not a parameter, and is not signalled by the response status. Authoring the drawing more carefully does not tell you what happened to it, and the one visual channel available shows only the canvas that is least likely to be affected. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for live text and a drawing that is real artwork rather than a picture of a page, which is the client's requirement for an editable file, and it names no construct, no importer and no failure. No earlier step claims to have solved it, because no earlier step has exported anything. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to re-author the construct itself, which means redrawing the dimensional artwork in a form that survives, or rebuilding the comparison in a different structure, and then re-running the readiness check and re-exporting, and the layout around the changed construct changes with it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Parse the returned markup per canvas and check, for each canvas rather than only the first: that every photograph resolved to real image data rather than the importer's placeholder, that the drawing arrived as path shapes rather than one flattened element or nothing at all, that the table arrived as real cells rather than a stack of loose text, that every text element carries the intended face and weight rather than a silent fallback, and that no element's resolved position runs past its declared canvas width. Then re-author whichever constructs did not survive, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and inspect again rather than assuming the second export took.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A counter poster and a slide set delivered as the client's editable file in which the dimensional drawing is gone or flattened, the spec comparison is a heap of loose text, and nobody notices because the only page anyone looked at was the line card.

why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these frames into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of machinery. IDENTITY: these are twelve specific parts with specific finishes that a technician orders and installs, and a generated part fabricates a finish, which on a page that also carries load and duty values is effectively a false spec claim. SPEC: the client needs one sheet per current part at US Letter and 300 ppi with fourteen spec values bound verbatim from their own stock export, twelve separately named sheet files each containing the part their filename claims, a grid tile per part showing the whole part, and no delivered file larger than its source. None of that can be produced or checked by generation. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next season's specs are a data change, and a native document with live text, a real table and real vector artwork so prices can move in March. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this placeholder get created, did this crop find the part, is this photograph in the photograph's frame, do these four finishes still read as four finishes. That is not a generation problem.

client_brief:
Recovery-gear image system with a controlled Ridge Blue colourway

We need Summit & Sable's field and bench photographs to read as one recovery-gear range. There are twenty supplied captures, with webbing, stitching and hardware that need to remain convincing at close range.

The Ridge Blue colourway is a particular concern. Please alter the webbing regions, not the whole photograph, and compare against the supplied spool reference. Where a digital change cannot make a trustworthy match, state the limit and whether a reshoot is needed.

First, the campaign masters:
Twenty masters brought across two source families to one house look (one white point, one black point, one contrast behaviour, and the same webbing colour for the same SKU in both families), plus one wide detail crop per SKU that actually contains the stitching and the hardware finish, plus one licensed camera-scale trail frame graded into the same world. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with its tradeoff record captured, and a per-frame parameter log naming which frames could not be brought all the way and why.

Then, Ridge Blue:
The second webbing colourway produced on the existing photography as a region confined build, with the weave, the sheen and the shadow inside the coil intact and behaving as one light, judged by eye against the supplied spool reference and delivered across every SKU that shares that webbing so the range carries one blue rather than several. Delivered with the parameters applied and with an honest written statement of how far the colour could be taken and what a reshoot would buy.

Finally, the retailer set:
Nine square marketplace primaries at intake size on a plain ground with nothing else in the frame, plus nine genuinely transparent variants used on the brand charcoal and over field grounds, both cut from the same graded master. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Materials supplied: summit_bench_packshots/ (9 frames, 5472 x 3648); summit_field_frames/ (11 frames); summit_ridge_blue_spool.jpg; summit_mark_export.png; summit_label_photo.jpg.

Also in the archive, for background only: summit_range.csv. These do not add deliverables to this commission.

Do not let a range-wide colour correction erase differences in weave, sheen or hardware. We need to see the actual products, consistently presented, across the plain and transparent outputs.

The final package should contain a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note, with every source file accounted for, including references and rejected or superseded material. Use the approved information without inventing missing facts. Only the stated stock or concept exceptions permit substitution; document every omission, replacement, reconciliation and material quality compromise.

Fee range: $4,000-$8,500 fixed
Delivery target: 4 to 6 weeks
Included reviews: Direction approval, first-production proof, and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

price_band_and_audience: Value band recovery and overlanding gear at thirty five to two hundred and twenty dollars, buyer twenty five to fifty, off-road and 4x4 owners buying on rugged credibility and price. The band is load-bearing and it cuts against the obvious instinct: the correct look here is honest, bright, hard-wearing and legible, flat daylight on the primaries and unstyled dust on the secondaries, with type that reads as workwear signage rather than as a lifestyle magazine. The same nine SKUs at a nine hundred dollar premium expedition band would correctly be shot dark and cinematic, low key, warm rim light, heavy blacks, tiny type in a lot of black space, and shipping that treatment here reads as pretending and prices the brand out of its own buyer's search results. Push the other way into hard flash, saturated orange and shouting sale-shaped graphics and it drops below its band into disposable import territory, which is exactly the comparison the detail crops exist to win. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even with every technical gate green. A posted job of this shape runs 800 to 2,000 dollars fixed, or an ongoing retainer.

brand_identity.tagline: Gear that looks like it works.
brand_identity.sector: E-commerce and retail, value-band recovery and overlanding gear
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019 in Boulder, Colorado. Small owner-run shop, under ten people, selling on a marketplace and its own storefront.
brand_identity.about: We make recovery straps, soft shackles and overlanding kit for people with a lifted truck and a real budget. Nine SKUs from 35 to 220 dollars. Our buyer is not paying for a name, he is paying because the gear looks like it will hold when he is stuck at dusk on a fire road. The detail is the whole argument: the stitching and the hardware finish are what separate us from the cheap import sitting next to us in search results.
brand_identity.audience: Off-road and 4x4 owners aged 25 to 50, buying on rugged credibility and price. They trust flat daylight and visible workmanship and they distrust anything that looks staged or expensive.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Value band, 35 to 220 dollars. The look is bright, hard-wearing and legible, honest daylight on the plain-ground shots and unstyled dust on the field shots. Never premium-expedition cinematic, never discount-banner loud. Either extreme reads as pretending and loses the buyer.
brand_identity.typography: Type should read as workwear signage: a sturdy condensed or grotesque for headlines and spec callouts, a clean neutral text face for body and the range table. Bold but balanced, plenty of negative space, nothing magazine-like.
brand_identity.voice: Blunt and plain. We say what the gear does and what it is rated for. Certified working loads are stated as certified and never rounded or dressed up.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The only brand mark file we can find is a flat screen-size export our old developer left us, plus a photo of the same mark on a woven label. We have no scalable artwork and no written guidelines. Charcoal is our storefront ground and Ridge Blue is the new webbing colour we are introducing. Treat the notes above as direction, not a locked system.
brand_identity.values: Honesty in the picture and the spec. Durability over shine. Fair price for real capability. If an edit would make the product look like something it is not, we would rather it stayed plain.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the colour the client named can be reached at all on this material. The correction runs, reports success and returns a strap that is blue, so there is no error, no warning and nothing in any response that distinguishes a move that landed from one that ran out of range. What only appears when the result is set beside the spool photograph is that a hue move of this distance does not arrive: the webbing comes back desaturated and a shade away, reading as a flat colour laid over a strap rather than as a strap in that colour, which is precisely the outcome the client wrote their acceptance line to forbid. Pushing the same move further does close the hue gap and takes the weave and the coil shadow with it, and that too reports success.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the distance between the current webbing and the named colour is a fact about two physical materials that no tool reports and that the spool photograph alone does not settle. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the brand is launching a second colourway and will not reshoot, and the acceptance line about naturalness is the client's standing requirement rather than a warning about range. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the answer is a different construction, building the colourway as a confined move plus a tonal rebuild rather than as a single hue shift, and possibly a different answer entirely, which is telling the client which of the two colourways can be shown honestly and which needs a shoot.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the colourway as a confined, multi-part build on the webbing selection alone, re-judge the weave and the coil shadow at full resolution rather than at preview scale after each attempt, re-do every SKU that shares that webbing so the range does not carry two different blues, and write the limit into the handover rather than shipping a flat strap and hoping.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A relaunch whose headline new product is a photograph of a strap with a flat blue rectangle where the weave was, delivered against an acceptance line that names that exact outcome as unacceptable, on a range whose entire price argument is that the gear looks like it works.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the isolated products are actually isolated. Three of the nine SKUs are soft shackles and sewn-loop straps whose eyes are open holes through the product, and a subject knockout has no way to punch an enclosed interior: it returns a cutout that is clean at the outer edge, complete looking and entirely convincing, with the eye quietly filled by the captured pale sweep. On the marketplace's plain near-white ground that fill is invisible, so the primary passes. The same cutout on the brand charcoal, and again over a field frame in the secondary tiles, shows a grey plug sitting in the middle of a hole. Nothing in the response distinguishes those three frames from the six solid ones.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it, because the defect is a property of the product's topology rather than of the sequence, and it is legible only on the second ground, which is a deliverable rather than a diagnostic. (b) Nothing states it: the brief lists the SKUs and says the primary must be on a plain ground, which is the intake rule, not a disclosure about holes. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the correct route is a different chain, selecting the sweep as a material so the selection reaches through the eye, inverting it, and filling, rather than asking a subject detector for a product.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-judge every cutout on the charcoal and over a field frame rather than on the plain ground, re-derive the three affected SKUs through a material-named sweep selection inverted and filled so the eye stays open, and re-cut both the primary and the charcoal tile from the corrected master so the two grounds do not disagree.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Nine primaries that pass intake and a storefront whose hero tiles show the brand's own soft shackles with their eyes plugged grey, which reads to this buyer as a fake product photograph on exactly the SKUs that carry the highest margin.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer treats the two heroes, which were authored differently for good reasons. The desktop hero puts the product to one side with real negative space, so the photograph is placed as an image element and survives. The mobile hero is a full bleed crop with type over it, which is naturally authored as a panel carrying the photograph behind its content, and that construction is discarded outright: the panel arrives as an empty box with correct geometry and no picture, at full success and with no warning of any kind. The document's rendition shows the first canvas only, and the first canvas is the desktop hero, which looks exactly right. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel in which the mobile hero, the two tile canvases and the section band exist at all.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Doing it right the first time presumes knowing which of two ordinary ways of putting a photograph on a canvas survives this importer, which no response reports and no checklist enumerates, and no ordering changes it because the drop happens at import and the import is the last step. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a desktop hero and a mobile hero and for negative space, which is art direction. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix re-authors the canvas around a different construction, an image element sized and positioned to bleed with the type placed over it, which changes how the whole mobile composition is built.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-author every canvas that carries a full bleed photograph around an image element rather than a panel, re-check the same markup for the other things that silently do not survive, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit all five canvases from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A storefront package delivered as an editable file in which the mobile hero, which is where most of this buyer's traffic actually lands, is an empty box with a headline floating on it, having reported success throughout and having previewed perfectly on the one canvas anybody looked at.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of recovery straps. IDENTITY: these are this brand's actual nine SKUs with their actual certified working loads, their actual hardware and their actual stitching, and the detail crops exist precisely to prove the physical product is not the cheap import, so a regenerated strap defeats the entire commission. The second colourway is a change to an existing photograph of an existing product, not an invention of a new one, and the client's acceptance line says so in their own words. SPEC: the marketplace intake demands a plain ground with nothing else in frame, square, above a minimum size and with no interpolated pixels, while the storefront demands the opposite ground from the same master, and a hole through a product must remain a hole; none of that is satisfiable or checkable in a generated image. EDITABILITY: the client asked explicitly for the file plus labelled exports so their own team can swap copy later, which is a definition of the deliverable, not a preference. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this colour move actually land, did this cutout leave the eye open, did this canvas keep its photograph.

client_brief:
Consignment listing photographs where the holder and label remain legible

SlabVault handles graded collectibles. A listing photograph has to show the item and the evidence around it: holder, label and seal. Glare is a problem in the current set, but we cannot replace unreadable information with a convincing guess.

Please bring the usable photographs to one neutral listing standard, then prepare the required placements. The full object must remain visible. If a label has no recoverable information in the capture, hold that lot back and tell us.

Listing masters and exception record: The consignment brought to one house neutral: one neutral, one black point, one ground and one slab height in frame across every lot that ships, with the glare worked back on the label wherever there is anything to work with, plus one licensed camera-scale surface frame graded into the same world. Per lot parameter log with a line on why each lot differs from its neighbours, and an explicit held-back list with a reason per lot.

Placement exports: Square site tiles on the house ground with the slab square in frame and given the room the reference page gives it, plus genuinely transparent versions carrying real alpha at the holder edge for the marketplace's dark band, plus the taller comparison-strip crops. Every output shows the whole graded item, holder, label and seal included. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with its returned tradeoff record retained. One set with one cut logic, not one picture at several sizes.

Files available: slabvault_consignment_2026F/ (14 seller-submitted frames, 3024x4032 to 6000x4000); slabvault_lot_card.pdf; slabvault_lots.csv; slabvault_house_note.txt; slabvault_results_reference.png.

We will compare the square, dark-band and tall versions together. They need to be variations of an honest master, not different representations of the collectible. Please include the source-size limits and the reason for any rejected crop in the handover.

Please work within $900-$2,400 fixed and the 7 to 15 business days target. Allow for one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

Alongside the finished work, we need a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and Stock license and asset IDs. Keep a clear record of the supplied files used, retained for reference, superseded and rejected. Approved source information remains authoritative. Record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and quality limits, and do not use an undeclared replacement or invented fact to conceal a source problem.

source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork graded-collectibles storefront post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, from an online graded sports-card shop asking for its own phone-shot product photographs to be cut out, centred on a clean ground, resized to the storefront's sizes and named to the store's handles. That real post names no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional house SlabVault Cards; the two grading partners are the invented companies GRADEX and APEX, never any real grader, and every player, set and title on the slabs is invented. The ledger row that sat here (AO-112) was a cutout-and-resize exercise, which is the thin half of that post: the real shop's actual problem is that it does not shoot anything, its consignors do, and the sale ships listings, printed sleeve tickets and a dated auction-week set off the same fourteen photographs. price_band_and_audience: Consigned lots at 150 to 5,000 dollars, buyer 25 to 60 and condition literate. The band is load-bearing. At this value the buyer is reading the holder, the label and the corners out of the photograph, so the house look must be a neutral grey and black stage with one restrained accent, generous room around the slab, and absolutely no invented edge, shadow or shine, because anything added reads as something concealed. The same fourteen lots at a five dollar bulk-reseller band would correctly be shot tight, warm and saturated with a bright coloured tile and burned-in price flashes, and shipping that treatment here destroys the trust the whole business runs on. Push the other way into auction-house black velvet, gold rules and a serif masthead and it misprices a 150 dollar hockey card as a fine-art lot. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Graded with confidence, sold with proof
brand_identity.sector: Graded-collectible consignment (trading cards and comics)
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019 in Providence, Rhode Island; a four person consignment house
brand_identity.about: SlabVault Cards is a small consignment house that lists and settles graded collectibles for private sellers. Lots run from roughly 150 to 5,000 dollars per item, and buyers decide from the photograph alone, zooming into the holder, the label and the corners before they bid. Consignors shoot their own slabs on their own tables, so the house exists to bring many different rooms to one credible standard. Trust is the entire product: everything SlabVault presents has to read as accurate, unretouched and verifiable.
brand_identity.audience: Condition-literate collectors aged 25 to 60 who buy graded cards and comics at 150 to 5,000 dollars a lot, read the grade and certification line straight out of the image, and walk away from anything that looks staged or concealed.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Mid to upper consignment. Not a bulk reseller or a toy shop, and not a fine-art auction room. The presentation sits deliberately between the two: neutral, generous and evidential, never cheap and flashy, never gilded and theatrical.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet, legible pairing: a humanist sans for body copy and roster data, and a slightly firmer grotesque or restrained slab for lot numbers and headings. Type stays small, even and confident. No decorative or display faces.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, factual, collector to collector. States the grade, the grader and the condition without hype. Never breathless, never salesy. The photograph does the persuading.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: SlabVault has never held a proper brand kit. What exists is a house note describing the palette in words (grey, black, one amber accent already used on the printed stationery and the sleeve ticket), the grading partner names spelled the way the graders require, and the sale details. There is no logo file, no type specimen and no template, so the house look has to be established fresh and held consistently across the listings, the printed tickets and the auction-week set.
brand_identity.values: Accuracy over polish. Show the item exactly as submitted, give every slab room to be read, and never add an edge, shine or shadow that was not there. The buyer's confidence is the asset the whole business protects.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the glared lots have anything left to recover. A stripe of holder glare that is merely bright and a stripe that is fully clipped look identical in a preview: both are a white band across the label. Ask for the light portions to come back inside a confined selection and the clipped ones return a frame that is visually the same as the one handed in, at full success, with no warning that nothing moved. The second half is the mask itself: selections come back with no intermediate values, so the correction that does land on the recoverable lots has a hard boundary, and whether that boundary shows as a patch on this particular holder finish depends on the finish.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the information lives in the pixels under the stripe and is not readable from the frame. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the stripe has to come down and the acceptance bar sets a legibility standard, neither of which is a disclosure that some lots are past saving. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different route per lot: for a lot whose duplicate submission exists, switch to the other consignor's frame and bring that one to the house neutral instead; for the rest, back the correction off until the holder stops showing a patch and then judge whether the label reads, or hold the lot and request a reshoot.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Compare each glare result against the frame it was given rather than against the response, re-triage the three that did not move, re-run the neutral pass on any substituted frame from the start because it was never in the graded set, and re-cut the tiles, comparison crops and ticket thumbnails for every lot whose source frame changed.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Lots listed at 150 to 5,000 dollars whose grade and certification line are unreadable behind a white band, or whose label carries a visible rectangular paint patch, on a business whose buyers decide from the photograph and read a patch as concealment.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the one-call knockout hands back a graded slab or the card that was inside it. A graded collectible is a card sealed in a clear rigid holder, so which of the two is the subject is genuinely ambiguous, and on the lots shot on a pale counter the holder's edge has almost no contrast against its ground. On those frames subject detection can take the card and drop the holder, returning a cutout that is clean, complete, correctly feathered and entirely plausible at preview scale, at full success. Which lots this happens to is a property of each frame's own counter and lighting, not of the request. The same call also silently reduces oversized inputs, reported only as a downscaled entry inside the returned tradeoff object with output dimensions below source dimensions.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it. The defensible order is straighten, neutralise, knock out at source scale and then choose the crop, precisely so the cut edge is visible before the crop is locked, and there is no parameter that tells the tool a transparent holder is part of the subject. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a version with nothing behind it, and the acceptance line about showing the whole graded item is the house's standing listing rule, not a warning about a tool. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the affected lots go through a different chain entirely: select the counter surface by its own material properties, invert that selection, fill to the house ground, then crop from the selection's own returned bounds.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Inspect every cutout at full size against the dark band rather than against white, re-plan the knockout route for the lots where the holder did not survive, re-derive both the house-ground plate and the transparent version through the material-named route for those lots, and re-read every returned tradeoff record for downscaled and upscaled entries before any tile is called delivered.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Cross-listed primaries showing a bare card where the buyer is paying for the holder, the label and the seal, which on a graded-collectible marketplace is not a cosmetic defect but a misrepresented lot.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's sleeve ticket actually is once converted, and whether the mapping built from the readout survived preparation. Six blocks that read as separate fields on the printed card can convert into one text frame, in which case fields are addressed by position inside one story rather than by frame. Worse, the readout of that story is lossy: it can omit a whole run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly the length of the missing run. The validation pass then returns VALID with no warnings, and the preparation step returns completed successfully, while only some of the six placeholders are actually in the document. Nothing in any response distinguishes six of six from three of six.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not help, because the conversion granularity and the readout are both properties of the supplied PDF and are only knowable after conversion; and doing it right the first time would mean distrusting a readout that the tool's own validator has just endorsed. (b) Nothing states it: the client says the ticket has six things on it and a little picture, which is a true description of the printed card. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the fix is a different source of truth: rebuild the offsets from the reconstructed story text taken out of the document's own interchange file rather than from the readout, then prepare again and re-audit.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Round-trip the prepared template and check for each of the six placeholders by name, recompute every offset from the true reconstructed story text, prepare the template again, verify a second time, then re-run the merge and re-read the proof, including the lots whose condition notes run long against a frame that gives no overflow signal.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen sleeve tickets printed and bagged with the certification line and the consignor code missing, on the one document whose entire purpose is to travel inside the bag as the lot's proof of identity.

Whether the converted ticket can be mapped frame by frame or has to be mapped by position inside one story, which cannot be decided before looking.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the submissions into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of trading cards in plastic cases. IDENTITY: these are fourteen specific consigned lots, each with a real grader, a real grade and a real certification number printed on a label that a bidder reads out of the photograph, and a regenerated slab is a fabricated lot. Reproducing a graded item's own label is the entire value claim, and inventing an edge, a shine or a corner on a collectible photograph is misrepresentation, not retouching. SPEC: the marketplace needs square tiles at a stated size with nothing behind them and no interpolated pixels, and the printer needs one file with page count equal to row count, one lot per page, in roster order, with the right thumbnail on the right ticket, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the auction-week set is defined by being editable, because the closing date moves every season and a four person house cannot re-commission it. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this cutout keep the holder, did anything move under that glare, did all six fields actually land in the template.
