client_brief:
Eight-player card run with matched portraits and checked player identities

Continental Cup needs the eight-player release prepared from the supplied portraits and roster. The pictures come from two stadium lighting rigs; the cards come from a printer's PDF we need to make usable again.

The licensed player information is fixed. Please do not tidy names, statistics or other copy by inference. Each finished card must carry its own player's photograph and details, with the small-format result checked after export.

Portrait treatment
Eight portraits shot across two floodlight rigs brought to one house look (one black point, one warmth, one crop logic) plus one licensed camera-scale ground frame graded into the same look, delivered at card-cell ratio and at launch ratios, every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log and every tool-reported resize transcribed. One set with one look, not eight separately optimised pictures.

Trading-card production
One page per featured player in roster order, at trading-card trim, page count equal to the reconciled player count, with every field bound verbatim from the licensing export and that player's own hero photograph in the card cell. Accompanied by one single-card file per player named to the player and identity verified by opening it, and by 300 ppi proofs rendered from the merged document for sign-off. Produced by reverse-engineering the printer's flat 2025 card into a live merge template, so the template and the record of how it was derived are part of the handover.

Final comparison
A source-to-final contact sheet at matched scale that proves set consistency, identity or material preservation, and the disposition of every outlier. It must reference Continental Cup featured photography, eight portraits plus the licensed banner ground and function as approval evidence rather than decoration.

We provide cup26_portraits_raw/ (8 frames, 4800px long edge); cup26_card_2025_PRINTER.pdf; cup26_players.csv; cup26_sleeve_patch.jpg; cup26_stadium_wide.jpg; cup26_licensing_notes.txt.

The reusable merge template is important, but it is not the finished job on its own. We need the combined print run, correctly named individual files and proofs that demonstrate the actual cards are right.

Please deliver a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record. Account for every supplied file and identify anything used only as reference, superseded or rejected. Stay with approved facts and copy. Do not silently replace weak assets; use only the stated stock or concept allowances, and record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and material compromises.

$4,000-$8,500 fixed; 4 to 6 weeks. Review structure: Direction approval, first-production proof, and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

price_band_and_audience: Premium licensed collector programme. Pack twelve dollars, sealed box ninety-five, featured base cards trading roughly thirty to one hundred and twenty dollars on the secondary market. Buyers are 16 to 45, they collect officially licensed cup sets and they can tell a licensed set from a fan-made one at a glance. The band is load-bearing: at this level the treatment is deep and saturated with real floodlit blacks, one dominant player per card with the stadium reduced to atmosphere, and type set large and confident. If this were a community-league set at three dollars a pack the correct answer is the opposite artefact: flat daylight, bright neutral grounds, four players to a sheet, and no isolation work at all. An agent that ships bright, flat and cheerful has misread the commission even if every field binds, and an agent that ships neon gradients and glow has misread it the other way. A posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,500 dollars fixed, or 50 to 85 dollars an hour over 30 to 45 hours.

brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The brand files are largely lost. The studio that designed last year's card has closed, and all that survives is the flat file the printer ran, whose layout the retailers already recognise and want kept. brand_identity.values: Authenticity of the licence above all. Depict the real featured players and the real competition mark faithfully, print the licensing copy exactly as supplied, and hold one premium look across print and store so the set reads as sanctioned, not imitated.

assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things the client cannot see. (1) Rafael Duarte was shot with a floodlight tower directly behind him. His white sleeve, his near shoulder and the ball at his hip are clipped to paper white with nothing left in them at all. On a screen it reads as the most dramatic frame of the eight, and the photographer flagged it as his favourite. A highlight recovery on it moves nothing whatsoever, and that readout of nothing is the only evidence that exists. (2) Luka Petrov is the keeper, in a dark navy kit, standing against a shadowed block of crowd at almost the same value as the kit. A subject knockout on him bites into the shoulder and the near arm where kit and crowd share luminance, and his raised arm encloses a genuine see-through gap between forearm and head that comes back filled with captured crowd. Both calls report full success and both defects are invisible against a light ground.

assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card file the printer ran last year. It is all we have. The layout is right, keep it." A real press PDF at trading-card trim, 63.5 x 88.9 mm, fonts embedded, produced from a genuine page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries the player name, squad number, position, honours line and set year, plus the player photograph and a small placed crest.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three properties of how the closed studio built the 2025 document, announced nowhere. First, the printed card looks like five separately labelled fields but the placed images split the flow into two text frames only, and the split falls in an unobvious place, so several of the five lines share one continuous story and can only be driven by ordered offset arithmetic inside it. Second, the mapping readout of that multi-line story silently omits the run holding the honours line while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well-formed and every character offset after it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on the resulting arithmetic and the placeholder step reports success, and two fields never become placeholders. Third, the crest frame is a fraction of the size the printed card suggests, so the reproduction size of the recovered crest is geometry inherited from a printer nobody can ask.

assets_supplied.name: cup26_players.csv
assets_supplied.kind: data
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Straight out of the licensing database. Contractual copy, goes on the card as written." Columns for player, squad number, position, honours line, set year and a photo filename.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Nine rows for eight featured players: a player who withdrew from the tournament squad is still emitted by the database, with a blank squad number. Headers are mixed-case with trailing spaces and the photo column is a plain header holding bare filenames, which neither matches the delivered frames nor satisfies the merge image-column contract. And Marco Ferraz's honours line is roughly three times the length of the other seven, because someone pasted his whole club honours history into the field, while the card's honours frame is fixed depth and the client has forbidden shortening. Nothing reports the collision at merge time.

assets_supplied.name: cup26_sleeve_patch.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The competition mark, embroidered on an official's sleeve. We have never had it as a file." 4000px phone frame, shot square on in daylight, the patch on dark technical fabric.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is thread, not ink. The satin stitch throws a specular sheen along every strand, so a trace of it comes back with stitch hairs running off the edges and with strokes broken wherever a highlight crossed them. The mark's inner ring encloses a field that background removal returns as one solid opaque disc rather than a knockout. How much of the fine ring and the stitched rule actually survives this photograph's thread through this trace, at the size the card's crest frame reproduces it, is empirical and no tool reports it.

assets_supplied.name: cup26_stadium_wide.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "A wide one of the ground at kickoff, if it helps for the banner." The same photographer, the same night.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is 2200px on the long edge. He exported it for a social post and the original is gone. It cannot carry the store banner at the width the launch set needs without inventing pixels, and the crop tool will interpolate toward its cap and say so only in a tradeoff entry that is easy to skip.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That one of the eight frames cannot be brought to the set at all. The Duarte frame was shot into a floodlight tower and its white sleeve, near shoulder and the ball are clipped with nothing left in them. The only way to learn this is to apply a highlight correction and read a result in which nothing moves. Every other frame in the set responds normally to the same move, this one responds by not responding, and the tool reports success either way. At preview the frame reads as the most dramatic of the eight and the photographer flagged it as his favourite, so nothing about looking at it suggests a problem.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot either. There is no readout of headroom anywhere in the connector, no histogram, no measurement of any kind, and the agent is explicitly not measuring pixels. A frame with genuinely empty highlights and a frame that is merely bright look identical until a recovery is attempted, and the attempt is the measurement. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the pictures do not match and that one is brighter than the rest, which is a client describing a mismatch, not a disclosure that a frame is unrecoverable. No asset note, no acceptance line and no deliverable names Duarte or clipping. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is not to re-grade with different numbers, it is to decide that this player's card hero has to come from somewhere else, which changes what is licensed, what is cropped and what is escalated to the client, and to say so in writing rather than shipping a card at eighty percent.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Confirm the frame is genuinely empty rather than merely under-corrected by attempting recovery from a different direction and reading the same non-response, then decide the fallback: crop into the frame away from the clipped shoulder if enough of the player survives, or hold the card and name the frame to the client under their own standing request. Re-lay the remaining seven plus whatever replaces it and re-judge the set as a set, because pulling one frame moves the set's centre and the other seven may need to move with it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A featured card ships with the player's shoulder and sleeve as a flat white shape with no detail, in a saturated high-contrast set where every other card holds its highlights, and the retailer sees it as a printing fault in a licensed product.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the card heroes actually hold at the edge, on the ground they are going to be used on. Petrov is in dark navy against a shadowed block of crowd at nearly the same value, so the knockout bites into the shoulder and the near arm where there is no contrast to work with, and his raised arm encloses a gap that comes back filled with captured crowd rather than punched through. Whether a given photograph gives the subject detector enough separation is a property of that frame's light and that player's kit, not of the tool or the plan. The failure is completely silent: the call succeeds, the returned cutout looks correct at normal viewing size, and on the card's own light ground the missing shoulder and the filled gap are invisible. Only the deep-navy retailer tile, at close inspection, shows the pale slab inside the arm and the chewed edge.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. Every frame must be knocked out regardless of order, and there is no property of the file, no metadata and no tool response that reports edge quality. A careful agent choosing the right route for a coherent subject still gets a bitten edge on the one frame where kit and ground share value, because the route is not the variable, the photograph is. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for each player lifted cleanly off the stadium and mentions the deep-navy tile, which is the client stating what they need, not a warning that one frame will resist. No asset note names Petrov's kit or the crowd behind him. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The fix is a different operation on a different principle: name the ground material, invert the selection and fill it, rather than ask for the subject, and for the enclosed gap the direct route can never be made to work at all. The earlier asset is replaced, not re-fed.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-cut the affected heroes by naming the material behind the player rather than the player, invert and fill to the flat ground, and handle the enclosed gap as its own selection composited into the mask rather than expecting the subject route to punch it. Re-place on the deep tile and inspect again rather than assuming the second attempt took. Check the other seven at the same close inspection, because the reason to look was found on one frame and the reason to trust the rest has not been established.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The retailer's display tile shows a keeper with a pale slab of stadium crowd sitting inside the arc of his own raised arm and a shoulder eaten into the crowd behind it, in a licensed premium set, having been signed off against a light-ground proof where none of it was visible.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card actually becomes as editable structure, and then whether the mapping built against it landed. Two facts arrive only by running. First, granularity: whether the five printed lines come across as five addressable frames or collapse into a continuous story, and whether the photograph and the crest arrived as real graphic frames with integer ids, is a property of how the closed studio built the 2025 document and is under nobody's control. Second, yield: the mapping tool's convenience readout of the story silently omits the run holding the honours line while keeping its line break, so the string still parses as well-formed prose and every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns valid on internally consistent wrong arithmetic, the preparation step reports success, and two fields never become placeholders. Only an independent reconstruction of the story from the exported IDML's content runs, followed by a round trip and a grep of the prepared file, makes either fact visible.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Neither ordering nor diligence dodges it. Granularity is not a parameter and has no read-ahead. Yield is worse, because the failure is produced by a readout that presents as complete, so an agent that reads carefully and computes offsets diligently from the string it was handed produces arithmetic that is internally consistent and wrong, and every downstream tool agrees with it. The defence is a second reconstruction of the same text from a different channel, which nothing in any tool description prompts. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the layout is right and should be kept, and mentions no frames, offsets or mappings. The acceptance bar states an output requirement, that every card carries every line, which is the client's standing requirement and not a description of a cause. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. What changes is the mapping strategy and its source of truth, from placeholder replacement against a tool readout to offset arithmetic computed against a reconstructed story with same-frame rows re-ordered. The mapping is re-authored from a different text, not re-fed.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story by concatenating the IDML content runs, recompute every offset against that string, re-order rows sharing a uid so their positions hold against the original text, rebuild and re-validate the mapping, re-run the preparation, and re-verify by round-tripping IDML and grepping for every placeholder before any page is merged. If the photograph or the crest did not come across as a mappable frame, the binding has to be re-planned before the merge rather than discovered after it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A press card file that binds the player, the number and the set year correctly on all eight cards while the honours line is simply absent from every one of them, silently, with every tool in the chain having reported success, going to a printer against a contractual copy requirement.

decision_gates: The surface split: cards to the merge surface because they are record per page against a layout the client wants preserved, launch set to HTML authoring because it needs three canvas sizes and must stay editable.
Whether one house look can be reached from both nights, and how far each frame is pushed before it stops being worth saving.
What to do with the frame that will not come back, given the client called it the best of the eight.
Knockout route per frame rather than per set, and how to treat a gap enclosed by a limb that the direct route cannot punch.
On which ground the cut edges are judged, given that the ground the client will use is the only one that shows them.
Crop policy for the set as a whole versus per frame, and on the tight frames whether to expand generated edge material or crop looser, knowing the generated edge must itself match the house look.
The row-count discrepancy in the licensing export: whether dropping a row the database emitted is the agent's call or the client's to confirm, and how to say so.

Whether to trust the mapping tool's own readout of the client's text or to reconstruct the story from the document. One route is fast and produces confidently wrong arithmetic that every downstream tool blesses.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a picture of a trading card. IDENTITY: these are eight specific photographs of eight specific players under this tournament's floodlights, and the crest is a specific embroidered mark that has to be recovered from a photograph, not reinvented. A regenerated player is a different person and a regenerated crest is a different competition, which is the one thing a licensed programme cannot survive. SPEC: the client needs one page per featured player at card trim with contractual copy bound verbatim from a licensing database, eight separately named single-card files each containing the player its filename claims, and print-resolution proofs. A generated image satisfies none of that and cannot be checked against a roster. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next season is a data change rather than a re-commission, and a document with live text and real vector geometry so the on-sale date changes without a redo. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this highlight recover, does this cut edge hold on navy, did this placeholder actually get created, is this record clipped at trim, does this trace still read at card size. None of that is a generation problem.

client_brief:
Wedding retouching pilot: one warm house look across changing light

We are Fernwell & Rowe, and this is a pilot using the Hartley wedding shortlist. There are sixteen photographs spanning window light, golden hour and the reception. We want a natural warm treatment that holds together through those changes without giving every person the same skin colour.

Please use the full shortlist to establish the look; the six starred selections also need their full-resolution delivery. We are judging whether this is a reliable house treatment, not whether one sunset image can look spectacular.

All sixteen shortlisted frames carried through one stated house recipe to a single warm, natural, true-skin finish that holds across window light, late sun and coloured uplight when read in gallery order, delivered at review size, plus the six starred frames at full resolution with no interpolation anywhere and every tool-reported resize transcribed. Any frame that would not take the pass is pulled and named rather than forced. This is one pass with one recipe, not sixteen individual rescues and not one picture at several sizes.

A proof set on the real light and dark destination grounds, including full-resolution edge inspections, delivery-size previews, and explicit pass/fail notes. It must reference Hartley wedding house pass: sixteen review renditions and six full-resolution keepers and function as approval evidence rather than decoration.

Shortlist and references: hartley_selects/ (16 frames, camera scale); fernwell_seal.jpg; venue_snap.jpg; house_look_notes.txt.

Also in the archive, for background only: fernwell_card_2025_PRINTER.pdf; guest_households.csv. These do not add deliverables to this commission.

Name the frames that resist the treatment and explain the practical limits. The proofs should reveal edge or placement problems at the intended sizes, and the full-resolution files should not rely on interpolation to appear larger than their sources.

The commission is budgeted at $900-$2,400 fixed. We have allowed 7 to 15 business days, including one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

Handover: a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note. Include an inventory showing how every supplied file was used or why it was set aside. Keep factual content tied to the approved inputs. Any missing coverage, substituted asset, reconciliation or quality compromise must be declared; a weak source is not permission to invent or silently replace it.

source_provenance.original_anchor: The ledger entry for PHOTO-18 carries no quoted posted brief and no absorbed task, so this is stated plainly rather than dressed up: the engagement is built to the posted-job archetype the ledger records, a wedding and event photographer needing a fast, consistent first-pass polish across a very large set so the gallery reads finished and even before client review, at a full-day coverage band of 3,200 to 5,500 dollars. That archetype is a standing category on the freelance marketplaces (walk-away batch retouching for wedding photographers, priced per event or per season) and it is the same shape the connector's own retouch-portraits routing describes: a folder of frames from one event, polished and returned ready to review. The rebuild verdict applies because the ledger concept as it stood was a single-surface batch operation whose deliverable list was one gallery at several sizes. Here the batch pass is the pilot half of a season partnership, and it is joined by the couple-facing print run and the studio's own venue-partner collateral, which is what a studio actually buys when it takes on a post-production partner. The studio, the couple, the households and the venue are all invented: Fernwell & Rowe, the Hartley wedding, the Orangery at Ashcombe Park.

real_brief_anchor: The ledger entry for PHOTO-18 carries no quoted posted brief and no absorbed task, so this is stated plainly rather than dressed up: the engagement is built to the posted-job archetype the ledger records, a wedding and event photographer needing a fast, consistent first-pass polish across a very large set so the gallery reads finished and even before client review, at a full-day coverage band of 3,200 to 5,500 dollars. price_band_and_audience: Full-day wedding coverage 3,200 to 5,500 pounds, couples aged 27 to 38, booking a Cotswolds country-house venue eighteen months out. The band is load-bearing on every decision. At this level the expected finish is warm, natural and true to skin, delivered fast and even across an entire day, because the couple's parents will look at these prints for thirty years. Push it toward a heavy stylised grade, crushed blacks, teal shadows and a strong preset signature, and it reads as a cheaper filtered package that the couple will regret; leave it flat and uncorrected and it reads as unfinished at the price. The venue leave-behind sits at the same band: warm paper, generous white space, one photograph doing the work, prices and dates set plainly. A glossy dark luxury treatment would misprice the studio to a venue that books at this level, and a bright busy collage would undersell it. emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That no single named recipe holds the whole day, and specifically where it breaks. The preset catalogue gives names and nothing else, the preset tool is whole-frame with no mask, and what a given recipe does to a face is a function of the illuminant in that frame. The reception block is not one illuminant: the uplighters were switched from amber to magenta partway through, so a warm recipe that is correct everywhere else pushes the post-switch frames to plum skin. Every call succeeds, every frame looks like a plausible photograph on its own, and the studio itself has never named the switch. The break exists only as a discontinuity in the run, so it can only be seen by applying the recipe to the whole set and then laying the result out in gallery order and looking at it as a sequence.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and diligence alone cannot either. There is no way to interrogate a preset except by applying it, no mask to confine it, and no measurement anywhere. An agent that previews the sixteen first sees sixteen plausible frames from a long day; the fact that two of them are lit by a different colour of light than the frames on either side of them in the same block is not visible as a defect until a single treatment has been applied to both and the two sit adjacent. (b) Nothing states it. The brief names three situations, which is the client's own account of their day and is what makes the trap work, and it says nothing about the uplighters changing. No asset note, no acceptance line and no deliverable names the switch or the frames. The acceptance bar asks for skin to be true across the run, which is the studio's standing quality requirement, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to change what the deliverable IS: the house pass stops being one recipe and becomes a recipe plus a named pre-correction for an identified group, which is the thing the studio will be held to for the rest of the season, and it has to be written up as such.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Split the reception block into two treatment groups by illuminant rather than by moment, apply a correction toward the house neutral to the post-switch group before the recipe rather than after it, re-run the recipe across the whole set so the pass stays one pass, and re-lay the run in gallery order and judge it again as a sequence rather than spot-checking the frames that were changed. Then rewrite the recipe in the note as what it actually is, because a recipe with an unnamed exception is not a recipe the studio can hold anyone to.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A gallery handed to a couple in which the first dance and everything after it has plum skin, sitting immediately after frames that are warm and true, delivered as the studio's proven house pass and about to be applied unchanged to nine hundred frames of the next wedding.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the studio's own card artwork actually exposes as editable structure. The printed card shows a photograph, so a per-household picture is a reasonable thing to plan for, and the guest data supports it. But the designer flattened the photograph into the page artwork rather than placing it, so the conversion exposes no addressable graphic frame for it at all, and per-household picture variation is structurally impossible inside the client's own file no matter how the data is shaped. On the text side the household line and the message share one continuous story while the date line sits alone, so the fields cannot be addressed uniformly. Both facts are properties of how a designer who is no longer reachable built a document two years ago, they are reported by nothing, and the conversion itself returns success either way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot substitute for it. Granularity is not a parameter, is not declared in the PDF, and has no read-ahead: the only route to the answer is to convert, export the document structure and look. A careful agent that plans the binding from the printed card plans a picture frame that does not exist. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the artwork came from the printer and that nobody knows how it was built, which is a client explaining why they have no working file, not a description of its internals. No asset note in the client's hands, no acceptance line and no earlier step says the photograph is baked in. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to re-plan the deliverable: one static hero shared by every household with variable text only, or a decision to escalate and ask whether the couple want the card rebuilt rather than merged, and either way a written statement to a client who believes their artwork can do something it cannot.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the card as variable text against a single shared hero, drop the per-household image column from the data file so it does not silently bind nothing, re-author the mapping as ordered offset arithmetic inside the shared story with the standalone field handled separately, re-validate, re-prepare and re-verify the placeholders by round-tripping the document rather than trusting the success message, and put the structural limit in the note in plain language so the studio knows what their own artwork can and cannot do before they commission the next one.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A card run that reports success at every step and prints twelve identical cards where the couple expected each household's card to carry the picture, or worse, an image mapping that binds nothing and is never noticed because a photograph is present on every card anyway, so the failure is only discovered by the couple when the cards arrive.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the two constructs the leave-behind is actually built on. The studio's signature treatment is warm ink laid over the photograph, which is a compositing behaviour in the authored source, and the seal is a trace of a wax impression. What comes back is only visible in the returned per-canvas markup and the first canvas's rendition: the treatment is normalised to a plain opaque panel that covers the photograph rather than tinting it, so the hero is buried under a solid warm rectangle, and the traced seal arrives as loose ungrouped geometry with its own opaque ground riding along, so editable and usable turn out not to be the same claim. The export reports success with no warning of any kind, the sheet's structure is intact, and only looking at the rendition and reading the markup shows that the picture the whole sheet is built around is not visible.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it. The normalisation is a property of the importer, is not documented anywhere the agent can read at run time, and is not reported in the response; the only channel that carries the answer is the markup the export returns, which exists only after exporting. Nor can the agent design around an unknown: the treatment is the studio's stated house look and has to be attempted. (b) Nothing states it. The brief describes the tinted vellum treatment as the studio's own look and asks for the photograph to be visible in the finished file, which is a client describing what they want, not a warning about an importer. No asset note and no earlier step says the construct will not survive. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The fix crosses back to a different surface and produces a different asset: the treatment has to be baked into the raster hero by a tinting or overlay operation at a strength chosen by eye, which is an imaging decision with its own judgement, and the seal has to be re-prepared with its ground stripped and possibly re-traced. The source is then re-authored around a picture that already carries the look, which changes the sheet's composition as well.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the imaging surface and bake the studio's treatment into the hero raster at a strength judged against the house look rather than relying on the authoring layer to composite it, re-prepare the seal so it arrives as clean transparent geometry, re-author the HTML around the pre-treated hero, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and verify again through both channels rather than assuming the second export took.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A leave-behind handed to three venues in which the A4 hero is a solid warm rectangle where the photograph should be and the seal is a smear of loose shapes on a white box, delivered as the studio's own signature look, with the export having reported success.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a pretty wedding picture. IDENTITY: these are the Hartley wedding, this couple, these guests and this studio's own wax seal, and the deliverable is those exact frames finished, not new frames invented. A regenerated face on a thank-you card is the single worst possible failure in this vertical. SPEC: the studio needs one card per household with names printed exactly as the guests wrote them, per-household files named and verified, print-resolution proofs, and full-resolution keepers with no invented pixels. None of that is checkable against a generated image. EDITABILITY AND REPEATABILITY: the actual product being bought is a recipe the studio can be held to across nine hundred frames next month, plus a merge template and an editable document they change per venue pitch. A one-shot render is not a recipe, cannot be applied to a set it has never seen, and gives the studio nothing to hold anyone to. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this pass hold in gallery order, does this artwork actually expose a picture frame, does this record clip at trim, does this trace still read at seal size, does the treatment survive the import. None of that is a generation problem.

primary_craft_problem: Create a coherent, truthful image system from inconsistent source photography and prove it at the actual delivery sizes. The lead output is Cascadia Founders Summit portrait set, eighteen people at one house treatment.
client_one_liner: Every speaker sent a headshot taken somewhere different, our own team's photos are worse, and the badges have to be at the printer in nine days.
client_brief:
Conference speaker portraits from eighteen very different submissions

Our Cascadia Founders Summit speakers have sent their own photographs. They need to sit together in the programme, in tight squares and on wide stage screens. Please make them look like one event without making the people look alike.

We are after a restrained, credible treatment and consistent head scale. The second set needs to work on our summit ground and over dark session video, where hair and shoulders are much less forgiving than on white.

The required sets are:

Eighteen self-submitted portraits shot in eighteen different rooms brought to one credible, understated house treatment with one scale of head in frame, no visible retouching signature and nobody made to look like a different person, delivered at the programme shape, the tight square and the wide stage shape, every output at or below its source dimensions, with a per-portrait parameter log, a stated decision on the frames that arrived already retouched, and every tool-reported resize and every edge expansion transcribed. One set with one treatment, not eighteen separately optimised pictures and not one picture at three sizes.

Every sitter placed on the summit's house ground for the programme and the badge, plus a ground-free version for the stage screens whose cut edge holds when placed over dark session video and not only over a light ground, with hair and shoulder edges judged on the ground the AV team will actually use.

A calibrated side-by-side approval sheet showing white point, black point, skin or material color, and crop consistency across the finished set. It must reference Cascadia Founders Summit portrait set, eighteen people at one house treatment and function as approval evidence rather than decoration.

Attachments: speaker_portraits/ (14 files) and staff_portraits/ (4 files); summit_badge_2025_PRINTER.pdf; speakers.csv; venue_render.jpg; summit_brand_notes.txt; programme_copy.txt.

Please check the actual programme and stage proportions before committing to a crop. Record any edge extension or unsuitable source; a portrait that cannot support a wide placement should not be enlarged and passed off as ready.

The final package should contain a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note, with every source file accounted for, including references and rejected or superseded material. Use the approved information without inventing missing facts. Only the stated stock or concept exceptions permit substitution; document every omission, replacement, reconciliation and material quality compromise.

Budget: $4,000-$8,500 fixed. Target: 4 to 6 weeks. Reviews: Direction approval, first-production proof, and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Two ledger anchors, both Freelancer.com. The first, 'Traditional Corporate Headshot Session Needed', whose grounding_note describes 'classic/formal corporate head-shots, neutral light-grey backdrop, colour + clean black-and-white versions, deliverables for social-profile/company website/print, one-week turnaround'. The second, a corporate-website retouch open call quoted verbatim in its grounding_note: 'professionally enhance a complete set of images for our corporate website', 'correct lighting imbalances and exposure issues', 'create a consistent visual style across all website images', 'showcase our facilities, operations, equipment and people', 'maintain a natural and realistic appearance'. Absorbs AO-104 and AO-20. The rebuild is needed because both absorbed tasks sat on a single surface and both ended in a set of crops, which is one deliverable, not four. The fuller commission an events client of this shape actually posts is the one here: the portraits are only useful once they are bound into the badge run the venue printer will actually print and into the programme and announcement collateral, and it is in the binding that a badly prepared crop stops being invisible. All names in the legacy grounding notes are discarded and replaced: the summit, its fourteen speakers and its four staff are invented and Western or European throughout (Marguerite Halloran, Peter Vance, Ines Moreau, Anders Lindqvist, Colm Byrne, Dana Whitfield, Estelle Rioux, Grant Mackey, Sofia Bellini, Nils Haugen, Robin Tate, Bernadette Cruz, Hugo Almeida, Karin Voss, plus staff Laurel Beckett, Owen Faraday, Mireille Dufort and Jonah Pryce).

price_band_and_audience: Delegate passes 600 to 1,200 dollars, two days, roughly four hundred attendees, speakers who are founders, operators and institutional investors, audience aged 28 to 55 who expense the ticket. The band is load-bearing. At this level the portraiture has to be understated, even and credible: neutral house ground, natural skin, no visible retouching signature, one consistent scale of head in frame across eighteen people so the programme grid reads as one event. Push it toward glamour retouching, smoothed skin, bright eyes and a warm glossy finish, and it reads as a consumer conference selling to the wrong buyer. Leave it flat and hard-lit and it reads as a free meetup. The programme and the announcement set follow the same rule: generous white space, restrained type, one strong photograph, and the summit's mark used quietly. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every crop is dimensionally correct. A posted job of this shape runs 1,500 to 3,000 dollars fixed on a nine-day turnaround.

assets_supplied.name: speaker_portraits/ (14 files) and staff_portraits/ (4 files)
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything we were sent. Fourteen speakers, four of our own team. Different rooms, different light, different everything." Mixed dimensions from roughly 1,100px to 5,600px on the long edge, all head-and-shoulders, Western and European sitters, no two grounds alike.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things nobody at the summit can see. First, three of the fourteen speaker frames are cropped so tightly at the top that the wide stage-screen shape cannot be derived from them without either clipping the crown of the head or inventing pixels, and the crop tool answers that with a tradeoff rather than a refusal and will interpolate toward its cap while reporting it only in a metadata entry. The only route that does not invent pixels is to add material at the edges first, and whether the added band actually matches that sitter's own ground and the house treatment is a property of that frame that cannot be known before it is done. Second, two of the frames arrived already heavily retouched by an agency, with skin smoothed and eyes lifted, so bringing them to the house treatment makes them read plastic beside the sixteen untouched ones rather than bringing them into line.

assets_supplied.name: summit_badge_2025_PRINTER.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: document
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The badge artwork our venue printer ran last year. We only have what they sent us." A real press PDF at 100 x 70 mm portrait, fonts embedded, produced from a genuine page layout. Carries the name, the role line, the affiliation, the summit mark and the person's picture.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed badge reads as a square picture chip, but the graphic frame behind it is a tall portrait rectangle at roughly three to four, and the frame fits whatever is bound into it on its own terms. A square badge crop bound into it is fitted to the frame's proportion and the crown of the head is cut on every single record, silently, with the merge reporting success and every badge looking deliberate in isolation. The frame's proportion is geometry inherited from a printer nobody at the summit can ask. On the text side the name and the role line share one continuous story while the affiliation sits alone, so the fields cannot be addressed uniformly.

assets_supplied.name: speakers.csv
assets_supplied.kind: data
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The speaker list as our registration system exported it. Role lines print as written, that is in the contracts." Columns for name, role line, affiliation, session and a photo filename.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Twenty rows for eighteen people: two speakers registered twice, once through the speaker portal and once through the general registration, with different affiliations on each row. Headers are mixed-case with trailing spaces and the photo column is a plain header holding bare filenames, which does not satisfy the merge image-column contract, so a naive run binds nothing while every badge still shows a picture. And the longest role line runs to more than sixty characters where the median is under thirty, which oversets the badge's fixed role frame at true trim while every other record sits comfortably. Nothing anywhere reports overset.

assets_supplied.name: venue_render.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The architect's render of the new venue. It is all anyone has because the building has not opened."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a CGI render with a synthetic sky and impossible interior light, and it will never sit beside photographic portraits on the same page, which is only obvious once the two are actually adjacent. It is also 1,400px on the long edge, so it could not carry a programme opener even if it belonged there.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That the badge's picture frame is not the shape the printed badge implies, and that everything bound into it is being re-fitted on the frame's terms. The 2025 badge reads as a square picture chip, so a square badge crop is the reasonable thing to prepare, and the summit's own brief asks for a tight square. The graphic frame behind it is a tall portrait rectangle, and the merge fits whatever is bound into it to that proportion, so the crown of the head is cut on every record. The frame's proportion is geometry inherited from a printer nobody at the summit can ask, it is not visible in the printed artefact, the merge reports success, and each badge looks like a deliberate tight crop when viewed alone. It only declares itself as a fault when the rendered proofs are actually looked at and the same cut appears on all eighteen heads.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot substitute for it. The frame's proportion is not stated in the PDF, is not visible in the printed card, and is not reported by the merge; the only way to it is to convert, read the frame bounds and then bind something and look at what came out. An agent that reads the bounds carefully before binding can catch it one step earlier, which is exactly the competent path this trajectory takes at step 10, and it still cannot know whether the frame fits or fills what is bound into it until a record is actually rendered. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for a tight square for badges and avatars, which is the summit describing the shape they use, and the acceptance bar asks that heads sit in the frame the same way on every badge, which is an ordinary client quality requirement. Neither is a disclosure about the artwork's internals. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to go back to the imaging surface and prepare a different asset: a badge crop at the frame's real proportion with the head placed for that proportion, which is a fresh composition decision per sitter, not the same crop re-fed. The square crop the summit asked for still ships as an avatar deliverable, so the two now diverge.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive a badge-specific crop at the picture frame's real proportion for all eighteen, composed for that shape rather than cropped down from the square, re-upload them and rebuild the image map against the new filenames, re-merge and re-render, then read the proofs again on all eighteen rather than on the ones that were changed. Keep the square crop as the avatar deliverable and say in the note that badge and avatar are now two different crops and why, so the summit does not later swap one for the other.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eighteen badges go to the printer with the top of every speaker's head cut off, on a run that reported success at every step and looked deliberate on any single badge, for an event whose paying audience reads calibre off exactly this.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the material added at the edges of the three too-tight frames actually belongs to those pictures. Adding edge material is the only route to the wide stage shape that does not invent pixels inside the picture, but what gets built at the edge is generated from that specific frame's own content: on one sitter it continues the office wall convincingly, on another it invents a lighting falloff that does not match the sitter's own ground, and on a third it produces a band that is plausible in isolation and a full step off the house treatment. None of that is knowable before the operation is run, nothing in the response reports it, and each result looks like a normal photograph on its own. It shows only when the eighteen wide shapes are laid out together as the stage set, where three of them carry a band along one edge that the other fifteen do not.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it. The expand has to happen after the house treatment is established, since the band has to match that treatment, and it has to happen before the wide crops are final. There is no parameter that guarantees a match and no readout that reports one; the seed parameter makes a result reproducible, not correct. A careful agent doing it right the first time is still handing an outcome to a generative step whose output it has not seen. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says a couple of frames are cropped tightly, which is the client noticing that some pictures are tight, and the acceptance bar requires added material to match, which is the client's standard for the work rather than a warning that it will not. No asset note names which frames or what the band will do. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is a different decision on a different axis: re-run the expand with different amounts or from a different side, correct the band as its own masked region, or abandon expansion for that sitter and accept a looser wide crop that loses the head scale the set is built on, which then changes what one scale of head in frame means for the whole set.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-run the edge material on the frames whose band does not sit, from a different side or at a different extent, and bring the band into the house treatment as a confined correction rather than re-grading the whole frame, which would move the sitter. Where it will not come, choose the looser crop and re-check what that does to the head scale across all eighteen wide shapes, then lay the eighteen out and judge them together again rather than checking only the three that were touched.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Three of eighteen lower thirds carry a visible band of invented wall along one edge in a different light from the rest, projected at stage scale in front of four hundred people who paid to be there.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every badge actually holds at true trim. The role lines are the speakers' own contracted titles, supplied by a registration system, and the longest of them is more than twice the median. The role frame's depth is fixed inside a printer's artwork that nobody at the summit can change and that the connector offers no way to resize, reflow or releaded. The two only meet on a typeset badge at real trim size. The failure is silent in every channel: nothing in the merge reports overset, the merge's own raster route renders at screen resolution where a clip does not read as a clip, and the badge looks finished at proof scale.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Neither ordering nor competence produces a fit. The agent cannot shorten the role line, because the summit has said it prints as contracted, and it cannot deepen or reflow the frame, because the mapping surface exposes only text, image and code mappings and no typographic or geometric control whatsoever. Both the constraint and the frame are fixed client property. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says role lines print as written, which is a standard contractual copy clause of the same kind the client already applies to their speakers, and the acceptance bar carries an ordinary quality line about nothing being clipped at trim. Neither says any record is long, and no asset note names the speaker. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the input the agent would want to change is the one it is forbidden to touch and the artefact it would want to alter cannot be altered. The checkpoint resolves into a judgement that has to be taken and then made consistent with the earlier decision about the duplicate registrations: either this is a freelancer who quietly edits a client's contractual copy, or one who names in writing what cannot be done inside the client's own artwork.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-render the affected record alone at true trim to confirm the clip is real rather than a proof artefact, then read all eighteen at trim rather than only the flagged one. Go back to the duplicate-registration decision and make the two consistent: name the over-length role line and the frame it will not fit, name the rows merged and the affiliation chosen and on whose authority, and put both to the client as questions with no copy shortened in either case. State whether the affected badge ships as it stands or is held, and carry the same decision into that person's single badge file.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A speaker who negotiated their title into a contract wears a badge for two days with it cut off mid-word, in front of the investors the summit sold the room to, discovered at the registration desk rather than before the file went to the printer.

decision_gates: The surface split, and reading the client's no-website instruction as a scope limit rather than as a limit on which surfaces may be used.
What one scale of head in frame means across sitters photographed at different distances, and holding it across eighteen files.
What to do with the two frames that arrived already heavily retouched, where the house correction makes them worse rather than better.
Ground route per portrait rather than per set, and on which ground the ground-free edges are judged.
Whether to interpolate a tight frame or add material at its edges, and whether the added material can be brought into the house treatment or the crop has to loosen instead.
The duplicate registrations: which affiliation prints, and whether that is the agent's call or the summit's to confirm.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the client's text or reconstruct the story from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification of the prepared template.

client_brief:
A coherent speaking and investor image set for an industrial-design founder

I am preparing speaking and investor materials for Astrid Vellacourt. The photographs and supporting pieces need to feel like the same person and practice: considered, credible and recognisably connected to industrial design.

There are four connected parts, with the portraits setting the tone for everything else.

Nine frames from a shifting afternoon brought to one composed, credible, understated look with no visible retouching signature and the sitter still recognisably herself, delivered at the four placement crops composed for the size each is actually used at rather than scaled from one master, every output at or below its source dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log and every resize or edge extension any tool reported. One set with one look, not nine separately optimised pictures and not one picture at four sizes.

Each selected frame delivered on the warm neutral ground the client asked for, replacing the studio grey, and as a ground-free version whose edge holds on the deep ground her press kit and investor deck use, with no pale rim and no hard-cut curl, judged on that ground rather than on white. Where a frame cannot be cut cleanly, it is named and the placement it was carrying is moved.

Speaker one-pager, banner and announcement as one editable document plus its source: Choose and adapt an Adobe Express template for these supporting pieces, using the supplied brand, approved copy and imagery. Select the strongest fit, replace the template content and correct its background as needed. Supply the editable design link and the requested export, in addition to the commissioned custom production work.

The monogram recovered from a photograph of a blind-debossed card as placeable, scalable vector geometry with a real viewBox and no opaque full-canvas ground path, delivered as a transparent mark and a solid variant for reversing, together with an honest written statement of where it holds and where it does not, specifically at profile-picture size and reversed on the deep ground, and what to use instead wherever it does not. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Please pay particular attention to the deep-background portraits and the small AV mark. Pale rims around hair and a monogram that only works when enlarged will be conspicuous in these uses. Where a placement is beyond the source, recommend the defensible alternative and identify the limitation.

What I can provide: vellacourt_session/ (9 frames, 5200px long edge); vellacourt_deboss_card.jpg; vellacourt_workshop_snap.jpg; vellacourt_placements.txt; vellacourt_bio_copy.txt; vellacourt_speakercard_template.pdf; vellacourt_talks.csv (8 engagements).

The supporting layouts must remain editable. I need an organised handover, not only a set of flattened previews, so the materials can be reused without reconstructing your work.

This is a fixed-price commission at $1,800-$4,500, with a target of 2 to 4 weeks. The agreed review allowance is one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_session/ (9 frames, 5200px long edge)
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Nine frames I like out of the half-day. Shot on grey paper in a studio. The light moved during the afternoon and they do not match." Seated and standing, three-quarter and straight on, no other people.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two things she cannot see. First, she has thick curly hair and the studio grey sits close in value to it in the frames shot after the key light was moved, so the knockout on those frames returns an edge that is either cut hard into the curl or carries a soft pale rim of captured grey. On white and on the warm neutral both look perfectly clean, which is why every version she has tried looked fine until it went on her deck. Second, the frame she has already decided is the press headshot, the one she calls her favourite, is the coolest of the nine and the furthest from where the other eight can reasonably be brought, so bringing the set to one look and honouring her choice of hero pull against each other, and nothing in the frame announces this until the nine are laid out together after correction.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_deboss_card.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our original card. The two letters are pressed into the paper with no ink at all, just the impression. It is the only version of the monogram that exists and the printer has closed." A 4,000px phone frame of a white cotton card on a pale desk, shot under a window at a raking angle.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: A blind deboss carries no ink and no colour, so the mark exists only as the shadow the raking light throws in the relief, and it exists only on the side the light came from. On the lit side the letterforms have almost no edge at all. What a selection returns is therefore a property of that one photograph's light rather than of the mark, and what the trace yields is a set of soft shadow shapes that read convincingly as the monogram at full canvas and break into fragments at the size a profile picture reproduces it. There is no option on the tracing step to tune this, so the only lever is the raster preparation, and which preparation is needed cannot be known until the result is placed at its real delivered size.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_workshop_snap.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "A phone picture of our workshop, if it is any use for the banner."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: 1,300px on the long edge, shot handheld under mixed daylight and fluorescent tubes, with the bench in front of the camera and nothing behind it. It cannot carry a wide banner at any usable width and its content offers no room for type, which is only apparent once a banner crop is actually attempted from it.

assets_supplied.kind: document
assets_supplied.visible_description: The four placements she needs and the delivered sizes each one is used at, the description of the warm neutral she wants in plain language, and the note that the press kit and the deck both sit on a very dark ground.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_bio_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: document
assets_supplied.visible_description: Her speaker biography, the studio's one-line description, the three confirmed talk titles and the announcement wording she uses when a talk is confirmed.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_speakercard_template.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: document
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The flat card my print shop set up for the speaker cards, one talk to a card. I want a run of them off my roster, one per talk, so I am not laying each one out by hand." A single-record A6 portrait card on the warm neutral ground: a portrait well across the top, the talk title, the event and the date beneath it, and the AV monogram in the bottom corner.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What the card looks like printed and how the file is set are two different things. The talk title, the event name and the date read as three tidy fields but are set as one continuous threaded story in a single frame, with the date sitting in the middle of that story, so a mapping read straight off the layout omits the date from every card and reports nothing wrong. The portrait area is the one real picture frame on the card and binds a photograph cleanly. The monogram in the corner is not a frame at all but flattened artwork baked into the supplied PDF at its own low resolution, so it cannot be bound per record and ships fuzzy on every card unless it is replaced with the recovered vector as a shared element. And the media box equals the trim with no bleed box present, so a press-ready-with-bleed run cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called, and none of this is visible in the printed sample.

assets_supplied.name: vellacourt_talks.csv (8 engagements)
assets_supplied.kind: document
assets_supplied.visible_description: "My speaking season. Every confirmed talk, panel and session between February and May, with the event, the date, the title and which of my frames goes on the card." One row per engagement, with a picture column pointing at the session frame each card's portrait comes from.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One engagement was confirmed last week and its picture cell is simply blank, which no header reveals and which the merge will not complain about. The dates are written in five different formats across the rows. Two of the rows are the same conference on the same day, a panel and a fireside, so they share an event name and even write that shared date two different ways, which means naming one card file per event collides and silently overwrites one with the other. And the picture cells point at the session masters, not at card-shaped crops, so a card portrait has to be cut to the card's own proportion for every row rather than reused from any of the four named placement crops.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What a blind deboss actually yields as artwork, and whether it survives the two placements the client named as the ones she cares about. There is no ink and no colour in the mark: it exists only as the shadow the raking light threw into the paper relief, and only on the side the light came from, so what a selection returns is a property of that photograph's light rather than of the monogram. The trace comes back as a set of soft shadow shapes that read convincingly as the two letters at full canvas, which is the only size at which anyone would look at them by default, and which break into disconnected fragments with one side of each letterform missing at the size a profile picture reproduces them, and lose their remaining edge entirely when reversed on the deep ground. Nothing reports any of this. The tracing step takes no options at all, so there is no parameter to have set correctly; the only lever is the raster preparation, and which preparation is needed cannot be chosen until the failure has been seen at real size on the real ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot pre-empt it. The trace's fidelity is a function of this photograph's raking light, the paper's texture and the selection that produced it. There is no measurement, no preview at delivered size, and no parameter on the trace. An agent that words the selection carefully and gets the polarity right still cannot know how much of each letterform survives without tracing it and putting it at avatar size. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the monogram is pressed into the paper with no ink and that it has to survive on a profile picture and reversed on the dark ground, which is the client naming her hardest placements and her standing requirement, exactly as she would to a designer. It does not say it will fail, and no asset note, earlier step or deliverable says which letter breaks or on which side. The client asking for a note about where it will and will not hold is a request for professional advice, not a disclosure that the answer is already known. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to go back and make a different asset: re-prepare the raster so the relief carries a usable edge before tracing, aim the selection at a different property of the photograph, or accept that the traced mark is a large-format asset only and build a different small-size lockup from the letterforms. Whichever it is, the one-pager, the banner and the announcement are then re-composed around a mark of a different weight and a different minimum size.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-prepare the raster to strengthen the relief before tracing rather than trying to fix the trace, re-select on a wording aimed at what actually distinguishes the mark in this frame, re-trace, strip the ground path and inject a viewBox again, and re-place at profile-picture size and reversed on the deep ground rather than assuming the second attempt took. If it still will not hold at the smallest size, decide and state what carries that placement instead, and re-author the canvases around the mark's real minimum size, which changes the composition rather than just the asset.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A founder raising a seed round uses a profile picture on which her monogram is a smear of disconnected grey shapes, and sends conference organisers a press kit whose mark disappears entirely into the dark ground, having been handed artwork that looked perfect in every file she was shown.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the ground-free version actually holds where it is used. She has thick curly hair, the studio grey behind her sits close in value to it in the frames shot after the light was moved, and the knockout resolves that either by cutting hard into the curl or by leaving a soft rim of captured grey around it. Which of the two a given frame gets is a property of that frame's light and that part of her hair, not of the route chosen or the care taken, and both are completely invisible on white and on the warm neutral ground, which is exactly why every version she has tried herself looked fine until it went on her deck. The operation reports success in both cases and the returned file looks correct at normal viewing size.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The ground-free version has to be made regardless of order, there is no metadata that reports edge quality, and no measurement is available. A careful agent choosing the right route still gets a rim or a hard cut on the frames where hair and ground share value, because the photograph is the variable. It also cannot be settled by inspecting the returned file in isolation: the failure only exists relative to the ground it is composited on. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says every version she has tried has a pale outline round her hair, which is the client describing the symptom that made her hire someone, not a description of which frames do it, why, or that the fix is ground-dependent. No asset note names the frames and no acceptance line explains the cause. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The fix is a different operation on a different principle, naming the paper behind her and inverting rather than asking for the subject, plus a decision about whether a frame whose curl cannot be cut cleanly stays in the set at all, which changes which frame carries which placement.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-cut the affected frames by naming the ground material and inverting rather than by asking for the subject, re-composite on the deep ground and inspect the curl again rather than assuming the second route worked, and check the frames that were not flagged at the same close inspection, since the reason to look was found on one frame and the rest have not been established as clean. If a frame will not cut cleanly at all, move the placement it was carrying to a frame that will and say so.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Her press kit and her investor deck both carry a portrait with a pale halo traced round every curl on a very dark ground, which is the precise defect she hired someone to fix, shipped back to her as fixed.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a licensed environmental frame can sit with her own portraits. Stock search returns a small CDN thumbnail; the frame's true light, its true neutral and its true black point only exist after it is licensed, downloaded at full resolution and brought toward her look, and whether it then reads as her studio or as a stock picture placed behind her is only visible with it and her nine graded frames laid out together. Two candidate frames that look equally warm and equally quiet at thumbnail size can be a full grade apart at full resolution, and one of them will never join a set built on a studio portrait's soft key.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The comparison needs both the licensed frame and the finished set to exist, so it cannot be moved earlier, and it cannot be settled by care, because a thumbnail is not evidence about light. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that the banner wants more room than a studio frame and that she will pay for one if that is what it needs, which is an invitation carrying no claim about how a candidate will behave. No asset, no acceptance line and no earlier step names it. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The likely response is to abandon the licensed frame and search again on different terms, which is a new licensing decision, a new grade and a new judgement, not the same operation on changed input, and it may instead resolve into extending one of her own frames at the edges and accepting a tighter banner, which changes the banner's composition and the type that sits on it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Push the licensed frame further toward her look, or, if it will not join, return to Stock with a search framed by the light her set actually has rather than by the subject matter, license a replacement and re-grade it, then lay the set out again and judge it as ten rather than checking the new frame alone. If nothing joins, extend one of her own frames at its edges instead and re-compose the banner around the room that produces, which is a different banner.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The banner at the top of a founder's profile reads as a bought photograph with a portrait pasted on it, in front of the investors and programme committees the whole kit exists to persuade.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a portrait of somebody who is not her. IDENTITY is the entire commission: these are nine frames of one specific person who is about to ask investors for money and conference committees for stage time, and her monogram is a specific impression in a specific piece of paper from a printer that has closed. A regenerated face is fraud and a regenerated monogram is a different studio's mark. SPEC: she needs four crops composed for four named delivered sizes, a version on a warm neutral ground and a version with genuine transparency whose edge holds on a dark ground, all at or below source resolution. A generated image satisfies none of that and cannot be checked. EDITABILITY: one deliverable is defined by being editable, three canvases in one document she changes per event so she is not paying for this four times, with live text and real vector geometry. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this hair cut cleanly on the ground it will actually sit on, does this shadow trace still read at avatar size, does this licensed frame sit with her portraits. None of that is a generation problem, and the honest note about where her mark will not hold is professional advice a render cannot give. And the speaker card run is a genuine one-record-per-page job: one printed card per engagement, each bound to its own talk's title, event and date and its own portrait, page count equal to the roster, with the mid-story date landing on every card and each proof carrying the engagement it claims. A model returns a picture of a card, not a run of them tied to a roster and checkable row by row, and cannot tell her that the file its print shop supplied carries no bleed.

client_brief:
An autumn image library that still looks like my ceramics

Hi, I am Marlo Quill, the maker behind Quill & Kiln. I have a month's worth of photographs from my phone and a borrowed camera, taken under four different kinds of light. I need help turning them into a usable autumn collection.

Please start with the fired swatches, not a fashionable preset. The work can have a signature look, but the glaze customers see must still be the glaze they receive. Several photographs of the same moment should not become several supposedly different posts.

marlo_autumn_month/ (18 frames, mixed sources); marlo_motifs_page.jpg; marlo_captions.txt; marlo_glaze_swatches.jpg; marlo_grid_reference.png; quillandkiln_card_template.pdf; quillandkiln_pieces.csv.

Here is the finished set I need:

The month brought to one look across two camera bodies and four lighting situations, with the clay and glaze colours held to the fired swatch reference, plus two licensed camera-scale frames graded into the same world. Per frame parameter log with a reason line for every frame that reached the look by a different route, a named and reasoned cut list, and a moment reconciliation so a burst counts as one post.

A source-to-final contact sheet at matched scale that proves set consistency, identity or material preservation, and the disposition of every outlier. It must reference The autumn month at one signature look and function as approval evidence rather than decoration.

I would find a clear cut list and a side-by-side comparison more useful than a folder full of near-duplicates. Please explain the pictures you leave out as well as the ones you keep.

Fee range: $900-$2,400 fixed
Delivery target: 7 to 15 business days
Included reviews: One technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

Please deliver a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note. Account for every supplied file and identify anything used only as reference, superseded or rejected. Stay with approved facts and copy. Do not silently replace weak assets; use only the stated stock or concept allowances, and record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and material compromises.

price_band_and_audience: A mid-tier creator retainer at 600 to 1,500 dollars a month, creator 22 to 34 and audience the same, buying 38 to 90 dollar stoneware. The band is load-bearing in both directions. The look has to read as one hand and still read as a real room, because this audience follows the person and treats a heavy uniform filter as evidence that the maker is now a brand, which costs conversion directly. Push the other way and leave the month untreated and it reads as careless at a price point where the photograph is the only way to judge a glaze. It also has to stay cheap enough to run monthly: an elaborate treatment that cannot be repeated next drop is the wrong answer even if this month looks superb. The same work at a 200 dollar gallery-ceramics band would correctly be sparser, cooler and shot on seamless, and shipping that here reads as a different maker.

assets_supplied.name: marlo_autumn_month/ (18 frames, mixed sources)
assets_supplied.kind: A month of self-shot content: phone frames at 4032x3024 and a borrowed mirrorless body at 6000x4000, covering studio mornings, a grey market Saturday, a coffee-bar collaboration and a night kitchen under one overhead bulb.
