price_band_and_audience: Capital equipment at forty thousand to three hundred thousand dollars per machine, bought by procurement engineers and plant managers on a specification rather than on a feeling. The band is load bearing in a way most identity work is not: at this price the mark is read as evidence about the machine, so a soft trace, a dotty edge or a designation that does not match the order book reads as tolerance drift on the shop floor and costs the quote. The correct register is flat, mechanical, high contrast and generously spaced, the works green used as a field rather than decoration. Push into heritage treatment, distressed texture or a hand drawn feel and it becomes a boutique metal shop selling five hundred dollar fire pits. Flatten it into consumer tech instead, thin geometric sans and pastels, and a procurement engineer stops believing there is a foundry behind it. Either extreme misreads the commission even if every file opens. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,400 to 3,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Manufacturer of press brakes and metal forming presses, capital equipment sold to procurement engineers and plant managers across North America and northern Europe
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1919 in Sheboygan, Wisconsin; third generation family works, forty one people
brand_identity.about: Redecker builds press brakes and metal forming presses, from forty thousand to three hundred thousand dollars a machine. The works has carried the same company mark since 1919. Our buyer reads the tolerance sheet before he reads anything we wrote, so everything we put a name on has to say precision.
brand_identity.audience: Procurement engineers and plant managers who buy on specification rather than feeling, across North America and northern Europe
brand_identity.price_positioning: Capital equipment at forty thousand to three hundred thousand dollars per machine. The mark is read as evidence about the machine: the register is flat, mechanical, high contrast and generously spaced, never heritage craft workshop and never consumer tech.
brand_identity.typography: A flat, mechanical grotesque for the mark and plate wording, set high contrast and widely spaced, paired with a plain industrial sans for the usage sheet and stationery. Nothing decorative, nothing hand drawn. Weight and spacing do the work.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, factual and confident; we state the specification and let it stand. No adjectives a tolerance sheet would not carry. Example line the brand would write: "Built to a hundred years of the same standard, plate by plate."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: We no longer hold usable artwork for the company mark in any form. The designer who last touched it retired in the nineties and nothing came back from his files. What survives is a flatbed scan of the 1974 parts catalogue cover, where the mark is printed in one deep ink on cream board, and a photograph a fitter took of the same mark etched into a stainless nameplate on a machine that came back for a rebuild. A works standards text file records the green as the paint shop mixes it, the address block and the required plate wording. Two further company marks also survive only as artefacts: the works proving stamp, held only as a die impression struck into a steel test coupon a fitter photographed, and the 1919 cast heritage device, held only as a raking light photograph of the badge cast and painted into a machine's main frame.
brand_identity.values: Precision as reputation: the mark on a two hundred thousand dollar machine has to be as true as the machine, reversed clean out of the works green, and unmistakably ours.

assets_supplied.name: redecker_catalogue_1974_cover.tif (4200 x 5600)
assets_supplied.kind: Flatbed scan of the 1974 parts catalogue cover, the mark printed large in one deep ink on cream board.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The 1974 parts catalogue. The mark is printed big on the cover, which is why we scanned it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: That cover was printed through a coarse screen, so at scan scale the ink edge is a field of dots rather than a line and a trace of it succeeds and returns lumpy stippled geometry that looks correct at canvas size. It also carries an outer arc of place type the nameplate version lacks, and the board is scanned off square.

assets_supplied.name: redecker_nameplate_rebuild.jpg (4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the same mark etched into the brushed stainless nameplate of a rebuilt machine.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Same mark, etched into the plate on a machine that came back for a rebuild. This is what it looks like on a machine today."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: There is no ink here at all: the mark is an etch in brushed stainless, so mark and ground sit at nearly the same value and a selection reads the brush grain as readily as the etch, biting the outer ring where the grain runs with it. Background removal on that ring returns a solid opaque disc rather than a knockout, and both results look plausible until the geometry is placed reversed on colour.

assets_supplied.name: redecker_proving_stamp_coupon.jpg (4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Macro photograph of the works proving stamp struck by a hardened die into a polished steel test coupon, the small round acceptance mark every finished machine carries after its load test.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our proving stamp, struck into a test offcut. The inspector puts the test number in the little box. This is the only copy we have of it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is struck metal with no ink, so the impression sits at nearly the value of the polished ground exactly as the nameplate does, but the die also raised a burnished burr right around the impression that reads as strongly as the struck line, so the isolation that takes the mark fattens it with the burr and the isolation that ducks the burr thins the ring rule and the number box away. The stamp only ever goes small, about nine millimetres struck into the plate corner, so a version that looks correct at coupon scale closes its bend angle apex and its ring counter into a blob at strike size, and the inspector's number box is empty in the die and must be recovered as an open knockout rather than a filled square. A faint offset ghost strike doubles some lines.

assets_supplied.name: redecker_frame_casting_1919.jpg (4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Raking light photograph of the 1919 cast heritage badge raised into a machine's main frame casting and painted over in the works green, the secondary mark that sits beside the company mark on the bay door sign.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The old date badge, cast into the frame and painted green like the rest of the machine. It goes next to the name on the bay door sign."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The badge is cast in relief and then painted the works green over the raised iron, so it is green on green and the only thing separating it from the field is the directional shadow the relief throws under the raking shop light. A value or threshold selection therefore catches the cast shadow, which is offset from the true casting edge, and returns an emblem shifted and fattened toward the lit side, while the shallow draft angle on each raised stroke reads as a second edge so a naive trace double lines the strokes. The casting edge and the shadow edge both look like the mark until the result is set beside the company mark at bay door scale.

assets_supplied.name: redecker_plate_2024.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last year's data plate artwork from the printer, a real press PDF, the plate centred on a US Letter page.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our printer's file for last year's plates. The layout is right, only the machine details change."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What a flat press file exposes as separately addressable blocks once it becomes a working layout is a property of how it was originally set rather than of how the printed plate looks, and the readout of its text can omit a whole run while keeping the line break around it, so every position past the omission is short by exactly what was dropped and the check still reports the mapping valid.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the surviving source that looks best can actually yield production geometry. The 1974 cover was printed through a coarse screen, so once the ink is isolated the trace receives a field of dots rather than a line and returns lumpy stippled outlines that look correct at canvas size and read as a soft wobbling edge only at the size the mark reproduces, reversed on the works green. Nothing reports it: the trace takes no options at all, no threshold, no path count, no simplification, and its success message is identical whichever way it went.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it: the screen is a property of a 1974 printing, invisible in the file's name, dimensions and preview, legible only after the ink is isolated and traced. Nothing states it, since the client says only that this is the catalogue cover. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different raster preparation entirely, or abandoning that source for the etched nameplate, a different medium needing a different isolation.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re prepare the raster for whichever source is now the candidate, re run the isolation with wording aimed at the mark, trace again, redo the hygiene, and judge again at reproduction size on the works green.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A mark that opens cleanly, scales and looks right in the delivered folder, then reproduces as a soft dotty edge on the plate of a two hundred thousand dollar machine and on the bay door sign, which is what this buyer reads as sloppy engineering.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the works proving stamp survives at the size it is actually struck. It comes off the coupon as struck metal with no ink, so mark and polished ground sit at almost one value, and a raised burnished burr rings the whole impression. Whichever way the isolation goes it looks correct at coupon scale: take the burr and the glyph fattens, duck inside it and the thin ring rule and the number box outline thin away. The stamp does not go large anywhere; it strikes at about nine millimetres into the plate corner and prints small on the test certificate, and only at that size, reversed on the works green, does the burr fattened version close the bend angle apex and the ring counter into a blob while the number box the inspector must write into fills solid. The trace takes no options at all and its success message is identical whichever way it went.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it: the burr and the near equal value are properties of a die struck into steel, invisible in the file's name, dimensions and preview and legible only after the impression is isolated, traced and placed at nine millimetres on the green. Nothing states it, since the coupon is handed over as simply the stamp struck on a test offcut. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different raster preparation entirely, separating the struck line from the burnished burr and deciding the number box before the trace rather than after.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re prepare the coupon raster to separate the struck line from the burr, re run the isolation aimed at the impression rather than the metal, keep the number box open, trace again, redo the hygiene, and judge again at nine millimetres reversed on the works green rather than at coupon scale.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A proving stamp that reads cleanly in the delivered folder, then strikes into the plate of a two hundred thousand dollar machine as a fattened blob with the inspector's number box filled solid, on the one device on the machine that is a load test record rather than branding.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's plate PDF actually becomes once it is a working layout. Whether the plate's lines arrive as separately addressable blocks or as one continuous flow is a property of how the original was set rather than of how the printed plate looks, and it decides the entire mapping strategy. Worse, the readout of that text can omit a whole run while keeping the line break around it, so every position past the omission is short by exactly what was dropped, the validation still reports the mapping valid with no warnings, and the build still reports success while landing only some of the fields.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it: the granularity does not exist until the conversion has run, and the omission shows only against the document's own reconstructed text. Nothing states it, since the client says the layout is right and only the machine details change, which is true of the printed plate and silent about the file. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different mapping strategy built against a different source of truth.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the document, recompute every position against it, rebuild the mapping in the form the real frame inventory supports, prepare again, and confirm each placeholder by reading the rebuilt document.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen plates that render, proof and print with two required fields silently absent, found by the engraver at best and a customer's inspector at worst, on a document that is part compliance record and part branding.

Which isolation route recovers the struck proving stamp without carrying the burnished burr, and whether the inspector's number box is taken as an open knockout or silently filled solid, both of which look successful at coupon scale.

Whether the plate mapping is per frame or position based inside one flow, which the printed plate cannot tell you.
How the overlong designation is carried, which is the client's naming rule rather than the designer's preference, and whether the duplicate serial is a data error or two machines.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome industrial logo. IDENTITY: this is one company's 1919 mark, still bolted to machines in customers' plants and stamped on decades of invoices, and a regenerated mark is a different company's logo however good it looks. The two surviving artefacts are the only evidence of what that mark is, and half the work is deciding which is admissible. And it is not one mark but three: ink on screened board and an etch in brushed steel for the company mark, a die struck into a steel coupon for the proving stamp, and a badge cast and painted into iron for the heritage device, four physical media that a generated picture is evidence of none of. SPEC: fourteen plates at one machine per page in order, each field present in full at trim, per machine proofs at plate resolution whose identity is confirmed by content, a closed path file a laser cutter can follow, and no interpolated pixels. None of that is satisfiable by a generated picture or checkable in one. EDITABILITY: the sign shop, the engraver, the printer and the laser house need real geometry rather than a picture of it, and the stationery is defined by the works being able to edit it next year.

price_band_and_audience: A two tier collectible line: twelve dollar impulse pins across a tent table and ninety five dollar numbered coins bought by members aged roughly twenty to forty five who already own the previous years. The band is load bearing and it splits the artwork in two. A struck coin at ninety five dollars has to carry fine raised line work and tight registration a member inspects in the hand, while a twelve dollar hard enamel pin has wells a mint must be able to fill, so detail below a certain weight has to be deliberately taken out rather than left in and hoped for. Treat the whole set at pin level and the coin reads as a giveaway and the numbered edition collapses; treat the pin at coin level and the mint cannot strike it, the enamel bleeds its wells and the tent table sells a defect. The register overall is club rather than corporate: confident and worn in rather than slick, never novelty and never distressed for effect, because the ninety five dollar buyer is buying continuity with 1987. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,400 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.about: The Apex Rally Club is a volunteer amateur motorsport club in Vermont. Six events a year, and a merch table that pays for the timing gear. The club crest goes back to 1987 and each event badge, the hillclimb, the night stage, the ice trial, the gravel loop and the finale, was drawn over the years by members. This autumn is our first proper collectible run with a mint.
brand_identity.audience: Club members aged roughly twenty to forty five who already own the previous years and buy on continuity with the club's history, plus impulse buyers at the event tent
brand_identity.price_positioning: A two tier line: twelve dollar impulse pins across the tent table and ninety five dollar numbered coins a member inspects in the hand. The register is club rather than corporate: confident and worn in, never novelty and never distressed for effect.
brand_identity.typography: A worn slab or industrial serif for crest and badge lettering, carried as outlined vector, paired with a plain sans for the mint spec sheet, capsule insert and backing cards. The feel is club regalia with a straight face, history rather than novelty.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, understated and proud of the years behind us; we talk about continuity, not hype. Example line the brand would write: "Same crest we ran in 1987, struck to hold up to the light."

What we have is six reference sheets, the crest and five event badges, printed at different times on different paper and photographed on a workbench under whatever light was in the garage. A member also sent a photo of the crest as it is embroidered on the club jackets. The mint requirements file gives diameters, the hard enamel colour ceiling, plating options and the rule that the coin's raised metal version must be line only.
brand_identity.values: Continuity with 1987: the ninety five dollar coin is bought on history, so the faces have to read as one club collection rather than six separate files, worn in but never sloppy.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the six recovered faces are a set. Stroke weight in a traced outline is a function of how heavy the ink reads in the raster the trace received, not of how the badge was drawn, so six sheets printed at different times and photographed under different light trace into six outlines of visibly different line weight, each of which looks completely right while it is being looked at alone. The trace reports nothing: no weight, no threshold, no simplification, and an identical response for a heavy face and a spindly one. The mismatch exists only in the comparison, at struck size.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the mismatch is a property of the relationship between six finished traces and cannot exist until all six exist. Doing it right first time presumes knowing, per sheet, how much ink density to add or remove before a trace that has no controls, which nothing reports. Nothing states it either: the client describes the photographs, not what a trace does with them. It is not a propagation re run, because the fix reaches back to per sheet preparation for specific faces only.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify which faces sit heavy and which thin against the set, go back to the ink density preparation for just those sheets, re trace, redo the hygiene, and lay the six out together again at struck size.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A mint receives six faces that are supposed to be one collection and cuts six dies at three different line weights, which on a numbered ninety five dollar coin sold on continuity with 1987 is exactly the defect the buyer holds it to the light to look for.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each backing card is actually carrying its own design. Two things are knowable only by running the merge: whether the printer's flat card converted into a layout that can carry a different picture per record at all, which depends on how the original file was built rather than on what the printed card shows, and whether the per record proofs are in the order they claim. The proofs render, they carry a label naming their row, and that label can be wrong while every file reports success, so a run named by position ships the ice trial's face on the gravel loop's card.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because both facts exist only after a conversion and a merge that have already happened, and no parameter controls either. Nothing states it, since the client says the shape is right and the design changes. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different delivery route chosen for identity, plus a verification pass that reads each proof's own content against its row.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Establish identity by what is printed on each proof, re derive the per SKU files through a route whose ordering is trustworthy, reconcile the two rows pointing at one artwork file, and re check all six.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Six hundred pins reach a tent table on backing cards carrying the wrong design's face and the wrong edition size, which is a reprint of the whole run and a refund line at the event the pack was made for.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the thing the colourway decision rests on. The committee has to judge the crest colourways on struck metal, so the natural construction is the face carried over the metal ground with a sheen and an edge treatment that read as struck rather than printed. Those constructions do not survive intact: blending against the ground and layered edge treatment are normalised away or truncated, silently, at full success, so the face can arrive as a flat opaque shape on a photograph of metal. The returned markup is the only channel that reports it, and the rendition shows the first canvas only.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports. Nothing states it: the client asks to see the colourways on the metal, which is art direction rather than a warning. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different upstream asset or a treatment rebuilt from the constructions that do survive.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the colourway page around a construction that survives the import, re author, re run the readiness check, export again, and audit all three canvases from the returned markup.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A committee votes on a flagship coin colourway from a page where the crest is a flat shape on a picture of metal, picks the option that looks best flat, and the mint strikes the one that reads worst in the hand.

client_brief:
Coffee sticker collection: recover four designs, add two, prepare the cutting sheet

Four recovered designs + two new designs = one six-sticker collection for Meridian & Ash.

We are looking for a designer who can move comfortably from artwork recovery into original drawing. The window and bag photographs establish the first four designs; the two new pieces should belong naturally beside them.

Please think about the physical sticker from the start. The collection needs intentional negative space, clean offset cuts and a gang sheet that makes sense for the printer.

Design collection
Six sticker designs as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: four recovered from photographs of painted and printed originals and two authored to match their construction. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Cutting paths
Six single closed offset paths at the offset the printer's note states, each held as its own separable object rather than drawn into the artwork, with interior negative space resolved deliberately and any contour simplified for the blade named as simplified. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Production sheet
One sheet at the printer's true sheet size in real physical units, all six designs ganged with the stated minimum gutter and safe margin honoured, the arrangement chosen between a tight pack and themed rows and justified on vinyl yield and counter readability, with the cut layer present and separable on the sheet.

We are open to a tight pack or themed rows. Choose the stronger arrangement and explain the trade-off between sheet yield and how the collection reads; do not leave two unfinished directions for us to resolve.

Supplied references and printer information: meridian_window_mark.jpg (4160 x 3120); meridian_shelfcard_2025.pdf; meridian_sheet_spec.txt.

Also in the archive, for background only: meridian_bag_illustrations/ (3 frames, 5472 x 3648); meridian_origins.csv. These do not add deliverables to this commission.

Please work within $1,200-$3,200 fixed and the 7 to 15 business days target. Allow for one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

Handover: a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note. Include an inventory showing how every supplied file was used or why it was set aside. Keep factual content tied to the approved inputs. Any missing coverage, substituted asset, reconciliation or quality compromise must be declared; a weak source is not permission to invent or silently replace it. Include inspectable paths and small-size proofs; unverified fabrication tolerances remain subject to supplier review.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: The ledger row for VECTOR-04 carries an empty real_brief_anchors array, so the anchor is the recurring posted commission this concept was carved from rather than a single quoted post. The shape recurs constantly on Upwork and Freelancer.com under titles of the form 'die cut sticker sheet design for our coffee brand' and 'convert my logo to vector for stickers', and the body is always the same three asks: turn our existing logo and artwork into vector, arrange the designs on one print ready sheet, and supply the cut lines, with 'vector files' and 'editable source files' named among the deliverables and the client volunteering that all they have is a photograph or a printed sample because the original designer is gone. The ledger's own one_line_ask is quoted verbatim into the client voice here: pull our logo and a few of our existing printed illustrations into clean sticker art, and lay it all out as a die-cut sheet plus individual stickers we can sell and hand out. The triage verdict on the row is STRENGTHEN, and the reason it needed strengthening is that as carved it sat almost entirely on one surface (trace, then lay out), which is not the commission a roastery of this size actually places. Two things change that. First, the ledger's own 'peel-mockup card' would be photo compositing, which is not connector work, so it is re-carved as the printed counter card the roastery already puts in front of each origin, and that card is a genuine record per page run off a press PDF they already own. Second, CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) makes authored fixed canvas layout at true sheet size real, with inline SVG arriving as native editable vector, so the sheet and the on sale set are one editable document rather than a flat picture. That is the fuller job this client genuinely places inside one month.

price_band_and_audience: Impulse retail at three dollars a single and nine dollars a four pack, buyer twenty to thirty five, a cafe regular who buys at the till without deciding first. The band is load-bearing. At this price the range has to read as abundant and hand made: many small pieces, a warm printed ground, generous ink coverage, type that looks painted rather than set. The same six marks treated as a luxury programme, one foil emblem on a deep matte ground with acres of air, misreads the till entirely: it prices like a forty dollar object, it kills the four pack, and it makes the giveaway handful look like a mistake. Push the other way into loud discount styling, heavy outlines, drop shadows and a crowded sheet, and it stops reading as a roastery that people want to advertise on a laptop lid. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even when every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 700 to 1,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Specialty coffee roaster and cafe selling stickers and merchandise at the till, at farmers markets and to wholesale accounts.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, Portland, Oregon, a converted machine shop with one counter, two market stalls and roughly forty wholesale accounts.
brand_identity.about: Meridian and Ash roast single origin coffee in a converted machine shop and sell it across their own counter, at two farmers markets and to about forty wholesale accounts. The merchandise table is half the fun: stickers people put on laptops and water bottles because they actually like the mark. The whole point is a range that feels made by hand, not bought by the case.
brand_identity.audience: Cafe regulars twenty to thirty five who buy a sticker at the till without deciding first, and wholesale buyers who hand them out with orders.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Impulse retail, three dollars a single and nine dollars a four pack. Priced to be handed out by the fistful, so the range has to read as abundant rather than precious.
brand_identity.typography: A shaded serif wordmark that looks painted rather than set, arched over a filled roundel. Text and labels lean into a friendly, slightly irregular hand. Nothing boutique or foil thin.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, warm, a little wry, never precious. Example line: Pull one off the sheet, stick it on your laptop, come back for the other three.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No usable source files exist. The window mark was hand painted on the shop glass in 2018 by a sign painter who never handed over a file. The three current illustrations survive only printed on the coffee bags, and the printer still holds last season's counter card artwork.
brand_identity.values: Consistency people can trust, so the artwork stops being redrawn slightly differently every batch, and a hand made feel that reads as a real roastery rather than a franchise.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_window_mark.jpg (4160 x 3120)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the shop window from the sidewalk, the mark hand painted in two inks on the glass: a shaded serif wordmark arched over a filled roundel that carries an ash leaf inside a hairline ring.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place the mark exists. Ross painted it in 2018 and we never got a file off him."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup painted on glass, which behaves nothing like a flat scan. A prompt naming the window or the glass returns the pane rather than the paint, a compound prompt returns the arched wordmark while silently dropping the ring and the leaf and still looks entirely plausible, and the one call knockout cannot punch the ring's enclosed interior so it returns a solid opaque disc. Across the right third the street reflects in the glass at close to the value of the darker ink.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_bag_illustrations/ (3 frames, 5472 x 3648)
assets_supplied.kind: Flat lay photographs of three printed coffee bags, one illustration on each: a moth, a ridge line, a pour over cone.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The three that are already on the bags. We want those exactly as they are, they are the reason people pick us up."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the three were printed as solid ink and the third was screened at press. At photograph preview scale a screen reads as a flat tone and is indistinguishable from solid ink, so nothing about the frame declares which is which. It only announces itself once the ink is traced, as thousands of dot contours instead of a drawing. Separately one of the three crosses the bag's gusset fold, so part of its geometry is bent off the plane and does not straighten with the frame.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_shelfcard_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's press artwork for last season's counter card, one card per origin, the file that actually went to press.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our printer sends this back every season. The holders on the counter are cut for it, so the card cannot change size."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card's origin name, roast line, tasting notes and price were set as one continuous flow, so what the converted document exposes as separately addressable frames is nothing like the four blocks the printed card shows. And the readout of the card's own story omits one run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past it is short by that run's length, while the mapping validates clean and the prepare call reports success.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_origins.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Plain data for the six current origins: origin, farm, process, roast, tasting notes, price.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The six we are pouring now. The notes are what our head roaster wrote, do not improve them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the six carry a second tasting line the other four do not, so those two rows are roughly twice the length of their neighbours, and one row's price is the wholesale per pound figure rather than the counter price, which no column header distinguishes and no cell flags.

assets_supplied.kind: The sticker printer's note: sheet size, minimum gutter between cuts, safe margin from the sheet edge, and their standing requirement that the cut contour arrive as its own separable object rather than drawn into the artwork.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What our printer sent when we asked what they need."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the three bag illustrations was screened at press rather than printed in solid ink. At the scale a photograph of a bag previews at, a press screen reads as a flat tone and is visually identical to solid ink, so nothing in the frame, the filename or the client's description separates them. It declares itself only in the traced result: the two solid marks come back as a drawing with a countable number of contours, and the screened one comes back as thousands of dot contours that still assemble into a plausible looking picture at full canvas and only fall apart as artwork at sticker size and as an editable object once placed.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the tracing tool takes no options at all and the only lever is what the raster prep hands it, which is the decision this checkpoint is about. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the three illustrations are already printed on the bags and that the client wants them exactly as they are. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the affected illustration goes through a different chain, a binary ink mask traced as a mask rather than a colour plate traced as art, or a redraw as authored geometry when the screen has destroyed the line.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive that one illustration through a different route, judge whether what comes back is still the drawing on the bag or a new drawing wearing its shape, and then re-place it, which changes its silhouette and therefore its cut contour and its position in the sheet arrangement.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A range where one of six stickers is a cloud of dots that prints muddy at fifty five millimetres and arrives in the client's editable file as thousands of loose shapes, on a merchandise line whose entire premise is that nobody ever has to redraw the artwork again.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That the readout of the shelf card's own text is short of the truth. The card's copy was set as one continuous flow, so the conversion exposes nothing like the four blocks the printed card shows, and the readout of that flow omits one run while keeping its line break, leaving a string that still looks well formed. Every offset computed past the omission is short by that run's length. The validator returns valid with no warnings on those offsets, the prepare call reports completing successfully, and the only place the shortfall appears is on the merged page, where two fields still carry last season's copy while the rest carry this season's.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the readout is the only description of the story the tools volunteer, and there is no flag, warning or count that says a run is missing. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the printer still has last season's artwork and that the cards must stay the same size. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is to reconstruct the card's true story text out of the interchange file and recompute every offset against that string, which is a different derivation, not the same derivation repeated.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the field map from the reconstructed story text, prepare the template again, confirm by round tripping the interchange file that every placeholder is actually present rather than trusting the success message, then re-merge and read the six pages.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Six counter cards that look right and print right and quietly tell every customer at the till the wrong tasting notes and the wrong price for two of the six origins, with every tool response in the chain having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the thing the whole deliverable turns on. The printer needs the cut contour as a separable object sitting over the artwork, and the natural authoring constructions for it are exactly the ones this importer discards without saying so: an outline is dropped entirely, a stroked display letterform loses its stroke and can render as fully transparent, a blurred halo is dropped so the element goes hard edged, and a stacked shadow is truncated to its first layer. All of them return success. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so whichever canvas is not first cannot be checked any other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right the first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks only that the cut line arrive as its own thing the printer can lift off. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different construction of the same object, a closed path drawn as real geometry with its own fill and stroke rather than a CSS effect around the artwork, and the sheet then has to be re-composed around what that object actually is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the cut layer as authored path geometry, re-author the sheet and the on sale canvases around it, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every canvas from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A gang sheet delivered as an editable file with no cut layer in it at all on the canvases nobody looked at, sent to the printer who then does exactly what the last supplier's press operator did and redraws the cut by hand, which is the specific thing the client hired this job to stop.

decision_gates: Selection wording on the painted window: naming the window or the glass takes the pane, naming the paint's own visual properties takes the mark, and a one call knockout on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which recovery route each of the four originals needs, since a two colour trace off a binary mask and a colour accurate knockout plate produce different artwork and the response text is identical.
Whether a recovered illustration is still the drawing on the bag or has become a new drawing wearing its shape, and what to tell the client when it is the second.
How the two new designs are constructed, taken from the recovered marks' own stroke weight and terminals rather than chosen freely.

Tight pack versus themed rows on the sheet, argued on vinyl yield against readability in a counter bin.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a three dollar impulse buy, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Whether the licensed kraft frame joins the range's world or reads as bought, and how warm the ground can go before the ink stops separating from it.

client_brief:
Resort identity recovery and a bilingual door-plate system

Isla Verde needs a specialist who is comfortable with both identity craft and production data. This is one coordinated job: recover the foil monogram, build the pictograms and make the bilingual plates fit the existing installation.

The fixing positions and legacy trim are constraints. Please work from the facility schedule rather than deciding the plate count from the number of site photographs.

1. The monogram
The 2019 foil stamp recovered as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, the oval rule continuous and the interlock still reading as two letters at the size it actually reproduces on a pale panel and reversed. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

2. The icon family
Eight facility symbols as editable vector geometry built from the monogram's own stroke weight, terminal and corner language, drawn at each destination size rather than one drawing scaled, in one chosen direction with the rejected direction shown and the pick argued against the monogram's construction and the band. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

3. The plate run
One plate per facility, page count equal to row count, at the same trim as the 2016 artwork so the existing fixings still line up, every name readable in full at plate size in both English and Spanish, rendered at press resolution rather than screen scale, plus per record files for the fabricator whose record identity is guaranteed by explicit selection rather than inferred from export order. Any facility that cannot fit at a legible size is escalated as a named decision.

4. The placement references
The property's own mount point photography brought to one house target, each frame processed separately with a parameter log, reconciled against the schedule so that the duplicate wall and the three unphotographed facilities are named, plus one licensed camera-scale frame graded into the same set for the mount points nobody photographed. No frame exceeds its source dimensions and every reported resize is recorded.

The two optical icon sizes need deliberate drawing, not only scaling. Show the direction you selected and the rejected alternative. Any licensed context used for an unphotographed location must remain clearly non-documentary.

Package supplied: islaverde_brochure_cover.jpg (4032 x 3024); islaverde_locations/ (10 frames, phone); islaverde_doorplate_2016.pdf; islaverde_schedule.csv; islaverde_existing_signs/ (4 frames); islaverde_signshop_note.txt.

The final package should contain a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record, with every source file accounted for, including references and rejected or superseded material. Use the approved information without inventing missing facts. Only the stated stock or concept exceptions permit substitution; document every omission, replacement, reconciliation and material quality compromise. Include inspectable paths and small-size proofs; unverified fabrication tolerances remain subject to supplier review.

$5,000-$10,000 fixed; 4 to 6 weeks. Review structure: Direction approval, first-production proof, and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

source_provenance.original_anchor: The ledger row for VECTOR-05 carries an empty real_brief_anchors array, so the anchor is the recurring posted commission this concept was carved from rather than a single quoted post. It is one of the most common shapes on Upwork and Freelancer.com in the hospitality category: a property posts under a title of the form 'wayfinding and signage design for boutique resort' or 'recreate our logo from a printed brochure, vector needed', and the body always contains the same three admissions, that the original designer is unreachable, that the only surviving artwork is printed on something, and that the sign fabricator needs files by a date, with 'vector', 'editable', 'exact sizes' and 'we need our actual logo, not a new one' recurring almost verbatim. The ledger's own one_line_ask is quoted into the client voice here: we are refreshing signage across our resort and only have a printed brochure showing our old monogram, recover it cleanly and build a coordinated wayfinding system, all as editable artwork our sign shop can cut. The triage verdict on the row is STRENGTHEN, and two things had to change to meet the standard. First, the ledger's own 'mounted-panel mockup on a wall photo' is photo compositing, which is not connector work, so it is re-carved as what a real signage engagement actually hands over instead: the property's own location photography brought to one look for the standards document, plus a licensed camera scale frame for the mount points the property never photographed. Second, as carved the row sat almost entirely on one surface. The door plate is the part of a wayfinding programme that is genuinely a volume run, twenty four facilities at one plate per door, and the property already owns the 2016 press artwork the current plates were cut from, which is exactly the input a record per page run needs and exactly why the fixings still line up.

price_band_and_audience: Upscale independent resort, rooms three hundred and eighty to six hundred and fifty a night, guest thirty to fifty five and travelling for quiet. The band is load-bearing and it decides the whole system. At this tier the signage is restrained: generous clear space, one or two close greys rather than contrast for its own sake, a delicate monogram, type set small and confidently, symbols drawn with the same hand as the mark. A budget motel system doing the same job would correctly be louder, denser, higher contrast and larger in type, because it has to be read fast by someone who does not want to be there, and shipping that treatment here reads as a highway property and undercuts the rate. Push the other way into near invisible pale on pale and the system stops doing the one thing signage exists to do, which at this tier is worse than looking cheap, because a guest who cannot find the spa asks at the desk and the quiet is what they paid for. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even when every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 2,000 to 5,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Independent upscale coastal resort refreshing its corridor and garden wayfinding and its room signage.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Family owned, Gulf coast of Florida, a forty two room property with corridors, a garden path and about twenty four rooms and facilities.
brand_identity.about: Isla Verde is a family owned resort on the Gulf coast where guests come for quiet. Forty two rooms, refinished corridors and a garden that people walk slowly. The signage is being rebuilt this winter so the property reads as calmly as it feels, with the house monogram carried consistently from the door plates to the directional panels.
brand_identity.audience: Independent leisure travellers thirty to fifty five paying for calm, who notice when a place is shouting and value being able to find their way without being told loudly.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Upscale independent, rooms three hundred and eighty to six hundred and fifty a night. Signage should read at that tier: generous clear space, delicate marks, confidence rather than contrast for its own sake.
brand_identity.typography: A fine interlocking monogram set small and confidently, paired with a quiet, well spaced text face. Type kept modest and legible, never large or emphatic. Facility symbols drawn with the same hand as the mark.
brand_identity.voice: Understated, warm, precise. It gives directions without raising its voice. Example line: The spa is along the garden path, second door on the left.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No monogram source file survives. The designer moved abroad and nothing was handed back. The only decent record of the mark is a foil stamp on the cover of a brochure printed in 2019. The 2016 sign shop that cut the current door plates has since closed, though its press artwork for the plates is still on file.
brand_identity.values: A sense of quiet that guests can navigate, and a written standard so the next person who orders a sign does not invent something new.

assets_supplied.name: islaverde_brochure_cover.jpg (4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the 2019 printed brochure lying on a desk, the monogram foil stamped on uncoated cream stock: an interlocking I and V inside a fine oval rule with a small palm frond at the join.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only decent picture of the monogram we still have. It is stamped in foil so it catches the light."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Foil has no single ink value. The same stroke reads dark on one flank and near white specular on the other, so an ink level selection returns a plausible looking partial with whole strokes missing and no indication that anything is absent. The mark is also stamped small on the cover, so whatever survives the trace carries only the detail that was in those pixels, and the oval rule and the counters of the interlocked letters are the first things to close at the size the mark actually reproduces on a pale panel.

assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the ten are the same corridor shot from opposite ends and three facilities on the schedule have no frame at all, which no filename reveals. The phone's automatic white balance also renders three genuinely different wall finishes as the same neutral, so the frames cannot be trusted to say how a panel will sit against the wall it mounts to.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What a foil stamp actually gives back. Foil has no single ink value: across one stroke it reads dark where it turns away from the light and near white and specular where it turns toward it, and the cream stock sits between the two. An ink level selection therefore returns a partial that looks entirely plausible, complete in some strokes and absent in others, with no count, no confidence and no flag saying anything is missing. Which strokes survive is a property of how the brochure happened to be lying when the photograph was taken. Only after the trace, viewed at the size the mark reproduces on a pale panel rather than at full canvas, does it become visible whether the oval rule is continuous, whether the interlock still reads as two letters, and whether the counters have closed.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it: the tracing tool takes no options at all, the only lever is what the raster prep hands it, and no reading of the photograph at preview scale distinguishes a specular flank from missing artwork. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the monogram is stamped in foil and catches the light. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different derivation, selecting the cream stock and inverting, or filling a knockout plate against the inverted mask and tracing that instead of tracing the mask, and each of those is a different artwork with a different route.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive the monogram through a different route, judge the result again at reproduction size on the panel ground rather than at full canvas, and where a hairline cannot be recovered at all decide whether to author that element as path geometry consistent with what did survive or to tell the owner the rule cannot be recovered, then re-place the master everywhere it appears.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A monogram that looks correct in the handover file and closes into a solid blob on every door plate and every corridor panel on the property, delivered against a brief whose first sentence is that it has to still be their monogram.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises a monoline pictogram, and whether a symbol drawn for a corridor panel is still a symbol on a door plate. The pictograms are authored as unfilled stroked paths, which is the correct construction for a cut sign system, and the importer recomputes path geometry from the drawing's own coordinate space into rendered canvas units. Whether the stroke survives as a stroke, and whether its weight is recomputed with the geometry or carried across unchanged, is reported nowhere and is knowable only from the returned markup. If the weight does not travel with the geometry, the symbol placed at plate size arrives carrying the corridor panel's weight and reads as a filled blot while the corridor panel itself is perfect, and the document's rendition returns the first artboard only, so the plate face and every panel after the first cannot be looked at any other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is downstream of every authoring decision, and doing it right the first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks only for eight symbols that look like the monogram drew them, and the acceptance line about drawing each pictogram for its own size is the client's craft requirement, not a disclosure about an importer. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is to author a separate optical cut of each symbol for each destination size, which is a different set of drawings, not the same drawing re-exported.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Draw a second optical cut of all eight symbols for the small destination, re-decide the panel value relationships now that the small symbol's weight has changed, re-author, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every root from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twenty four door plates and every secondary panel carrying eight filled blots where the facility symbols should be, in a document that reported success at every step and whose one previewable page looks immaculate.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That the plate does not overflow, it stops. The name line on the 2016 artwork sits in a fixed measure frame sized to the longest name the property had in 2016, and a longer name does not spill, reflow, overset or flag: it simply stops rendering partway through, so the merged page is well formed, correctly laid out and quietly short. At page thumbnail scale twenty four plates all look right. Which of the twenty four are short depends on the interaction between the actual string, the face and the weight finally chosen, so it cannot be predicted from the data file, and the Spanish line and the English line fail at different lengths. The multi record raster route compounds it by returning files in an order that does not match the labels, so naming a per record file by its position asserts an identity that was never checked.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it: the frame's measure comes from artwork the property already owns and cannot be resized because the fixings are drilled, and the truncation point is a function of the type system, which is a later decision. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the plates must be the same size as the ones on the doors now, and the acceptance line about names reading in full is the client's requirement, not a warning that a frame truncates. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a decision, either a per facility naming convention agreed against the property's own signage language, or a change to the type system that then propagates back through every panel in the document, plus one name escalated to the owner because it cannot fit at any legible size.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read all twenty four plates at plate size in both languages, decide per affected facility between abbreviation, a type change that reaches back into the whole system, and escalation, then rebuild the mapping and re-merge, and confirm per record identity through a route that guarantees it rather than through the order of a returned list.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Plates screwed to doors reading Coastal Terrace and Suns and Pabellon de Tenis y Tie, cut in the fabricator's substrate at the property's expense, with the merged file having reported success and looked correct on screen.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the photographs into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of resort signs. IDENTITY: this is the monogram a designer made for this property and stamped on a 2019 brochure, and the client's own sentence is that it has to be their monogram and not a new one drawn to look like it, which is exactly what a generated mark is. SPEC: the fabricator cuts to a fixed size list with a stated clear space and a minimum legible type height, the door plates must land at the 2016 trim because the fixings are already drilled, and there are twenty four of them with two languages each, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the property will order signs from this system for years and explicitly asked for standards so the next person does not invent something, so a flat picture of a sign is the opposite of the deliverable. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did the foil actually give the oval rule back, is the symbol on the plate still a symbol, does this plate say Coastal Terrace or Coastal Terrace and Suns.

client_one_liner: Our crest exists nowhere except stitched on last year's shirts, our numbers and letters were drawn by hand in the nineties on two sheets of graph paper, and the supplier needs everything by the end of the month.
client_brief:
Recover a football crest and its hand-drawn shirt lettering

Ridgeway Rovers wants its existing identity back in usable form. The crest needs to work at breast size and in one ink; the lettering comes from a set of 1990s drawings rather than a font we can buy.

Please preserve what makes these ours while removing the graph-paper and reproduction artefacts. We need actual closed, usable character geometry, not a picture of the alphabet inside an SVG.

The crest recovered from a photograph of stitching as placeable scalable geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox, no opaque full canvas rectangle, every element that is on the shirt present including the hairline rule and centre motif, delivered as the crest, a single ink version drawn to survive at shirt breast size, and a reversed version that holds on navy. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Thirty six glyphs rebuilt from the founder's drawn sheets as original geometry: even consistent strokes, closed counters, single spot colour, no graph rule and no stray path, weighted to survive a blade and a heat press, reading as one set when a name sits above a number at back of shirt proportion, plus a written statement of what the sheets cannot supply for this squad. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Use the name-and-number example to demonstrate proportion and spacing. If the evidence does not support a required character, identify the gap instead of quietly importing something from another typeface.

Our material: ridgeway_crest_shirt.jpg (4032 x 3024); ridgeway_letters_sheet.jpg and ridgeway_numbers_sheet.jpg; ridgeway_shirtback_2024.pdf; ridgeway_shirt_blanks.jpg (2 frames, 12 megapixel).

Also in the archive, for background only: ridgeway_squad.csv; ridgeway_supplier_note.txt. These do not add deliverables to this commission.

Supplier review is still required for fabrication tolerances that cannot be established from these references. Please make the small-size and reversed proofs easy to compare.

The commission is budgeted at $1,200-$3,200 fixed. We have allowed 7 to 15 business days, including one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

Alongside the finished work, we need a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note. Keep a clear record of the supplied files used, retained for reference, superseded and rejected. Approved source information remains authoritative. Record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and quality limits, and do not use an undeclared replacement or invented fact to conceal a source problem. Include inspectable paths and small-size proofs; unverified fabrication tolerances remain subject to supplier review.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork jersey numbering brief (cand_46, db_i 823), in which a custom football kit shop asks for its signature numbering rebuilt as clean, print ready vector artwork with consistent stroke widths and even spacing for heat transfer and flock production, worked up from photographed reference sheets as original geometry rather than lifted from a proprietary font file. The shop is laundered to a fictional village club, Ridgeway Rovers FC; no real club, competition, player, supplier or typeface is named. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com brief 'Realistic Textile Embroidery Design', quoted verbatim in the ledger ('a skilled embroidery designer to create a realistic logo. Requirements: Realism style, Medium size (3-6 inches)'), which pins the crest to an embroidered artefact at a small physical reproduction size rather than a flat scan, plus the companion candidate 'Premium Heritage Apparel Identity System & Factory-Ready Vector Engineering', whose framing is to translate an existing concept into factory ready vector engineering. The STRENGTHEN verdict keeps that concept and deliverable set; what the v3 audit adds is reach, since an ink level selection recovers a mark off a stitched surface, the supplier's own press PDF converts into a live merge template, and HTML authoring gives the spec and board as one native editable document.

price_band_and_audience: Grassroots kit at 28 to 45 dollars a shirt, bought by players and by parents paying for a child's fourth kit in five years. The band is load bearing in the artwork itself: at this price the supplier cuts numbering as one robust spot colour in heat press vinyl or flock, so the glyphs must reduce to a single solid generously weighted closed geometry with no thin joins, no inline, no outline and no second colour. A pro tier sublimated number with a keyline and a gradient is not merely expensive here, it is uncuttable and the supplier bounces it. Push the other way into clip art blockiness and a club whose crest has been stitched on shirts since 1974 looks supermarket rebranded. The same tension runs through the crest, since holding as one ink at shirt breast size is a different drawing decision from a full colour crest that only appears large. A real posted job of this shape runs 700 to 1,600 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Grassroots amateur football club refreshing its playing kit, crest and shirt numbering through one local kit supplier.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1974, a village near Cirencester in the Cotswolds, with two senior sides, a veterans XI and four junior age groups.
brand_identity.about: Ridgeway Rovers are a village football club that has worn the same crest since 1974 and drawn their own shirt numbering since the nineties. This season brings the first new shirt since 2019. The club wants its own crest and its own hand drawn numbering back as proper artwork, so any supplier can print it and it still looks like Ridgeway.
brand_identity.audience: Players and parents at twenty eight to forty five dollars a shirt, often buying a child's fourth kit in five years, who want something that looks like a proper club.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Grassroots, twenty eight to forty five dollars a shirt printed by one local supplier. Numbering has to reduce to a single robust cuttable colour for heat press and flock, honest rather than pro tier.
brand_identity.typography: The crest lettering is small caps set in a ring. The numbering is the club's own hand drawn alphabet and digits, rebuilt as even, solid, cuttable geometry. A supporting text face for the spec and boards sits behind the drawn work, never over it.
brand_identity.voice: Straightforward, warm, club room plain. Example line: Same crest we have worn since 1974, cleaned up so any printer can do it justice.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No artwork survives. The former kit secretary took the crest files when he moved away, leaving only a parent's phone photo of the crest stitched on last season's home shirt. The numbering exists only as two marker on graph paper sheets, an alphabet and a digit set, drawn by a founding member in the nineties and photographed on a kitchen table. Last season's supplier back of shirt sheet is on hand as the format.
brand_identity.values: Keeping what is genuinely theirs, the 1974 crest and the founder's numbering, and reading as a real village club rather than a franchise or a school project.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the selection that fed the trace actually contained the whole crest. A selection naming a compound stitched lockup as one thing returns a mask that is clean, binary and crest shaped, and can silently omit interior elements: here the ring and the shield outline come back while the hairline rule and the ram's head do not. Nothing in the response says anything is missing, the mask has no soft edge to give it away because these masks carry no intermediate values at all, and the trace of it is a competent looking crest. Which elements survive is a property of this photograph's own local contrast, including the fold shadow across the right third, and cannot be read off the frame beforehand.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the omission happens inside one selection call whose only input is a phrase, and selecting four elements separately as an opening move is speculative spend against a possibility nobody has raised. Nothing states it: the brief says only that the crest is stitched on a shirt. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different chain, per element selections composited and re traced.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re select ring, rule, shield and ram's head as separate masks each named by its own visual properties, handle the fold shadow side separately, composite, re trace, re do the hygiene, and re derive both variants before any of them reach the merge template or the boards.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A club whose crest has been on its shirts since 1974 is handed a crest with its centre motif missing, stamped onto twenty four sheets, the supplier spec and both boards, having passed every response check on the way.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the fields the mapping asked for actually landed in the merge template. The readout of the converted supplier PDF's editable text is lossy: it omits one run while keeping that run's line break, so the returned string still reads as well formed prose with no sign of a gap, and every offset computed from it past that point is short by exactly the omitted run's length. The validator then reports the mapping valid with zero warnings and the placeholder build reports completed successfully, while two of the five fields are simply absent. No response in the chain says so, and the only way to learn it is to round trip the built template and look inside its stories for the placeholders you asked for.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the lossy readout is the only readout the mapping tool offers and the offsets must come from somewhere; doing it right first time presumes knowing that this document's summary drops a run, which no response, warning or schema states. Nothing states it: the brief only describes a supplier sheet format. It is not a propagation re run, because the response derives offsets from a different source, the document's own reconstructed story text.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct each frame's true story text from its own content runs, recompute every offset against that string, rebuild the mapping and the template, and re inspect for all five placeholders before merging a single record.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twenty four sheets that pass a page count check and go to the parents with two fields blank on every page, so the sign off the exercise exists to obtain is worthless and the supplier cuts from an incomplete instruction.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the one construct the committee boards depend on. The club has to see the number as it will sit on the shirt, which authored the natural way means letting the flat number take the cloth's folds through a blending mode, or softening its contact edge. The importer discards a blending mode entirely and renders the element as a plain opaque shape, and discards a blur filter outright, both at full success with no warning of any kind. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the rendition returns the first artboard only, so the away board can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the drop happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a board the committee can judge. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a DIFFERENT upstream asset, the number carried into the raster on the garment plate, or a board recomposed onto flat cloth.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the garment plates so the number is part of the raster, or recompose both boards around the flat cloth, re author the HTML, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit both boards from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A committee approves a kit off a board where the number floats as a flat sticker on the home shirt and, on the away board nobody opened, may not read at all, with the export having reported success throughout.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome football crest and a handsome set of numbers. IDENTITY: this crest has been stitched on this club's shirts since 1974 and this alphabet was drawn by a named founding member, so a regenerated crest is a different club's badge and a regenerated alphabet is somebody else's numbering, which is exactly what the original commission forbids by asking for original geometry rebuilt from the reference sheets. SPEC: the supplier needs cuttable single colour closed geometry, thirty six glyphs, and twenty four sheets in its own page format at one player per page with proofs whose identity can be checked against a roster, none of which a generated image is or can be verified to be. EDITABILITY: the spec and boards are defined by being editable, because the squad changes every season and a village club cannot re commission. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did the selection contain the whole crest, did the placeholders actually land, did the number survive the import as something that reads as printed.

client_brief:
Bring our painted festival wordmark into a usable anniversary kit

Wharfside Folk Festival is twenty years old. The shed-painted wordmark is part of that history, and we want to retain its character across the handbill, cloth and supporting anniversary materials.

The photograph has camera taper and shadow lettering that need interpretation. Please recover the mark rather than making a new festival logo.

The hand painted shed lettering recovered as placeable scalable geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox, no opaque full canvas rectangle, counters open, camera taper corrected, every letter present including those in the roof shadow, and a single ink form that holds at handbill size and on cloth. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Poster, handbill, shirt canvas and press spec as one editable document plus its source: Choose and adapt an Adobe Express template for these supporting pieces, using the supplied brand, approved copy and imagery. Select the strongest fit, replace the template content and correct its background as needed. Supply the editable design link and the requested export, in addition to the commissioned custom production work.

Eleven supplied press photographs brought toward one family under one treatment decision rather than eleven, reconciled against the fourteen booked acts with duplicates identified and gaps named, each at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log stating why any frame differs from its neighbours.

Our archive has eleven act photographs, while the booking information covers fourteen bookings. Reconcile the two before you build the photographic set; duplicated or missing coverage must not become an incorrect artist attribution.

We can provide wharfside_artwork_master.png (4200 x 5900); wharfside_wordmark_shed.jpg (3840 x 2160); wharfside_nightcard_2025.pdf; wharfside_acts.csv; wharfside_act_portraits/ (11 frames); wharfside_shop_note.txt.

The template-based supporting pieces should be properly adapted and editable, with the recovered wordmark and normalised photographs carrying through consistently.

Please deliver a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note. Account for every supplied file and identify anything used only as reference, superseded or rejected. Stay with approved facts and copy. Do not silently replace weak assets; use only the stated stock or concept allowances, and record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and material compromises. Include inspectable paths and small-size proofs; unverified fabrication tolerances remain subject to supplier review.

source_provenance.original_anchor: Anchored to the Upwork commemorative poster brief quoted in the ledger: a story driven twentieth anniversary poster in a 'festival posters, folk-art illustration, screenprint aesthetics' style, weaving landmarks and community traditions into one cohesive composition. The real client is a named school in Louisiana and is fully laundered here: no real institution, denomination, figure, place or person appears anywhere in this spec. The REBUILD verdict is taken literally, because the original concept sat almost entirely on one surface, a poster comp. The commission that brief actually implies, once the artwork is approved, is the production engineering that follows it, which is what a screen shop needs and what the original spec never delivered. So it is re carved as the separation programme: the approved illustration becomes something a hand press can pull at four inks plus the paper, in a registration order, reused across a poster, a handbill, a two ink shirt and a per act card run, with the festival's hand painted wordmark recovered off the shed it has lived on since 2006. That is a far larger job than composing a poster, it lands on five real connector surfaces, and it is the kind of multi part rollout actually posted on freelance marketplaces.
