So it is re carved as the separation programme: the approved illustration becomes something a hand press can pull at four inks plus the paper, in a registration order, reused across a poster, a handbill, a two ink shirt and a per act card run, with the festival's hand painted wordmark recovered off the shed it has lived on since 2006. That is a far larger job than composing a poster, it lands on five real connector surfaces, and it is the kind of multi part rollout actually posted on freelance marketplaces.
price_band_and_audience: A community festival at 35 to 60 dollar tickets, with posters sold afterwards as 20 dollar framed keepsakes to an audience that already owns the last five years of them. The band points the opposite way from most price logic: the visible, slightly imperfect, hand pulled limited ink look IS the product here, so flat opaque ink, visible registration, the paper colour doing real work and a coarse tone screen are value rather than defects to design out. A slick full process reproduction would be cheaper to make, would read as corporate, would stop being worth twenty dollars on a wall, and would break continuity with nineteen years hanging in local kitchens. Push the other way into deliberate crudeness, three ink grunge and distressed edges, and it reads as a pastiche of a folk festival rather than one that has run since 2006. The judgement is which four inks buy the most of the painting, and that judgement is the commission. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,400 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2006, on the working harbour at Fairhaven, Maine, a three night festival printed by a two person hand screen shop two streets away.
brand_identity.about: Wharfside is a three night folk festival on the working harbour at Fairhaven, in its twentieth year. The visible, hand pulled look is the festival's signature, and people frame the posters every year.

brand_identity.typography: The wordmark is the hand painted lettering that has been on the harbour shed since 2006. Supporting type sits beside that painted hand without imitating it, set for flat opaque ink and visible registration. Coarse tone screens carry the sky and water.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the painting actually separates into the fields the eye reads in it. Two fields that look distinct, the rust of the shed roofs and the ochre of the hillside behind them, run to nearly the same value along the ridge where they meet, so a selection naming either comes back as a clean, complete looking, fully binary mask that has quietly taken both. There is no soft edge to give it away because these masks carry no intermediate values at all, the call reports success, and the plate looks correct on its own. It becomes visible only when the plates are laid together and reassembled against the painting, at which point one ink is doing two jobs and the ridge has vanished.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it: selection by material is the only route to a field, its output is binary, and the tool exposes no confidence about what it took, so selecting every field twice with different phrasings as an opening move is speculative spend. Nothing states it: the brief says the press runs four inks plus the paper and nothing about the painting's values. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different carving strategy that changes the ink plan itself.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re open the ink plan, re carve the affected fields through a different selection strategy and polarity, re fill and re proof every plate touching the ridge, and re run the reassembly before anything downstream reuses the separations, since poster, handbill and shirt all inherit them.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A poster pulled in what the shop believes is four inks, in which the ridge line separating the town from the hills does not exist, printed on the shed and in every shop window and sold as a twentieth year keepsake beside nineteen years that do have it.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the tone plate reads as a screen at BOTH printed sizes. The screen has exactly one control, its coarseness, and no frequency parameter of any kind, so what it does is fixed in the raster and cannot be re specified per output. A coarseness chosen against the poster's true printed size, where it reads as an open hand pulled screen, is the same raster reproduced at roughly a third of that on the handbill, where the dots close into one another and the sky becomes a flat field, losing the tone the plate exists to carry. Both exports report success, both plates are correct in isolation, and the difference exists only as the relationship between one raster and two physical sizes.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the coarseness must be chosen before the plate exists and its adequacy is a function of a size that only exists once the layout does; doing it right first time presumes knowing where one raster stops reading across a three to one reduction, which no tool reports and no parameter expresses. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a handbill of the same thing. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a SECOND tone plate at a different coarseness, so the handbill is no longer the same separation set as the poster.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Generate a second tone plate judged against the handbill's own printed size, decide whether the shirt needs a third, re author the affected canvases, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, audit from the returned markup, and rewrite the spec so the press knows which screen belongs to which piece.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Handbills whose sky and water print as two flat slabs of ink where the poster has weather, handed out at the tourist office all season as the festival's own advertisement, with every export having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the shop's card actually is underneath. The printed page shows act name, stage, set time and a portrait panel as four visibly separate blocks, so it reads as a four frame layout with a picture box. What the conversion exposes is not under anyone's control: this card's text was set as one continuous flow and its portrait panel was drawn rather than placed, so the document arrives as a single story with no graphic frame at all. There is nothing to bind a per act portrait to and the four fields cannot be addressed as four frames. Nothing in the conversion response says any of this, the document converts cleanly, and the only way to learn it is to export the round tripped structure and read the actual frame inventory.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and nothing about the PDF predicts it, because frame granularity is a property of how the original was set, invisible in the printed page and in the file's appearance, so doing it right first time presumes knowing the answer before inspecting. Nothing states it: the brief says only that the shop's card format is attached. It is not a propagation re run, because the response changes both the mapping strategy and the deliverable shape.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Compute offset based mappings against the reconstructed story text rather than per frame bindings, decide whether the portraits leave the merge and become a separately delivered plate set the shop places by hand or whether the card is re cast as text only, tell the festival which it is, and rebuild and re verify the template before merging any of the fourteen.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen cards that merge, page for act, with the names and times landing wherever the offsets happened to point and the portrait panel showing last year's opening act on every single one.

Whether the paper is treated as a background or worked as one of the five colours, which is the difference between a screen print and a reproduction at this band.
How each field is named for selection, given that naming the object rather than the material pulls the mask elsewhere and the result is binary with no edge to warn you.
What happens to the fifth colour in the water: its own ink, folded into a neighbour, or explicitly surrendered and recorded.
The screen's coarseness, which is one number with no frequency control, judged against a physical printed size rather than against the file.
Whether the shirt is a reduction of the poster or its own drawing, given two inks, cloth and a stated minimum line weight.
Selection wording on the shed: naming the sign takes the plank, disjoint lettering defeats a subject led knockout, and enclosed counters cannot be punched by background removal at all.
One treatment for eleven portraits from eleven photographers, and what to do about the three acts with no portrait and the two files that are the same act.

client_brief:
Distillery mark recovery and a matching founder portrait set

This is a focused identity-production commission for Coble & Vane. We need the existing mark recovered in colour and true one-ink form, alongside three founder photographs that currently disagree because of their lighting.

The work we are commissioning is below:

The mark reduced from a full-colour tonal illustration to placeable, scalable one-ink artwork with a real viewBox and no opaque ground path, in the variant set the applications require and in on-light and on-dark colourways. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Three founder-shot frames taken under two different lights brought to one house neutral (one white point, one warmth, one black point) plus one licensed camera-scale frame graded into the same set, every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame log of corrections and of every reported resize.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork product-packaging brief behind this ledger slot, a trading firm launching its first private-label line that needed an approved master logo extended into a working variant system, swappable per-SKU labels and single-colour cartons built as data-driven templates, plus a digital asset pack for suppliers. Laundered to a fictional coined brand, Coble & Vane; no real company, product, person or trademark is named. The ledger verdict was REBUILD, because as banked the concept sat on one surface: trace the logo, hand back four SVGs. A supplier-facing mark system is judged on the stamped and printed objects it lands on, and the client who commissions one almost always has a packaging run in flight and a printer holding the only copy of last year's artwork. VECTOR-08 restores that commission: a colour illustration that has to become one ink, a die sheet nobody at the distillery has opened, twelve cask releases needing labels, and a supplier sheet that has to stay editable.

price_band_and_audience: Bottles 55 to 120 dollars (standard gin 55, cask-strength single malt 95 to 120). Buyer 30 to 55 buying a gift or a considered bottle, plus the merchant deciding whether the bottle earns its shelf facing. The band is load-bearing: at this tier the one-ink treatments read as restraint and heritage, a single deep ink, generous clear space, emboss and wax finishes carrying the value, and a supplier sheet written as instruction rather than advertisement. A twelve-dollar brand would take the opposite answer, louder and higher-contrast, and would not care whether the stencil and foil versions were different drawings. An agent that ships a loud, dense set has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,500 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: A two-person coastal distillery making small-batch gin and cask-strength single malt, sold shop-direct and through independent merchants.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2020, on the Northumberland coast, England. A two-person distillery: Iris runs the still, her partner runs everything else.
brand_identity.about: Coble & Vane is a working distillery on a stretch of the North Sea coast, named for the flat-bottomed fishing boat that once beached below the still house. We release twelve casks a year and nothing we cannot stand behind. The bottle is meant to earn its place on a shelf and in a hand, not to shout across the shop.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers aged 30 to 55 choosing a gift or a considered bottle, and the independent merchant deciding whether the bottle earns its shelf facing. People who read a label closely and reward restraint.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Bottles 55 to 120 dollars: standard gin at 55, cask-strength single malt from 95 to 120. Upper-craft tier, sitting deliberately apart from the twelve-dollar shelf. Value is carried by finish, emboss and wax rather than by loud print.
brand_identity.typography: Display in an engraved-feeling serif with real weight in the caps, set with generous letter spacing. Text in a quiet humanist sans for supplier and label copy. The type stays out of the way and lets a single ink do the work.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, dry, unhurried. Written as instruction, not advertisement. Example line: "One ink, plenty of air, and nothing shiny. If our own list looks wrong to you, say so before you make it."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The house mark was drawn six years ago by an illustrator who has since moved abroad and cannot be reached. It survives only as a full-colour illustration flattened to a single PNG. There are no vector files, no one-ink versions, and no supplier guidance sheet. Every single-colour version a supplier has ever received was improvised from that one file, and no two have matched.
brand_identity.values: Restraint and honesty. One deep ink, generous clear space, and finishes that carry the value instead of the print. Say plainly what a version can and cannot do.

assets_supplied.name: house_mark_colour.png (3600 x 3600)
assets_supplied.kind: The distillery's only surviving copy of its mark: a full-colour engraved-style illustration of a beached coble under a rope ring carrying the two family names, flattened to PNG.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our mark as she drew it. This file is all we have and there is nobody to ask for anything else."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. Hull, sail and water are shaded with fine engraved cross-hatch and the rope ring is two interleaved strands in two closely related inks, so the mark's weight comes from tone rather than line and reducing it to one ink is a decision about what stops existing rather than a trace. It was also composited over a warm laid-paper texture and flattened, so any preparation separating ink from ground by lightness takes part of the paper with it.

assets_supplied.name: cask_labels_2025_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF for last season's cask release labels, from a real page layout with embedded font subsets, one page, 210 x 148 mm.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What Redgate ran for us last year. We have never opened it. Keep the label as it is."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two structural facts nobody at the distillery could tell you and nothing in the PDF announces. The page is not a label, it is the die sheet: front and back labels sit side by side because that is how the cutter is set, so one cask is one sheet carrying two dissimilar labels. And the back label's whole copy block came across as one continuous story rather than addressable lines, with the mapping readout silently omitting one run so every offset past it is short while the validator still reports the mapping valid.

assets_supplied.name: cask_release_2026.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The cask book export, one row per release: cask number, expression name, strength, filling date, bottling date, outturn, volume, distilled-at line, photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This year's twelve, straight out of the cask book. Iris writes the expression names herself and they go on the label as written."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. Three casks were re-numbered after a re-racking last autumn and the photo column still carries their old numbers, so three rows bind a photograph of the wrong cask while every filename resolves. And the filling and bottling dates are transposed on two adjacent rows, settleable only by reading them against the strength and outturn rather than by validating the file.

assets_supplied.name: packaging_shots/ (3 frames, 4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Phone photographs the founders took of their own packaging: a wax seal over a bottle neck, a stencilled crate end, and a cap from above.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our own wax, our own crate, our own cap. Use these on the sheet so a supplier can see what we mean."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. Wax and cap were shot indoors under a warm work lamp and the crate outdoors in flat daylight, so the three will not sit together without different corrections. And the wax seal is deep oxblood on near-black glass, so its shadowed lower rim and the glass share luminance and a subject knockout returns success while quietly eating the bottom of the seal.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What this illustration becomes when reduced to one ink, judged where it will be used. Its weight is carried by fine engraved cross-hatch and by a rope ring drawn as two interleaved strands in two closely related inks, and the tracing call takes no options at all, so the only lever is the raster preparation. Every preparation succeeds and every result is crisp at canvas size. Only at cap size, and only on the oxblood wax and kraft crate rather than on white, does one preparation show the hatch closing into a solid mass while another shows it dropping out entirely and the ring breaking into dashes. Nothing in any response distinguishes the outcomes, and the polarity flip between light and dark grounds changes which strokes survive.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot either, because there is no parameter to reason about: the tracer has no options, so the correct preparation is knowable only by making one, tracing it and looking at real size on the real ground. Nothing states it, since the brief asks for the mark in one ink, lists where it goes, never mentions hatching or stroke weight, and never asks what the safe minimum size is. And the response is not a re-run but a different raster and usually a changed variant architecture.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Produce a genuinely different plate: a selection worded for the structural line rather than the tonal field, a masked flattening of the hatch before tracing, or the colour-accurate fill-then-trace route. Re-trace, re-inject the viewBox, re-strip the opaque path and re-place at each application size on each ground. Then re-take the variant count, because a mark that will not hold at cap size needs a different drawing rather than a smaller copy, and the sheet's structure depends on that answer.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A wax supplier the distillery will never speak to presses a seal from a file whose rope ring has closed into a solid ring and whose hull has gone to a black blob, on a bottle selling at a hundred and twenty dollars, from artwork that looked flawless in every preview.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's file actually is and what it exposes, which arrives only by converting, exporting IDML and reading the frame geometry. The page is not a label, it is the die sheet: front and back labels sit side by side because that is how the cutter is set, so one cask is one sheet carrying two dissimilar labels with different frame counts and different mapping strategies. And the back label's entire copy block came across as one continuous story, with the mapping readout omitting one run so every offset computed past it is short, while the validator reports the mapping valid and the prepare call reports the placeholders created successfully.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Frame granularity and page imposition are properties of a document made by a printer nobody at the distillery has spoken to; they are not parameters and nothing reports them before the conversion, so no ordering reaches them earlier. Nothing states it: the client calls the file the label and says to keep it as it is, a requirement rather than a description of its internals. And it is not a propagation re-run, because the mapping strategy changes shape, from per-frame replacement to ordered offset arithmetic against an independently reconstructed story, planned twice over for two dissimilar halves of one sheet.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the IDML content runs, recompute every offset from that string, plan front and back as two mappings against one row, order rows sharing a page item so positions descend, re-validate, re-prepare, and re-verify by grepping the round-tripped IDML for every placeholder before any page is merged. Then write the sheet-versus-label finding into the handover so the bottling hall is not counting the wrong artefact.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A press run of twelve cask sheets where the front label is perfect, strength and cask number bind correctly, and the filling date and distilled-at line are silently absent from every back label, delivered as finished artwork with every tool having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the importer does to the delivered artwork once it is inside the document. The returned per-canvas markup is the only channel, because the rendition preview shows canvas one and nothing else, so the application spread and the trade canvases can be inspected only as markup. A traced mark arrives as loose ungrouped shapes rather than one coherent object, the opaque full-canvas path rides along with any variant it was not stripped from and shows as a filled box on the oxblood or kraft panels, and a wrapper sized by its contents rather than explicitly collapses and throws the artwork off the artboard edge. Every one of those returns success with no warning.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Normalisation is the importer's behaviour on this construct and there is no read-ahead, and care cannot dodge it either, because the same authoring choice behaves correctly on one canvas and fails on another depending on how the wrapper resolved. Nothing states it: the brief asks for an editable working file with the mark as real artwork and says nothing about grouping, wrappers or canvases. And it is not a propagation re-run, because the answer changes the artwork and the composition rather than the input.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Parse every canvas's returned markup rather than trusting the export, strip the opaque path from every variant that still carries one, re-anchor every wrapper with explicit left, top, width and height, re-author the panels whose marks arrived as scattered geometry, re-run the readiness check and re-export. Where a variant will not hold on a dark panel, re-take the panel rather than shipping a mark with a box behind it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A supplier sheet handed to four suppliers in which the reversed mark sits in a visible opaque rectangle on the wax panel and the crate panel's artwork has run off the canvas edge, on the pages nobody could preview, delivered as the editable file the distillery will work from every season.

decision_gates: What in a tonal colour illustration is the mark and what is shading, decided before any preparation is made.
Selection wording: whether the prompt takes the drawing or the laid-paper texture it was flattened over.
Which polarity to hand a tracer that takes no options, and whether to trace the binary plate or the colour-accurate plate.
How many variants the applications genuinely need, and whether a fine and a stencil version are one drawing at two sizes or two preparations.
Whether to strip the opaque ground path and inject a viewBox, which nothing in the chain does and nothing warns about.
Isolation route per subject, when a knockout is right for a cap on a bench and wrong for an oxblood seal on near-black glass.
Whether the cask book matches the photographs, when three rows carry pre-re-racking numbers and two rows have transposed dates and all validate.
Whether repointing a client's own data silently is the same act as repointing it and saying so.

vertical: Technology & SaaS (eleven-person seed-stage company selling scheduling infrastructure to logistics operations teams, Denver, Colorado)
primary_craft_problem: Recover production artwork from imperfect physical references while separating faithful reconstruction from unsupported fabrication claims. The lead output is Halcyon Grid production mark family.
client_one_liner: Eleven people, six weeks to a developer conference, three logos our founder generated at two in the morning, and a printer who has already told us he cannot use what we sent him.
client_brief:
Turn rough raster brand concepts into a credible SaaS identity system

Halcyon Grid is a small logistics software team. We have three AI-generated raster marks, but we do not yet have a usable identity. We need a designer to resolve the geometry, not preserve every artefact in those images.

The result has to survive the small app-icon and favicon uses as well as the wordmark lockups. Please check the enclosed spaces and remove any halo before presenting the family.

Identity deliverables: Three marks rebuilt from generative rasters as placeable, scalable artwork with real viewBoxes, no opaque ground paths, no halo debris and enclosed shapes genuinely enclosed, in on-light, on-dark and one-ink colourways, plus horizontal and stacked wordmark lockups, an app icon and a favicon. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Team imagery: Eleven self-submitted phone frames shot under no common direction brought to one credible house treatment (one white point, one warmth, one black point) plus one licensed camera-scale frame graded into the same set, every output at or below its true source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame log of corrections and of every reported resize.

There are eleven phone portraits to bring together. They should look like the same team without depending on enlargement or an implausible skin treatment.

Files supplied: halcyon_master_mark.png (1400 x 1400); subbrand_marks/ (2 PNGs, 1024 x 1024 and 1600 x 1600); team_roster.csv; team_photos/ (11 self-submitted frames, 1200 to 4000 px); halcyon_booth_code.png; founder_notes.txt.

Also in the archive, for background only: exhibitor_card_2025_PRINT.pdf. These do not add deliverables to this commission.

The final package should contain a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note, with every source file accounted for, including references and rejected or superseded material. Use the approved information without inventing missing facts. Only the stated stock or concept exceptions permit substitution; document every omission, replacement, reconciliation and material quality compromise. Include inspectable paths and small-size proofs; unverified fabrication tolerances remain subject to supplier review.

Fee range: $2,500-$6,000 fixed
Delivery target: 2 to 4 weeks
Included reviews: One direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork brief in which the client's logo had been 'created on AI' and needed turning into a 'vector file so it can be used in multiple platforms', kept 'high-quality across different formats'. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com open call 'Vectorize Logos & Packaging', where the client already has 'AI-generated artwork ... but it is still in raster form and not ready for production' and needs 'everything redrawn as clean, fully-editable vectors so I can scale them for any application without loss of quality', with scope including preserving 'every colour, gradient, and detail exactly as in the original concept while improving line sharpness and overall balance'. Both are laundered to a fictional seed-stage company, Halcyon Grid; no real company, product, person, trademark or AI tool is named in any task-facing field. The ledger verdict was REBUILD, because as banked it sat on one surface: three traces, done. The second anchor's own wording is also a trap the connector will not honour, since a trace of a gradient returns dozens of near-identical flat fills, so the honest commission is a reduction argued and defended rather than exact preservation promised. VECTOR-09 restores what these clients needed: a mark family that has to hold together, a printed run in flight against a conference date, and a sheet somebody else can work from.

price_band_and_audience: Seats 20 to 60 dollars per user per month, sold to engineering and operations leads at mid-sized logistics firms, decided by a technical evaluator rather than a brand buyer. The band is load-bearing: this audience reads pixel-crisp geometric restraint as engineering credibility and reads gloss, glow and decorative detail as a company that spends on appearance rather than reliability, so the correct answer is a reduction toward sharp minimal geometry with quiet type, and a mark sheet that reads as documentation rather than marketing. A consumer lifestyle app at the same price would take the opposite answer and it would be wrong here. An agent that preserves the founder's glow because the founder is attached to it, without arguing the case, has ducked the commission even if every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,500 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: A seed-stage software company selling scheduling infrastructure to logistics operations teams, with a main product and two sub-products.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2024, Denver, Colorado. Eleven people, six weeks out from their first developer conference.
brand_identity.about: Halcyon Grid builds scheduling infrastructure for logistics operations teams, sold by the seat to the engineers and operations leads who run the floor. The product is judged on reliability, and the brand is meant to say the same thing the software does: precise, plain, and built to be depended on.
brand_identity.audience: Engineering and operations leads at mid-sized logistics firms, decided by a technical evaluator rather than a brand buyer. An audience that reads fuss as sloppiness and crispness as competence.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Seats 20 to 60 dollars per user per month. Mid-market infrastructure pricing, sold on reliability and evaluation rather than on brand aspiration. The visual language reads as engineering credibility, never as marketing spend.
brand_identity.typography: Wordmark and headings in a geometric grotesque with tight, even weight and no decorative detail. Body and documentation in a clean neutral sans with strong numerals. Type is set to read as documentation, not as a campaign.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, unadorned, engineer to engineer. No hype, no gloss. Example line: "Sharp, plain, restrained. If something in our own list turns out to be a bad idea, tell us before you build it."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The three marks (the main mark and two sub-product marks) were generated by the founder in an AI tool two years ago, on separate nights with different settings. Only the soft-edged raster exports survive, with no source files. They go soft as soon as anyone scales them, and the printer and the app store listing have both said they cannot use them. No production vector artwork exists.
brand_identity.values: Reliability and restraint. Geometry over decoration, documentation over marketing. Say honestly what the artwork can and cannot do, including the founder's gradient.

assets_supplied.name: halcyon_master_mark.png (1400 x 1400)
assets_supplied.kind: The primary mark as exported from a generative image tool: an angular interlocking figure with a soft outer glow, filled with a blue to violet gradient, on transparency.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our main mark. This export is everything we have of it. It goes soft as soon as anybody scales it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. The figure's two supposedly matching arms were never drawn to match: the generator produced them freehand, so their widths and corner angles differ, which the soft edges of a 1400 pixel export hide completely and which becomes legible only once the shape is real geometry seen large. And the outer glow is part of the artwork rather than a background, so any preparation separating artwork from ground by lightness carries a fringe of it through as a ring of stray shapes.

assets_supplied.name: subbrand_marks/ (2 PNGs, 1024 x 1024 and 1600 x 1600)
assets_supplied.kind: The two sub-product marks, generated separately several months apart with different settings.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The two sub product marks. They were made at different times and they have never quite matched the main one."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. One sits on transparency and the other was flattened onto a plate whose white is a very light warm grey, so the preparation that isolates one correctly returns the substrate on the other and the failure looks like a plausible mask either way. And one of the two is built around an enclosed ring, so the one-call knockout route returns a solid opaque disc with the plate still inside it while reporting success.

assets_supplied.name: exhibitor_card_2025_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF for last year's exhibitor card, from a real page layout with embedded font subsets, one card per page, 89 x 51 mm.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What our printer ran last year. Nobody here has the working file. Keep the card."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two structural facts nothing announces. The name, role, product line, email and booking link came across as one continuous story rather than five addressable frames, and the mapping readout silently omits one of those runs, so every offset past it is short while the validator still reports the mapping valid and the prepare call still reports the placeholders created. And the card's code block converts to an ordinary graphic frame that accepts a per-record code mapping, validates it and reports it created, while no code is ever produced on any rendered page.

assets_supplied.name: team_roster.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The HR sheet export, one row per person: name, role, product line, email, booking link, photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This year's eleven. The product line column is which of the three things each person owns."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. The photo column keys on surname and two people share one, so two rows bind the same photograph while every filename resolves. And one row's product line names a fourth product announced internally that has no mark in the supplied artwork, so that card carries a field the mark set cannot answer.

assets_supplied.name: team_photos/ (11 self-submitted frames, 1200 to 4000 px)
assets_supplied.kind: Photographs the eleven people sent in themselves, taken on phones in offices, at home and outdoors, with no common direction.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everyone sent in whatever they had. They are all recognisable, which is mostly what matters."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. Two were shot against bright office windows, so the sitter's shoulder and the blown window share luminance and a subject knockout returns success while quietly eating the shoulder line. And one is a 1200 pixel copy pulled off a profile page rather than an original, so it binds and resolves like the rest and simply prints soft at card trim, where no route can put back detail the original export already discarded.

assets_supplied.name: halcyon_booth_code.png
assets_supplied.kind: A single scannable code image the company generated from its own booking system, pointing at the shared booth page.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The code for our booth page. We made this one ourselves."

assets_supplied.name: founder_notes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Half a page from the founder about what the mark is meant to mean and what she likes about it, with no hex values and no measurements.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What she was going for. Read it, then tell us what you think."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What is actually inside these three generative exports, legible only once they are real geometry. The master's two supposedly matching arms were drawn freehand and differ in width and corner angle, which a 1400 pixel soft-edged export hides completely; at trace, seen large, the mark is visibly lopsided. The outer glow belongs to the artwork rather than a background, so a preparation that separates by lightness carries a fringe through as a ring of stray shapes. And the two sub-brand marks, made months apart, come back with materially different stroke mass from each other and from the master even where every preparation succeeded. Nothing reports any of it: every selection returns a plausible mask, the tracer takes no options, and each mark inspected alone at thumbnail size looks finished.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is no parameter to reason about and no read-ahead: the tracer has no options, so the only way to learn what a preparation yields is to make it, trace it and look at it large. Nothing states it, since the brief says only that the exports are soft and that the sub marks have never felt like family, the client's complaint rather than a description of the geometry. And the response is not a re-run but a different preparation per mark, a decision about whether a construction fault in the client's own mark is correctable here or reportable, and usually a change to which mark carries which application.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-prepare each mark on a different route, a selection worded for the structural edge rather than the luminous field, or the colour-plate route instead of the binary route, then re-trace, re-strip the opaque path, re-clear the halo debris and re-place large and at tab size. Decide explicitly what to do about the asymmetry and the gradient, since neither can be redrawn here, and re-take the icon and favicon derivation, because a mark that only holds above a certain size needs different small artwork rather than a smaller copy.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A brand system shipped to a printer, a fabricator and an app store in which the company's primary mark is visibly lopsided at every size it is now sharp enough to show it, ringed by halo fragments, with two sub marks that still do not belong to it, delivered as the production-clean artwork the client paid for.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card exposes and what it will actually carry. The name, role, product line, email and booking link came across as one continuous story rather than five addressable frames, and the mapping readout omits one of those runs, so every offset computed past it is short while the validator reports the mapping valid, the prepare call reports the placeholders created successfully, and only some of the fields land. And the card's code block converts to an ordinary graphic frame that accepts a per-record code mapping, passes validation and is reported created, while no code is ever produced on any rendered page. The client asked in good faith for each card to point at that person's own link, because last year's card did.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Frame granularity is a property of a document made by a printer nobody has spoken to, and the code binding is documented and accepted by every tool in the chain right up to the render, so no ordering and no amount of care reaches either fact earlier. Nothing states it: the brief states the goal, that each card points at that person's own booking link, a client requirement rather than a description of what the tooling will do. And it is not a propagation re-run, because the mapping changes shape to offset arithmetic against an independently reconstructed story, and the per-person code must be re-planned into a different deliverable.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story from the IDML content runs, recompute every offset from that string, re-validate, re-prepare and re-verify by grepping the round-tripped IDML for every placeholder before any page is merged. Then take the code decision explicitly: bind the single booth code the client already supplied to every card and set each person's own link as live text, or ask the client for eleven exported code images so they bind through the per-row image column, and say in writing which was done and why.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A press run of eleven exhibitor cards on which the booking link is silently missing from every card and the code block is last year's flat placeholder pointing nowhere, handed to a printer six weeks before a conference, with every tool having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the licensed frame belongs with this set, a question that exists only once the two are adjacent. Stock search returns a 240 pixel thumbnail and true dimensions and says nothing about the light, so the frame's real colour temperature, contrast and grain arrive only with the full-resolution download, and the comparison it must survive is against eleven phone portraits just pulled to one house treatment. A frame that looked crisp and neutral as a thumbnail can land warm, soft and evidently lit by somebody else, and the failure is not that it is a bad photograph but that it reads as bought the moment it sits beside the team.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The judgement requires both halves to exist and the graded portrait set is the second half, so ordering cannot bring it forward. Care cannot dodge it either, because nothing in the search response describes the light and the thumbnail is too small to read it. Nothing states it: the brief never mentions a photograph at all, and the panel is the agent's own proposal. And it is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different frame, a materially harder grade, or a panel re-composed around type and the marks.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Lay the downloaded frame beside the graded portraits at panel size and judge it there rather than alone. Then either search again on the light rather than the subject and license a replacement, or push this frame with masked corrections until it sits with the set, or drop it and re-author the booth panel without a photograph, which changes the panel's composition, its type hierarchy and which mark variant carries it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A booth panel standing next to eleven cards at a developer conference in which the hero photograph is visibly lit by a different person on a different day in a different colour from every face beside it, in front of the exact audience the brief says reads fuss as sloppiness.

decision_gates: Whether three superficially similar generative exports are one problem or three, when one sits on transparency, one on an off-white plate and one encloses a ring.
Selection wording per mark: whether the prompt takes the artwork or the plate it was flattened onto.
Which polarity to hand a tracer that takes no options, and whether to trace the binary plate or the colour-accurate plate.
What honestly happens to the founder's gradient, and whether to say so or to quietly ship whatever the trace returned.
Whether a construction fault in the client's own mark is correctable inside this engagement, reportable, or both.
Whether to strip the opaque ground path and clear the halo debris, which nothing in the chain does and nothing warns about.
Isolation route per portrait, when a subject knockout is right against a plain wall and wrong against a blown window.

Whether to bind the client's own surname-keyed photo references or rebuild the image map against the agent's graded masters, and whether repointing a client's data silently is the same act as repointing it and saying so.

why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these assets into a frontier image model and it returns three nice logos. It fails all three gates. IDENTITY: the commission is that these three specific marks, which the founder made and the company has used for two years, must survive being rebuilt rather than be replaced; a regenerated mark is a different company's logo, and the printer, the fabricator and the app store listing all receive it. The eleven faces are eleven real colleagues standing at a booth, not eleven plausible portraits. SPEC: one card per person in roster order at 89 x 51 mm and 300 ppi with five named fields bound verbatim from their own roster, eleven separately named card files each containing the person their filename claims, artwork with real viewBoxes and no opaque ground paths, and no delivered file larger than its true source. A generated image satisfies none of that and cannot be checked against a roster. client_brief:
Six painted crest lockups prepared for an apparel capsule

Evergreen Provisions needs the six painted crest lockups prepared for its small garment capsule. The brush character matters, but the artwork must hold at the actual garment width rather than only in a large presentation.

Alongside that, please bring the panel and blank-garment photographs into one believable set. We need to see the real garment colours, not a colour grade that makes unrelated blanks appear identical.

Recovery and reductions
Six crests recovered from photographs of hand painted panels as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, compound lockups complete rather than missing their centre element, and each holding its hairlines and open counters at the width the schedule says it prints, on the garment colour it prints on. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Photographic presentation
Six panel captures brought to one capsule palette across two shooting visits, and five garment blanks corrected to their honest colours so ink contrast decisions made against them can be trusted, plus one licensed camera-scale counter surface frame graded into the same world. Per frame parameter log with one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours.

Please work within $2,500-$6,000 fixed and the 2 to 4 weeks target. Allow for one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

The pack contains evergreen_crest_panels/ (6 frames, roughly 4200 x 4200); evergreen_garment_blanks/ (5 frames); evergreen_spec_card_2024.pdf; evergreen_plate_schedule.csv; evergreen_ink_book.txt.

Please inspect counters and fine material details at the intended small use. The handover should make it clear which conclusions are supported by the artwork and which production tolerances still belong with the supplier.

Alongside the finished work, we need a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note. Keep a clear record of the supplied files used, retained for reference, superseded and rejected. Approved source information remains authoritative. Record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and quality limits, and do not use an undeclared replacement or invented fact to conceal a source problem. Include inspectable paths and small-size proofs; unverified fabrication tolerances remain subject to supplier review.

source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork apparel capsule post quoted in this line's ledger grounding_note, from a vertically integrated cannabis retailer asking for 'a production-ready apparel design system for a branded retail capsule' that 'hands cleanly to manufacturers and decorators (vectors, tech packs)', in an 'elevated streetwear' direction, on palette with no rework. The real post names no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional dispensary Evergreen Provisions (a generic dictionary pairing, no trademark collision), and the post's stated purple and black palette is dropped along with its from scratch garment art and embroidery digitising, which the ledger's own triage concedes are not connector work. What survives is the half that client genuinely needed and could not get: a decorator will not quote from a photograph, so the commission is recovery of the artwork that already exists into per ink plate art, plus the spec the shop floor actually works from. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that the honest fuller commission rather than a thin one, because an ink level trace off photographed painted collateral recovers real artwork, HTML authoring produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes for the separation sheets and the teaser set, and the InDesign convert and merge chain turns the decorator's own last season spec card PDF into a live per design run. Verdict STRENGTHEN honoured: the concept and the six item collateral set are kept intact and the depth is raised from what sat on one vector surface to five honestly counted ones.

price_band_and_audience: Craft dispensary lifestyle capsule at 32 dollars a tee and 70 dollars a hoodie, buyer 25 to 45, bought at the counter on the strength of the wall panels they already photograph. The band is load bearing. At this price the painted origin is the product, so the plates have to retain brush edge, dry brush breakup and a halftoned paint field, and the palette stays earthy and limited to the inks the decorator already keeps on his shelf. Flatten those crests into clean geometric marks with a mass retail two ink treatment and the capsule reads as gas station merch, which will not hold 70 dollars. Push the other way into a foiled, sparse, monogrammed designer drop look and it misprices a counter sold 32 dollar tee and stops looking like the panels on the wall, which is the only reason the customer walked over. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every plate separates correctly. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: A vertically integrated cannabis retailer running two dispensary storefronts, launching a short-run counter-sold apparel capsule.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019, Bend, Oregon. Two owned dispensary shops, owner-run, with a small counter-retail apparel line.
brand_identity.about: Evergreen Provisions runs two dispensary shops in Bend, built around six house strain families. Two years ago the owners paid a local sign painter to hand-paint a crest panel for each family onto the shop walls. Customers photograph them constantly and ask where they can buy them, and the first apparel capsule exists to answer that question without losing the hand that made the panels.
brand_identity.audience: Craft-minded dispensary customers aged 25 to 45 who buy at the counter on the strength of the wall panels they already photograph. People who pay for the painted origin, not for a logo.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Tees at 32 dollars, hoodies at 70 dollars, short-run and counter-sold. Elevated streetwear priced above gas-station merch and below a designer drop. The painted texture is the product, so the value sits in the brush surviving, not in gloss or foil.
brand_identity.typography: Display in a painted or brushed-character face that echoes the sign painter's hand, kept legible. Support and spec type in a plain workhorse sans so the plates and sheets read cleanly. Type never competes with the painted crest.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, plain-spoken, shop-floor honest. No luxury posturing and no carnival hype. Example line: "These are hand painted panels and that is the entire reason anyone wants them. Keep the brush in it, and tell us plainly what came back and what did not."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The six crest panels were hand-painted by a local sign painter who has since moved to Montana and left no sketches or files. The only surviving artwork is a set of bench photographs of the finished panels, shot over two visits under mixed light. There is no vector art and no separation art, which is exactly why the screen printer cannot quote a run.
brand_identity.values: Craft and honesty. Keep the painted hand, hold the palette to the inks the decorator already stocks, and say plainly what the paintings can and cannot give a screen.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether these particular traces still hold at the width they actually print, on the garment colour they actually print on. The paintings carry dry brush hairlines and small painted caps whose counters are barely open in the paint itself, and the tracer takes no options at all, so the only lever is the raster prep upstream. At canvas scale every trace looks clean and complete. The sleeve hit prints at a fraction of the chest widths, and whether its counters close and its hairlines drop out at that size, against olive or against black rather than against white, is a property of that one painting meeting that one reproduction size and is not reported by anything.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the answer does not exist until the plate has been traced and laid down at its true width on the corrected garment ground, and there is no tracer parameter that would have prevented it. Nothing in the brief or the schedule states it: the schedule gives print widths because a decorator needs print widths, not as a warning about counters. It is not a propagation re run either, because the response is a different route for that design, either rebuilding the plate as a masked and flattened solid before tracing so the stroke carries weight, or accepting a coarser reduction for that placement and saying so.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster prep for the affected designs, rebuild those plates through a mask and flatten route rather than tracing the painterly stroke directly, re trace, redo the vector hygiene, and re judge every affected design at its stated width on its stated ground before any of it reaches a sheet.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A capsule where the sleeve design prints as a plugged blob and the small painted caps close up on press, discovered by the decorator after screens are burned, on a capsule whose entire premise is that the brush survived.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the construct the separation sheets are built on. A separation sheet shows each ink as its own layer sitting over the ones beneath it so the decorator can read the overlap and the trap. Authored the natural way that is a blended or partially transparent stack, and the importer discards the blend outright and returns a plain opaque shape, at full success and with no warning of any kind. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so every sheet after the first can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step of the authoring, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. Nothing states it: the brief asks for one piece of art per ink and says nothing about how a sheet is drawn. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different construction, either separating the plates spatially into registered panels with a printed offset key, or baking the overlap into a raster upstream so the trap is part of the picture rather than of the layout.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the separation roots around whichever construction survives, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every sheet from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Separation sheets handed to a decorator on which the top plate covers the ones beneath it, so every design appears to be a one ink job, with the export having reported success throughout.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the decorator's spec card actually is once converted, as opposed to what its printed face suggests. Its four blocks read as separate on paper, but the conversion decides the frame granularity and can collapse a continuous flow into a single frame, so there may be no separate name frame and ink frame to map fields to at all. Compounding it, the readout the mapping tool returns omits a run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed, every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length, and the validator returns valid with no warnings on offsets that are wrong.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is no ordering that avoids it and no parameter that controls it, because the granularity is a property of how that PDF was made and the readout's omission is invisible in the readout. Nothing states it: the client says only that the printer wants the same card again. It is not a propagation re run, because the correct response is a different mapping strategy computed from a different source of truth, the reconstructed story text from the round tripped document rather than the tool's own readout, plus a decision about which fields the exposed frames can carry at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Recompute every offset from the reconstructed story text, re prepare the template, verify by a second round trip that each field placeholder is genuinely present rather than trusting the success message, re merge, and where two blocks collapsed into one frame decide which fields move into the note instead.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A spec card run that reports success, renders the right number of pages, and reaches the decorator's floor with the ink list and the plate order silently missing from every card.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the photographs into a frontier image model and it returns pretty crests. IDENTITY: these are one named sign painter's six actual panels, hanging on the wall of two shops, that customers already photograph. A regenerated crest is a different painting, and the entire commercial premise of the capsule is that the customer recognises the thing on the wall. SPEC: a decorator burns screens off one piece of art per ink, with correct polarity, a real viewBox, no ground rectangle and open counters at a stated print width on a stated garment colour, none of which a generated image is or can be checked for, and a press PDF whose page count equals the reconciled design count is a hard count rather than a picture. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did this trace keep its hairlines at sleeve width on black, did the plate under the top one survive the import, did the field the tool said it wrote actually land in the template.

client_brief:
Recover the market's apron mark and prepare our site photographs

Hello from Cedar Commons. We help run the farmers' market, and the apron print is the version of our mark people recognise. Could you help us get it into a form we can place cleanly, without a box around it?

We also have four phone photographs of the site. Please make them feel like one May morning, keeping the market recognisable. Tell us which can genuinely support the intended sign use.

The two things we need:

The market's compound lockup recovered from a photograph of a screen print on coarse canvas as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: bough, arched wordmark and ring rule all present, a real viewBox, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, and the ring's interior genuinely open rather than a filled disc. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Four phone frames of the site levelled and brought to one May morning look with one white point and one black point, plus one licensed camera-scale outdoor frame graded into the same world so it does not read as bought. Per frame parameter log with one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours, and a plain statement of which frame can carry a sign and which cannot.

We can give you cedar_commons_apron.jpg; cedar_commons_site/ (4 frames, phone camera); cedar_commons_sign_blank.jpg; cedar_commons_plate_card.pdf; cedar_commons_signage_list.txt.

Also in the archive, for background only: cedar_commons_stalls.csv. These do not add deliverables to this commission.

The bough, arch, wordmark and ring should remain a complete mark, with the interior genuinely open. Please include the small-size and light/dark proofs, and be clear about anything a production supplier still needs to confirm.

$2,500-$6,000 fixed; 2 to 4 weeks. Review structure: One direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

Please deliver a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note. Account for every supplied file and identify anything used only as reference, superseded or rejected. Stay with approved facts and copy. Do not silently replace weak assets; use only the stated stock or concept allowances, and record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and material compromises. Include inspectable paths and small-size proofs; unverified fabrication tolerances remain subject to supplier review.

price_band_and_audience: A free public community market funded entirely by 25 to 60 dollar daily stall fees, audience the neighbourhood families and weekend walkers who come on foot or park in the wrong lot. The band is load bearing and it points the opposite way from a retail brief. At this budget the whole set has to be a small number of flat inks on white coroplast and vinyl, with type heavy enough to be read from a moving car and a mark reduced to a cut that survives at six inches and at eight feet. brand_identity.sector: A volunteer-run weekend farmers market in a municipal park, free to the public, funded by daily stall fees.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, in a park in Burlington, Vermont. Volunteer-run, 36 to 44 stalls, open weekends May through October.
brand_identity.about: Cedar Commons is a neighbourhood farmers market that runs on weekends in a Burlington park, free to walk into and funded entirely by the vendors who pay a daily stall fee. It has outgrown its chalkboards and its bedsheet banner. The signage exists to get families to the right lot, past the entrance and to the stall they are looking for, printed cheaply and well at a local sign shop.
brand_identity.audience: Neighbourhood families and weekend walkers who arrive on foot or park in the wrong lot, plus the vendors and volunteers who run the morning. Read from a moving car and from across a field.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A free public market funded by 25 to 60 dollar daily stall fees, often part-donated. Everything prints on coroplast and vinyl at a local sign shop. Flat inks and heavy type, never a refined tint palette that would be unreadable outdoors and would make a free market look like it is charging.
brand_identity.typography: Display in a friendly high-contrast slab or bold grotesque, weighted to be read from a car. Wayfinding and schedule copy in a plain heavy sans with one clear instruction per sign. Real weight matters more than refinement.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, plain and welcoming, like a volunteer at the gate. Example line: "Cheerful, legible from a distance, few colours, and it lives outdoors in the rain. Not precious. Tell us what our mark can and cannot do."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The market mark was drawn nine years ago by a volunteer's cousin, who is not reachable, and screen-printed onto aprons and tote bags. No file of any kind was ever kept. The best surviving copy is a photograph of one apron folded on a picnic table. There is no vector art, so the mark has to be recovered from that photograph rather than redrawn.
brand_identity.values: Community and thrift. Recover the real mark rather than replace it, keep the set to a few flat inks that print cheaply, and tell the committee what the mark can and cannot do before they pay for plates.

assets_supplied.name: cedar_commons_apron.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of a volunteer's canvas apron with the market mark screen printed on it, folded on a picnic table in daylight.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The best copy of our mark that still exists anywhere."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark is a compound lockup, a cedar bough over an arched wordmark inside a ring rule, so a single compound selection returns the ring and the arch while silently dropping the bough, and a background removal on the ring hands back a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched. The apron is coarse canvas, so the printed ink is broken at stroke level, and the fold runs through the lower third of the ring.

assets_supplied.name: cedar_commons_site/ (4 frames, phone camera)
assets_supplied.kind: Phone photographs of the market site taken one May morning: the park entrance and its fence, the gravel parking approach, the vendor row, and the info tent corner.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our chair took these one morning in May so you can see where things go."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The parking approach frame was shot into the light with the sky fully clipped behind the exact fence line where the sign has to stand, so a highlight recovery on that region returns success with nothing moved. Two of the four are off level, and the vendor row frame, the only one that includes the fence, has a delivery van parked across the position the mockup wants.

assets_supplied.name: cedar_commons_sign_blank.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of a blank white coroplast yard sign on its wire stake, pushed into the gravel by the parking approach, shot for scale.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "A blank sign on a stake so you can see how big they actually are."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The sign's lower edge and its wire stake sit at almost the same value as the wet gravel behind them, so a one call knockout returns a cutout that reads clean and complete at preview scale and is bitten along the stake and the bottom rail at full size. The blank also leans a few degrees in the gravel.

assets_supplied.name: cedar_commons_plate_card.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The sign shop's six by six inch stall plate artwork from two seasons ago, supplied as the press PDF they reprint from: a stall number block and a vendor name line.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the parking approach frame can carry a sign at all. The sign has to stand against the fence line, and that frame was shot into the light, so the question is whether there is any information left in the sky behind that fence. A highlight recovery on that region returns success and the readout is that nothing moves: the pixels come back identical because the channel is already fully clipped, and no tool in the connector measures or reports it. Looking at the frame beforehand shows a white sky, which is exactly what a recoverable sky and an unrecoverable one both look like.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is no ordering that avoids it, because the answer exists only after the operation has been run and the result compared, and there is no parameter that would have made a clipped channel recoverable. Nothing states it: the client says only that the chair took the photographs one morning in May. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is to change which frame carries the mockup, which changes the composition, or to license and grade an outdoor frame into the same morning, which changes the source.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re plan which frame the staked mockup stands on given that the frame with the fence has a van across the sign position, either recomposing the mockup onto a different site frame or licensing a camera scale outdoor ground and grading it into the same May morning as the rest of the set, then re grading the whole site family so the substituted frame does not read as bought.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A mockup board handed to a committee showing a sign standing against a blank white void where their park's tree line should be, on the one deliverable that exists specifically because half the committee cannot read a plan.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the staked blank can actually be cut off the gravel. The sign's lower edge and its wire stake sit in the same value range as the wet gravel behind them, which is where a knockout has the least to work with, and the tool reports success either way. The returned cutout reads clean and complete at preview scale. Whether the bite has taken the stake, the bottom rail, both or neither on this photograph is a property of this photograph and only appears when the cutout is laid on the site ground at the scale the mockup actually uses.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because subject detection is given no contrast to find at that boundary and reports no confidence for it. Nothing states it: the client supplied the blank purely so the committee could see how big a yard sign is. It is not a propagation re run, because the correct response is a different chain, selecting the gravel field by its own material properties, inverting it and filling, rather than running the one call knockout again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the one call route for that frame, select the gravel as a material by its own visual properties, invert, fill and re cut, then re judge the cutout on the site ground at mockup scale, or recompose the mockup so the compromised boundary sits outside the frame, which changes what the board shows.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A mockup in which the market's new sign appears to float above the gravel with its stake half eaten, presented as the picture the committee approves the whole season's spend from.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What this roster does inside this plate card's existing name frame. The frame is a fixed measure that does not spill: a name longer than the frame does not overflow, wrap or overset, it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, and the merge reports success with a page count that matches the roster exactly. Which vendors this bites, and where in the name the cut lands, is a joint property of the frame's real bounds, the applied face and each individual record, and none of that is visible in any response. The only channel is rendering the run and reading every page.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the behaviour of that frame under that record cannot be known until the record is in the frame, and there is no fitting parameter to set. Nothing states it: the roster is just the roster and the client says the sign shop reprints from this card as is. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a decision about the template and the data, re mapping the name into a frame whose real bounds can hold it, restructuring the field across two lines, or agreeing an abbreviation rule with the committee, each of which changes what is merged rather than merging the same thing again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify every affected record by reading the rendered pages, decide between re mapping the field into a differently bounded frame, restructuring the name field, or agreeing an abbreviation rule, re prepare or re bind accordingly, re merge, re render and read every page again before any plate count is called delivered.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Forty four plates printed on coroplast at a volunteer market's entire signage budget, with a handful of vendors' names cut off mid word at trim, discovered on the Saturday morning they go into the ground.

decision_gates: Selection prompt wording on the apron: naming the garment takes the apron, naming the print's own visual properties takes the ink, a compound prompt loses the bough, and background removal on the ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
How to handle the coarse canvas weave in the trace, given that it reads as texture at banner size and as noise at plate size, and therefore how many cuts of the mark the set actually needs.
Which site frame can carry the staked mockup, given that the one with the fence has a van across the sign position.
Whether to license an outdoor ground and grade it into the site world, or to recompose the mockup onto a frame that already works.
Knockout route on the staked blank: the one call route versus selecting the gravel as a material by its own properties, inverting and filling.
What scale to author the banner at, and how to state that scale so a sign shop outputs the right finished size rather than the canvas size.

The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged on legibility from a moving car on white coroplast, plus the real numeric weight per family, where the wrong weight is the whole failure.
What the plate card's exposed frames can actually carry, and whether a long vendor name is solved in the template, in the data, or by an abbreviation rule agreed with the committee.

client_brief:
One streetwear graphic family adapted properly for four manufacturing methods

Static Union needs production-minded artwork adaptation for small goods. The same detailed drawing will not work unchanged as embroidery, enamel, a sticker and a woven label. We are looking for someone who understands those differences and can make deliberate reductions.

The production variants:

Per graphic, three genuinely different pieces of art rather than one drawing at three sizes: an embroidery reduction within the stated thread count and minimum stroke that stays readable at patch size on dark twill, separated metal line and enamel fill plates whose wells close and whose bridges meet the pin maker's minimum, and full detail sticker face art with a true outward kiss cut line carrying the enclosed windows the converter asked for, plus the woven label lockup. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

The evidence we need with them:

An inspectable proof of Static Union manufacture art, three media at every claimed reproduction size and on light/dark grounds, with open-path, closure, transparency, contour, and unsupported-feature findings stated plainly.

Please retain the family resemblance while respecting thread limits, metal bridges, closed fill wells and the sticker's intended negative spaces. Simplification is expected where necessary, but it needs to be visible and explained, not hidden inside a flattened preview.

Materials and supplier references: static_union_marks/ (four graphics, 2,000 to 3,600px); su_maker_limits.txt; su_copy.txt.

Also in the archive, for background only: su_woven_label_photo.jpg; su_hangtag_2025.pdf; su_smallgoods.csv. These do not add deliverables to this commission.

A file extension is not approval for manufacture. Identify unsupported tolerances and let the supplier review those points before anyone treats the artwork as production-cleared.

Handover: a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note. Include an inventory showing how every supplied file was used or why it was set aside. Keep factual content tied to the approved inputs. Any missing coverage, substituted asset, reconciliation or quality compromise must be declared; a weak source is not permission to invent or silently replace it. Include inspectable paths and small-size proofs; unverified fabrication tolerances remain subject to supplier review.

The commission is budgeted at $1,200-$3,200 fixed. We have allowed 7 to 15 business days, including one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

The band is load-bearing in a specific way: the price ladder is a fidelity ladder. The 4 dollar sticker keeps the full drawing because vinyl costs nothing to hold detail. The 18 dollar patch is deliberately reduced to bold thread blocks because thread cannot hold the drawing and because a patch that looks like a printed sticker looks cheap on a garment.
