emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the tracer actually returns from a graphic that looks flat and is not. Two of the four exports came out of screen print separations and carry a fine halftone dot through their solid areas plus a soft gradient across one element. At every size a person views them at, including full screen, they are indistinguishable from the genuinely flat pair, and the colour flattening done in the raster preparation addresses the regions that can be seen and leaves the dot untouched because there is nothing visible to address. The trace of those two comes back as scores of near identical fills instead of the handful the patch maker permits, and it renders identically to the eye, so the file looks correct and the SVG is a thread specification no factory will accept. The tracer reports success, takes no options at all, and offers no readout of what it produced. There is no parameter that could have been set correctly, and which of the four graphics carries the hidden texture cannot be established before tracing them.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot pre empt it. A careful agent flattens the visible colour regions, gets the polarity right and strips the ground path, and still gets an exploded trace on exactly the two files whose defect is invisible. (b) Nothing states it. The maker limits file states the thread count as a hard bar, which is the client passing on the factory's own constraint exactly as he would to a designer, and the brief says the July attempt was refused, which is the symptom that caused the hire. Neither says which graphics are separations, that a hidden dot exists, or that the trace will multiply it. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is to go back into the raster with masked fills that consolidate the affected areas into true solids, which is a different operation on a different principle from the reduction already done, and it changes both the patch plate and the pin's enamel field boundaries.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster preparation and consolidate the affected areas into genuine solids with masked fills rather than trying to simplify the traced result, re trace, and re check the fill count rather than assuming the second attempt took. Then re derive the pin's enamel fields, since their boundaries came from the same prepared plate, and correct the colour list on the maker spec sheet, which was written from the first trace.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The patch factory refuses the art a second time on the same grounds, after the label paid someone specifically to stop that happening, and the pin maker quotes an enamel count that does not exist.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the reduction that satisfies the maker's limits is the same reduction that survives on the maker's ground. The plates are convincing at canvas size on white, which is the only size and ground anyone looks at them at by default. At two and a half inches on dark twill the badge's arc lettering closes its counters and the inner rule merges into the ring, so the mark reads as a filled disc with a smudge in it, and at one inch on metal the bolt's thinnest strokes fall below the metal line minimum in places the eye did not flag at full size. Both plates pass a colour count check and both look right in every file the client would be shown. Nothing measures this, no operation reports it, and the two failures are different in kind: one is legibility at size, one is a manufacturing minimum, and neither is visible until the art is placed at its delivered size on the ground it is delivered onto.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The plates have to exist before they can be placed, there is no measurement available, and no amount of care at the reduction stage substitutes for looking at the result at real size, because the reduction that meets the thread count and the reduction that stays readable in thread are not the same reduction and only the second one can be seen. (b) Nothing states it. The maker limits file gives the sizes, the grounds and the minimums, which is the constraint. The brief says the patch factory called the art not patch art, which is the client repeating a rejection he does not understand. Neither says which element closes, at which size, on which ground. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a design decision about which detail is sacrificed to keep the mark readable at patch size, or about moving a graphic to a different item in the pack, both of which change the allocation made at triage and change what the woven label lockup can carry.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Redraw the reduction so the elements that close are opened or dropped rather than shrunk, which means going back to the raster preparation and in some cases back to the graphic to item allocation, then re place at true size on the true ground rather than assuming the heavier version worked. Check the plates that were not flagged at the same real size, since the reason to look was found on one and the others have not been established as clean. If a graphic will not hold as a patch at all, say which item it becomes instead and re author the spec sheet around it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The label ships a patch on which its own badge is an unreadable filled disc and a pin whose thinnest strokes cannot be struck, discovers it when the sample arrives from the factory, and misses the drop date it commissioned this work to hit.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's tag actually is as a document, and what survives the merge onto twelve real records. The printed page shows the item name, colourway, price and code as visually separate blocks, but the tag face was set as one continuous flow, so what the conversion exposes bears no relation to what the page suggests, and the convenient readout of that flow omits one run while keeping its line break, leaving a string that still looks well formed and every position past the omission short by the exact length of the omitted run. A mapping built on those positions validates cleanly and the template preparation reports success while some fields never land at all. Separately, on the records whose colourway name is longest, the text simply stops at the frame edge rather than overflowing anywhere a person would notice, so a tag looks correctly set and ends mid field. None of this appears in any response. It appears on the merged pages, and only on some of them.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. Frame granularity from a converted PDF is not under the agent's control and cannot be predicted from the printed page, and the truncation is a property of one field's length against one frame's width on specific records, which does not exist until those records are merged. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the printer has last season's tag and asks for one tag per item with nothing retyped, which is a client describing what he has. No asset note says the tag is one flow, that a run is omitted, or which records run long. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is to reconstruct the frame's true text from the document structure and recompute every position against it, which is a different method from the one the tooling steers toward, plus a copy decision about the records that will not fit, which is the client's business rather than a re export.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping from the reconstructed story text rather than the readout, re prepare the template, and confirm the placeholders are present by inspecting the document again rather than trusting the success message. Re merge and read all twelve pages, not the ones that failed before, since a corrected offset can move a different field. For the records that still end early, shorten the copy with the client's own wording from the supplied file and record which records changed.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twelve hang tags go to the printer with fields missing on some records and colourway names cut off mid word on others, the run is printed, and the label pays for it twice because everything the tooling said along the way said the job had succeeded.

decision_gates: Which graphic becomes which item, given that the most detailed drawing fails hardest as thread and the simplest is wasted on vinyl.
How much detail each medium loses, and where a reduction stops being a reduction and becomes a different mark.
How to word a selection so it returns the graphic rather than the surface the graphic is printed on.
Whether to rebuild the compound badge per element or accept a single mask that looks like a badge.
How much of the preparation happens in the raster, given that the tracing step offers no controls of any kind.
Whether a plate that meets the stated limits but closes up at delivered size is fixed by opening the drawing or by moving the graphic to another item.
Where the enamel bridges go, since a bridge added for manufacture is a change to the drawing.
Whether the tag's printed blocks correspond to anything addressable in the converted document, and what to build the mapping from if they do not.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of patches. IDENTITY is the commission: these are four specific graphics a label has been putting on garments for two years, one of which now exists only as a photograph of a woven label, and a redrawn eagle or a regenerated badge is a different label's mark on the same body of customers. SPEC is manufacturing: three factories have written limits on thread count, minimum stroke, metal line width, enamel bridging and enclosed window size, and the deliverable is art that satisfies them, in separated plates, at stated physical sizes on stated grounds. A generated image satisfies none of it and cannot be checked against it, which is precisely how the label got refused in July. EDITABILITY runs through two deliverables: a merge template bound to a spreadsheet so twelve tags run without retyping, and one document with live text the founder edits as items get pulled. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this reduction still read in thread at two and a half inches, does this trace carry a colour count a factory will quote, does this converted tag expose anything the fields can attach to. None of that is a generation problem, and the note explaining which graphic will be refused again is advice a render cannot give.

client_brief:
Recover our jewellery wordmark from three disagreeing references

Maison Serault has three captures of the existing wordmark and monogram. They disagree in apparent colour and weight. We need a careful reconstruction of the identity, not an average of three photographs.

Please distinguish actual letterforms from lighting, surface and reproduction effects. Explain which source supports the chosen brand colour and why the others are less trustworthy. We understand that this is not a physical colour proof.

Both house marks recovered as the house's own letterforms from captures that disagree, delivered as placeable, scalable vector geometry with a real viewBox and no opaque full canvas ground path, with every counter present as a genuine hole and no stroke thickened or thinned by the capture it came from. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

The three captures, taken years apart under three different lights, brought to one neutral so the house colour can be stated and defended, with a per capture parameter log and a written statement of which capture the colour was taken from and why the other two were not trusted. This is the deliverable the client asked for by name when she said she needs to be told what her colour is and to hear why, and it is the reference every foil and ink specification downstream is written against.

Source pack: serault_wordmark_export_2019.png; serault_wall_sign.jpg; serault_card_monogram.jpg; serault_supplier_specs.txt; serault_copy.txt.

Also in the archive, for background only: serault_enclosure_card_press.pdf; serault_collection.csv. These do not add deliverables to this commission.

The final shapes should preserve the intended weight and open counters at a small size. The image corrections should make the evidence easier to compare, without pretending that a neutralised photograph proves an exact ink or foil specification.

Please deliver the light/dark and reduced-size checks with the vectors, not only the most flattering large rendering.

Budget: $2,500-$6,000 fixed. Target: 2 to 4 weeks. Reviews: One direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

The final package should contain a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note, with every source file accounted for, including references and rejected or superseded material. Use the approved information without inventing missing facts. Only the stated stock or concept exceptions permit substitution; document every omission, replacement, reconciliation and material quality compromise. Include inspectable paths and small-size proofs; unverified fabrication tolerances remain subject to supplier review.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Ledger anchor for VECTOR-13 (Freelancer.com). The grounding note records a real posted logo production brief whose client wanted a mark that "feels unmistakably modern... bright, energetic colours paired with clean, abstract shapes", that looks "just as sharp on a website header as it does on packaging", delivered as "full-colour and single-colour versions, vector source files (AI or SVG), and high-resolution exports, along with a simple production note." The note states the brief was IP laundered to a fictional brand throughout, with no real person, brand, organisation or trademark appearing anywhere, and that it was reshaped to the connector's real capabilities. The house here is Maison Serault, the owner is Camille Roussel, and nothing real is referenced. The STRENGTHEN verdict keeps the concept and the collateral set exactly: a recovered wordmark master, a recovered monogram master, single path foil and engrave outlines of each, a reversed variant for dark stock, a packaging application sheet as an editable document, and a foil on dark presentation. What the rebuild adds is depth rather than scope. The posted brief's two hard sentences, sharp on a header and on packaging, and a simple production note, are precisely where this commission is difficult, because the packaging is a 10mm ribbon and a foil block on dark stock, and the production note is a professional statement of where the client's own mark does not hold.

price_band_and_audience: Fine jewelry, pieces from 600 to 4,000 dollars, buyers roughly 30 to 55 buying as a gift or for themselves, plus a small number of stockists. The band is load-bearing on the mark itself and on every canvas it appears on. At this tier the refinement is hairline and high contrast, the mark sits in a great deal of negative space, and the packaging is quiet: a small foil block on a large dark field is the whole design. A mass market jewelry house would want the opposite, a bolder mark with thicker strokes and more of it, and shipping that here would look like a different, cheaper business even if every file were technically correct. The same discipline runs through the application sheet, which is a supplier document and should read as a specification rather than as marketing, and through the presentation canvas, where restraint is the point. There is a second, harder consequence of the band: hairline refinement is exactly what a 10mm ribbon and a foil block cannot always hold, so the band creates the commission's central tension rather than merely decorating it. The ledger records the base concept at 700 to 1,500 dollars; this fuller commission, with the supplier artwork and the editable sheet, runs 1,600 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

assets_supplied.name: serault_wordmark_export_2019.png
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The flat export the designer sent in 2019. It is the only file version of the wordmark that exists and he never sent the working files." A 2,600px PNG of the wordmark on a pale ground, with a warm cast over the whole image.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Its lightest brand tone sits flat at the top of the file's range, so the obvious attempt to bring that tone back returns an image in which nothing at all moves, reported as success, and a flat lightest tone is exactly what a correct flat vector export is supposed to look like. assets_supplied.name: serault_wall_sign.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our wordmark on the boutique wall, brushed brass letters on plaster, taken on a phone under our shop lighting." A 4,200px frame, shot slightly from below.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Under this lighting each brass letter sits at close to the same value as its own cast shadow on the plaster, so a selection returns letter and shadow as one shape and a trace made from it thickens every stroke by a consistent amount, which reads perfectly well as the wordmark until it is set beside the export. Nothing in the selection or the trace reports that the shape includes a shadow.

assets_supplied.name: serault_card_monogram.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: image
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One of our old cards, with the monogram foil blocked on it, photographed by my sister in daylight by a window." A 3,900px frame of a cream card on a linen cloth.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Foil is a mirror, so the monogram's colour in this photograph is whatever the foil reflected from the room rather than any house colour, while the card ground carries the truest neutral of the three captures. The interlocked letterforms share enclosed counters that any route treating the monogram as one object fills in, returning a solid shape that reports success.

assets_supplied.kind: document
assets_supplied.visible_description: The box supplier's and the engraver's stated requirements in their own words: foil spread allowance, minimum stroke for foil on the dark stock, ribbon width at 10mm and the wordmark's used width along it, the engraver's single closed outline requirement and his minimum cut width, the box face and card dimensions, and the clear space the supplier wants around the mark.

assets_supplied.kind: document
assets_supplied.visible_description: The card printer's existing flat press file for the enclosure card that goes in the box with each piece: the monogram foil blocked at the head, then the piece name, a reference and metal line, a price and the house care line, with a small square window for a photograph of the piece. "The card our old printer already runs. This is his file, set by hand for one piece."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three things the printed card does not show. The piece name, the reference and metal line and the price read as three separate blocks but are set as one continuous text story in a single frame, so a field is reached by its position in that story rather than as its own object, while the care line is a second short story of its own. The monogram at the head is the printer's own crude redrawn tracing held as a group of vector paths, not a picture frame and not the recovered master, so it must be replaced rather than reused; the one genuine picture frame on the card is the small piece window, and naming the monogram as the place to bind a picture binds nothing. And the sample carries a piece name, an old reference and a price baked into its own text from the card it was set for, none of which match the current list, so the template's own words have to be replaced rather than trusted. The media box equals the trim with no bleed box present, so nothing derived from it can be delivered press ready with bleed.

assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The list is not a clean run of cards. Two pieces share a name across two metals, so a file named per piece by name collides and silently overwrites, and the key has to carry the reference. One piece is marked archived and should get no card, so the row count is not the card count. Several picture cells are simply blank because those pieces were never photographed, which no header reveals and the merge will not complain about, and pieces offered in two metals reuse one photograph across both rows. Prices are written inconsistently across rows, some with a currency mark and a thousands comma, some as a bare number, some with cents and some without.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which capture is actually allowed to be the colour authority. The 2019 export is the obvious candidate because its edges are by far the cleanest and because it is the only file version of the mark, and the natural move is to correct its cast and take the house colour from it. What only running the recovery reveals is that on this file the attempt does nothing at all: the lightest brand tone already sits flat at the top of the file's range, the returned image is indistinguishable from the input, and the operation reports success with no readout of any kind that says the tone did not move. A flat lightest tone is also exactly what a correct flat vector export ought to look like, so nothing about viewing the file suggests anything is wrong. The consequence is structural rather than cosmetic: the truest colour has to come from one of the photographs, which are the softer sources, while the cleanest geometry stays in the export, so colour and geometry are separated across two files and the client's stated assumption about her own master file is wrong.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot pre empt it. Whether a tone can be recovered is a property of the file's own range, there is no measurement available anywhere in the connector, and the only signal is the visible difference between input and output, which is nil. An agent that corrects the cast carefully and reads the result at normal viewing size sees a file that looks entirely reasonable. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the three captures disagree about the house colour and asks to be told which is right and why, which is a client describing her problem and asking for the judgement she is paying for. No asset note, deliverable or earlier step says the export is unrecoverable or that the answer lies in a photograph. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is to change which file is the authority for colour, re correct the other two toward it instead of toward the export, and then carry a colour from one capture onto a mark whose geometry comes from another, which is a different method rather than the same operation on changed input.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re establish the neutral from the capture that actually holds it, re correct the other two toward that reference rather than toward the export, and re examine the wordmark plate, since it was extracted from a file that is now the geometry source only and its colour cannot be trusted for any downstream spec. Then write the reason down, because the client asked for the justification as an explicit deliverable and the reason is now specific rather than general.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The house adopts a wrong colour, taken from the one capture that could not be corrected, and it goes onto boxes, ribbon, cards and clasp plates for a decade because everything in the recovery reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the refined mark survives the ribbon and the dark stock. Both marks are entirely convincing at canvas size on white. At the wordmark's used width along a 10mm ribbon the high contrast letterforms lose their hairlines, and reversed on the box's dark stock with the supplier's stated foil spread the counters in the monogram's interlocked letterforms close into solid, so what the client would receive is a foil block with an unreadable smudge in the middle of it and a ribbon carrying a broken line of type. Both artefacts pass every structural check: single closed path, counters present as holes, viewBox correct, minimum stroke met as drawn. The failure is what the physical process does to a drawing that is correct on screen, and nothing in any response measures or reports it. The tracing step takes no options, so the only levers are the raster preparation and the drawing itself, and which lever is needed cannot be chosen until the failure has been seen at real size on the real ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The marks have to exist before they can be placed, no measurement is available, and meeting a stated minimum stroke as drawn does not establish that the mark reads once foil spreads into dark stock at that size. An agent that refines carefully and respects every stated minimum still gets closed counters, because the variable is the house's own high contrast letterforms at 7mm, not the care taken. (b) Nothing states it. The supplier file gives the ribbon width, the used width, the foil spread allowance and the minimum stroke, which is the constraint, and the brief says a thin mark on dark card is where things go wrong, which is the client naming her worry exactly as she would to a designer. Neither says which counter closes, on which mark, or at which of the two placements. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a drawing decision: open the counters and weight the hairlines for a ribbon cut that is a genuinely different artefact from the master, or accept that the refined mark is a large format asset and build a separate small size lockup, either of which changes the application sheet's composition and the production note.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster preparation and to the drawing to produce a ribbon cut with opened counters and a heavier hairline rather than trying to rescue the master by scaling it, re trace, re strip the ground path and inject the viewBox again, then re place at ribbon width and reversed on the dark stock rather than assuming the heavier version took. Check the placement that was not flagged at the same real size. If neither mark holds at ribbon width, state what carries the ribbon instead and re author the application sheet around the mark's real minimum size, which is a different sheet.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A house that sells pieces at four figures wraps them in ribbon carrying a broken wordmark and boxes carrying a foil block with a closed up monogram in it, having been handed artwork that was flawless in every file she was shown, and finds out after the supplier has run the order.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the delivered document actually contains. The application sheet's entire job is to show a hairline foil mark reversing out of a dark ground at real size, and the constructs that express foil, sheen, a debossed edge, a hairline rule around a reversed panel, are exactly the ones whose treatment on import cannot be predicted: some survive intact, some are silently dropped so the element renders as a flat shape, and at least one route makes a text element present in the document and completely invisible on the canvas. The export returns success identically in every case, with no warning of any kind, and the visual preview resolves the first canvas only, so the second canvas exists solely as returned markup. An element that vanished and an element that arrived look the same from the response. The available documentation is not a substitute for looking either, since it is wrong in both directions on several constructs, claiming support that fails and warning against things that work.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The document has to be exported before its contents can be inspected, and no amount of care at authoring time establishes what a given construct became, because the failures are silent and the response is identical. Choosing conservative constructs everywhere is not the answer either: the sheet has to show foil on dark convincingly enough for a supplier to quote from it, and that is the whole design problem. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for an editable sheet showing the mark at real sizes and something showing how the foil sits on the dark stock. No asset, acceptance line or earlier step says which construct will be normalised or dropped. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is to re author the affected panel out of different constructs, which is a design change to the sheet rather than a re export of the same page, and it may change how the foil is represented at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify from the returned markup exactly which elements arrived and in what form, re author the affected panel with constructs that survive rather than adjusting the ones that did not, re export, and re verify per canvas rather than assuming the second attempt took. Check the canvas that was not flagged at the same element by element level, since only one of the two canvases can be seen and the other has never been established as correct.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The client sends her new box supplier an application sheet on which the foil panel is a flat rectangle and part of the specification text is present but invisible, and the supplier quotes from it.

decision_gates: Which capture is allowed to be the authority for colour and which for geometry, and what to do when they are not the same file.
Whether a tone that will not move is a correct flat colour or an unrecoverable one, and how to tell the client the difference.
How far each of three lights is pushed to reach one neutral, and where correcting a capture becomes inventing a colour.
How to word a selection on brushed metal letterforms whose value sits close to their own cast shadow.
Whether the monogram is treated as an object or as a graphic, given interlocked letterforms with shared enclosed counters.
How much refinement the letterforms take, since hairline refinement is what the price band wants and what the ribbon cannot always hold.
Whether the reversed variant is drawn for foil spread or produced by inverting the positive.
Whether a mark that fails at ribbon width is opened up into a separate small size cut or declared a large format asset, and what carries the ribbon if it is.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the three captures into a frontier image model and it draws a new jewelry logo. IDENTITY is the whole commission: this is one house's existing wordmark and monogram, surviving only as a 2019 export, a photograph of brass letters on a wall and a photograph of a foil block on a card, and a regenerated mark is simply a different house with the same name. SPEC is a manufacturing specification: a single closed outline at a stated minimum cut width for the engraver, artwork drawn for a stated foil spread on a named dark stock, a wordmark at a used width along a 10mm ribbon, clear space to the supplier's rule. A generated picture satisfies none of it, cannot be quoted from, and cannot be checked. The enclosure cards compound this: they are a record per page run bound to the house's own current list, one card per piece carrying that piece's own reference and price at press resolution at trim, which a generated image neither produces nor can be checked against, and the list has to be reconciled and its pictures cut rather than typed out. EDITABILITY is an explicit deliverable: one document with live text and real vector geometry that the owner revises when the card copy changes, not a flat image of a layout. And the core of the engagement is judgement about material reality that no render can perform: deciding which of three disagreeing captures is telling the truth about a colour that will sit on ten years of packaging, and telling a client honestly that her own mark will not survive her own ribbon. The client asked for that second thing by name, and it is advice rather than an image.

client_brief:
Rebuild our club lettering and use it in the Founders Five bib run

Ironway Run Club's lettering comes from Del's 1994 drawings. We want the ten numerals, twenty-six letters and singlet logo made usable again, followed by the Founders Five bib production.

This needs both drawing judgement and reliable record handling. The race team cannot discover at registration that a filename belongs to a different runner.

Lettering and logo
Ten numerals and twenty six letters recovered from the founder's ink sheet as one weight normalised single colour set, plus the club mark recovered from a screen printed garment, all as placeable scalable artwork with a real viewBox and no opaque full canvas path underneath. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

Bib run
Last season's press PDF reverse engineered into a live merge template carrying the recovered mark, bound to the reconciled roster and delivered twice off one merged document: a press file whose page count equals the reconciled roster count with pages in roster order, and per member single record files named to the roster with identity guaranteed rather than inferred from output position. Plus fabricator proofs at press resolution at trim.

We provide ironway_numbering_sheet.jpg (4032 x 3024); ironway_singlet_mark.jpg (4032 x 3024); ironway_bib_2025.pdf; ironway_roster.csv; ironway_kit_swatch.jpg; ironway_kit_shop_note.txt.

Please show that the normalised strokes and counters work in one ink, then inspect the merged output at print size. The printer's combined file, individual runner files and reusable template should agree with the reconciled roster.

Alongside the finished work, we need a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record. Keep a clear record of the supplied files used, retained for reference, superseded and rejected. Approved source information remains authoritative. Record omissions, substitutions, reconciliations and quality limits, and do not use an undeclared replacement or invented fact to conceal a source problem. Include inspectable paths and small-size proofs; unverified fabrication tolerances remain subject to supplier review.

source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post 'Recreate Sports Jersey Font from Reference Image (Vector SVG / EPS)' (cands/cand_46.json, db_i 823), which asks a freelancer to 'Vectorize and recreate a sports jersey font from a reference image, including both letters (A-Z) and numbers (0-9)', lists 'Matching style and proportions from the reference image / Clean vector artwork', names the use as 'Football/Soccer jersey printing, DTF/Flex/Flock production', and requires 'Consistent stroke widths and spacing'. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com post 'Graphic Designer for DTF T-Shirt Printing' (cands/cand_50.json), wanting one 'clean, polished, print-ready file' with 'Transparent background, clean edges suitable for direct film transfer' and 'the original editable source file'. ENRICHED to the commission that client actually needed: a glyph set alone is an atomic op, and the real post's own framing shows the set exists to serve a season, so the season is the job. price_band_and_audience: A forty dollar per season volunteer club, roughly thirty eight members, no sponsor. The band is load bearing in both directions. Downward it dictates one colour throughout: a single ink on the bib stock, a single cut colour on the heat transfer, numerals heavy enough to read from a marshal's distance in poor light, and no element that adds a plate or a pass. Upward it rules out the paid entry race look an agent drifts into by habit, which is a multi colour bib with a sponsor band, a timing chip zone, a tear off stub and a photo tag block, all of which cost money this club does not have. The founder's hand is the entire brand, so the treatment is reduced by necessity rather than by taste. Ship a premium event look and every technical gate can still pass while the commission is wrong. A posted job of this shape runs 400 to 900 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Volunteer run community road running club with its own spring race, printing kit and race bibs for its members.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1994 by Del in Providence, Rhode Island. A volunteer run club with roughly thirty eight members on the books.
brand_identity.about: Ironway Run Club is a volunteer community running club in Providence with about thirty eight members. Its identity is the numbering the founder drew by hand in 1994, which the members treat as the club itself, and a screen printed club mark that survives on an old singlet. Each spring the kit goes to the heat transfer shop and every member runs the club's own Founders Five race with a bib.
brand_identity.audience: Members aged roughly 22 to 68, half of whom pin a bib on in the dark before a wet April race. Volunteers, not customers.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A forty dollar per season volunteer club with no sponsor. Everything printed must be cheap at volume and survive weather: one colour throughout, nothing that adds a plate or a pass, and nothing that looks like a paid entry event.
brand_identity.typography: The founder's hand drawn numerals and alphabet are the display face and the whole brand. A plain, sturdy sans handles member names and directory copy where legibility at a marshal's distance matters more than character.
brand_identity.voice: Friendly, plain, volunteer to volunteer. A line the club would write: "Founders Five is on. Pin your bib, mind the puddles, we will see you at the line."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No digital brand files exist. The numbering survives only as a phone photograph of the founder's original ink sheet on drafting paper, and the club mark only as a photograph of it screen printed on an old singlet. Nobody knows who made the mark and there is no file of either. Last year's bib survives as the printer's returned press PDF.
brand_identity.values: The founder's hand is the club, so it is kept faithfully. Legible beats clever, and every member gets the same thing for their forty dollars.

assets_supplied.name: ironway_numbering_sheet.jpg (4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: A phone photograph of the founder's original ink style sheet: numerals and the full alphabet drawn by hand on gridded drafting paper, lying on a table under a window.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Del's sheet. This is the lettering everybody in the club knows."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The sheet is a field of many disjoint strokes rather than one coherent mark, so a single selection returns a plausible looking mask that silently omits whole glyphs, and the printed grid sits close to the ink in value across the lower third where the founder pressed lighter. It also carries eleven numeral forms for ten numerals, an open top four and a closed top four side by side with nothing saying which is current, and the top two rows were drawn with a heavier nib, which is invisible on a sheet where every glyph is a different size.

assets_supplied.name: ironway_singlet_mark.jpg (4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the club mark screen printed on an old singlet laid flat: a chevron and rail device inside a ring of small caps type, one ink on a mid tone jersey.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place our mark still lives. Screen printed, a few seasons old, slightly faded."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The knit breaks the printed edge into a sawtooth the trace records faithfully, and it is a compound lockup, so a prompt naming the badge returns the type ring and outer arc while quietly dropping the inner chevron. Naming the garment returns the singlet instead of the ink, background removal on the ring gives back a solid opaque disc, and the ink runs close to the jersey in value along the fold crossing the lower left.

assets_supplied.name: ironway_bib_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last season's bib artwork as the printer returned it: a genuine press PDF at the club's bib trim, one ink, with the club mark placed as an image at the head of the page.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The bib we ran last year. The printer sent the file back and we kept it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What the printed page shows and what the file is made of are different things, and the second is knowable only after conversion: the four blocks the eye reads as separate do not correspond to four editable frames, and the readout that describes the document's text is not the text the document holds. It also carries no bleed, and none can be introduced through this route.

assets_supplied.name: ironway_roster.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The membership roster as the secretary keeps it: member name, assigned number, pace group, emergency contact name and phone, in the order the club wants the bibs stacked.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Thirty eight rows, in the order we want them stacked at packet pickup."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two members hold the same number after a returning member rejoined, one row has an empty number cell, and the name column runs from six characters to a thirty one character double barrelled surname, none of which the secretary has noticed. A record whose name exceeds the space the artwork gives it does not push the layout or announce itself. It stops.

assets_supplied.name: ironway_kit_swatch.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the new singlet fabric with the heat transfer shop's cut colour chip laid on it, so artwork is judged on the ground it will sit on.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The new kit colour and the transfer colour the shop stocks."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What last season's bib actually is once it is a layout document, and whether the mapping built from the tool's own description of it survived into the template. Frame granularity from a converted PDF is not under anyone's control: blocks the eye reads as separate can arrive as one continuous story, so a per frame plan is not expressible and fields must be reached by position inside a single story. Worse, the readout the mapping was computed from is lossy in a way that leaves the text looking well formed, dropping a run while keeping its line break, so every position past the omission is short by the length of the dropped run. The validator returns valid with no warnings on those positions and the preparation step reports that placeholders were created successfully. Only the prepared template's own interchange form says which fields exist.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no care prevents it: granularity is a property of how the printer built the file, and the omission sits inside the readout the tool exists to provide. An agent that already distrusts the readout and derives positions from the document itself simply passes this reading and continues, which is the right outcome for competence. (b) Nothing states it; the brief says only that the printer sent the file back. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different construction: positions recomputed against the true story, fields regrouped onto the frames that exist, insert rows re-ordered by descending position.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping from the document's own text rather than the tool's description of it, regroup the roster fields onto the frames that actually exist, re-prepare the template, and re-read its interchange form field by field before any merge is run.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A thirty eight page press run in which every bib is missing the pace group and the emergency contact, delivered with a success message at every step and a template the club re-runs next season with the same holes in it.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every member's bib carries that member's whole name. The name sits in a fixed measure frame inherited from last season's artwork, and text that exceeds it does not push the layout, does not wrap to a second line and does not raise an overset warning in the output. It stops. The page renders complete, the run reports success, and the only evidence is a surname ending mid word on the pages of members whose names are long. Which records are affected is a property of the club's actual names against a frame width that came from a file nobody measured, and cannot be known before the run exists.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not help and no parameter reflows a frame inherited from a converted document. (b) Nothing states it: the roster is presented as clean and the brief asks only that each member's name appear. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the fix is not another merge of the same data. Either the data changes under a house rule for shortening a name, applied across the whole roster and disclosed, or the field is re-bound so the surname carries its own line, and either way the run must be re-read at its extremes afterwards.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify every affected record by reading rendered pages rather than responses, decide and apply one consistent rule across the whole roster rather than patching individuals, re-merge, and re-read the extremes again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Several members collect a race bib with their surname cut in half, at a club run by volunteers where the bib is the only thing every member receives for their forty dollars.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the traced numbering holds where it is actually used. Traces of hand drawn ink are clean and convincing at canvas scale. At the shop's stated number height on the club's kit colour, the counters of the rounder glyphs can close into solid shapes, the sawtooth the trace inherited from paper fibre and jersey knit becomes a visible ragged edge, and the heavier nib the founder used on the first two rows reads as a different weight beside the rest of the set, which nothing on the sheet reveals because every glyph there is drawn at a different size. None of that is visible in the trace, in any returned value, or on the sheet.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the information exists only once the set is at reproduction size on the real ground, and the tracer takes no options at all, so there is no parameter that could have been set correctly the first time. (b) Nothing states it: the brief calls the sheet the club's lettering and asks for artwork the shop can cut. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because every lever lives upstream in the raster preparation: a different confined correction before the lift, a differently worded stroke level selection, a re-trace, and the same judgement made again at size.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-prepare the affected glyphs in the raster stage, re-lift and re-trace, normalise the set to one weight rather than accepting the sheet's two, and re-judge the whole set together at reproduction size on the swatch instead of glyph by glyph on white.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A kit run where the club's own numerals print with filled counters and mismatched weights, unrecoverable after heat transfer, paid for out of a forty dollar per member season.

decision_gates: Which deliverable belongs on which surface, given that a per member run at volume, a two canvas authored document and raster archaeology are three different kinds of work.

Selection wording on the founder's sheet: naming the paper takes the substrate, naming the drawn line's own visual properties takes the ink, and the grid sits closest to the ink exactly where the drawing is lightest.
How to treat the eleventh numeral form, since the sheet offers two fours and the client has not noticed.
Whether to normalise the founder's two nib weights into one system or preserve the hand as drawn. Preserving it is defensible on a poster and indefensible on a numbering system.
Which form of the recovered mark goes where: scalable transparent artwork onto the authored surfaces, raster plate into the layout frame, never the reverse.
Whether the compound lockup came back whole, since a partial selection succeeds, looks plausible and is missing an element.
Whether the printed bib's visible blocks correspond to anything the converted document contains, which decides the whole mapping strategy.
How to reconcile a roster the client believes is clean, given a duplicated number and an empty number cell, and how to say so without embarrassing the secretary.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of race bibs and a plausible set of numerals. IDENTITY: the numbering is one specific person's hand from 1994 and the mark is this club's actual screen printed mark, so a regenerated set is a different club's lettering, which the members recognise instantly because that lettering is what they think the club looks like. SPEC: the run is thirty eight pages in the club's own roster order, each page carrying that member's real name, number, pace group and emergency contact, plus per member files named to real people, at press resolution at trim, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the merge template must be re-runnable next season with a new roster by the club's next volunteer, and the spec sheet must be retypeable. client_brief:
Restore the Exchange crest and rebuild the suite-plate workflow

Marchfield Exchange is a listed 1911 building. The crest needs recovering from brass and letterhead references; the suite plates need updating from the 2019 production PDF. We are preserving an identity and an installation, not commissioning a redesign.

Please quote the complete package:

The house crest recovered from physical survivors rather than redrawn, as placeable scalable artwork with a real viewBox and no opaque full canvas path underneath, delivered as the master, a reversed variant for dark ground, and an engraving ready single closed outline whose counters are true holes. Do not treat a trace alone as production approval: deliver transparent SVG, rendered small-size proofs, and an inspectable geometry report. Any unverified contour or fabrication tolerance must be labeled for supplier review.

The 2019 sign shop's press artwork reverse engineered into a live merge template bound to the reconciled schedule, delivered as one press file whose page count equals the reconciled suite count in schedule order, plus per suite named files with identity guaranteed rather than inferred from output position, plus fabricator proofs at press resolution at trim. No plate carries a blank field and no suite appears twice.

An inspectable proof of Recovered Marchfield crest and engraving geometry at every claimed reproduction size and on light/dark grounds, with open-path, closure, transparency, contour, and unsupported-feature findings stated plainly.

We need the plate run reconciled to the suite information, with no blank or duplicate records. Please check the actual per-suite files, not only the combined run. For engraving, identify the closed outlines and open spaces clearly and leave unverified fabrication tolerances for supplier review.

source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post 'Logo Vectorization + Brand Identity Kit' (cands/cand_45.json, db_i 0), whose client has 'an existing logo I love' and needs a designer to 'Vectorize and clean up my current logo to print-ready quality' and 'Build out a full set of logo variations and brand files I can use across everything', listing 'Master logo in vector format', a 'One-color version (white on dark, black on light)' and files 'sized and ready for' named physical applications, and stating 'Please do NOT apply if: You only deliver JPG or PNG files'. Co-anchor: the Upwork post 'Logo Design & Challenge Coin Artwork' (cands/cand_38.json, db_i 95), which asks for artwork 'that can be sent to a mint/manufacturer', insists on 'True vector artwork, not raster images' and requires it be 'Readable at small sizes'. Neither post names a real client; the managing agent, the building, its crest and its tenants are invented here. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the first post's 'exact hex, CMYK, and Pantone codes' and 'Font identification' are not connector work, since nothing here measures a colour or identifies a typeface from an image, so the commission is carried by what is real: recovery of a mark surviving only on physical objects, engraving ready geometry judged against a fabricator's stated minimum stroke, panels authored at true physical sizes as a native editable document, and a per suite plate run built off the previous sign shop's own press artwork.

price_band_and_audience: A listed heritage building letting at forty five to seventy five dollars per square foot to law, architecture and accountancy firms, with a board approving the spend. At this tier the programme is engraved brass and stone appropriate metalwork, a serif with real heritage credibility, deep margins, generous clear space around the crest, and a directory that reads as a document rather than as signage. Push down into a budget system and it becomes moulded plastic, a condensed grotesque, tight margins and a loud contrast board, which at this rent reads as neglect and undermines the one asset the tenants pay for. Push up into contemporary luxury and it becomes a minimal sans on a dark monolith, which fights a 1911 stone entrance and reads as a refurbishment a conservation officer would refuse. Either extreme misreads the commission even where every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 4,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: A listed 1911 commercial building, managed by a property agent, let as office suites to professional firms, with a heritage sign programme.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Building completed 1911 in Portland, Maine. Fourteen lettable suites, overseen by a managing agent and a building board.
brand_identity.about: The Marchfield Exchange is a listed 1911 commercial building let to law, architecture and accountancy firms. The building itself, its stone entrance and brass fittings, is the reason tenants take space here. Its house crest is original to 1911, and the sign programme is being rebuilt as one coherent system that respects the building's character.
brand_identity.audience: Professional firms choosing a building with a stone entrance and brass fittings, and a building board approving the spend. Tenants who read signage as a signal of how the building is kept.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A listed heritage building letting at 45 to 75 dollars per square foot. The programme is engraved brass and stone appropriate metalwork, deep margins and generous clear space. Anything that would look at home on a retail park reads as neglect at this rent.
brand_identity.typography: A heritage serif with real credibility carries the building name and the crest lockup. A quieter companion serif or restrained roman sets the directory and suite plates, so the board reads as a document rather than as signage.
brand_identity.voice: Formal, measured, understated. A line the agent would write: "The Marchfield Exchange. Established 1911. Professional suites in the heart of the city."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No drawing, plate or digital file of the crest exists, and the original architect's practice closed in 1961. The crest survives in exactly two places: engraved on the weathered brass entry plaque, photographed on the wall, and printed on a 1950s tenant letterhead, scanned. The suite plates survive only as the 2019 sign shop's single press PDF.
brand_identity.values: The building's history is the asset, so the crest is recovered rather than reinvented, and the programme is kept editable so the agent can update a tenant name without a designer.

assets_supplied.name: marchfield_plaque.jpg (5472 x 3648)
assets_supplied.kind: The original engraved brass entry plaque photographed on the facade in late afternoon raking light, handheld, the crest filling most of the frame.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The plaque by the door. This is the crest, on the real thing."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The polished bevel throws a specular ridge sitting brighter than the engraved field, so a graphic level selection takes the ridge as if it were part of the crest, while along the shaded left third the incised line and the brass run to nearly the same value and the wreath does not come back there at all. Neither is apparent on the photograph, which reads as the sharper and more authoritative of the two sources.

assets_supplied.name: marchfield_letterhead.jpg (3400 x 4400)
assets_supplied.kind: A flatbed scan of a 1950s tenant letterhead carrying the same crest at about thirty millimetres, one deep ink on cream stock, the sheet foxed at the edges.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "A letterhead a tenant found in a filing cabinet. Same crest, much smaller."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: At the size it was printed the ink gained, so two of the crest's interior rules have run into one another and the ribbon's counters have filled, a closure invisible on the sheet and obvious only beside the other candidate. The crest also occupies a small part of a large scan, so what looks like a high resolution source is a small source inside a big file, and nothing downstream may enlarge it.

assets_supplied.name: marchfield_facade.jpg (6000 x 4000)
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the entrance bay taken for the board's approval mockup, the existing plaque in place in a shaded stone reveal.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The entrance, so we can see the new plaque where it will actually go."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: In the shaded reveal the limestone surround and the brass plaque field run to nearly the same value along the left edge, so an automatic isolation of the plaque area reports success, previews convincingly and bites that edge, leaving a crescent of the old engraving and a ragged stone boundary that appears only at full resolution.

assets_supplied.name: marchfield_suite_plate_2019.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The previous sign shop's print ready artwork for a single suite plate from the 2019 refit, a genuine press PDF at plate trim, one ink.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The plate artwork from the last refit. It is the only file the old sign shop left us."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The suite number and the firm name look like two separate blocks on the page and are one continuous run in the file, so fields have to be reached by position inside a single story rather than frame by frame. It also carries the abandoned 2019 numbering convention in its own text, which no longer matches the schedule, and no bleed can be introduced into anything derived from it.

assets_supplied.name: marchfield_schedule.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The managing agent's current tenant schedule: suite number, floor, firm name and lease status, in the order the directory board is to read.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our current schedule. Fourteen suites, in the order we want them on the board."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two suites appear twice, once under their 2019 number and once under the number in use since the renumbering, so the row count is not the suite count. One suite is vacant with an empty firm cell, which merges into a plate carrying a blank line rather than being skipped, and three firm names carry an ampersand while one runs to thirty eight characters.

assets_supplied.name: marchfield_sign_survey.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The fabricator's site survey as plain text: entrance sign, directory board and suite plate sizes in millimetres, substrate and fixing for each, and the shop's minimum engraved stroke width at final size.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What our fabricator measured and what his machine can hold."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which of the two surviving records of the crest is usable, and the answer is that neither is usable whole. The plaque photograph is larger, sharper and the real object, but the raking light's specular ridge along the bevel traces as if it were geometry and the shaded left third gives no separation at all, so the wreath is simply absent there. The letterhead is even and complete but was printed small, so the ink gained until two interior rules merged and the ribbon's counters filled, a closure invisible on the sheet that declares itself only beside the other trace at suite plate size. Both traces succeed, both look convincing at canvas scale, and the failures are in different places on each.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not avoid it, and tracing both is competent practice rather than a dodge, because what cannot be known in advance is where each source fails, which is a property of this light on this metal and this ink on this stock. The tracer has no parameters at all. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the crest survives in two places and must come back as the building's crest. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different chain: a confined correction over the shaded third to open a separation that does not yet exist, a re-worded selection at incised level, a re-trace, and a fresh comparison at the same reproduction sizes.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster stage on the chosen capture, lift the shaded region with a confined correction rather than a whole frame move, re-select and re-trace, and judge the result again at the smallest reproduction size on brass before anything downstream is built on it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A heritage crest shipped to a brass engraver with a specular ridge cut into it as if it were part of the design, or with a wreath that stops a third of the way round, permanently, on a listed building's entrance.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the treatment the whole programme's look rests on. An incised, engraved register is reached in an authored page by exactly the constructions this importer quietly discards: a blur filter is dropped outright, a layered shadow is truncated to its first layer, a text shadow is dropped, an outline is dropped, and a stroked letterform written with a text stroke and a transparent fill comes back fully invisible rather than as an outline. Every one of those returns success with no warning. The document's own rendition shows the first panel only, so the entrance sign may look right while the directory board and the plate sheet have lost the treatment entirely, and the returned per panel markup is the only channel that reports it.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time would mean knowing in advance which of several equally reasonable constructions survives, which nothing reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a quiet traditional register and for panels the agent can edit later. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different construction: the incised register rebuilt from what does survive, real strokes on shapes, a single shadow layer, borders and gradients, or carried up into the raster stage so the treatment is part of the artwork rather than a page effect, then a re-author and a fresh audit of every panel.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the incised treatment from constructions the importer keeps, re-author the HTML around that decision, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every panel from the returned markup rather than from the first one.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A sign programme approved by a building's board on the strength of the one panel anybody looked at, with the directory board and the plate sheet arriving flat, and in the worst case a panel whose lettering is present in the document and invisible on the canvas.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the plaque field in the facade photograph can be isolated cleanly at all. In the shaded reveal the limestone surround and the brass run to nearly the same value along the left edge, and an automatic isolation there returns a result that reports success, previews convincingly at the scale anyone would check it at, and bites that edge, so a crescent of the old engraving survives inside the supposedly cleared field and the stone boundary comes back ragged. Where it bites, and how far, is a property of this bay in this light and appears only at full resolution.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the tool has no edge tolerance to set and the failure is in the material rather than in the call. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks only to see the new plaque on the building before the board commits. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different chain: select the limestone as a material by its own surface properties, invert that selection, and drive the fill from the ground instead of from the object, a route the naive attempt never touches.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the object led isolation, select the surrounding stone as a material, invert it, fill from that mask, and inspect the boundary at full resolution rather than at preview scale before the mockup panel is authored around it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: An approval mockup in which the old engraving is still faintly visible under the new plaque and the stone edge is chewed, put in front of a building's board as the thing they are asked to sign off.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are authored panels at fixed physical sizes and which is a genuine record per page run, given that only one surface here composes free form layout.
Which surviving record of the crest is the master, when the more authoritative looking capture is not necessarily the more even one and the answer may be neither on its own.
How much of the crest's detail survives at suite plate size, and whether a simplified interpretation is needed below a stated size or whether one drawing serves every panel.
How to produce true interior holes, given that background removal fills an enclosed interior and returns something that looks correct until it sits on a colour.
What the fabricator's minimum stroke means per panel, since a hairline that is fine on an entrance sign can be unroutable on a plate.
How to reconcile a tenant schedule the client believes is the suite list, given a renumbering that left duplicates and a vacant suite that would otherwise print a plate with a hole in it.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a listed 1911 building at forty five to seventy five dollars a square foot rather than against a signage category.
How to deliver identity safely across fourteen plates, since files named by their position in a response are not files named by whose door they go on.

normalized_process_checks.text: Every required connector operation has a normalized execution record.

The sign document is editable by the managing agent next season: live retypeable text, the crest as real vector shapes, and the source it was built from delivered alongside.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome heraldic crest and pictures of signs. IDENTITY: this is a specific 1911 building's own crest, surviving on two physical objects, and a regenerated crest is a different building's history, which is exactly what a listed building's board is paying not to receive. SPEC: the fabricator engraves from geometry, so the deliverable is a closed outline with true interior holes whose every stroke clears his machine's stated minimum at each panel's real size, and the plates are a page per suite in the agent's own schedule order carrying real tenant names at press resolution at trim, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the whole point of the handover is that the agent changes a tenant name themselves when a lease turns over, so the directory has to be live cells and the plate template has to be re-runnable. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: which capture holds where, whether this counter is still a hole at plate size, whether the isolation bit the stone, whether the treatment survived on the panels nobody previewed.

residual_limits: Express work is template adaptation, not unrestricted canvas authoring.
